audits.f: Correct method of checking postural blood pressure 52.4%; correct identification of postural hypotension 33.3%; confidence in identification 47.6%.
audits.c: Educational programme for MDT members (PDSA cycle).

audits.t: 1255 IMPROVING COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEXT OF KIN AND MEDICAL STAFF FOR OUR MOST VULNERABLE PATIENTS: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.st: NICE NG27, NG97 and NG96
audits.f: 25/55 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion in 74%; treatment plan discussions 81%.
audits.c: Education of the medical team and a written prompt in the patient's notes
audits.r2: 39/71 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion 82%; treatment plan discussions 97%.

audits.t: 1575 IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF COMPREHENSIVE GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT THROUGH INCORPORATION OF SKIN ASSESSMENT
audits.st: Skin assessment as part of comprehensive geriatric assessment documented by doctors
audits.f: 15.8% of skin assessments documented by doctors (80.7% by nurses).

audits.r2: After PDSA 3, 8.8% of skin assessments completed.

audits.t: 1660 QUALITY IMPROVEMENT FOCUSSED ON IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF DELIRIUM IN OLDER SURGICAL PATIENTS
audits.st: 4AT delirium screening of patients aged over 65 on arrival and at 48 hours
audits.f: 36% likely to have delirium on 4AT; 5% coded as delirium and 19% had delirium documented in notes; average 4AT completion 40%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles introducing 4AT and delirium sections in care plans, plus teaching and supporting materials around the PINCHME acronym for SAU staff.
audits.r2: Average 4AT completion rose from 40% to 64%, reaching 100% after interventions but falling back between them.

audits.t: 1581 POSTURAL HYPOTENSION – A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.tp: Lying and standing blood pressure measurement
audits.st: National Audit of Inpatient Falls: lying and standing BP for patients over 65, using RCP technique
audits.f: LSBP measured in 28%; correct technique 12%; medication review 0%; lifestyle advice 0%.
audits.c: Formal and informal teaching, RCP guidance displayed on noticeboards and BP devices, and a postural hypotension sticker
audits.r2: LSBP measured in 96% (p<0.00001); correct technique 37.5%; medication review 87.5%; lifestyle advice 37.5%.

audits.t: 21 An audit of vision assessment in patients presenting for a review of falls
audits.tp: Falls risk screening and multifactorial assessment
audits.st: NICE 2013 falls guideline (formal vision assessment for all) and BGS/RCP bedside vision assessment tool
audits.f: 11 (69%) not asked about vision; of 5 asked, only 2 had documented visual field assessment; none had all RCP-recommended checks.
audits.c: Planned: basic visual assessment tools (e.g. Snellen chart), updated falls proforma and staff education before re-audit.

audits.t: 8 A prospective audit on outpatient clinical activity in a consultant-led general medical and specialist geriatric clinic
audits.st: National protocol for outpatient waiting list management; Clinically Recommended Timeframe (CRT)
audits.f: 94% seen within the CRT; both urgent referrals (2) not seen within the CRT; median waitlist 15.5 weeks.

audits.t: 67 Audit of discharge summaries on a geriatric ward against the Health Information and Quality Authority (HIQA) National Standard
audits.st: HIQA National Standard for discharge summaries
audits.f: Only 4 (20%) had all relevant information; 8 (40%) had complete clinical course; 8 (40%) had medication omissions; 5 (25%) omitted stopped medications and reasons; 5 (25%) had incomplete future plans; 4 (20%) omitted complications.
audits.c: Discharge Summary Flowchart introduced as a guide; ongoing continuous audit by SHOs and interns.

audits.t: 79 Aiming to be champions: stroke swallow screen audit
audits.tp: Swallow screening within 4 hours of stroke
audits.st: Stroke swallow screen completed within 4 hours of presentation (National Stroke Guidelines 2022)
audits.f: 44% (39 patients) had a swallow screen; only 13% (11 patients) within 4 hours.
audits.c: Planned: SLT-led training of relevant staff and a swallow screen QI programme for 2023.

audits.t: 88 An audit of the quality of documentation during the end of life phase of older adults in acute hospital settings
audits.st: BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care 'Guidance for completing End of Life Structured Judgement Review' quality indicators
audits.f: Stroke vs AIGM: recognition of dying 92.9% (26/28) vs 94.1% (16/17); DNAR 100% vs 100%; escalation plan 84.6% vs 75%; risk of dying communicated to family 75% vs 59%; anticipatory medicines prescribed 94.1% vs 92.9%; spirituality documented 17.9% vs 5.9%; patient wishes 7.1% vs 0%.

audits.t: 91 Audit of percentage of stroke patients having swallow screen performed within 4 hrs of diagnosis on the stroke ward in OLOL Hospital Drogheda
audits.tp: Swallow screening within 4 hours of stroke
audits.st: HSE National Guideline for Swallow Screening 2017: swallow screen within 4 hours of diagnosis
audits.f: 24 of 29 had a documented swallow assessment; only 3 were screened within 4 hours of diagnosis.
audits.c: Planned: teaching sessions and reminder charts for on-call NCHDs and nursing staff.

audits.t: 101 An audit of falls risk assessment in older adults in an Irish general practice
audits.tp: Falls risk assessment in community-dwelling older adults
audits.st: World Guidelines for Falls Prevention and Management in Older Adults (September 2022): all patients 65 and over asked 3 Key Questions, appropriate referral, and routine falls prevention advice
audits.f: 3 Key Questions asked 0%; appropriate referrals 75%; falls risk advice 9%.
audits.c: Practice education session, falls algorithm in every room and a consensus meeting.
audits.r2: 3 Key Questions asked 50%; appropriate referrals 89%; falls risk advice 22%.

audits.t: 145 Audit of yearly prevalence of atrial fibrillation in ischemic stroke patients admitted to a level III acute Irish hospital
audits.tp: Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after stroke
audits.st: Published evidence of AF burden around 30% in acute ischaemic stroke
audits.f: 41% (N=65) had AF deemed the cause of stroke: 18% (N=29) newly diagnosed and 23% (N=36) known AF. Of known AF, 13.8% (N=5) not anticoagulated, 58.3% (N=21) on adjusted dose, 27.7% (N=10) not fully compliant.

audits.t: 168 A quality improvement initiative to enhance dementia inclusivity within the physical environment of an older persons’ acute hospital ward
audits.st: Irish National Audit of Dementia (INAD-2) environmental checklist and national standards
audits.f: Reduced compliance with national standards; no figures given.
audits.c: Orientation clocks, orientation whiteboards and increased signage and labels on the ward.
audits.r2: Increased compliance with national standards; no figures given.

audits.t: 191 Intermittent: an audit of venous thromboembolism prophylaxis on our stroke unit
audits.st: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (UK and Ireland): IPCs for immobile patients days 3 to 30
audits.f: VTE risk section completed in 21 (68%); of 9 eligible immobile patients none had IPCs prescribed and 1 (11%) had them in situ; 56% had no VTE prophylaxis.

audits.t: 221 A one-year audit of intracranial haemorrhages that presented to a level 4 hospital and died within 30 days
audits.st: Target blood pressure ≤140 mmHg within 2 hours of diagnosis; stroke unit admission
audits.f: 3/8 (38%) with arrival systolic BP 150-220 mmHg achieved ≤140 mmHg at 2 hours; 5/11 (45%) who died were admitted to the stroke unit; 3 of 5 anticoagulated patients received a reversal agent.

audits.t: 224 Profiling the first service users of a Community Specialist Team for older persons: a retrospective chart audit
audits.tp: Community specialist team for older people service profile
audits.st: NICPOP framework; target length of stay six weeks
audits.f: 80% frail (CFS ≥5); average length of stay 10 weeks, exceeding the six-week target.

audits.t: 235 A clinical audit of detection and management of sarcopenia in a mixed stroke ward in an academic teaching hospital
audits.st: International and European Clinical Practice Guidelines for sarcopenia screening and treatment
audits.f: No patients were screened for or had sarcopenia documented on admission; muscle strength assessed in 53% under geriatric care vs 38% under other teams; no patient had muscle quality analysis.

audits.t: 236 Assessing communication of duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on discharge letters: an acute stroke unit audit
audits.tp: Dual antiplatelet therapy after minor stroke or TIA
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: DAPT duration documented in discharge letters of 28/34 (82%); 5 of these were still inappropriately on DAPT at follow up; 19 of 22 co-prescribed PPI had no documented PPI plan.
audits.c: Results presented at stroke unit teaching; NCHD education and EMR changes recommended

audits.t: 254 The use of delirium screening tools during acute inpatient hospital admissions: a local audit
audits.st: Local HSE guidelines: formalised delirium screening tool within 24 hours of ED presentation for all adults over 65
audits.f: 21.4% (n = 12) had a delirium screening tool documented, all using 4AT and all completed by the OPAL/ED Frailty Intervention Team.

audits.t: 277 Audit of intentional rounds to measure compliance and explore patient feedback in a rehabilitation hospital for older adults
audits.st: Intentional rounding KPI of 90% compliance with the IR check-list
audits.f: 2 wards achieved the KPI (90%); others fell short mainly due to incomplete check-lists on night-duty shifts.

audits.t: 297 Assessing continence care in a rehabilitation unit: insights from an audit
audits.tp: Continence assessment and care in older inpatients
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard
audits.f: 26 (83.9%) wore incontinence wear, 21 (80.8%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 13 (41.9%).
audits.c: Continence added to NCHD teaching schedule and MDT proforma adjusted to include a patient-specific continence record.
audits.r2: 27 (67.5%) wore incontinence wear, 19 (70%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 18 (45.7%).

audits.t: 304 Increasing the intensity of physiotherapy in a subacute stroke rehabilitation unit—results of audit and intervention
audits.st: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (2023): high-intensity therapy, total of 3 hours daily, and improved reporting of exercise prescription
audits.f: Average recorded repetitions per week 77.9 (range 0–288).
audits.c: Stroke exercise class restructured into a twice-weekly circuit class (5 x 6-minute stations) with outdoor mobility, tally counters, more semi-supervised practice and a 'champions board'.
audits.r2: Average recorded repetitions per week 1,043 (range 245–2095); average 462 repetitions in the exercise class.

audits.t: 305 Assessing patient attire in a medical gerontology ward: impact of an ‘End PJ Paralysis’ audit
audits.tp: End PJ paralysis (patients up and dressed)
audits.st: 'End PJ Paralysis' campaign
audits.f: Breakfast: 38.5% sat out, 25.6% own clothes, 69.2% pyjamas, 5.1% hospital gowns. Lunch (n=38): 84.2% sat out, 78.9% own clothes, 2.6% gown.
audits.c: Staff education on PJ paralysis, promoting day room use at lunchtime, communication with patients/relatives about personal clothes and footwear, and a clothing donation drive.
audits.r2: Breakfast: 56.8% sat out, 18.2% own clothes, 81.8% pyjamas. Lunch: 81.8% sat out, 75% own clothes, 25% pyjamas; no hospital gowns.

audits.t: 307 An audit of dual antiplatelet prescribing after minor ischaemic stroke
audits.tp: Dual antiplatelet therapy after minor stroke or TIA
audits.st: American Heart Association class 1A recommendation for DAPT in minor ischaemic stroke (NIHSS 3 or less); rationale documented if not prescribed
audits.f: 8 commenced on DAPT; 48.3% (n = 14) either prescribed DAPT or had a documented rationale for SAPT.

audits.t: 313 Audit of adherence to the National Standards of acute stroke metrics in a tertiary hospital in Dublin, Ireland
audits.st: 2021 Irish National Audit of Stroke key performance metrics
audits.f: Thrombolysis rate 18% with 75% receiving tPA within 1 hour of arrival (INAS 10% and 56%); median door-to-image 24 mins and door-to-needle 42 mins (INAS 63 and 43 mins).

audits.t: 324 Statin prescribing in ischaemic stroke patients: quality improvement of an acute stroke ward in a model 4 tertiary teaching hospital
audits.st: High-intensity statin (SPARCL trial) and Medicines Management Programme recommendation of atorvastatin as preferred drug
audits.f: 19 of 21 patients on a statin at data collection (13 before admission); 76% had a change in statin type or dose during admission; 95% were prescribed their statin at night.
audits.c: Planned education session with pharmacy on atorvastatin/rosuvastatin prescribing timing, with re-audit to follow.

audits.t: 1940 Delirium in acute medicine inpatients - are we still missing it? Results from an 8-year audit in a District General Hospital
audits.st: Admission delirium screen and documentation of delirium within the first 48 hours
audits.f: Delirium screening completion 3%; explicit delirium diagnosis 10%; potentially missed delirium 18%.

audits.r2: Delirium screening completion 87%; explicit delirium diagnosis 32%; potentially missed delirium 10%.

audits.t: 1941 Working as a multidisciplinary team to reduce weight loss - a quality improvement project to improve nutrition in older patients
audits.tp: Nutritional screening and weight loss in older inpatients

audits.r2: 55% lost weight during admission; 80% had weekly MUST assessments.

audits.t: 2254 Improving the quality and breadth of advance care planning discussions on gerontology wards in an acute London trust

audits.r2: Preferred place of death 60% (p 0.011); treatment escalation plan 75% (p 0.014); preferred place of care 71% (p 0.066).

audits.t: 2320 DNAR: all or nothing: impact of education sessions Re-audit
audits.tp: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation

audits.t: Under Pressure: An Audit of Pressure Injury Documentation in Hospitalised Older Adults
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: An Audit Of Health And Ageing Online Resources: Evaluating Information On Periodontitis And Cardiovascular Disease Associations
audits.st: 2019 EFP/WHF consensus report on periodontal disease and cardiovascular disease
audits.f: Only 8 (8.8%) sites had information on the PD-CVD link within five years, of which 5 (5.5%) gave actionable oral health guidance.

audits.t: Ensuring Patient Care Continuity: An Audit of Discharge Letter Completeness in Accordance with National Standards
audits.st: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary Information (25 variables), 80% completeness per variable
audits.f: 17 of 25 variables 100% complete (automatically included); discharge medication and follow-up over 80%; allergy status 27%; blood and radiological investigations 49%.

audits.r2: Further improvement in lying and standing blood pressure and polypharmacy assessments.

audits.t: Audit of Lithium Monitoring in a Mental Health for Older Persons (Dublin North City Central) Service
audits.st: Irish Medication Safety Network (IMSN) guidance for prescribing and monitoring lithium therapy
audits.f: Poor compliance with lithium monitoring against the standard (figures not stated).

audits.r2: Improvement in recording of blood monitoring (figures not stated).

audits.t: An Audit Of Falls Admissions Documentation To A University Hospital: Cycle 1

audits.t: Quality Of Care In Parkinson's Disease: Lessons From A National Audit
audits.st: De novo audit tool based on international standards, guidelines and audit tools
audits.f: 16.8% seen less than annually; motor and mobility assessment >75%; cognition 70%; pain 64%; saliva management 50%; bone density 18%; PD nurse access 65%; physiotherapy 69%; SLT 53%; OT 50%; written information after diagnosis 24%.

audits.st: NICE: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; HSE VTE Prevention Programme template

audits.t: Audit of Medication Reconciliation by Admitting NCHDs in a Sample of Older Adults in a Model 2 Hospital
audits.st: Completion of all 5 subsections of the medication reconciliation page in the MAU admission booklet
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Education session on medication reconciliation for NCHDs.
audits.r2: 1 page fully completed, 26 partially completed and 2 not completed; medication list section fully completed in 7, partially in 20 and not in 2.

audits.t: A Multidisciplinary Prospective Audit of Practices of Providing Hydration to Patient in An Acute Care Setting. Stop, Think and Drink
audits.st: HIQA nutrition and hydration standards (used to develop audit tool); Dementia Friendly Hospital Guidelines 2018
audits.f: Almost all patients had a drink and water jug available; 38% required prompting or reminding to drink.

audits.t: Quality Improvements in Dementia Care in an Acute Hospital Setting
audits.tp: Dementia and delirium care in hospital

audits.f: 85% compliance with the 4AT tool; 17/20 charts had complete 4AT scores.

audits.f: Only 25% of patients had formal pain assessment documented on admission.

audits.t: Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR) Status Awareness Among Healthcare Staff For Patient's Under Their Care: A Clinical Audit

audits.c: Recommended: keep only original coloured DNAR forms on the ward, file forms at front of charts, add a DNAR status column to medical and nursing handover sheets.

audits.t: Audit Of Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) Screening In Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) Admitted Patients In A Model-2 Hospital
audits.st: Local frailty screening pathway: all MAU patients aged 75 or over screened with the Clinical Frailty Scale using a bespoke sticker; CFS 6 or more triggers referral to the CNS for the Older Adult
audits.f: Of 94 eligible patients (of 247 attendees), 81% (n=77) had a bespoke sticker and 71% of these were completed (n=55). Of 40 admitted, 57.5% (n=23) referred and seen by CNS, 35% (n=14) appropriately not referred, 2.5% (n=1) not referred but should have been, 5% (n=2) referred but not seen.

audits.t: An Audit of Best Medical Therapy Adherence Among Patients with Carotid Artery Stenosis Attending a Tertiary Stroke Centre
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in carotid stenosis
audits.st: European Stroke Organisation guidelines for best medical therapy; LDL-C target below 1.8

audits.t: An Audit On Minimising Unnecessary Catheter Use In An Older Population Attending The Emergency Department
audits.tp: Urinary catheter use in older patients

audits.f: Catheterisation consistent with best practice in 20 (91%); indication clearly documented in 8 (36%); none removed in ED (0%).

audits.t: Improving Delirium Care: A Retrospective Audit of Early Detection and Management Practices

audits.t: An Examination of EOL Trajectories and Audit of EOL Documentation In Patients Admitted Under the Department for Older Persons Services
audits.st: Oxford Audit Assessment Tool for Care of the Dying (1–5 point scale)
audits.f: Greater than 90% of patients had satisfactory, good or excellent end-of-life documentation.

audits.t: DNAR: All or Nothing: Impact of Education Sessions Re-Audit in a Model 3 Hospital
audits.tp: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation

audits.f: DNAR status in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion documented 45%; reasons if excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 18%.
audits.c: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.
audits.r2: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if excluded 25%.

audits.t: 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety
audits.st: Microguide local antimicrobial guidance; indication, route, duration and choice of antibiotic

audits.t: 2888 De-prescribing anti-Hyperglycemics in the elderly—a quality improvement project

audits.t: 2669 Diagnosing delirium on the Care of the Elderly Ward: a quality improvement project
audits.st: NICE guidelines: 100% of patients on geriatric wards to have delirium considered via the 4AT
audits.f: 50.7% (21) suspected delirious; of these 9.5% (2) had a delirium assessment on the same day.

audits.t: 3225 Delirium assessments in an acute frailty ward: an audit of current practice

audits.t: 980 An Audit of a Surgical Ambulatory Service [SAmS] Performance Pre And Post COVID-19 - The Impact of Senior Decision Making
audits.st: Ambulatory service principle: consultant led and delivered service
audits.f: 20% of sessions consultant led; 27% of cases completed on index attendance.

audits.r2: 100% of sessions consultant led; 64% of cases completed on index attendance.

audits.t: 945 Re-Audit of Incorrect Tcis; Are We Now Listing the Right Teeth
audits.st: TCI forms correctly list teeth planned for extraction
audits.f: 6 forms where teeth listed differed from teeth planned for extraction; two wrong tooth extractions in 2018.
audits.c: Change to TCI forms following root cause analysis.
audits.r2: No incorrect TCI forms and no wrong tooth extractions.

audits.t: 850 Addressing Fertility Preservation in Patients Under the Age of 35 Diagnosed with Breast Cancer. A Ten-Year Audit in A Regional Unit
audits.tp: Fertility preservation counselling in young breast cancer

audits.f: Over 50% of patients had at least one child before referral and less than 5% had considered pregnancy during or after treatment; counselling rate not reported.

audits.t: 56 ‘A Closed-Loop Audit on The Appropriateness of Urine Testing Carried Out on Surgical Patients in The Acute Surgical Unit in University Hospital Limerick as Compared with Hospital Guidelines’
audits.st: University Hospital Limerick guidelines on urine testing
audits.f: 68% had urinalysis and 48% urine culture; only 23 of 47 (49%) cultures were indicated

audits.t: 57 A Closed Loop Audit of Post-Operative Driving Advice Documentation
audits.st: DVLA guidance on resuming driving after surgery; driving advice documented on discharge summaries
audits.f: 62% had driving advice documented on discharge summaries.
audits.c: Posters encouraging inclusion of driving advice and showing how to add it to discharge summaries

audits.t: 99 Perfecting the Proforma – A Full-Cycle Audit on The Quality of Documentation of The Hand Trauma Proforma At the Regional Plastic Surgery Department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: X-ray findings documented 55%; antibiotic plan 35%; post-op plan 100%; post-op antibiotics 90%; follow-up plan 95%
audits.c: Updated hand trauma proforma including a free text box
audits.r2: Overall completion increased; responsible consultant 100%; X-ray findings 85%; antibiotic plan 80%; but post-op plan fell to 85%, post-op antibiotics 75% and follow-up plan 60%

audits.t: 100 Assessing the Admission Proforma: A Multi-Cycle Audit Evaluating the Quality of Documentation of The Burnsadmission Proforma At the Regional Mersey Burn Unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: History 94%, comorbidities 94%, drug history 95%, TBSA 83%, treatment plan 91%, admission documentation 24%, consultant confirmation of TBSA 5%.

audits.r2: 58 of 61 comparable fields (95%) improved; history, comorbidities and drug history 100%; TBSA 93%; treatment plan 95%; admission documentation 51%; consultant confirmation of TBSA 10%.

audits.t: 144 For Audit's Sake: An Audit of Audits
audits.st: 100% of audits should be full cycle (BMJ) and 100% must be measured against explicit standards (NICE)
audits.f: 38 audits registered, 7 not completed; re-audit compliance 35% (7/20); standards compliance 84% (5 without pre-determined standards).

audits.t: 185 Comparing the Contents of The On-Call ENT SHO Bag at A Busy District General Hospital to ENT UK Guidelines – A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: ENT UK guidelines on on-call bag contents (checklist)
audits.f: Bag missing numerous items (tongue depressors to nasal catheters) and contained bulky unnecessary items such as Lahey forceps.
audits.c: Bag replenished, unnecessary items removed, PPE added and a nightly SHO checklist introduced.
audits.r2: Bag remained well stocked with only minor items missing (Merocel packs, Sofradex drops), with alternatives present.

audits.t: 225 The Management of Acute Cholecystitis in a District General setting: An Audit of Practice
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: NICE: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis of acute cholecystitis
audits.f: 285 (87%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days; of 43 who did not, 31 had clinically justified delay; 285/297 (96%) met the NICE standard.
audits.r2: Re-audit showed significant improvement (no figures reported).

audits.t: 267 An Audit of The Management of Acute Cholecystitis At ELHT
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: NICE CG188: offer early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis for acute cholecystitis
audits.f: 51 (47%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within a week of diagnosis.

audits.t: 277 Smoking and Alcohol Use Assessments in Head and Neck Surgical Inpatients: An Audit to Improve Health Promotion
audits.st: CQUIN smoking and alcohol questions in discharge summaries; local standard 95% completion
audits.f: Smoking status documented 27.3% (27/99); alcohol use 36.3% (36/99).
audits.c: Education of ENT juniors (foundation and core trainees) and ward-based prompts.

audits.t: 295 Secondary Prevention of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Patients Admitted Under the Vascular Service - Full Cycle Audit
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
audits.st: NICE CG147 and TA607 for peripheral arterial disease
audits.f: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant 100%; lipid modification 82%; diabetic referral for high HbA1c 75%; smoking cessation advice/documentation 19%.
audits.c: Single teaching session for junior doctors and a dedicated computer for the vascular morning ward round.
audits.r2: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant 100%; lipid modification 26 (96%); diabetic referral 100%; smoking cessation 100%.

audits.t: 315 Chaperone Documentation in The Breast Clinic: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: GMC and Chelsea & Westminster Trust guidelines: consent, chaperone use/refusal, and chaperone role and identity documented
audits.f: Consent 0%; chaperone identity 12%; chaperone role 8%; chaperone use/refusal 27%.
audits.c: Teaching to breast MDT, introduction of electronic notes (Cerner) and an instructional video on creating an automatic documentation template.
audits.r2: Consent 38% (p < 0.0001); identity 35% (p = 0.0003); role 23% (p = 0.0091); use/refusal 35% (p = 0.3305, not significant).

audits.t: 347 Read the First Page: An Audit on Medicine Reconciliation in General Surgery Inpatients at London District General Hospital
audits.st: NICE: complete medicines reconciliation within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: 38.0% had incomplete reconciliation.
audits.c: Sequential: baseline data presented at a team meeting with posters; pharmacists flagging missing medicines on the daily jobs list; medicines reconciliation ward round.
audits.r2: 2.8% incomplete after the medicines reconciliation ward round (p=0.001).

audits.t: 379 Improving Flow: A Quality Improvement Project on The Processing of Vascular Surgical Microbiology Samples
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Results available 9.1 days after sampling (7.3 days after lab receipt); average transit 44 hours (71 hours for Friday surgery); one sample missing.
audits.c: Use of the existing urgent sample pathway and raising staff awareness
audits.r2: Average transit 33 hours (36 hours on Friday); results available 7.7 days after sampling.

audits.t: EP.TU.79Assessed and Discharged - An Audit of Discharge Summaries Completion During On-Calls
audits.st: NHS Standard Contract: discharge summaries completed within 24 hours of assessment and discharge
audits.f: 18/47 (38.3%) had a clinical note or discharge summary on the electronic system; 6 (12.8%) had a discharge summary.

audits.t: 421 Closed loop analgesia audit, a Single Centre Experience in Raigmore Hospital, Inverness, Scotland
audits.st: WHO analgesic ladder, with reasons documented when not followed
audits.f: 83.3% prescribed analgesia following the ladder; of the rest, only 50% had reasons documented.
audits.c: Presentation at audit meeting, educational sessions, information leaflets and email reminders.

audits.t: 495 Audit on Blood Ordering Requests in Mastectomies: The Need for a Routine Group and Hold
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All patients had a routine preoperative G&H; 2/100 received post-operative blood transfusion (transfusion probability 2%); only 15% had a post-operative haemoglobin checked

audits.t: 501 Antiplatelet Therapy Following Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Closed Loop Audit in a Tertiary Centre
audits.st: Guidelines recommending 12 months DAPT after PCI followed by emergency CABG
audits.f: All except 2 received lifelong aspirin or a DOAC/NOAC; of 3 with STEMI/NSTEMI in the preceding 12 months, 2 received DAPT and 1 aspirin plus DOAC; variation in DAPT duration for stable CAD.
audits.c: Antiplatelet prescription aid designed, taking surgeon preference into account.
audits.r2: Improvement in consistency of prescribing (no figures given).

audits.t: 521 Optimising Anaemic Patients for Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Implementation of Day-Case Iron Infusion Pathway and Closed Loop Audit of Anaemia Management in Colorectal Cancer Patients
audits.st: NICE recommendation to screen for and treat anaemia; local guideline advocating pre-operative IV iron via day-case unit
audits.f: 27.5% (11/40) anaemic; 18% (2/11) received pre-operative iron infusion; 45% (5/11) of anaemic patients had post-operative transfusion.
audits.c: Departmental education on anaemia management and further publicity of the day-case iron infusion pathway.
audits.r2: 45.4% (20/44) anaemic; 60% (12/20) received iron infusion; 20% (4/20) of anaemic patients required post-operative transfusion.

audits.t: 530 An Audit of Appropriate Documentation Following Urethral Catheterisation
audits.st: Trust guidelines: 10 documentation items for urethral catheterisation
audits.f: Only 28% (14/50) had all 10 items documented; indication best at 94% (47/50); chaperone and groin examination lowest at 44% (22/50)
audits.c: Electronic record 'smart phrase' (.icat, i-CATHETAR mnemonic) prompting all 10 items; second cycle under way

audits.t: 531 An Admission Proforma to Improve Clerking Documentation in the ENT Department During the Covid-19 Pandemic: A Full Cycle Audit
audits.st: Good Surgical Practice; Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (ten key items) and VTE risk assessment
audits.f: Referral source 28%, consultant in charge 35%, name/grade/bleep 25%, VTE risk assessment 14%.
audits.r2: Referral source 97%, consultant in charge 90%, name/grade/bleep 94%, VTE risk assessment 78%.

audits.t: 543 Improving the Management of Acute Ureteric Colic in A Multi-Centre District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: BAUS 2018 guidance on acute ureteric colic, including clinic follow-up within 4 weeks
audits.f: Baseline figures not reported separately.
audits.c: Teaching sessions for doctors and nurses in A&E and urology.
audits.r2: Serum calcium 60.4%, CT KUB within 24 hours 97.7%, NSAIDs 67.2% (increases of 20.4%, 0.4% and 5.2%); only 26.4% seen in clinic within 4 weeks, mean wait 41 days.

audits.t: 572 Closed-Loop Clinical Audit on Blood Results in Urology Department During Ward Rounds
audits.tp: Blood result flagging on ward rounds
audits.st: Institutional protocol: daily blood sheet with outstanding bloods flagged
audits.f: Outstanding blood results flagged in 70%; baseline eGFR documented in 32%; 73% of results filed in the correct patient folder.
audits.c: Discussions with nursing and medical staff and posters on the ward and in staff rooms.
audits.r2: Flagging 74%; baseline eGFR documented 44%; results correctly filed 100%.

audits.t: 573 What's in A Name? An Audit of Correct Identification of Patients During Ward-Rounds in A Surgical and Urology Receiving Ward
audits.st: Clinical governance: every patient should have a named consultant, with bedside whiteboard matching the electronic system (TrakCare)
audits.f: 7 (18.4%) bed-boards had incorrect or no entries (2 no consultant name, 5 incorrect)
audits.c: Verbal and written communication with nursing staff and junior doctors
audits.r2: Third cycle: only 1 (2.6%) missing consultant's name

audits.t: 576 Audit of Instillation of Intravesical Mitomycin-C Following Transurethral Resection for Bladder Tumour
audits.st: NICE guidelines: intravesical chemotherapy after TURBT for new and recurrent tumours
audits.f: Mean time from end of TURBT to mitomycin C instillation 7.66 hours.
audits.c: Improved communication between theatre staff, nursing staff and pharmacy to deliver IVCT to theatre.
audits.r2: Third cycle: mean interval 4.24 hours; 24-hour administration rate >90%.

audits.t: 580 Vascular Distal Bypass Early Surveillance Audit
audits.st: Society for Vascular Surgery: clinical examination, ABPI and duplex at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months then annually
audits.f: 8 patients (40%) had a duplex within 1 month; 10% had no scan; time to first duplex 1-11 months (mean 4 months); all discharged on antiplatelet, 70% on statins.
audits.c: Suggested booking duplex in theatre after the procedure, junior doctor education and re-audit in 1 year (not yet done).

audits.t: 606 AUDIT: IV Fluid Prescribing in Surgical Patients
audits.st: NICE CG174: maintenance 25-30ml/kg/day water and 1mmol/kg/day sodium, potassium and chloride
audits.f: Maintenance fluids prescribed for 76%; mean 2.3L/day; net sodium +221mmol, potassium -62mmol, chloride +162mmol (295% excess sodium, 216% excess chloride, 82% less potassium than required).

audits.t: 607 A Close Loop Audit on Proper Documentation of Ventriculo-Peritoneal (VP) Shunt Valve Settings in Operation Note
audits.tp: VP shunt valve documentation in operation notes
audits.st: Documentation of shunt valve type and settings in the operation note
audits.f: Valve type and settings documented in 209/247 procedures; 3 of 55 programmable valve procedures lacked documentation.
audits.c: Action plan agreed after first audit (details not reported).
audits.r2: Documented in 96/107 procedures; all 33 programmable valve procedures properly documented.

audits.t: 623 Completed Audit Cycle of Indications for Excision of Fibroadenomas At A University Hospital
audits.st: ABS guidelines (excision for B3 lesions, pain, increasing size) and local consensus (excision over 30mm on ultrasound)
audits.f: 83.7% met ABS or local criteria.
audits.c: Presentation and teaching at local departmental meeting.
audits.r2: 88.9% met ABS or local criteria; 11/18 met ABS criteria, 11/18 met local criteria, 2/18 met neither.

audits.t: 636 Optimising Operative Capacity for Hand Trauma - An audit
audits.tp: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
audits.st: Departmental and BSSH guidelines for hand trauma (tendon surgery within 5 days)
audits.f: Main non-compliance was waiting time for tendon operations, with a 30% breach rate (>5 days).
audits.c: Planned before re-audit: on-call junior doctor based in the hand trauma unit all day to do minor procedures at the bedside, freeing minor ops capacity for tendons.

audits.t: TP9.2.27A closed loop audit looking at the use of a checklist in surgical ward rounds to improve ward round documentation. Can we improve patient safety?
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians 'Ward Rounds in Medicine'
audits.f: First checklist used in a mean of 13% (SD 22%); documentation with checklist 67% vs 26% without (t(64)=8.85, p<.00001).
audits.c: Novel peri-operative ward round checklist, revised after feedback for the second audit.
audits.r2: Second checklist used in a mean of 56% (SD 28%), t(75)=7.59, p<.00001.

audits.t: 648 The Use of Antibiotics in Acute Pancreatitis - A Re-Audit of Current Practice
audits.st: NICE guidance against prophylactic antibiotics in acute pancreatitis; local antimicrobial guidelines
audits.f: Previous audit: 74% of patients received antibiotics without clear indication.
audits.c: Recommendations from the previous audit and improved awareness.
audits.r2: 31 (40%) received IV antibiotics, of whom 14 (45%) had no clearly documented indication.

audits.t: 661 Improving Antibiotic Prescribing in a District General Hospital: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Local hospital antibiotic guidelines for appendicectomy
audits.f: 68.8% (11/16) compliance with local antibiotic guidelines; non-compliant cases had correct antibiotics but different gentamicin doses.
audits.c: Antibiotic prescribing teaching for surgical and anaesthetic doctors, including use of the gentamicin dosing calculator.

audits.t: 670 Documentation and Communication of National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Mortality and Morbidity Scoring with Patients Prior To Consenting: Are We Following the Best Practice?
audits.st: NELA guidance on preoperative risk stratification and NELA fifth report recommendations
audits.f: NELA risk score documented in 26%; NELA score discussion with patient/family documented in 14%.

audits.t: 701 Resuscitation and Escalation Status Documentation in Acute Surgical Admissions: A Re-Audit Feb 2020
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: 704 An Audit of Marking of Cutaneous Lesions in A Two-Week Wait Skin Malignancy Service
audits.tp: Skin lesion marking for clinical photography

audits.f: Clinical photography in 148 (83.2%); marking inappropriate in 44.6% of those photographed (66 cases: 12 multiple lesions without letters, 52 incorrect indicator, 8 no indicator).

audits.t: 795 Adequacy of Surgical Excision Margins in Lentigo Maligna: An Audit
audits.st: NICE guidelines on excision margins for lentigo maligna

audits.t: 883 A Closed-Loop Audit to Improve Admissions Documentation in A Busy ENT Department
audits.st: Modified Royal College of Surgeons of England documentation guidelines (25 parameters)

audits.t: 621 Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy: A Complete Audit Cycle of Our First 118 Cases
audits.st: Pasadena consensus panel (2015) best practice for RARC
audits.f: Across all 118 cases: median operating time 376 minutes, median blood loss 250mls, 79% intracorporeal diversion, median length of stay 8 days, Clavien-Dindo III or higher 12.7%, 86% alive; consistent with Pasadena recommendations.

audits.t: 757 An Audit of Post-Vasectomy Semen Analysis Adherence
audits.st: 2016 Laboratory Guidelines for Post-vasectomy Semen Analysis (British Andrology Society) for clearance
audits.f: 132 (51.6%) had PVSA at median 16.4 weeks; 71 (54.5%) cleared, 45 (63.4%) after a single PVSA; 7 (9.9%) special clearance; 2 (1.5%) not cleared despite meeting special clearance criteria.

audits.t: 1284 Comparison of British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) 2008 and NICE 2015 Guidelines for Patients with Suspected Urinary Tract Cancer: An Audit of Haematuria Referrals
audits.st: NICE 2015 suspected cancer referral criteria (superseding BAUS 2008 haematuria guidelines)
audits.f: 123 (39%) referrals used BAUS 2008 criteria and 193 (61%) NICE 2015; for visible haematuria, urinary tract cancer found in 20% of NICE vs 4.4% of BAUS referrals.

audits.t: 894 An Audit of Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in A Busy ENT Department
audits.st: ENT UK VTE prophylaxis guideline
audits.f: VTE risk assessment clearly done for 39%; 22/63 (35%) meeting LMWH criteria received it; 5/96 (5%) meeting TEDS criteria received it; 45% had both prescribed according to the guideline
audits.c: Planned only: departmental policy and staff education

audits.t: 923 How Did the Initial Wave Of COVID-19 Affect CEPOD Waiting Times for Vascular Surgery? A Comparative Audit
audits.tp: Emergency theatre delays and NCEPOD timing
audits.st: CEPOD booking category target timescales
audits.f: 133 emergency vascular procedures; amputations 47%.

audits.r2: 98 procedures; amputations 53%; median waits for category 1 and 2a significantly shorter, category 3 longer; no significant difference in proportion operated within target.

audits.t: 935 Identification and Management of Electrolyte Abnormalities in Surgical Patients Requiring Total Parenteral Nutrition: An Audit of Current Practice at A University Hospital
audits.st: Electrolytes monitored every 48 hours; abnormalities treated within 24 hours; dietetics referral within 48 hours of nil-by-mouth

audits.t: 1023 An Audit of The Prevalence of Frailty and The Impact on Surgical Management and Resource Use, For Vascular Inpatients Using the National Vascular Registry (NVR) Frailty Classifications
audits.st: National Vascular Registry frailty score recorded on all eligible patients
audits.f: Frailty status documented in 65%; 43% (28/65) frail.

audits.t: 1050 An Audit of the Management of Acute Epididymo-orchitis
audits.st: Local antibiotic guidance; use of ultrasound and microbiological testing
audits.f: 3/64 received antibiotics in line with local guidance; ciprofloxacin used in 49/64; ultrasound in 46/64 (28 showed epididymo-orchitis, 15 normal, 1 abscess); urine MC&S sent in 25/64.

audits.t: 1080 An Audit on Compliance with Recommended Duration of Surgical Antimicrobial Prophylaxis in St. Vincent’s University Hospital, Dublin, Ireland
audits.st: SVUH Antimicrobial Guidelines recommended surgical prophylaxis regimens and duration
audits.f: 64 (79%) compliant with prophylaxis duration; 17 (21%) not compliant.
audits.c: Targeted smartphone application introduced to improve access to prophylaxis guidelines.

audits.t: 1100 A Closed Loop Audit Comparing Admission Rates Post Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour (TURBT) Before and After Day Case Procedure Was Made the Standard Goal
audits.st: British Association of Day Surgery: 60% of TURBTs could be performed as day case
audits.f: 36% of TURBTs performed as day case; readmission 12%; bladder perforation 3.8%.
audits.c: All TURBTs listed as day case from 1 December 2019 (protocol change).
audits.r2: 64% performed as day case; readmission 3% with no urology input needed; bladder perforation 1.6%.

audits.t: 1114 Getting it Right First Time: An Audit of Length of Hospital Stay for Mandibular Fractures
audits.tp: Length of stay for mandibular fractures

audits.f: 78% had surgery within 24 hours of admission and 92% were discharged within 24 hours post-operatively; average length of stay met the 2-day standard.

audits.t: 1132 How Much Are Junior Doctors Aware and Knowledgeable of Colorectal Enhanced Recovery Program? A General District Hospital Audit
audits.tp: Junior doctor knowledge of enhanced recovery

audits.f: Average knowledge score 52.9%; 5/8 (62.5%) aware of ERP.

audits.t: 1138 Complete Cycle Audit of Adults with Incapacity Documentation
audits.st: Adults with Incapacity (Scotland) Act 2000; target 90% accuracy of documentation over 6 months

audits.t: 1144 How Much Does Colorectal Enhanced Recovery Program Education Affect Knowledge of Newly Joined Junior Doctors? A General District Hospital Re-Audit
audits.tp: Junior doctor knowledge of enhanced recovery
audits.st: Local hospital guidelines: 100% knowledge of colorectal ERP
audits.f: Average knowledge 52.9% (original audit).

audits.t: 1186 Audit Driven Standardisation Of Perioperative Risk Profiling in Carotid Endarterectomy
audits.st: GMC 2008 guidance, Consent: patients and doctors making decisions together

audits.t: 1230 Infrainguinal Bypass Informed Consent: An Audit Driven Standardisation Of Perioperative Risk Profiling
audits.st: GMC 2008 guidance, Consent: patients and doctors making decisions together
audits.f: Intended benefits documented in 100%; NVR inclusion 0%; documented risks: maximum 15 (79%), median 8 (42%), minimum 3 (16%) of 19 complications.
audits.r2: Benefits 100%; NVR inclusion 80%; documented risks: maximum 16 (84%), median 10 (53%), minimum 4 (21%); 16 items improved and 9 complications recorded above 50%.

audits.t: 1231 A Full-Cycle Audit Of ‘Safe’ Surgical Handovers in A Tertiary Centre
audits.st: RCS 'Safe Handover' guidelines
audits.f: Briefings 70%, single audible speaker 30%, educational discussions 50%, awareness of on-call consultant 80%.

audits.r2: Briefings 100%, single audible speaker 70%, educational discussions 100%, awareness of on-call consultant 100%.

audits.t: 1280 A Retrospective Audit of The Management of Facial Lacerations in The Emergency Department in A Busy South Wales Tertiary Centre
audits.st: NICE laceration guidance
audits.f: Neurovascular examination documented 37%; no tetanus risk assessment in 58%; analgesia considered 43%; antibiotics prescribed 20% (flucloxacillin 10%, chloramphenicol 90%).
audits.r2: not reported (post-implementation data still being collected)

audits.t: 1333 A Retrospective Audit Against National Standards and Guidelines of The Management and Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis in A London District General Hospital
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines: mortality <10% (<30% severe), diagnosis within 48h, gallbladder ultrasound within 24h, severity stratification within 48h, cause established in >80%, ICU for severe cases, definitive gallstone treatment within 14 days

audits.t: 1348 Quality Improvement Project to Promote Betablocker Therapy Post CABG In Patients with Low Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF): A Single Centre Study

audits.f: 90 (89%) discharged with beta-blockers; 83 (81%) with a recommended beta-blocker; 11 (11%) not discharged on beta-blockers.
audits.c: Departmental presentation and raising awareness; discharge checklist inclusion recommended.

audits.t: 1359 Everyone Deserves to Smile: An Audit on The Success Rate of Dental Implants in Complex Maxillofacial Patients
audits.st: Local standard of 90% implant success
audits.f: 68 implants placed in 22 patients (15 head and neck reconstruction, 5 atrophic edentulous, 2 trauma); success rate not given.

audits.t: 1364 Quality Control of Discharge Summaries for Endocrine Surgery Patients; A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Discharge summaries (TTOs) should accurately record type of operation, diagnosis and postoperative instructions

audits.t: 1385 “Pre-Op Fasting Times Audit in Colorectal Surgery at A University Teaching Hospital”
audits.st: Trust guidelines on fasting times before major elective surgery
audits.f: Compliance 10% (2/20) for liquid and 5% (1/20) for solid fasting times.

audits.t: 1387 Audit of Pregnancy Status Documentation in Emergency Admissions to A Tertiary Colorectal Surgery Unit
audits.st: Complete pregnancy status documentation (β-hCG and gynaecological history) in females aged 16-55
