audits.t: 481 An Audit on the Completion of Hand Trauma Proformas – a Tertiary Centre Experience
audits.st: BSSH guidelines; RCS England Safe Handover minimum data
audits.f: X-ray obtained in 80%; hospital of X-ray documented in 40%; X-ray findings documented in 60%.
audits.c: Access to a generic doctors' account for external PACS as a temporary measure; re-audit planned in 6 months

audits.t: 493 Audit of Antibiotic Prescriptions in Appendicectomies and Adherence of Surgeons to National and Local Trust Guidelines: Preoperative and Postoperative
audits.st: BMJ Best Practice (preoperative prophylaxis for all; postoperative antibiotics only for complicated cases) and local trust MicroGuide guidelines
audits.f: 100% received prophylaxis but only 25% of penicillin-allergic and 2.2% of non-allergic patients received trust-adherent agents; 100% of complicated cases had postoperative antibiotics while 80% of uncomplicated cases had them unnecessarily.

audits.t: 568 Audit of Laceration Management and Documentation
audits.st: NICE guidelines on laceration management
audits.f: Laceration size documented 49%; infection risk 9%; wound cleaning 72%; appropriate closure 77%; dressing type 19%; tetanus appropriately managed 59%; detailed wound care instructions 36%; 6% given antibiotics despite closed wound.
audits.c: Planned: laceration clerking template with compulsory elements, with re-audit in February.

audits.t: 596 A Local Audit Assessing Completeness of Morbidity and Mortality Records in Vascular Surgery in a Tertiary Centre in the UK
audits.st: Good Surgical Practice and Royal College of Surgeons advice that formal records of M&M discussions are kept
audits.f: No record included the hospital number; 20.6% had all five sections complete; 'when' completed in 29.4% and 'attending consultants' in 41.2%; 29.4% had no record of discussion; 35.2% no action plan; 47.0% no responsible person.

audits.t: 612 Consultant Review in the Emergency General Surgical Take: A Single-Centre Audit for Compliance to Royal College of Surgeon’s Guidelines
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England timeframes for consultant review
audits.f: 70% reviewed within recommended time; 10% missing documentation; 20% seen 1 to 2 hours outside the window.
audits.c: Educational sessions and email reminders on documentation
audits.r2: 80% reviewed within recommended time; 5% missing documentation.

audits.t: 634 Analgesia Use in Acute Renal Colic Patients- Complete Audit Cycle
audits.st: NICE NG118: NSAIDs first-line analgesia for renal colic, then IV paracetamol and opiates
audits.f: 60% compliance.
audits.c: Findings presented at departmental meetings and posters of the analgesic pathway in clinical areas.

audits.t: 639 An Audit to Evaluate the Prevalence and Efficiency of the ‘Acute Abdomen Pathway’ Proforma Used in a Large District General Hospital
audits.st: Use of the acute abdomen pathway proforma for patients meeting its criteria
audits.f: Only 4 of 112 eligible patients were started on the pathway; with the proforma, CT request to report 5 hours (from 14), triage to diagnosis 5 hours (from 12), triage to management 5 hours (from 13).
audits.c: Planned: raise awareness of the pathway and re-audit.

audits.t: 640 Ambulatory Ultrasound - Could We Be More Efficient? Re-Audit -a District General Hospital Experience
audits.st: National guidelines on ultrasound in selected patients with RIF pain
audits.f: 41% had working diagnosis matching USS request; 13% had working diagnosis matched with USS results.
audits.r2: 94 (86%) had working diagnosis matching USS request; 22 (20%) had working diagnosis matched with USS results.

audits.t: 683 Closed Loop Regional Audits on Quality Predictive Indicators for Renal Cell Carcinoma Management in Northern Ireland
audits.st: Ten NHS Scotland National Cancer Quality Steering Group QPIs for renal cell carcinoma
audits.f: Targets met in 3 of 10 QPIs (nephron sparing surgery, trifecta rate, 30/90-day mortality).
audits.r2: Targets met in 7 of 10 QPIs (additionally pre-treatment CT/MRI, histodiagnosis in cryotherapy and chemotherapy, MDT discussion).

audits.t: 690 Quality Improvement Project: Improving Engagement with Smoking Cessation Services Among Emergency Surgical Admissions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Smoking status documented 83% (n=166); proforma completed 55% (n=112); among 49 smokers NRT prescribed 29%, CURE involvement 31%; 10% accepted ongoing support.
audits.c: Structured teaching session on smoking cessation for incoming doctors (August 2022)
audits.r2: Smoking status documented 96% (n=157); proforma completed 91% (n=148); among 47 smokers NRT 40%, CURE involvement 64%; 21% accepted ongoing support.

audits.t: 691 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance Audit
audits.st: ESGAR/EASES/EFISDS/ESGE joint guidelines (6, 12 and 24 monthly scans for 6-9mm polyps; cholecystectomy >10mm); local trust guideline of 12 and 24 monthly scans
audits.f: Of 82 (36.6%) 6-9mm polyps, 62 (75%) followed up; mean time to second scan 472 days, median 556 days; timing not within recommended guidelines.

audits.t: 699 Audit of Post-Splenectomy Patients in Primary Care
audits.st: National immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines for post-splenectomy patients
audits.f: Three patients had outstanding pneumococcal vaccine in the past five years; 100% compliance with annual influenza vaccine; two patients on incorrect antibiotic prophylaxis and four without antibiotic prophylaxis.

audits.t: 722 Audit on Improving the Management of Pre-Operative Medication Prior to Elective Surgery
audits.st: Correct prescribing and management of regular medications before elective surgery
audits.f: 19/50 (38%) received medications correctly.
audits.c: Posters in elective surgical wards (first cycle) and local departmental teaching (second cycle).

audits.t: 730 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescription in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.st: NICE NG104 on acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 65.5% prescribed antibiotics on admission; 12.1% for necrosis, 12.14% for concurrent cholecystitis, 33.4% without indication.
audits.c: Results and NICE guidance disseminated to general surgery team and at governance meeting.

audits.t: 733 ERAS Audit: Junior Doctor Compliance with the Elective Colorectal Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Pathway at Bristol Royal Infirmary
audits.st: Elective colorectal ERAS pathway: early postoperative nutritional drinks and avoidance of postoperative opioids
audits.f: Early postoperative nutrition and/or solid food in 60 (68.2%); nutritional drinks prescribed for 39 (44.3%), average 3 days to prescribe; systemic opioids avoided in 7 (7.9%).
audits.c: Face-to-face education for new colorectal junior doctors and posters in the doctors' office.

audits.t: 804 Audit of Hand-Written Consent Form Documentation for Skin Lesion Excisions in the Plastic Surgery Procedure Room
audits.st: Local consensus of the consultant body on consenter details, form completion and documented risks (no standard guidelines)
audits.f: All consenters documented job title, signed and dated; 100% used correct form, documented procedure, site and risks and labelled every page; intended benefits 83%; procedure name in full 58%; risks documented: bleeding and infection 100%, pain 54%, re-excision 75%, recurrence and wound breakdown 71%, scarring 96%, injury to surrounding structures 46%, anaesthetic risk 0%.

audits.t: 861 Getting the Surgical Handover Right: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons twelve-point handover guideline
audits.f: Highlighting need for additional review 33.3%; handover of outstanding tasks 31.5%; resuscitation status 7.0%.
audits.r2: Highlighting need for additional review 91.0%; outstanding tasks 84.3%; resuscitation status 9.2%.

audits.t: 900 Assessing the Use of GIRFT Guidelines and the Role of a Natural Language Processing Artificial Intelligence System for Operation Note Documentation in Emergency General Surgery – a Closed Loop Prospective Audit & Comparative Study
audits.st: GIRFT procedure-specific operation note guidelines
audits.f: Five consecutive operation notes each for laparoscopic appendicectomy, laparoscopic cholecystectomy, open inguinal hernia and emergency laparotomy/small bowel resection scored against GIRFT.
audits.c: All surgeons educated on the four GIRFT guidelines.
audits.r2: Median scores improved by +12.3% (p = 0.033) LA, +0.6% (p = 0.500) LC, +25.5% (p = 0.006) IH, +9.5% (p = 0.030) ELS; best was LA in cycle 2, median 72.7% (IQR 8.5).

audits.t: 906 A Prospective Clinical Audit of Pre-Operative Fasting Practices at a Tertiary Care Hospital in India
audits.st: Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists national preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.f: Median fasting 10 hours from clear fluids and 12.5 hours from solids; 99% gave an incorrect reason or did not know the reason for fasting.
audits.c: Patient information leaflets in English and the local language distributed to every ward for patients the day before surgery; surgical and anaesthetic trainees and nurses made aware of the findings.
audits.r2: Median fasting 3 hours from clear fluids and 11 hours from solids; 35% knew the correct reason, 50% gave an incorrect reason, 15% did not know.

audits.t: 946 A Complete Cycle Audit of the Appropriate Management of Stable Patients Presenting Acutely with a Lower GI Bleed Using the Oakland Score Risk Stratification Tool in Order to Avoid Unnecessary Admissions
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidance on Oakland score risk stratification (safe discharge threshold ≤8)
audits.f: 6/63 (10%) had a documented Oakland score; three patients with OS <8 were inappropriately admitted.
audits.c: Tailored teaching with a summary sheet and link to an e-calculator, after a departmental survey.
audits.r2: 16/38 (42%) had a documented Oakland score; all 8/8 with OS ≤8 appropriately discharged.

audits.t: 987 Audit of Prophylactic Antibiotic Prescriptions in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Adherence of Surgeons to Local Trust Guidelines
audits.st: Local trust prophylactic antibiotic guidelines (MicroGuide)
audits.f: 100% given prophylactic antibiotics; compliance 100% for uncomplex dentoalveolar/salivary surgery, 20% for fractured mandible and 0% for all other categories.

audits.t: 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle
audits.st: BAUS and NICE renal colic recommendations: CT within 14 hours, NSAIDs, referral criteria
audits.f: NSAIDs prescribed 87%; CT within 14 hours 93%; 100% meeting referral criteria referred; 67% not meeting referral criteria referred.
audits.c: Updated NSAID dosing and updated health board renal colic pathway.
audits.r2: NSAIDs prescribed 50%; CT within 14 hours 100%; 50% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.t: 1039 Preventing Avoidable Harm with Safe IV Fluid Therapy – a Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE CG174 intravenous fluid therapy
audits.f: Regular hydration assessment 10%; appropriate resuscitation fluid 32%; maintenance fluid when indicated 52%; correct maintenance composition 0%.
audits.c: Findings presented at a local meeting, posters and regular teaching on safe IV fluid prescribing.
audits.r2: Regular hydration assessment 28%; appropriate resuscitation 66%; maintenance fluid when indicated 84%; correct composition 15%.

audits.t: 1041 Audit of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Protocol in Elective Colorectal Surgery (A Loop Audit)
audits.st: ERAS guidelines for elective colorectal surgery
audits.f: Overall adherence 63.9% (pre-admission 59.2%, pre-operative 73.9%, intra-operative 70.1%, post-operative 52.7%); no ERAS anaesthetic component; mean LOS 9.8 days.
audits.r2: Overall adherence 81.1% (pre-admission 88%, pre-operative 80.25%, intra-operative 76.8%, post-operative 79.6%); all anaesthetic components included; mean LOS 7.1 days.

audits.t: 1083 Evaluating Adherence to Best Practice for Tissue Sampling in Diabetic Foot Surgery: A Quality-Improvement Study
audits.tp: Microbiology sampling in diabetic foot infection
audits.st: NICE guidelines on tissue sampling in diabetic foot surgery
audits.f: Clinically clean bone samples 68% (n=40); microbiology changed targeted antibiotics in 58% (n=33).
audits.c: Departmental teaching programme, then an online operation note proforma
audits.r2: Clinically clean bone samples 89% (n=24) (p=0.140); antibiotics changed in 95% (n=19).

audits.t: 1120 Time to Revascularisation for Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia – Audit of a Major UK Vascular Service
audits.tp: Time to revascularisation for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia
audits.st: VSGBI PAD-QIF 2019 and CQUIN 2022/23: revascularisation within 5 days of referral for inpatients and 14 days for outpatients
audits.f: 59 inpatients and 33 outpatients; 54% of inpatient and 83% of outpatient revascularisation candidates breached targets. Most inpatient breaches revascularised within 6-10 days; most outpatient breaches within 46-75 days.

audits.t: 1144 Audit of Microbiological Sampling in Patients with Diabetic Foot Infections Presenting to a Tertiary Vascular Centre in the North-East of England
audits.tp: Microbiology sampling in diabetic foot infection
audits.st: NICE NG19 and International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot guidance on microbiological sampling
audits.f: 56.8% (21/37) had microbiology sent; 47.6% (10/21) before antibiotics; tissue samples 35.1% (13/37).
audits.c: Introduction of a podiatrist-led 'Hot Foot Clinic'.
audits.r2: 74.2% (23/31) had microbiology sent; 23.5% (4/17) of tissue samples taken before antibiotics.

audits.t: 1162 Management of Acute Gallstone Disease at an Urban Acute Trust During the Pandemic – Closed-Loop Audit
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: National guidelines on early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.f: 49 patients had LC, only 20% performed acutely; 70% of acute operations were during re-admissions.
audits.c: Hot cholecystectomy list opened to other surgeons and acute LC encouraged on the emergency theatre list.
audits.r2: 21% underwent LC, of which 52% were acute operations; 50% of emergency operations were in re-admissions.

audits.t: 1237 Audit Project on Golden Patient Policy Adherence and Its Improvement to Theatre Efficiency
audits.st: Local trust Golden Patient criteria (ASA grade/anaesthetic type, case duration, team availability, sent for before 08:30)
audits.f: Baseline operation start times of first patients on list (figures not reported).
audits.c: Golden Patient policy: first patient on next day's list identified and reviewed the day before.
audits.r2: Start times improved by 30 minutes on average; 62.9% of Golden Patients met all criteria; 68.6% sent for before 08:30; 97.1% met ASA/anaesthetic and 94.3% case duration criteria.

audits.t: 1268 An Audit of the Time to Surgery Following Diagnosis of Gallstone Pancreatitis
audits.st: BSG guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within 2 weeks of discharge
audits.f: 14 (67%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 9 (64%) of these within 2 weeks; 7 (33%) had no surgery; median wait 3 days, average 64 days; 6 readmissions while waiting.
audits.c: Weekly semi-emergency theatre list introduced; re-audit planned.

audits.t: 1326 Temporal Artery Biopsy for Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA): A Ten-Year Retrospective Audit in an Irish Hospital
audits.tp: Temporal artery biopsy for giant cell arteritis
audits.st: American College of Rheumatology criteria for giant cell arteritis
audits.f: 107 (69%) met the guidelines; 27 (17.4%) biopsies positive for GCA.

audits.t: 620 Re-Operation Following Initial Breast Conservation Surgery for DCIS and Invasive Breast Cancer at ELHT Breast Unit, in 2021
audits.st: Association of Breast Surgery margin guidance; national re-excision rates of 13% (invasive) and 22% (DCIS)
audits.f: Re-excision rate 15.1% (31/205) for invasive disease and 33.3% (9/27) for DCIS.

audits.t: 589 Medication Prescribing for Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) and Review of Left Ventricular (LV) Function Documentation - A Departmental Audit
audits.st: 2016 ESC guidelines: ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker and MRA prescribed, titrated or contraindication documented in HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less)
audits.f: Compliance ACEi/ARNI 67% (10/15), beta-blocker 80% (12/15), MRA 67% (10/15).

audits.t: 712 Improving Post-Op Length of Stay (PLOS) in First-Time Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG)- a Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: National average post-operative length of stay 7.9 days after first-time CABG
audits.f: Average post-operative length of stay 9.4 days.
audits.c: Encouraging early nurse-led mobilisation of post-operative patients.
audits.r2: Average post-operative length of stay 8.5 days.

audits.t: 1016 A Quality Improvement Project Addressing the Healthcare Dimension of Effectiveness in a Large Cardiothoracic Surgery Department by Ensuring the Contents of the Current Emergency Surgical Chest Drain Boxes Are Correctly Stocked Through Additional Rigorous Checks by June 2022, by Using the Model for Improvement Approach
audits.st: Complete stocking of emergency chest drain boxes (target date June 2022)
audits.f: Missing equipment prevalent in emergency chest drain boxes (baseline number of missing items not stated).
audits.c: Revised stock checklist produced with the project champion, thoracic audit lead and procedural document team, introduced over two PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 81% reduction in the 3-month average number of reported missing items; 92% increase in perceived confidence that the box will be correctly stocked.

audits.t: 455 Fine-Needle Aspiration, Ultrasound and Thyroidectomies in Patients with Thyroid Nodules Presenting to a District General Hospital – a Retrospective Audit
audits.st: RCPath Thy category malignancy risks and BAETS guideline for investigation of thyroid nodules
audits.f: 21% malignant; Thy1a/c malignancy 5% vs 4% nationally; 100% of Thy3–5 had diagnostic hemithyroidectomy; 84% compliance with repeat FNAC and 97% with MDT discussion; 15 lacked U classification.

audits.t: 943 An Audit of the Management of Necrotizing Otitis Externa Within Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital
audits.st: ENT UK advice (swabs and imaging in outpatient recognition)
audits.f: At admission 66% had a swab and 7% had imaging; IV antibiotics started within 24 hours in all; microbiology consulted within 6 days in 93%.

audits.t: 1208 Post-Tonsillectomy Re-Admissions – a Real Pain in the Mouth for Our Patients
audits.st: National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit and ENT UK Tonsillectomy Commissioning standards: overall readmission <15%, pain readmission <1%, return to theatre <1%
audits.f: Overall readmissions 15.5%, pain readmissions 1.4% (n=1), return to theatre 2.8%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 83%.
audits.c: Departmental education and dissemination of post-operative verbal/written patient education.
audits.r2: Overall readmissions 9.3%, pain readmissions 2.3% (n=1), return to theatre 0%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 98%.

audits.t: 706 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing in Acute Pancreatitis and Introduction of a Patient Safety and Cost Saving Diagnostic Tool
audits.st: Antibiotics only for infected pancreatitis
audits.f: 19/52 (36.5%) with uncomplicated pancreatitis given antibiotics; 22/36 (61.1%) with infection received antibiotics; 36/41 (87.8%) given broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.

audits.t: 895 A Retrospective Analysis of National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Data at a Tertiary Hospital
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) national figures used as comparison
audits.f: Mean length of stay 33.59 vs 15.1 days nationally (median 15 days); geriatrician review 87% vs 24% nationally; 30-day mortality 5.5% vs 9.7% nationally
audits.c: Proposed only: special discussion of long-staying patients in weekly ward round meetings

audits.t: 905 To Operate or Not to Operate? a Clinical Audit in the Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction
audits.st: National audit of small bowel obstruction 2017 and Bologna guidelines
audits.f: IV fluids 100%; analgesia 38 (88.4%); anti-emetics 36 (83.7%); NG tube 21 (72.1%); 37% of conservatively managed patients received water-soluble contrast; average time to theatre 4 days (96 hours).

audits.t: 1068 Are There Delays to Emergency CEPOD Theatre Times? a Closed-Loop Audit Before and After Having a Dedicated CEPOD Registrar
audits.st: Hospital policy: first patient sent for by 08:40 AM and arrival by 09:00 AM
audits.f: Single on-call registrar: mean time sent for 09:33, arrival 10:00, turnover 00:39.
audits.c: Dedicated CEPOD registrar separate from the on-call registrar.
audits.r2: Dedicated CEPOD registrar: mean time sent for 09:08 (p=0.015), arrival 09:32 (p=0.010), turnover 00:11 (p=0.018).

audits.t: 1193 Review of Pre-Operative Antibiotic Prophylaxis (POAP) in National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Patients in a Regional Acute Tertiary Hospital
audits.tp: Antibiotic prophylaxis timing in emergency laparotomy
audits.st: WHO: pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision; SIGN: 30-60 minutes
audits.f: 83% had documented POAP; 68% of these had a recorded time before incision (mean 99 minutes, range 19 to 386); 77% of those received POAP within 120 minutes.

audits.t: 1202 National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA): Difficulties Achieving the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) Criteria
audits.st: NELA Best Practice Tariff: 80% of NELA high-risk patients have consultant surgeon and consultant anaesthetist present during surgery and are admitted directly to critical care
audits.f: 57% of high-risk cases met BPT criteria; consultant surgeon present 100%; consultant anaesthetist 63% (37% SAS-grade anaesthetist); 87% admitted to critical care.

audits.t: 871 Audit on Compliance and Documentation of GMC Guidelines Regarding the Use of Chaperone During the Intimate Examination
audits.st: GMC guidance on chaperones during intimate examination
audits.f: 9/168 (5.3%) had chaperone documentation, of which 1/9 (11%) complete; perianal examination 1/23 (4.3%); abdominal examination 8/141 (5.6%).
audits.c: Results shared with the department with education; chaperone stickers (name, position, gender) to be attached to notes.

audits.t: 102 An Audit of Phimosis Management at Primary Care Level
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons recommendations for phimosis management and paediatric surgical referral
audits.f: 25 (71.4%) referred; 32% of referrals (n = 8) without a topical steroid trial; 53.5% of steroids (n = 15) weaker than RCS recommends; 14 (73.7%) reviewed had physiological phimosis.

audits.t: 333 Inequity of Access to Investigations and Treatment of Varicose Veins by Clinician Grade: A Single Centre Retrospective Audit
audits.st: Norfolk and Waveney CCG referral to treatment criteria: only disease above C4 treated
audits.f: 71 referrals rejected and 158 should have been; of 70 seen in clinic 35 did not meet criteria; 62.9% (22) of ineligible attenders had investigations; discharge rate SpRs 13.3% vs consultants 45% (p=0.046).
audits.c: Education of SpRs on referral criteria recommended

audits.t: 347 General Surgery Ward Round Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Locally created 15-point ward round checklist
audits.f: Documented management plan 100% (other baseline figures not reported)
audits.r2: Improvement in 11 of 15 items: 3-point patient ID 100% (+43.7%), NEWS/observations +22.5%, medication review +26.7%, thromboprophylaxis +53.4%, examination +45.3%, escalation/DNACPR +37.7%; management plan remained 100%

audits.t: 649 Closed Loop Audit: Improving Surgical Handover in a Major Trauma Centre (RSCH)
audits.st: RCS handover guidelines
audits.f: Age documented 73%, responsible consultant 92%, significant investigations 60%, management plan 64%.
audits.c: Teaching session and RCS guidelines given to all surgical doctors.
audits.r2: Age 97%, responsible consultant 98%, significant investigations 93%, management plan 96%.

audits.t: 732 Who’s Your Consultant Surgeon? - a Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Francis Inquiry Report (2013) Recommendation 236: all inpatients should have a nominated responsible clinician
audits.f: 71% did not know their surgeon's name and 62% did not know their nurse's name; 76% of ward whiteboards had correct nominated staff information; 2% of bed-headboards had the surgeon's details.
audits.c: Junior doctor education to encourage communication with patients about their responsible care team
audits.r2: 14% improvement in awareness of surgeon's name; whiteboards correct 95%; bed-headboards with surgeon's details 24%.

audits.t: 759 Electronic Discharge Summary Audit
audits.st: PRSB electronic discharge summary guidance (endorsed by NICE), 13 categories
audits.f: 8% overall compliance.
audits.c: Poster outlining EDS criteria placed in doctors' office after cycle 1; teaching session for junior doctors before cycles 3 and 4.

audits.t: 1078 Assessing the Compliance & Adherence to the Emergency General Surgery Admission Proforma via ‘Take 10’ Principles - a Complete Clinical Audit
audits.st: 'Take 10' principles on the admission proforma
audits.f: Observations 25%, antibiotics 63%, IV fluids 25%, VTE risk 45%, nutrition 48%, estimated LOS 10%, ceiling of care 12%.
audits.c: Education of the surgical on-call team and use of the Take 10 checklist on the post-take ward round.
audits.r2: Observations 95%, antibiotics 90%, IV fluids 95%, VTE risk 100%, nutrition 100%, estimated LOS 85%, ceiling of care 78%.

audits.t: HPB P36 Good Medical Practice: Patient's right to the information - An audit of the patient's understanding and satisfaction with the information provided to the patients with acute pancreatitis
audits.st: NICE and Good Medical Practice: written and verbal information for people with pancreatitis and families
audits.f: 60% not satisfied with information; none given written information; more than 90% not shown a diagram; not informed about investigations 40%, treatment 60%, verbal information 26%, alcohol as cause 27%.
audits.c: Results shared with surgical team and patient information leaflet designed and given to every patient
audits.r2: Improvement in almost all areas; overall satisfaction improved from 60% to 92%.

audits.t: 1246 High Output Stoma Management Audit
audits.st: Association of Stoma Care Nurses national guidelines on high output stoma
audits.f: 51% of survey answers correct.
audits.r2: 72% of answers correct; 83% used the checklist; IV fluids 50% to 100%, fibre restriction 37% to 70%, loperamide dosing 5% to 30%.

audits.t: 1263 Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment and Thromboprophylaxis Among Hospitalised Patients: A Single-Centre Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE NG89: all patients risk-assessed for VTE on admission and re-assessed at consultant review; NHS Standard Contract
audits.f: VTE risk assessment completion 16.67%; median time to re-assessment 97 hours.
audits.c: Use of technology for VTE risk assessments, mandatory teaching sessions and prompts in clerking proformas.
audits.r2: VTE risk assessment completion 100%; median time to re-assessment 21 hours.

audits.t: 1309 A Quality Improvement Project on Small Bowel Obstruction Operative Mortality Rate
audits.st: ASGBI and NCEPOD recommendations on small bowel obstruction management
audits.f: 198 emergency laparotomies with 24 mortalities (12%); 87 SBO cases with 12 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 14%); SBO accounted for 50% of emergency laparotomy deaths.
audits.c: SBO management flowchart and allocation of a theatre slot within 72 hours for patients suitable for operation.
audits.r2: 152 emergency laparotomies with 13 mortalities (9%); 57 SBO cases with 3 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 5%); SBO-related deaths 23% of emergency laparotomy deaths.

audits.t: 104 Audit on Adherence to the BOAST Guidelines on the Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets
audits.st: BOAST guidelines on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets
audits.f: Pressure recorded in 230 (87.8%) limb procedures; tourniquet type documented in 8.2% and exsanguination method in 34.7%; no record of skin isolation or skin condition.

audits.t: 925 Consent for Carpal Tunnel Decompression and Trigger Finger Release – Are We Following Standards? a Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: GMC and RCS consent guidance for carpal tunnel decompression and trigger finger release
audits.f: Risks explained 88%; alternatives discussed and documented 61%; 'new' risks on consent form not in clinic letter 66%.
audits.c: Re-education of surgeons on the consent process.
audits.r2: Risks explained 100%; alternatives 100%; 'new' risks on consent form not in clinic letter 79%.

audits.t: 679 Regional Closed Loop Audits on Quality Predictive Indicators of Renal Cell Carcinoma Management in Northern Ireland
audits.st: Ten NHS Scotland National Cancer Quality Steering Group QPIs for renal cell carcinoma
audits.f: Targets met in 3 of 10 QPIs (nephron sparing surgery, trifecta rate, 30/90-day mortality).
audits.r2: Targets met in 7 of 10 QPIs (additionally pre-treatment CT/MRI, histodiagnosis in cryotherapy and chemotherapy, MDT discussion).

audits.t: Mastitis and Mammary Abscess Management Audit (MAMMA) in the UK and Ireland
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incision and drainage rate 21.0 per cent; ultrasound-guided aspiration of abscesses 61.0 per cent; 22.5 per cent admitted, of whom 72.9 per cent received intravenous antibiotics.

audits.t: HPB O08 Championing benign biliary patients in Emergency General Surgery: A 3 year quality improvement project
audits.st: Biliary key performance indicators: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 2 weeks of pancreatitis, time to Lap-C, inpatient Lap-C rate
audits.f: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 27%; average time to Lap-C 68 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 2%.
audits.c: Consultant-led biliary service, live biliary patient tracking system, increased inpatient Lap-C, ambulatory pathways and integrated care approach.
audits.r2: 2-week Lap-C 79% (43% as inpatients); average time to Lap-C 13 days; inpatient Lap-C 19%.

audits.t: AHP P06 Optimizing Coagulation Screen Practices in CVC Removal Amongst Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Audit Assessing Necessity, Compliance, and Implications
audits.tp: Coagulation screening before central line removal
audits.st: Same-day coagulation screen before CVC removal
audits.f: 41.8% had same-day coagulation screens, 17.9% the day before and 40.3% more than one day before; non-compliance 44%; INR normal in 88%, PT 74.6%, APTT 58.2%.

audits.t: EGS P09 Audit of Management of Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding against National Standard
audits.st: BSG-led multisociety AUGIB care bundle (2019); target 100% for each step
audits.f: All OGDs had consultant supervision; significant gap in applying the care bundle, Glasgow-Blatchford risk scoring and resuscitation and medical management (detailed figures in table, not given in text)

audits.t: EGS P18 A single centre retrospective audit into the early management of acute pancreatitis in an UK District General hospital
audits.st: Comparison with the PANC study; Royal College of Radiologists guidance on CT use
audits.f: Gallstones 45% (PANC 50.6%), idiopathic 33% (PANC 22.4%), alcohol 18%; 45% of idiopathic cases had further screen and 10% EUS; CT used in 51% (PANC 53%); antibiotics within 48 hours in 55% (PANC 34.6%).

audits.t: EGS P30 Audit on the assessment of upper abdominal pain for cardiac and respiratory differentials (AUPCR)
audits.tp: Cardiorespiratory assessment in upper abdominal pain
audits.st: Trust protocol: all patients with upper abdominal pain require chest assessment; those older than 40 require ECG
audits.f: Chest assessment in 48%; ECG in 28% of patients older than 40.
audits.c: Staff education on chest assessment and ECG interpretation, protocol flyers and posters in A&E and SAU, and electronic system changed so ECGs can be uploaded.
audits.r2: Chest assessment rose to 85%; ECG in patients older than 40 rose to 61%.

audits.t: EGS P32 Audit for evaluation of using the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) as risk assessment calculator for high-risk surgical patients undergoing emergency laparotomy
audits.st: NELA guidelines for risk assessment and documentation in emergency laparotomy
audits.f: About 21% of CEPOD booking forms had a recorded NELA score; NELA form or risk score missing in up to 97% of files and operation notes.

audits.t: EGS P33 Audit of Serial Lactate Measurement in Septic Patients Admitted in Acute General Surgery Department
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: lactate measured within 3 hours of admission and repeated within 4–6 hours if ≥2 mmol
audits.f: Surgical ward: lactate repeated in 16 (28.6%) patients with high lactate, 9 (56%) of these at ≥8 hours. HDU/ICU: 12 (92%) had lactate repeated in the target time.

audits.t: EGS P34 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery
audits.tp: Emergency theatre delays and NCEPOD timing
audits.st: Allotted CEPOD time to theatre
audits.f: 638 (84%) achieved the desired time frame; 122 (16%) delayed; 99/122 (81%) appropriately booked.

audits.t: EGS P38 Audit of operative notes/ Clinical documentation of emergency laparotomy & laparoscopic bowel resection procedures
audits.st: GIRFT, RCS and ASGBI Best Practice for Laparotomy and Laparoscopic Bowel Resection Surgery Documentation
audits.f: Indication 99%; operator names, position, incision and findings 100%; anaesthetist name 48%; WHO checklist 20%; bowel perfusion at transection 43% (of 64 resections); VTE prophylaxis 87%; antibiotics 65%; suture/clip plan 13%.

audits.t: EGS P39 The first cycle of an audit assessing the quality of documentation of emergency laparoscopic appendicectomies at Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, a District General Hospital
audits.st: GIRFT documentation recommendations (34 criteria) for laparoscopic appendicectomy
audits.f: 23% of criteria documented well (>75%), e.g. closure 96%, recovery instructions 97%; 19% moderately (port location 70%, haemostasis 62%); 23% poorly (ports under direct vision 38%, residual appendix 39%); 36% very poorly (e.g. histology, doctor grade).

audits.t: OGBN P12 Use of Computed Tomographic Scan in Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pancreatitis; A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Local policy on CT use in acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 42 (79.2%) had CT; 12 (28.5%) of scans considered unnecessary.

audits.t: 745 Improving Time to ERCP for Acute Gallstone Cholangitis Admissions at a District General Hospital: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.tp: Time to ERCP in acute gallstone cholangitis
audits.st: NICE: ERCP within 72 hours for acute gallstone cholangitis
audits.f: Median time to ERCP 10 days (5–24); moderate-to-severe 8 days (5–19); mild 28 days (9–46).
audits.c: Results presented to the surgical MDT; referral pathways to 3 nearby tertiary centres for ERCP.
audits.r2: Median time to ERCP 6 days (4–9); moderate-to-severe 6 days (6–8); mild 4 days (4–25).

audits.t: HPB P45 Assessment of quality of documentation for Laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a quality improvement project
audits.st: GIRFT and RCS England recommendations for documentation of laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.f: Indication, consent, WHO checklist and surgeon details documented in all cases. Omissions: pneumoperitoneum technique 19%, intraoperative drugs 54%, intra-abdominal pressure 95%, number of clips 66%, retrieval method/port 38%, port removal under vision 32%, haemostasis 12%, fascial closure 26%, critical view of safety 49%, anaesthetist names 62%, first surgeon signature 41%.
audits.c: Planned: teaching presentations and an electronic documentation template.

audits.t: HPB P55 An audit of the quality standards for Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy. Compliance with the AUGIS standards (AUGIS: Association of Upper Gastrointestinal Surgery of Great Britain and Ireland)
audits.st: AUGIS quality standards for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.f: Compliant with only 1/6 criteria; 67% (38/56) day case; no emergency cholecystectomy within 7 days of presentation; 7/56 readmitted; no bile duct injuries.

audits.t: OGC P09 Benchmarking of OG cancer care across the United Kingdom: a collaboration of 2 national clinical audit systems
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Staging CT: England 83.1%, Scotland 98.5%, Wales 92.2%. MDT curative treatment plans: England 40%, Scotland 29%, Wales 34%; actual curative treatment 24–31%. Longitudinal margin positivity: Scotland 2.4%, England 5.4%, Wales 8.2%.

audits.t: OGC P35 A clinical audit looking at how efficient the current pathways are for detecting upper oesophageal cancer
audits.st: NHS England 62-day referral to treatment standard; NICE: urgent OGD for dysphagia and barium swallow not first line
audits.f: Of 348 oesophageal cancers, 14 cervical cases; 9 analysed. 6/9 first referred to ENT. 4/9 had OGD, 5/9 barium swallow (4/5 as first-line) and 7/9 rigid oesophagoscopy. Median GP referral to treatment 108 days vs 62-day standard.

audits.t: OGC P61 Audit of diagnosis and treatment of early pneumonia after elective oesophagogastric resections
audits.tp: Postoperative pneumonia diagnosis and antibiotic choice
audits.st: US CDC criteria for pneumonia diagnosis and NICE guidelines for antibiotic choice
audits.f: 30.2% treated with antibiotics for pneumonia; 42.4% of these had sputum taken at suspicion; 69.7% prescribed a NICE-approved antibiotic; 17.4% met CDC pneumonia criteria.

audits.t: OGC P63 The Influence of PET-CT on the Therapeutic Pathway of Oesophageal and Oesophago-Gastric Junction Cancers. A Clinical Audit in a High Volume UGI Cancer Unit in the UK
audits.st: NICE: PET-CT for all oesophageal and OGJ cancers except T1a
audits.f: Mean wait for PET-CT 17 (1–57) days; 14 (32%) had CT/PET-CT discrepancy; 5 (11%) distant metastasis on PET-CT; 9 (20%) incidental uptake; further investigations added mean 15 (1–28) days delay.

audits.t: Frailty in Emergency Laparotomy and Laparoscopic Scottish Audit (ELLSA) Patients
audits.tp: Frailty and geriatric review in emergency laparotomy
audits.st: NELA frailty and care of the elderly review recommendations (compared with 31.8% in 8th NELA report)
audits.f: 98.6% had documented Clinical Frailty Scale score (mean 3.6); 87.7% reviewed by SAFT; 63.3% had pre-operative frailty review.
audits.c: Frailty screening on admission, weekly ELLSA MDT and designated ELLSA MDT board introduced, aiming for 100% geriatrician review.

audits.t: Assessment for the risk of malnutrition and nutritional support in older emergency laparotomy patients: a clinical audit
audits.st: NICE 2017: MUST on admission and nutritional support for high-risk (MUST 2 or above) patients
audits.f: 98% had a MUST score; of 114 high-risk patients, 35% had no dietetic review and 24% received no oral or parenteral supplementation.

audits.t: Prescription Practice Protocol of Antibiotics in A&E for Acute Diverticulitis in DGH: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE 2019 antibiotic prescribing guidance for diverticulitis
audits.f: 98% of patients treated with antibiotics regardless of requirement; not compliant with NICE.
audits.c: Local guideline based on NICE, teaching sessions and template presentations on wards.
audits.r2: 71% treated with antibiotics and 71% needed them per NICE; 100% compliant.

audits.t: Lower GI bleed audit
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: BSG guidelines on risk stratification with Shock Index and Oakland score
audits.f: 1 patient (3%) had shock index documented; Oakland score rarely used.

audits.t: Clinical audit to assess diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.st: National guidelines and the Atlanta criteria for diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.f: Severity scoring completed in 33% and used incorrectly in the majority; almost half of CT scans were deemed unnecessary.
audits.c: Acute pancreatitis protocol created with Upper GI surgeons (re-audit not yet reported).

audits.t: O162: A Surgically Led Quality Improvement Initiative in Surgical Antibiotic Prophylaxis (SAP): A One-year Review of Practice and Change in an Irish Context
audits.st: Local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (indication, agent, timing and duration)
audits.f: Compliance with all four aspects 72/303 (23.7%); correct agent 43.5% (71/165); given post-incision 18.9% (21/111); mean duration 70.4 hours.
audits.c: Education of surgical prescribers and anaesthetists, edited sign in/time out sheet and an antibiotic duration sticker on the drug chart
audits.r2: Overall compliance 39.8%; correct agent 65.3% (94/144); given post-incision 10.8% (14/129); mean duration 28.2 hours.

audits.t: 765 Enhancing the Quality of Referrals to Vascular Surgery at a District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Professional Record Standards Body (PRSB) referral guidelines
audits.f: Median 2.5 of 10 PRSB criteria fulfilled; demographics 60%, referrer details 51%, reason 93%, family history 40%, patient ICE 40%.
audits.c: Vascular surgery referral proforma emailed to a dedicated vascular surgery inbox.
audits.r2: Median 9 of 10 criteria fulfilled (p <0.0001); demographics 100%, referrer details 100%, reason 100%, family history 84%, patient ICE 81%.

audits.t: 522 A Snapshot Audit of Incisional Hernia Rates Following Colorectal Cancer Resection
audits.tp: Abdominal wall closure and incisional hernia
audits.st: European Hernia Society guidelines: small bites closure and off-midline incisions
audits.f: Incisional hernia rate 31.4% at mean 24.9 months; small bites used in 38 (23.6% hernia) vs large bites in 80 (35.0%); midline 40.7% vs off-midline 6.3%.

audits.t: 854 Bridging the Communication Gap in Surgery: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Surgical Juniors’ Confidence in Navigating Difficult Conversations and Documentation
audits.tp: Next of kin communication after surgery
audits.st: NICE CG83 1.13; best practice of documenting NOK discussion within 12 hours
audits.f: Documented NOK discussions 3-5 days post-operatively in 36%; NOK update after ITU step-down in 33% of 10 patients.
audits.c: Communication skills workshop for surgical juniors and coloured cards in notes folders to flag patients needing NOK discussions.

audits.t: 208 Head and Neck Surgical Oncology Handover Audit Using ‘RAAAIDDSS’ Method
audits.st: RAAAIDDSSS handover method (Royal College of Surgeons Safe Handover guidance 2007)
audits.f: Good compliance overall; least compliant component was 'structure' at 62%.
audits.c: Results presented at grand ward round; format built into the handover sheet.
audits.r2: Almost all components 100% compliant except 'intake' at 90%.

audits.t: 1088 The Quality of Information Recorded in Neurosurgical Operation Notes: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (18 parameters)
audits.f: 100% for date, surgeon, assistant, procedure, diagnosis and signature; prosthesis 0%; blood loss 1%; extra procedures 1%; elective/emergency 1%; time 4%; complications 19.8%.
audits.c: Template proforma for post-operative instructions recommended

audits.t: 1087 Factors That Impact Cold Ischaemia Time for Deceased Donor Kidney Transplants: Results of a National Transplant Access to Theatre Audit (NTACT)
audits.tp: Cold ischaemia time in deceased donor transplantation
audits.st: National cold ischaemia time recommendations
audits.f: Median CIT 10:55 (IQR 08:11-15:13) for DBD and 11:19 (IQR 08:31-15:10) for DCD; 42% of DCD and 15% of DBD organs exceeded national CIT recommendations.

audits.t: 60 Audit of Outpatient Management of Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss at St George’s Hospital
audits.st: ENT UK guidelines: oral steroids first line, intratympanic steroids if no improvement
audits.f: 36 referred, 18 (50%) confirmed on PTA; 15 (83.3%) received oral prednisolone, 3 (20%) improved; of 13 with no or partial response, 5 (38%) received IT steroids; 4 of 6 (67%) given IT injections improved.

audits.t: 75 Audit of Pain Control in Surgical Inpatients
audits.st: WHO analgesic ladder and NICE 147 guideline
audits.f: Pain managed adequately in 30%; anti-emetics offered to 92%.
audits.r2: Pain managed adequately in 46%; prophylactic laxatives prescribed in 100% of eligible patients; anti-emetics 82%.

audits.t: 184 Closed-Loop Audit on Upper Limb Bite Injuries at a Major Trauma Centre
audits.st: Departmental guideline on upper limb bite injuries, updated in line with the British Society for Surgery of the Hand
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Departmental guideline updated in accordance with BSSH guidance, with an action plan
audits.r2: 86% of all patients, including 100% with infection, who required an operation had it within 24 hours; first contact practitioners gave thorough ED washout in 25%; 30% needed formal theatre washout, of whom 25% needed a second operation

audits.t: 221 A Ward-Based Intervention to Improve Understanding of ‘Enhanced Recovery After Surgery’, and Improve Compliance with Early Post-Operative Mobilisation: A Prospective Audit
audits.st: Local ERAS post-operative mobility goals (4 x 60m walks)
audits.f: 10% of patients aware of ERAS; 77% completed the recommended 4 x 60m walks.
audits.c: Ward-based educational posters at each bedspace and bathroom door.
audits.r2: 46% aware of ERAS; 87% completed 4 x 60m walks; 24% increase in sitting out of bed for meals.

audits.t: 249 High Output Stoma Management – a 3-Cycle Audit
audits.st: Association of Stoma Care Nurses (ASCN) guidelines on high output stoma management
audits.f: Junior doctors answered 51% of knowledge questions correctly.
audits.c: Poster and checklist summarising ASCN guidelines, then teaching sessions for surgical junior doctors and an improved checklist.
audits.r2: 91% of answers correct; 85% of junior doctors reported applying knowledge from the teaching session.

audits.t: 274 Audit of the Written and Oral Assessment of the Dissertation Component of a Laparoscopic Surgical MSc Programme Using Internal and External Benchmarks
audits.tp: Dissertation assessment in a surgical MSc
audits.st: Queen Mary University London internal and University College London external assessment benchmarks
audits.f: Practice exceeded the 50% rule and double-blind marking requirements (18 vs 9); marking trails kept electronically; moderation not needed; mark differences resolved by discussion (dissertation) or splitting the difference (viva).
audits.c: Planned: electronic viva marking sheets; re-audit in 2024/2025.

audits.t: EP186 - Blood transfusion documentation in surgical patients - are we doing it correctly? An audit on the blood transfusion documentation in surgical patients at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom
audits.st: British Society for Haematology guideline on administration of blood components and local trust guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Discussion with junior doctors to raise awareness of transfusion guidelines.
audits.r2: Adherence above 80% in most criteria that needed improvement in cycle 1.

audits.t: 310 Documentation and Consent Audit in HPB Patients
audits.st: Trust and national guidance on record keeping and consent
audits.f: All entries legible and signed but GMC number and designation often omitted (81%); allergy status and drug history omitted in 62% and 63%; consent forms all present and described name/benefits/risks; information leaflet not documented in 77%; carbon copy given in 23%; abbreviations used in 54%.

audits.t: 329 An Audit into the Prescription of Maintenance IV Fluids for General Surgery Patients
audits.st: NICE guidelines on maintenance IV fluids (25-30 ml/kg/day water; approximately 1 mmol/kg/day potassium, sodium and chloride; approximately 50-100 g/day glucose)
audits.f: No patients were given IV fluids according to NICE guidelines.
audits.c: Proforma and teaching to foundation doctors on the ward.
audits.r2: Second cycle in progress; early signs show a positive improvement (no figures reported).

audits.t: 341 Improving Plastic Surgery Inpatient Referrals at a Major Trauma Centre: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Complete and appropriate online referrals with clinical photography
audits.f: 147 (14.2%) rejected; 63% of rejections inappropriate; 41.5% submitted without clinical photography; incomplete referrals 7.5%.
audits.c: New referral form with a prerequisite referral checklist, wound assessment section and required clinical photography.
audits.r2: 37 (22.0%) rejected; inappropriate referrals 70.3% of rejections (p=0.64); 19% without clinical photography (p=0.37); incomplete referrals 5.4% (p=0.07).

audits.t: 357 An Audit of Quality of Discharge Summaries in Cardiac Surgery
audits.st: Local e-discharge summary template standards; target 100%
audits.f: 5 of 16 domains complete in 100%; reason for admission misplaced 43%; GP request reasoning in allocated box 55%; N/A for no GP requests 23%; no ECHO specified 20%; acronyms avoided 17%
audits.c: Results shared at a team meeting and on a poster in the MDT office
audits.r2: 7 of 16 domains complete in 100%; reason for admission misplaced 40%; GP request reasoning 57%; N/A for no GP requests 48%; no ECHO specified 27%; acronyms avoided 15%

audits.t: 372 Imaging in Gynaecomastia: Audit of Imaging Practice at BHRUT to Establish Guidelines
audits.st: National standards on imaging for gynaecomastia (not named)
audits.f: Ultrasound performed in all; all P1 and P2 patients were U1/U2 and M1/M2; mammography in 0/19 P1, 20/113 P2 and 4/11 P3; one P3 biopsy (M4U4) showed invasive carcinoma.

audits.t: 380 Audit of the Management of Suspected Ureteric Colic in Barnet Hospital Emergency Department
audits.st: BAUS/NICE guidelines for suspected ureteric colic
audits.f: 98% had CT-KUB within 14 hours (mean 4 hours 50 minutes); 52% received analgesia in ED (mean 3 hours 26 minutes from triage); calcium measured in 51% and urate in 4%.
audits.c: Education and pathway review; second cycle in progress

audits.t: 401 Cardiovascular Risk Factor Optimisation Amongst Inpatients with Peripheral Artery Disease – a Single-Centre Audit
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
audits.st: NICE secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease (smoking cessation, lipid modification, antiplatelet therapy, blood pressure control, diabetes risk assessment); target 100%
audits.f: Smoking cessation 40.5%, lipid modification 18.8%, blood pressure control 29.5%, diabetes risk assessment 21.1%, antiplatelet therapy 38.9%.

audits.t: 432 Perioperative Antithrombotic Agent Use in Cutaneous Surgery: A Complete Audit Cycle
audits.tp: Perioperative antithrombotic management in skin surgery
audits.st: BSDS and BSH perioperative antithrombotic guidelines
audits.f: Postoperative bleeding 8.6%; aspirin monotherapy not stopped 80%; pre-op INR for warfarin 75%.
audits.c: Poster 'cheat sheet' of antithrombotic advice displayed in the department.
audits.r2: Postoperative bleeding 7.4%; aspirin monotherapy not stopped 71.4%; pre-op INR for warfarin 100%.

audits.t: 458 Post-COVID-19 Regularisation of Emergency Laparoscopic Cholecystectomies: A Single-Centred Multi-Cycle Audit
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: AUGIS advice: emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours of diagnosing acute cholecystitis
audits.f: Median admission to theatre 106.5 hours; median length of stay 7.5 days.
audits.r2: Median admission to theatre 70.7 hours (IQR 48.4-107.7); median admission to imaging 11 hours; median length of stay 5.6 days.

audits.t: 469 Operation Notes Audit: Excellent Bridge in Continuity of Care
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons (England) Good Surgical Practice 1.3 'Record your work clearly, accurately and legibly'
audits.f: not reported separately
audits.c: First-cycle results presented at a regional meeting.
audits.r2: Almost all domains 100% compliant except DVT prophylaxis (10%), blood loss (5%), antibiotic prophylaxis (85%) and anaesthetist's name (50%).

audits.t: 581 A Standard Base Audit Regarding Documentation of Urinary Catheterization of the Patients Who Had a Urinary Catheter Inserted in a General Surgical Ward at Sri Jayewardenepura General Hospital, Sri Lanka
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for documenting urinary catheterisation
audits.f: Only 2% had complete documentation.
audits.c: Printed catheterisation documentation form filed in patients' notes.

audits.t: 582 A Re- Audit of the Metabolic Screening for Patients with Urinary Tract Calculi and the Implementation of an Electronic Requesting Bundle
audits.tp: Metabolic evaluation in urinary stone disease
audits.st: NICE and EAU guidelines: serum calcium and uric acid measured as metabolic screening
audits.f: Serum calcium measured in 65%; uric acid measured in 46%.
audits.c: Education and posters after previous audits.
audits.r2: Serum calcium measured in 46%; uric acid measured in 37%.

audits.t: 612 A Quality Improvement Project of Management of Acute Pancreatitis in a District General Hospital; How Well Are We Doing Against NICE Guidelines?
audits.st: NICE NG104 (cause, antibiotic stewardship, nutrition, severity and complications, lifestyle advice)
audits.f: Cause identified 55% (86% within 48 hours); antibiotics 51%, indication recorded in 23%; nil by mouth 91%, reason recorded in 20%; severity documented 6%; lifestyle advice 33%.
audits.c: Ongoing: Pancreatitis Management Bundle, local clinical guidelines, staff awareness and patient education (no re-audit reported).

audits.t: 656 Is Routine Group and Save Required for Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy? An Audit of a High Volume NHS Centre
audits.st: Valid group and save sample within 72 hours pre-operatively
audits.f: 383/571 elective and 245/265 emergency patients had a valid G&S; no elective patient required transfusion and no patient needed intra-operative transfusion.

audits.t: 686 National Audit Assessing the Imaging of Acute Pancreatitis at Mater Dei Hospital, Malta
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists recommendations: CT at least 72 hours after symptom onset, prognostic factors in report, gallbladder US within 24 hours
audits.f: Of 99 CTs, 25.3% at least 72 hours after symptoms; 24.2% reported all 3 prognostic factors; 20.2% had gallbladder US within 24 hours.
audits.c: Planned educational sessions for emergency doctors, surgeons and radiologists.

audits.t: 718 An Audit of Chaperone Documentation in the Breast Clinic
audits.st: GMC and NHS Lothian guidance: chaperone offered for all intimate examinations and patient response documented
audits.f: not reported (baseline figures not given)
audits.c: Posters reminding doctors to document and nursing staff to check.
audits.r2: Junior doctor documentation of chaperone offer increased by 43.7%; consultant documentation fell by 20% and ANP by 34%; chaperone grade recorded in 3% more cases.

audits.t: 752 VTE Prophylaxis and VTE Assessment Form in Plastic Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: Trust VTE risk assessment guideline and form; target 100% compliance
audits.f: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 69.5%; VTE risk assessment form used 0%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 18.8%.
audits.c: Results presented at departmental meeting; VTE checkbox added to handover list; posters in doctors' office with VTE forms attached.
audits.r2: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 95%; VTE form used 70%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 8%; mechanical prophylaxis increased by 15.8%.

audits.t: 759 Lost in Translation: Breast Surgery Pathology Reporting Audit
audits.st: RCPath dataset for pathology reporting of breast disease in surgical excision specimens: 90% of reports to include items
audits.f: Specimen type, histological grade and invasive disease well reported; date of surgery 0%, core biopsy site 1.5%, microinvasion 4.3%.

audits.t: 760 Intravenous Maintenance Fluid Prescribing in Nil-by-Mouth Patients in General Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE recommendations for maintenance IV fluids in nil-by-mouth patients
audits.f: Significant lack of potassium and glucose prescribing.
audits.c: Teaching sessions for FY1/2 doctors and posters on surgical wards.
audits.r2: 82% met daily water, 94% sodium and 96% chloride requirements; only 24% met glucose and 16% potassium requirements.

audits.t: WP2.13 - Local Audit based on MAGIC study to improve abscess management at Royal Devon University Healthcare Trust
audits.st: MAGIC (Management of Acute surGIcal absCesses) national audit; recommended practice from literature review (no benefit of postoperative packing; antibiotics only in specified circumstances)
audits.f: 22/31 had surgical intervention (17 general, 5 local anaesthetic); 18 had antibiotics before admission and 19 on admission; of the surgical cohort 19 underwent packing and 6 were discharged with antibiotics.

audits.t: 893 Addressing the Potential Harms in Vascular Surgery Inpatients with Diabetes: A Double Audit and Intervention Project on HbA1c Monitoring and Diabetes Management
audits.tp: HbA1c monitoring in vascular surgery inpatients
audits.st: Locally agreed guidance-based 3-monthly HbA1c monitoring
audits.f: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 25%; repeat HbA1c required in 38%; mean staff knowledge score 56%.
audits.c: Educational teaching programme on diabetes management for clinical staff
audits.r2: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 86%; repeat HbA1c required in 50%; mean knowledge score 77%.

audits.t: 929 An Audit of the Perioperative Clinical Assessment and Documentation of Delirium in Older Patients Following Vascular Surgery
audits.st: Centre for Perioperative Care: daily delirium screening with a validated tool such as the 4-AT in patients 65 and over
audits.f: 4-AT screening in only 39.2% (n=20), on average 90 hours post-operatively; never documented in consultant-led post-operative review (100%, n=51).
audits.c: Recommended: stakeholder discussion, the mantra 'Post-op bloods and 4AT', and education on the 4-AT proforma.

audits.t: 943 Audit of Endoscopy Service Safety in District General Hospital Rated ‘Inadequate’ by the CQC
audits.st: Joint Advisory Group on GI endoscopy measures and published complication rates
audits.f: Readmission within 8 days 0.002% (1 ERCP, 1 OGD, 4 colonoscopy); mortality 0.0003% (1 post-ERCP pancreatitis).

audits.t: 965 What Did You Say? a Completed Cycle SSNHL Management
audits.st: ENT UK guidelines for SSNHL
audits.f: not reported separately
audits.c: Data presented to the local department with updated SSNHL guidance and treatment pathway.
audits.r2: 80% received proton pump inhibitors with oral steroids in the second cycle.

audits.t: 975 A Re-Audit on Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in a Surgical Unit of a Tertiary Care Hospital, Sri Lanka
audits.st: ESGE bowel preparation guidelines
audits.f: Low fibre diet 22.72% (n=20); enhanced instructions 14.7% (n=13); split-dose 42.04% (n=37); specific instructions 28.4% (n=25); routine enema used.
audits.c: Protocol based on ESGE guidelines, education of nursing and junior staff, adjusted split-dose timing, stopping enemas, clear patient instructions and a checklist.
audits.r2: Low fibre diet 90.62% (n=87); enhanced instructions 70.8% (n=69); split-dose 81.25% (n=78); specific instructions 97.9% (n=94); routine enema eliminated.

audits.t: 980 Audit of the Day Case Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Pathway in Frimley Park Hospital
audits.st: GIRFT: anticipated day case rate 90%, plus recommended technique (e.g. low pressure insufflation 10mmHg, no drains)
audits.f: Day case rate 45% (58 of 107 stayed overnight); no surgeon documented pneumoperitoneum pressure.

audits.t: 986 Is the NELA Section on the CEPOD Form Completed for General Surgical Patients Upon Emergency Theatre Booking? - a Closed-Loop Audit
audits.tp: NELA data entry and case ascertainment
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit requirement to assess all emergency surgical patients for inclusion
audits.f: 42.7% of CEPOD forms included the completed NELA section.
audits.c: Formal emails to surgical junior doctors, informal discussions with doctors and nurses, and posters near where CEPOD forms are collected.

audits.t: EP584 - The standard of evening handover in the acute surgical department of a single regional centre: a closed-loop audit
audits.st: RCSEng guidelines on safe handover ('minimum' standard)
