audits.t: ThP1.4 - Evidence-Based Perioperative Improvements in Microvascular Breast Free Flap Reconstruction: An Audit-Centric Evaluation & Retrospective Cohort Study
audits.tp: Perioperative care in breast free flap reconstruction
audits.st: ABS and BAPRAS guidelines; length of stay target under 3 days
audits.f: 22 flaps; average LOS 5.47 days (target <3d); no unplanned readmissions; 18% return to theatre; 18% total complication rate.
audits.c: Planned: evidence-based modified ERAS protocol via MDT collaboration.

audits.t: ThP5.3 - A Clinical Audit on Assessing Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Improving the use of the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria and outcomes
audits.st: Glasgow-Imrie Criteria scoring on admission for acute pancreatitis; scores ≥3 reviewed by senior and/or HDU/ITU
audits.f: 44% (22/50) of patients were scored using the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria.
audits.c: Presentation, posters and email, then a scoring tick box in the electronic clerking notes
audits.r2: 84% (49/58) scored; escalation of scores ≥3 rose from 17% to 100%.

audits.t: ThP6.13 - A closed loop clinical audit on adherence of weight-based and renal function-adjusted venous thromboprophylaxis prescribing to local guidelines in emergency general surgical patients
audits.st: Local trust guideline on weight- and renal function-adjusted VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 49 (86.0%) prescribed per guideline; of 8 non-adherent, 5 (62.5%) had no prophylaxis and 3 (37.5%) incorrect doses.
audits.r2: 39 (90.7%) adhered; no dosing errors, but 4 (9.3%) had no prophylaxis prescribed.

audits.t: ThP6.17 - ‘If it’s not documented, it didn’t happen’: an audit into surgical ward documentation and clinicians expectations in a district general hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on adult surgical ward round documentation
audits.f: 21 daily and 21 post-take ward round entries: date 90%, consultant name 95%, time documented 29% and 35%, examination findings 33% (DWR) and 40% (PTWR), presenting complaint 45% of PTWR.

audits.t: ThP7.15 - An audit to assess the usefulness of investigations for patients with acute appendicitis
audits.st: NICE: acute appendicitis should be diagnosed clinically
audits.f: Imaging in 50.9%; CT 91.5% accurate, bloods 65.5%; ultrasound detected 57.1% of histologically proven appendicitis and reported 52% as normal.

audits.t: ThP7.16 - Multidisciplinary management of elderly patients undergoing emergency laparotomy: an audit at a small district general hospital
audits.st: NELA: early geriatrician involvement for patients aged over 80, or 65 and frail
audits.f: 17 patients met criteria for early geriatrician involvement; frailty score recorded in 22 of 34 aged 65+ (64%); less than 10% had early geriatrician input.

audits.t: ThP7.18 - Post-operative management and outcomes in emergency laparotomy - an audit of the updated 2023 NELA Standards in a busy district general hospital
audits.tp: Critical care admission after high-risk emergency laparotomy
audits.st: Updated 2023 NELA standards: high-risk patients (NELA risk 5% or more) admitted directly to critical care
audits.f: 38 of 43 high-risk patients directly admitted to critical care; median LOS 14 days, 7 died within 30 days (O/E mortality 1.12).

audits.t: FP1.11 - An audit of post colonoscopy Colorectal cancers within a Northern Ireland Health and Social Care Trust
audits.st: BSG key quality indicator of PCCRC rate (published rates 2-8%)
audits.f: 33 of 524 CRCs (6.3%) were PCCRCs; of these 21 (63.6%) had complete colonoscopy, 22 (66.6%) fair/satisfactory bowel preparation, 24 (72.7%) a lesion detected, 3 (9%) prior IBD.

audits.t: FP1.14 - A Re-audit of the prevalence of faecal incontinence in hospital inpatients
audits.tp: Identification of faecal incontinence in inpatients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nursing bowel documentation 90%, medical 48%; 10.8% had FI; 31% would have been identified by medical documentation; all (100%) referred appropriately
audits.r2: Nursing bowel documentation 94%, medical 47%; 5.3% had FI; only 28% would have been identified by medical documentation; some action taken in 71.42% but no referral arranged in any

audits.t: FP3.5 - Colonoscopy post diverticulitis – Compliance with ACPGBI guidance in a single centre audit
audits.st: ACPGBI guidance on colonoscopy after diverticulitis
audits.f: 90 uncomplicated diverticulitis without surgery: 71 (59% of total) had colonoscopy, 19 (16%) did not; 78.9% of uncomplicated cases had colonoscopy, which may have been unnecessary. Complicated: 15 surgery, 15 no surgery, 11 (9.2%) colonoscopy, 4 (3.3%) no colonoscopy.

audits.t: FP4.6 - A Re-audit on the completion of pathology request forms following Colorectal Cancer Resection
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists parameters for colorectal cancer resection request forms
audits.f: Approach mentioned 78%; diagrams 44%; preoperative therapy 4.5%.
audits.r2: Approach 30%; diagrams 36%; preoperative therapy 20%; no significant overall improvement.

audits.t: FP5.12 - Write what you know: A retrospective documentation audit
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians: every entry dated, timed and signed with name and designation, standardised structure and chronological order
audits.f: 89.8% dated; 42.0% timed; 93.2% standardised structure; 6.8% had author designation and 3.4% signature.

audits.t: FP5.14 - Enhancing Patient Communication in Surgical Care: an Audit of Practice at a DGH
audits.st: NICE guideline on patient experience in adult NHS services (clear information on diagnosis, oral and written communication, communication with family)
audits.f: Understanding of diagnosis varied before the intervention.
audits.c: Clear written information on imaging results and plans, and a patient information sheet to use throughout admission and share with family.
audits.r2: Majority (n=9) felt information was appropriately pitched; 13 received accessible information and found the sheet helpful.

audits.t: FP6.13 - A Quality improvement project to reduce the number of readmissions to surgical assessment unit (SAU) in East Sussex hospitals (ESHT) following laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: UK national average readmission rate of 5%
audits.f: Readmission rate 8.1%; about two-thirds on day one after discharge, half due to pain; almost 90% needed no intervention.
audits.c: Proposed: more clinic time for consent, junior doctor and nurse education, and patient leaflets and websites

audits.t: FP7.7 - Evaluation of small bowel obstruction management: A local audit in comparison to NASBO guidelines
audits.st: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations
audits.f: CT on admission 98.3% (NASBO 80%), average time to CT 9 hours; surgery 27% with average time to surgery 2.4 days (NASBO 1 day); nutritional screening 100% (NASBO 90%).

audits.t: FP7.10 - An audit assessing the documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on an acute surgical unit
audits.tp: Antibiotic indication and review date documentation
audits.st: Documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on drug charts at prescription (recommended in numerous publications)
audits.f: Indication documented in 54.0% and course length in 42.0%.
audits.c: Results presented to junior doctors and reminder cards attached to drug charts
audits.r2: Indication documented in 74.0% and course length in 68.0%.

audits.t: EP51 - Uses of pharmaceutical and mechanical VTE prophylaxis - A clinical audit
audits.st: Local and NICE CG46 guidance on pharmacological and mechanical VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: Proforma completed in 87%; appropriate pharmacological prophylaxis 100%; appropriate mechanical prophylaxis under 40%.
audits.c: New proforma and teaching of junior doctors.
audits.r2: not reported (post-intervention data still being collected)

audits.t: EP127 - Audit on Acute PR Bleed Admissions to the Surgical Assessment Unit and the Use of the Shock Index and Oakland Score
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology: Shock Index (≤1) and Oakland Score (≤8) for safe discharge in acute PR bleeding
audits.f: SI documented in 0/37 and OS calculated in 1/37 at clerking; 12/34 (35%) managed appropriately; by OS, 20/34 (58.9%) incorrectly discharged.

audits.t: EP181 - The role of abdominal X-rays in the acute abdomen: a retrospective audit
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines on AXR in the acute setting
audits.f: 97% of AXR requests compliant with RCR guidelines; 30/62 also had CT after AXR.

audits.t: EP218 - A closed-loop audit on the assessment of the documentation of frailty at admission in emergency general surgery admission at a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: NHS frailty guidelines: frailty score documented at first contact for patients aged 65+
audits.f: 3/136 (2.2%) had frailty documented at first encounter.
audits.c: Discussion at clinical governance, teaching for junior doctors and a specific frailty section added to documentation.

audits.t: EP230 - A Closed Loop Audit for Peri-Operative Outcomes Comparing Laparoscopic and Robotic-Assisted Nephroureterectomy for Upper Tract Transitional Cell Carcinoma
audits.tp: Time to mitomycin C after nephroureterectomy
audits.st: EAU guidelines: MMC instillation 2–10 days after radical nephroureterectomy
audits.f: Laparoscopic RNU: average time to MMC 14 days (SD 6.7); average length of stay 5 days; bladder recurrence 41% (n = 14).
audits.c: Expansion of the robotic-assisted RNU service.
audits.r2: Robotic RNU: average time to MMC 2 days (SD 0.57); average length of stay 4 days; bladder recurrence 30% (n = 8).

audits.t: EP274 - A clinical audit on nasogastric tube placement documentation and adherence with NICE guidelines in general surgical patients across a district general hospital
audits.st: NICE guidance on confirming NG tube position by aspirate pH testing or X-ray if indeterminate
audits.f: Correctly documented NG tube position confirmation 60%; feeding tubes 4/4 correct; drainage tubes 45.5% correct; insertion length documented 33.3%; X-ray requested and documented in all inconclusive pH cases.

audits.t: EP335 - Audit of the Use of WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and its Awareness, Perception and Acceptability Amongst Theatre Personnel in a Tertiary Hospital in Sub-Saharan Africa
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Checklist used in 52.1% of surgeries (80% major, 5.4% minor); activities stopped at Time Out in 23%; Sign Out least completed.

audits.t: EP359 - Introduction of a pathway to improve post operative nutrition for patients undergoing a Whipple procedure - a closed loop audit
audits.st: Local post-operative nutrition pathway
audits.f: Pathway adherence day 2 22%, day 3 11%; median 8 days to soft diet; median day 9 to stop parenteral nutrition; median length of stay 15 days.
audits.c: Pathway updated so all patients followed the same oral pathway (then second cycle); education session for surgical trainees by a dietitian (before third cycle).
audits.r2: Adherence day 2 57%, day 3 43%; median days to soft diet 5; median day stopping parenteral nutrition 6; median length of stay 10 days.

audits.t: EP403 - Departmental Engagement in NELA AUDIT and Royal College Standards of Risk Assessment
audits.st: NELA and Royal College standards: NELA score documented by ST3+, frailty assessment in patients 65+
audits.f: NELA score documented 39.6%; documented by ST3+ 24.8%; P-POSSUM documented 61.4%; both NELA and P-POSSUM 32.7%; frailty assessed in 38.6% of patients 65+.

audits.t: EP421 - The multidisciplinary management of acute pancreatitis at a district general hospital – an NCEPOD audit
audits.st: NCEPOD Acute Pancreatitis 2016 recommendations
audits.f: Cause identified in 70%; 100% of alcoholic pancreatitis referred to alcohol services; nutritional assessment in only 10%; uncontrolled comorbidities not referred onwards.
audits.c: MDT teaching sessions and an admission proforma (second loop planned).

audits.t: EP427 - Are we following the RCS England Guidelines for documentation of the operation note for a laparoscopic appendicectomy: A complete audit loop
audits.st: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014 (18 parameters)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Compliance increased significantly in 9 of 18 parameters, 6 unchanged at almost 100%; post-op antibiotic instructions 83%, DVT prophylaxis 53%.

audits.t: EP442 - An Audit on the Application of Enhanced Recovery Post Emergency Laparotomy
audits.st: Enhanced recovery protocols (NG tube and catheter removal)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: EP465 - Transfusion Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO) Audit - A prospective analysis of adherence to standards ensuring safe transfusions
audits.st: SHOT recommendations (pre-transfusion TACO risk assessment with mitigation, reporting and incident review) and NICE NG24 weight-adjusted red cell dosing
audits.f: TACO checklist completed for 15% of transfusions (35% nationally); mitigation considered for 4%.
audits.c: Teaching sessions, information leaflets and posters, induction pack presentation, and liaison with transfusion practitioners to modify the transfusion pathway.

audits.t: EP474 - Recycling Theatre Waste: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 86.6 tons of waste; 18.4% recycled; monthly range 9.3% (January) to 35.0% (December).
audits.c: Quick guide for waste disposal and recycling made with the environmental department, disseminated electronically and physically.

audits.t: EP529 - The Impact of Royal College of Surgeon (RCS) Guidelines on the Quality of Operation Notes Documentation: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (2014) operation note guidelines
audits.f: Documentation rate 37.5%; timing of surgery, findings, complications, additional procedures, blood loss, closure technique and DVT prophylaxis lacking.
audits.c: Improved version of the operation note introduced in line with RCS guidelines.
audits.r2: Documentation rate 83.3%, with all parameters exceeding 83% (overall improvement 45.8%).

audits.t: EP551 - Assessment of Surgical Management for Mild and Moderate Acute Gallstone Pancreatitis in Accordance with AUGIS Guidelines: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks for surgically fit patients with mild to moderate gallstone pancreatitis
audits.f: 19 (16.5%) had inpatient cholecystectomy, 42 (36.5%) outpatient cholecystectomy, 4 (3.5%) declined, 10 (8.7%) unfit; no documented reason in 40 (34.8%).

audits.t: MS O02 - OGC An audit of waiting times of the oesophagogastric cancer diagnostic pathway at a high-volume, tertiary centre
audits.st: NHS England target: 21 days from OGD to communication of treatment plan
audits.f: 13.8% met the 21-day target; only 13.3% had next-day CT after OGD (median 5.0 days); median pathway 49.0 days curative vs 35.0 palliative.

audits.t: EGS SO03 - Audit of wound complications after Emergency laparotomies in A University Teaching Hospital: 2-cycle Prospective Audit
audits.st: Established guidelines on complication rates after emergency midline closure
audits.f: Wound infection 123/621 (19.8%); acute fascial rupture 66/621 (10.6%); incisional hernia 87/621 (14%).
audits.r2: Wound infection 49/802 (6.2%); acute fascial rupture 34/802 (4.3%); incisional hernia 42/802 (5.2%).

audits.t: EGS SO05 - Improving the Flow of Patients Attending Surgical Assessment Unit: Introduction of Ambulatory USS Slots - Closed Loop Audit
audits.tp: Ultrasound waiting times in acute surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median wait from arrival to ultrasound 2 hours 15 minutes (range 59 minutes to 3 hours 39 minutes).
audits.c: Two daily ultrasound slots for SAU patients negotiated with radiology.
audits.r2: Median wait 1 hour 5 minutes (range 4 minutes to 2 hours 20 minutes); 48% reduction.

audits.t: EGS SO09 - Documentation Of Mortality While Consenting For Major Emergency Operation In General Surgery : Are We Informing Patients Or Just Impressing NELA? A Three-Cycle Clinical Audit
audits.st: NCEPOD 2011: risk of mortality explicitly discussed and documented on consent forms and in medical records
audits.f: Mortality documented in NELA 93%, consent forms 40%, medical notes discussion 35%
audits.c: Periodic reminders for surgeons during meetings and posters
audits.r2: Mortality documented in NELA 90%, consent forms 92%, medical notes 51% (consent improvement p < 0.0001)

audits.t: OGC SO12 - Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Postoperative Oesophagogastric Cancer Patients: A Completed Audit
audits.tp: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
audits.st: NICE: extended pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery
audits.f: Pre-2014: 13/92 (14.1%) discharged with 28-day prophylaxis; post-2014: 423/490 (86.3%) (p<0.05); VTE 0.17%
audits.c: Trust-wide policy of 28-day extended VTE prophylaxis after discharge adopted in 2014
audits.r2: 63/68 (92.6%) received prophylaxis (86.3% to 92.6%, p=0.145); VTE 0%; no bleeding readmissions

audits.t: OGC SO20 - Audit of the guidelines for staging laparoscopy in gastro-oesophageal cancers
audits.tp: Staging laparoscopy and peritoneal cytology in gastric cancer
audits.st: Local staging laparoscopy and peritoneal washings guidelines
audits.f: 225 had washings; 2 appropriately not done due to extent of disease; 12 had washings not in line with policy, all with a clinical reason.

audits.t: OGC SO23 - Audit on Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) in Oesophago-gastric Resections for Cancers
audits.st: Trust ERAS protocol for oesophagectomy and gastrectomy (oral intake, drain, catheter and epidural removal, mobilisation, discharge medications)
audits.f: Oral diet started on time 85%; epidural removal 52.6% (95% within 24 h); catheter 55% (90%); apical drain 55.6% (100%); basal drain 53.8% (85.7%); abdominal drain 81.8% (90.9%); daily mobilisation 65%; VTE prophylaxis 100%; discharge medications 86.7% to 100%.

audits.t: OGC SO36 - Complications of palliative oesophageal cancer stent insertion: Audit for a five year period
audits.st: Published international standards (not specified)
audits.f: 45% had stent-related complications; 14% stent migration into the stomach; 25% tumour overgrowth. Median survival after stenting 94 days.

audits.t: BN SO02 - Cholecystectomy HRG Coding Audit
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Correct HRG coding based on comorbidity and complication index
audits.f: 69.23% of procedures coded incorrectly; £72,232 lost potential tariff (£372.33 per cholecystectomy); commonest correct code GA10J (CCI 3 in 29%), commonest wrong code GA10K (presumed CCI 0).
audits.c: Education and awareness under way before re-audit.

audits.t: BN SO11 - Optimising Day Case Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A GIRFT-Based Audit and Efficiency Analysis
audits.st: GIRFT national median day case rate of 60%
audits.f: Day case rate 64% (55/86), exceeding the national median of 60%.
audits.c: Business case to extend DSU recovery staffing and hours from 6pm to 9pm; coding team asked to separate elective from hot list cases.

audits.t: BN SO13 - Re-Audit of Biliary Pancreatitis Management: Enhancing Compliance with Timely Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
audits.st: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission for biliary acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 32.6% compliance.
audits.r2: 64.5% had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission.

audits.t: BN SO29 - Overinvestigation and unnecessary surgery for Gallbladder Polyps: An audit of compliance with ESGAR guidelines
audits.st: 2021 ESGAR guidance on management of gallbladder polyps
audits.f: 35 (36%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including all with polyp >10mm; histology cholecystitis 69%, true gallbladder polyp 6%; 47% of symptomatic patients had two ultrasounds and two clinic appointments. Adherence to ESGAR was inconsistent.

audits.t: HPB SO25 - The impact of chest physiotherapy on post-operative recovery from open liver surgery: A quality improvement project
audits.tp: Chest physiotherapy after open liver surgery
audits.st: Early postoperative chest physiotherapy as part of the enhanced recovery protocol
audits.f: 18/50 (36%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1; 16 (32%) received none; PPCs 20%.
audits.c: Intensive preoperative patient education, poster campaign and increased engagement with physiotherapists about timely chest physiotherapy
audits.r2: 20/36 (57%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1 (p=0.07); 7 (19%) received none (p=0.19); PPCs 8% (p=0.13).

audits.t: HPB SO38 - Assessing current pancreatic cancer reporting practice against the PACT-UK Synoptic Reporting Template: An initial clinical audit
audits.st: PACT-UK synoptic reporting template for pancreatic cancer CT; compliance defined as more than 90% of information available
audits.f: Compliance 0% for initial presentation scans and 4.2% (n=1) of 24 staging scans; the only compliant scan used the PACT-UK template

audits.t: HPB SO60 - A Re-Audit: Radiological Investigations In Patients Diagnosed With Gallstone Disease
audits.st: NICE guidance: liver function tests and ultrasound first line for suspected gallstones, MRCP/EUS if not detected
audits.f: 44 CT scans; CTAP as first scan in 38 patients.
audits.c: Findings presented at local general surgery clinical governance meeting and communicated to hospital doctors.
audits.r2: 31 CT scans (30% decrease); CTAP as first scan in 21 patients (45% drop).

audits.t: HPB SO63 - A Closed-Loop Audit on Surgical Ward Round Documentation in a Tertiary Hospital
audits.st: Key components of ward round documentation (date, time, diagnosis, procedure, consultant, author, information given, observations, investigations, plan)
audits.f: Time, history, NEWS and plan recorded in more than 50%; diagnosis, consultant, author, information to patient, wound and medication review, fluid balance, investigations and discharge plans in less than 50%.
audits.r2: Date and time 94%; consultant and author initials 84%; examination, information to patient, wound and medication review more than 80%.

audits.t: HPB SO65 - An audit of the day-case rate of laparoscopic cholecystectomies at a busy district general hospital and factors affecting this
audits.st: Model Hospital target day-case rate of 75% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.f: 34% (29/85) were not day cases; causes included post-operative nausea or pain (11), monitoring (9), MRCP (3), social issues (3), bleeding (2), IV antibiotics (1).

audits.t: HPB SO67 - An audit to improve the perioperative administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) to reduce the need for peri- and post-operative blood transfusion in major HPB resections
audits.st: RCS England recommendation (following NHSBT amber alert): tranexamic acid for all adult surgical patients where more than 500 ml blood loss is likely
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Prompt for TXA added to the WHO timeout pre-operative checklist.
audits.r2: The prompt did not increase the likelihood of a pre-operative TXA dose; change in haemoglobin and transfusion rates were similar between groups.

audits.t: O2 Are elderly patients undergoing emergency laparotomy receiving appropriate geriatrician input: a closed loop audit as looking at NELA standards
audits.st: NELA: CFS documented on admission for all aged 65+; geriatrician review for aged 80+ or 65+ with CFS 5 or more
audits.f: 70 laparotomies, 42 aged 65+; CFS documented in 40%; zero geriatric referrals.
audits.c: Email on how to refer, posters in offices and a talk by a senior geriatric medicine registrar at the governance meeting.
audits.r2: 59 laparotomies, 40 aged 65+; CFS documented in 58%; 15 had inpatient geriatrician review.

audits.t: eP12 Identifying and Managing Surgical Site Infections in Emergency and Elective General Surgery: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: GIRFT and PHE recommendations on SSI surveillance; CDC SSI definition
audits.f: 153/699 (21.8%) flagged as probable infection; 20/153 (13%) true infection; wound assessment clearly documented in 86/153 (56%).
audits.c: Electronic SSI bundle to standardise documentation.

audits.t: eP24 Streamlining Diverticulitis Care: An Audit of Hospital Admission Practices
audits.st: NICE guidelines on diverticulitis (admission, antibiotics, dietary advice, outpatient colonoscopy)
audits.f: Baseline figures not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Findings presented at M&M and teaching sessions, and posters across the department.
audits.r2: Dietary advice increased by 57.8%; outpatient colonoscopy requests rose by 30.7%; no reduction in IV antibiotic use for uncomplicated diverticulitis.

audits.t: eP27 Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) Completion Rates in Emergency Surgical Admissions: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Target of TEP completion on first consultant ward round
audits.f: 19 (15%) had TEP forms; 5 (26%) by parent surgical team; median time to completion 2 days; 39 of 47 operated patients (83%) had no TEP.
audits.c: Results presented at departmental meeting and target set for TEP completion on first consultant ward round.
audits.r2: 26 (17%) had TEP forms; 11 (42%) by parent surgical team; median time 1 day; 56 of 69 operated patients (81%) had no TEP.

audits.t: eP48 Multi-cycle audit on antibiotic duration and stepdown following laparotomy
audits.st: Local trust guidelines on antibiotic stewardship in intra-abdominal infection after source control
audits.f: Average post-operative antibiotic duration 11.2 days (± 7.7).
audits.c: Results presented locally to the surgical team, highlighting trust guidance on intra-abdominal infection prescribing, with microbiology input.

audits.t: eP52 Enhancing Acute Pancreatitis Management through a Multidisciplinary Upper Gastrointestinal Team Approach: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Acute pancreatitis management metrics: Glasgow score within 48 hours, imaging within 24 hours, cholecystectomy within 2 weeks, escalation and referral
audits.f: Escalation of severe cases 0%; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 75%; transfer of non-gallstone cases to gastroenterology 33%.
audits.c: Weekly benign UGI MDT with gastroenterology and radiology, streamlined ERCP pathway, hot cholecystectomy pathway, and targeted surgical education.
audits.r2: Glasgow score within 48 hours 50%; escalation 60%; imaging within 24 hours 100%; median admission to ERCP 5 days; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 100%; transfer to gastroenterology 50%.

audits.t: eP55 Nela Compliance in A District General Hospital: A Clinical Re-Audit
audits.tp: NELA data entry and case ascertainment
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) data entry for all emergency laparotomies
audits.f: 66% (n=73) of laparotomies entered into the NELA database.
audits.c: Surgical registrars added to the NELA team, redesigned theatre booking form and continuity of team roles during doctors' inductions

audits.t: eP66 Do emergency general surgery patients know their consultant? An audit based on the Francis Report
audits.st: Francis Report: 100% of patients aware of their responsible consultant
audits.f: 56.5% of patients were aware of their responsible consultant; 43.5% of headboards showed the named consultant.
audits.c: Results presented to FY1 doctors and surgical departments; juniors given whiteboard pens for headboards

audits.t: eP71 Audit of Emergency Laparotomy Workload in a District General Hospital: Are We Compliant with NELA Data Entry?
audits.tp: NELA data entry and case ascertainment
audits.st: NELA requirement: all emergency laparotomies registered and submitted by the deadline
audits.f: 31 (50%) entered; 4 (13%) met submission deadline; 18 (67%) registered more than 6 months after discharge; average delay 206 days.
audits.r2: 84% registered in Year 9 and 95% in Year 10; average time to entry 100 days; all submitted before the deadline.

audits.t: 1008 Management of Suspected Testicular Torsion – Audit of Current Practice
audits.st: NCEPOD and GIRFT recommendations for suspected testicular torsion
audits.f: 53.1% (n=17) reviewed by surgical team within 1 hour; 37.5% (n=12) explored within 1 hour of review; torsion in 21.8% (n=7), 3 (42.8%) needed orchidectomy.
audits.c: Data presented at local governance meeting and a new clinical pathway created.

audits.t: eP80 Transitioning from trauma: Audit on discharge quality for major trauma patients
audits.st: RCP discharge summary toolkit; target 100% completion
audits.f: Average completion 44.1%.
audits.c: Standardised discharge proforma for multiply injured patients, local training and education, then further reinforcement.
audits.r2: Third cycle: 78.92% (trauma ward 81.08% vs outlier wards 76.76%; t(50)=2.12, p=0.037).

audits.t: eP85 Documentation of Consent in Appendicectomy: A Closed Loop Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Legal consent standards and the Montgomery ruling
audits.f: Risk documentation: blood transfusion 0%, drain insertion 16.7%, adhesions 38.9%; EIDO leaflet use 11.1%; COVID risk 66.7%.
audits.c: EIDO leaflets provided on the surgical unit and consent teaching at induction (two PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: Blood transfusion 71.4%, drain insertion 85.7%, adhesions 76.2%; EIDO leaflet use 66.7%; COVID risk 28.6%.

audits.t: eP87 To pack or not to pack (abscesses) - that is the question. An audit evaluating local practice and its estimated environmental impact
audits.st: Consensus guidelines: intra-operative packing for haemostasis; insufficient evidence for regular post-operative packing
audits.f: Intra-operative packing 100%; regular packing after discharge recommended in 89%.
audits.c: Results discussed with the department, recommending post-discharge packing only when necessary
audits.r2: Intra-operative packing reduced by 10% and post-operative packing by 43%.

audits.t: eP93 The Effect of an eReferral Pathway on the Emergency General Surgical Take – A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: 481 Improving Practices in Extravasation Injury Management: A Retrospective Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Time of recognition documented in 53%; infusion stopped and limb elevated in 67%; injury photographed in 56%; plastic surgery advice sought in 81%.

audits.t: 193 Breaking Barriers in Achieving Excellence for National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Documentation: A Successful Quality Improvement Framework
audits.tp: NELA data entry and case ascertainment

audits.f: Only 11.7% (n=7) documented on NELA.

audits.t: 329 Audit of Compliance of Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment and Prescription of Prophylaxis in the General Surgery Directorate at Darlington Memorial Hospital (DMH)

audits.t: 601 Are Surgical Ward Rounds EPIC? – Audit of Ward Round Documentation Following Introduction of an Electronic Health Care System
audits.st: RCS Edinburgh SHINE Ward Round Tool and unit consultant consensus on the ideal ward round note
audits.f: Essential information missing in several domains.
audits.c: Feedback/educational session with resident doctors responsible for ward round documentation.
audits.r2: Improved recording of names of team members present, examination findings, patient understanding and management plan (p <0.05).

audits.t: 618 Improving Adherence to Antibiotic Prescribing Guidelines in Patients with Intra-Abdominal Sepsis: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: Local guideline: IV co-amoxiclav plus gentamicin first line; gentamicin, teicoplanin and metronidazole if penicillin allergic; stop 24 hours post-surgery or continue 5-7 days if no source control

audits.c: Two teaching sessions and guideline dissemination via posters.
audits.r2: Compliance 33.3% (16/48); penicillin-allergic regimen 6.25% (3/48); duration 5.71 days; 39.6% (19/48) received under 5 days.

audits.t: 736 Diagnostic and Documentation Quality in First-Time TURBT Performed in North Devon District Hospital
audits.st: NICE bladder cancer guidance 1.2.6 and 1.2.7 (documentation of tumour size and number, and mitomycin instillation)
audits.f: 78.20% of operation notes did not include mitomycin instillation or justification for not giving it; tumour number documented in 98.71% and tumour size in 88.46%
audits.r2: Quality of operation note documentation improved doubly (no further figures given)

audits.t: 761 Closing the Loop: Evaluating and Enhancing Adherence to a Local Acute Abdomen Pathway
audits.st: Local Acute Abdomen pathway
audits.f: Imaging within timeframe 60%; surgical review within timeframe 38.2%; antibiotics within 1 hour for septic patients 80%; NELA score documented 5.5%.
audits.r2: Imaging 78% (p=0.03); surgical review 91% (p<0.01); antibiotics within 1 hour 50% (p=0.33); NELA score 1% (p=0.15).

audits.t: eP73 “Why Radiology Requests are not Being Accepted”, a quality improvement audit in a surgical department
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guidance that requests include comprehensive relevant information
audits.f: 73% (52/71) of radiology requests accepted; rejections due to inappropriate imaging (4/19), duplicate requests (4/19) and insufficient clinical details (4/19), each 21%.
audits.c: Structured request format developed and staff educated on its use.

audits.t: 1136 Turning Data into Action: A Regional Audit and Quality Improvement Project to Elevate Core Surgical Training Standards
audits.st: JCST Quality Indicators for core surgical training
audits.f: Consistent theatre access 45% (9/21); scheduled clinic time 19% (4/21); over 75% unable to attend mandatory teaching.
audits.c: Findings presented to the Surgical Trainee Committee and trust leadership, leading to rota redesign, resource reallocation and improved planning.
audits.r2: Theatre access 78% (20/26); clinic time 50% (13/26); over 75% still unable to attend mandatory teaching.

audits.t: 953 Improving Documentation of Operation Notes for Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: 8-point TURBT operation note checklist
audits.f: Number of tumours 86.21%; size of largest tumour 65.52%; recurrent or primary 31.03%; CIS assessment 3.45%; clinical stage 10.34%; separate base biopsy 10.34%; detrusor muscle visualisation 71.43%.
audits.c: 12-point standardised TURBT operation note template introduced June 2024.
audits.r2: Number of tumours 100%; size 88.89%; recurrent or primary 66.67%; CIS assessment 55.56%; clinical stage 55.56%; base biopsy 66.67%; detrusor muscle visualisation 55.56%.

audits.t: SP1.05 Optimizing Day Case Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A GIRFT-Based closed loop audit
audits.st: GIRFT day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy rate (national median 60%)
audits.f: Day-case rate 64% (55/86).

audits.t: SP3.02 Unnecessary Preoperative Blood Tests for Patients Undergoing Abscess Incision and Drainage: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE: ASA 1 or 2 patients should not receive preoperative blood tests for abscess incision and drainage
audits.f: 71 abscess I&D cases, 55 ASA 1 or 2; 50/55 (91%) ASA 1–2 cases had routine bloods, costing £2,151.
audits.c: Findings disseminated to the department and posters advising not to take bloods for routine abscess I&D.
audits.r2: 63 cases, 55 ASA 1 or 2; 15/55 (27%) had routine bloods, costing £406.

audits.t: SP3.05 Improving Fluid Resuscitation and Maintenance Prescription Practices in Surgical Admissions: Closed loops double audits
audits.st: British Consensus Guidelines on Intravenous Fluid Therapy for Adult Surgical Patients (GIFTASUP)
audits.f: Resuscitation (n=59): 43% received optimal fluid resuscitation, 36% received no fluids, 34% prescribed non-optimal fluid types. Maintenance (n=53): 74% prescribed fluids, 66% met daily sodium requirements, 47% met free fluid requirements.
audits.c: Targeted educational interventions for junior doctors.
audits.r2: Resuscitation (n=53): optimal fluid resuscitation 83%, non-optimal prescriptions 17%, fluid prescription rate 64% to 94%. Maintenance (n=24): prescription rate 91.7%, sodium requirements 91.7%, free fluid targets 75%.

audits.t: SP3.09 Promoting Good Clinical Practice Certification Amongst Resident Doctors in a Major Surgical Emergency Unit: a Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Mandatory completion of NIHR Good Clinical Practice online training for SEU resident doctors
audits.f: 37.2% of resident doctors had completed GCP training at baseline (48.1% of 27 full-time SEU staff).
audits.c: Cycle 1: instructional email plus verbal instructions at handover, M&M and weekly RAP meeting; cycle 2: reminder email to non-completers and departmental newsletter reminder.
audits.r2: Completion 51.2% after cycle 1 and 62.8% after cycle 2 (p=0.001); full-time staff 63.0% then 77.8% (p=0.008).

audits.t: SP4.04 A Standards-Based Audit of Elective Procedures in a Tertiary Care Vascular Surgery Department in London
audits.tp: Rescheduling of cancelled elective operations within 28 days

audits.f: 165 of 402 scheduled procedures cancelled; 28-day rescheduling 14.75% (17.5% open, 12.0% endovascular).

audits.t: SP4.08 Enhancing Pediatric Appendicitis Care in Alignment with GIRFT Guidelines: A Two-Cycle Audit at a District Hospital

audits.t: SP4.09 A follow up audit of negative appendicectomy rates in a single site acute hospital
audits.st: UK negative appendicectomy rate estimated at 20%; comparison with previous local study
audits.f: Preoperative imaging 69%; NAR 10.3%.

audits.r2: Preoperative imaging 88% (mostly CT); NAR 3% (histology available in 84).

audits.t: SP4.12 An Audit of the investigations of suspected ureteric/kidney calculus in adults in Great Western Hospital, Swindon

audits.f: CT within 24 hours in 100%; serum calcium measured in 21%.

audits.r2: CT within 24 hours in 100%; serum calcium measured in 72%.

audits.t: SP9.10 Rethinking waste for a greener tomorrow in General Surgery: A two-cycle audit

audits.t: MTP1.14 Optimising Day Case Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: An Audit of Success Rates and Influencing Factors

audits.t: MTP3.06 Optimizing Blood Retesting Intervals: A Surgical Audit on FBC and U&E Tests in surgical in-patients

audits.f: not reported

audits.t: MTP7.04 The Extended Surgical Team – The role of the doctor’s assistant as part of the surgical team, a closed loop audit

audits.t: eP514 General Surgical Inpatient Falls: An Audit of Current Practices
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians national falls guidance and local protocol

audits.st: VTE prevention guidelines (risk assessment, prescription accuracy and timing)

audits.t: 370 Evaluating Noise and Light in Critical Care and Their Impact on Patients’ Sleep: A Closed-Loop Audit

audits.t: SRS101 - A closed loop audit assessing the rate of surgical site infections after wound closure with sutures in Major Lower Limb Amputations

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: 422 Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Gallstone Pancreatitis – Audit and Improvement of Trust Performance

audits.t: 1080 Assessing Surgical Education and Exposure Amongst Foundation Trainees in the Yorkshire and the Humber Deanery: A Comparative Audit

audits.t: 288 Improving Operation Note Documentation Against Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) Standards: A Completed Audit Cycle in the Department of Surgery, Holy Family Hospital, Pakistan

audits.t: TPW 5.04 Introduction of Post-Operative Antibiotic Guidelines Leads to Reduced Length of Post-Operative Stay and Improved Antimicrobial Stewardship in Uncomplicated Appendicectomy: A Single Centre Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: World Journal of Emergency Surgery Jerusalem guidelines: no postoperative antibiotics for uncomplicated appendicitis
audits.f: 54.3% of uncomplicated appendicitis cases (n=46) did not receive postoperative antibiotics; mean postoperative stay 23.3 hours.
audits.r2: 78.3% of uncomplicated cases (n=46) did not receive postoperative antibiotics (p = 0.0024); mean postoperative stay 14.5 hours (p = 0.0002).

audits.t: TPW 5.06 Emergency Appendicectomy Outcomes: A Benchmark Audit Against National Standards
audits.st: GIRFT and Royal College of Surgeons benchmarks for operative approach, length of stay, complications and readmission
audits.f: Laparoscopic in 95.0%, conversion 0.8%; median LOS 1 day (IQR 1–2), mean 2.0 days; 30-day readmission 6.7%; SSI 4.2%.

audits.t: TPW 5.08 Improving Outcomes in Emergency Laparoscopic Appendicectomy: A Two-Cycle Audit in a UK Tertiary Centre
audits.st: National and WSES recommendations for laparoscopic appendicectomy
audits.f: Time to diagnosis 16.8 hours; diagnosis to surgery 28.1 hours; CT 80%; scoring system use 0%; negative appendicectomy 8.9%; drains 44%; postoperative antibiotics 92.1%; complications 17.8%.
audits.r2: Time to diagnosis 8.27 hours; diagnosis to surgery 20.54 hours; CT 77.8%; scoring system use 3.3%; negative appendicectomy 7.7%; drains 31%; postoperative antibiotics 75.6%; complications 3.3%.

audits.t: TPW 6.13 Timing of Cholecystectomy for Gallstone Disease in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Compliance, Readmissions and Service Burden
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: Guideline-recommended cholecystectomy within 10 days for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis
audits.f: Of 73 patients fit for surgery, only 11% underwent cholecystectomy within 10 days.

audits.t: TPW 7.03 Shared Decision-Making and Documentation before ERCP for Choledocholithiasis: A GMC-Aligned Audit Using Prespecified Operative-Risk Strata
audits.st: UK legal and professional (GMC) standards: documentation of material risks and reasonable alternatives (options-based shared decision-making) before ERCP
audits.f: Options-based SDM documented in 73/356 (20.5%) ERCP episodes: low risk 19/78 (24.4%), medium 21/141 (14.9%), high 33/137 (24.1%) (p=0.105). Increased from 12.5% (2023Q4) to 31.8% (2024Q4) (p=0.160). LCBDE 38/38 (100%).

audits.t: TPW 7.13 Audit into the Management of Gallstone Pancreatitis at A Tertiary Care NHS Trust
audits.st: NICE: cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge for non-severe gallstone pancreatitis
audits.f: Of 30 mild or moderate cases, 2 (6.6%) had cholecystectomy during index admission; of 14 (45%) with elective surgery within five months, 2 (14%) were within two weeks.
audits.c: Planned dedicated hot cholecystectomy pathway with protected theatre capacity and re-audit.

audits.t: TPW 7.16 Improving Compliance with Severity Scoring in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology: severity scoring within 48 hours of admission
audits.f: 2 of 12 (16.7%) had a Glasgow Imrie score recorded.
audits.c: Targeted teaching for resident doctors and a process for the on-call team to ensure scoring of all new admissions.

audits.t: TPW 7.20 Closed Loop Audit: Assessing Parenteral Nutrition in General Surgical Patients in A Busy Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Local nutrition standards
audits.f: Height and weight documented 11/14; MUST score 9/14; PN commenced 9/14; median HLOS 30 days (6-44).
audits.r2: Height and weight 15/18; MUST 17/18; PN commenced 15/18; all reviewed by PN nurse within 1 day; median HLOS 17 days (7-38).

audits.t: TPW 9.02 Routine Preoperative Investigations in Low-Risk Elective Inguinal Hernia Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE guidance on routine preoperative tests by ASA grade
audits.f: Poor overall compliance with NICE guidelines (figures not given).
audits.c: Results presented locally; updated trust guidance and a digital decision-aid tool.
audits.r2: ASA 1 unnecessary tests fell by 20.5% (FBC), 21.4% (haemostasis), 22.6% (U&E), 33.0% (ECG); ASA 2 fell by 75.0%, 16.7%, 11.9% and 9.4%.

audits.t: TPW 9.08 Establishing and Evaluating a Laparoscopic Peritoneal Dialysis Catheter Insertion Service in NHS Lanarkshire: A Two-Cohort Comparative Audit
audits.tp: Laparoscopic peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion outcomes
audits.st: International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis (ISPD) guidelines
audits.f: 0% 30-day peritonitis and SSI; 6-month PD peritonitis 22% (4/18); urinary retention 11% (2/18); overnight stay 83% (15/18).
audits.c: Maturation of the reintroduced service over time (no specific change described).
audits.r2: 0% 30-day peritonitis and SSI; 6-month PD peritonitis 5.8% (2/34); urinary retention 2.9% (1/34); overnight stay 44.1% (15/34).

audits.t: TPW 9.16 Comparative Re-Audit of Unplanned Delays in Emergency General Surgery Theatre Lists
audits.st: Operating Theatre Efficiency Guideline: late start is time into operating room after the scheduled session start time
audits.f: 81% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 50% delayed; Mondays 77% and Thursdays 69% delayed
audits.c: Educational intervention for surgical and anaesthetic teams and an updated registrar role
audits.r2: 66% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 55% delayed; Mondays 56% and Thursdays 43% delayed

audits.t: TPTh 1.09 Improving Prescribing of Regular Medications in Nil-by-Mouth Surgical Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit at a District General Hospital
audits.st: National guidance to continue most regular medications while nil by mouth
audits.f: Regular medications prescribed while NBM on day of surgery 13.7%; emergency patients 15.0% (n=20); omission 4 or more days 19.6%.
audits.c: Graphical reminders in clinical workspaces and a departmental presentation
audits.r2: Prescribed 28.6% (p=0.12); emergency patients 43.5% (n=23, p=0.054); omission 4 or more days 11.9% (p=0.40).

audits.t: TPTh 2.12 Regional Adherence to National GIRFT Surgical Guidelines on Post-Operative Antibiotic Prescribing in Paediatric Appendicitis: Multi-Centre Multi-Cycle Audit of Clinical Practice
audits.st: GIRFT guidelines on post-operative antibiotic prescribing in paediatric appendicitis
audits.f: Compliance 46-75% between hospitals (p=0.08); average 20.5 cases per site (range 13-34); median 4.5 days antibiotics after uncomplicated appendicectomy.
audits.c: Findings presented at governance events; targeted education for junior doctors, clear antibiotic plans in operation notes and empowering juniors to challenge prescriptions.

audits.t: TPTh 2.14 Enhancing Guideline Adherence in Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding Through Structured Risk Stratification: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: BSG risk stratification guidance for lower gastrointestinal bleeding (Shock Index and Oakland score)
audits.f: Shock Index calculated in 27% (18/66), Oakland score in 36% (24/66); admission rate 53% (35/66); 44% (15/35) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.
audits.r2: Shock Index 82% (47/57), Oakland score 79% (45/57); admission rate 38% (22/57); 18% (4/22) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.

audits.t: TPTh 3.08 Multi-Centre Audit of Abdominal Pain CT Pathways to Identify Emergency Laparotomy Patients Shows an Innovative “Straight to Test” Pathway from ED Triage is Possible Without Senior Surgeon Input in More than just One Hospital
audits.st: Hospital abdominal pain CT pathway criteria and RCEM CT criteria at triage
audits.f: 67/70 (96%) met hospital abdominal pain CT pathway criteria at triage; 10/70 (14%) met RCEM criteria; mean time to CT from ED arrival 11 hr 36 min.

audits.t: TPTh 3.09 Audit of Diagnosis and Management of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Tract Bleeding (LGIB) in a Rural General Hospital, can we reduce hospital admissions?
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 LGIB guidelines (Oakland score for safe discharge)
audits.f: 13 minor and 60 major by Oakland score; 4 discharged same day; median stay 3 days; 72% managed conservatively; 18 transfused, 3 had surgery.

audits.t: TPTh 4.02 A Retrospective Audit of Routine Preoperative Blood Grouping and Saving in Laparoscopic Appendicectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No patients required transfusion; 75% had two G&S samples and 21% had one.
audits.r2: No transfusions required; similar G&S sampling pattern.

audits.t: TPTh 4.03 Improving Antimicrobial Stewardship in Acute Appendicitis Through Education and System-Level Documentation Redesign: A Closed-Loop Audit at Wirral University Teaching Hospital NHS Trust
audits.st: WSES 2020 guidelines: post-operative antibiotic use and duration, intra-operative documentation of severity and contamination, microbiological sampling
audits.f: Mean antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis 9.2 days.
audits.c: Consultant-led education and a revised electronic laparoscopic appendicectomy theatre note with guideline prompts.
audits.r2: Antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis fell to 8.4 days.

audits.t: TPTh 4.09 Post-Operative Antibiotic use Following Appendectomy: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Adherence
audits.st: BMJ Best Practice guidance on post-operative antibiotics after appendicectomy (total duration 5 days)
audits.f: 52/67 (77.6%) uncomplicated cases received post-operative antibiotics; where op note said no further antibiotics this was followed in 14/29 (48%); compliance with specified duration or route 27.78%; 47 complicated cases received ~3 days IV then 5 days oral.
audits.c: Recommendations implemented and targeted teaching sessions for junior doctors; second cycle planned.

audits.t: TPTh 4.12 Utilisation of Risk Scoring and Imaging in Acute Appendicitis Diagnosis: A Retrospective Audit of Appendicitis Diagnostic Pathways
audits.st: WSES (adults) and GIRFT (children) guidance: risk score all suspected appendicitis to guide imaging
audits.f: No adult had a risk score documented; 2 (9%) children had one; 9/46 (20%) imaged adults were low risk; 34/46 (74%) had CT first line.

audits.t: TPTh 4.13 Social History Documentation in NoLap National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Patients: A Retrospective Audit
audits.st: NELA: formal frailty assessment for patients over 65 (NoLap patients)
audits.f: No patient had a clinical frailty score; social history recorded in 34 (72%); no cognitive documentation in 33 (70%); baseline mobility not recorded in 21 (45%).

audits.t: TPTh 4.15 Negative Appendicectomy Rate Audit in our Local Trust
audits.st: Negative appendicectomy rate compared with UK rate of 20% (RIFT study 2020) and global 13%; trust requires preoperative imaging
audits.f: NAR 4.67% (7/150), all with preoperative imaging; NAR 11.54% in patients aged 16–25.

audits.t: TPTh 5.09 Evaluating Adherence to ATLS Protocols in the Assessment of Trauma Patients: A Full-Cycle Audit in a District General Hospital
audits.st: ATLS protocols: documentation of primary and secondary surveys
audits.f: Primary survey done in 9%; secondary survey in 7%; missed injury rate 4.5%.
audits.c: Resident doctor education on ATLS principles, promotion of ATLS certification, and a structured ATLS trauma clerk-in template.
audits.r2: Primary survey 78%; secondary survey 69.5%; no missed injuries.

audits.t: TPTh 5.11 An Audit of Carotid Symptoms to Referral Time would be helpful in Developing the Carotid Pathway to Improve Timely Referrals
audits.tp: Carotid endarterectomy symptom to surgery time
audits.st: National standards (National Vascular Registry): surgery within 14 days and referral within 7 days of symptoms
audits.f: 60% had surgery within 14 days (national 49%); median symptom to surgery 13 days (national 14); 60% referred within 7 days (national 72%).

audits.t: TPTh 6.07 A Multi-disciplinary Approach to Improving Paediatric Major Trauma Tertiary Survey Compliance, a Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: South-East Scotland Major Trauma Guidelines: tertiary survey within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Tertiary survey completed in 34% (15 of 44); within 24 hours 20% (3 of 15); median time 44.5 hours.
audits.c: Educational package and major trauma coordinators empowered to enforce tertiary surveys as a discharge prerequisite, with weekly check-ins.
audits.r2: Completed in 72% (124 of 172); within 24 hours 56% (70 of 124); median time 15.9 hours.

audits.t: TPTh 7.05 Urgent MRCP Pathway Performance: A Baseline Audit of Delays and Service Impact
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median request to scan 3 days (IQR 2-6), mean 7.99 days; inpatients (n=85) median 2 days (IQR 1–4); outpatients (n=34) median 13 days (IQR 3–31).

audits.t: TPTh 7.07 The Effectiveness of Systematic Interventions Leading to Change in Practice: A Three-Cycle Clinical Audit on Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.st: NICE and BSG recommendations against prophylactic antibiotics in acute pancreatitis
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed in 45.9% (n=17/37); inappropriate prescribing 52.9% (n=9/17).
audits.c: Awareness posters after the first cycle, then targeted teaching in weekly junior doctor sessions after the second cycle.
audits.r2: Antibiotics prescribed in 47.8% (n=11/23); inappropriate prescribing 9.1% (n=1/11) (p for trend = 0.016); documentation of indication 100%.

audits.t: TPTh 8.13 Escalation Planning in Acute General Surgery: Persistent Gaps Highlighted in a 300-Patient Audit
audits.st: Local trust standard (with Resuscitation Council UK guidance): TEP and DNACPR documented within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Ceiling-of-care decisions documented in 18% (n=54); only 6% (n=18) had TEP or DNACPR documented within 24 hours; DNACPR present in 12% (n=36), 40% of which lacked clear clerking documentation.
audits.c: Planned: structured training for junior doctors and strengthened admission proformas, then re-audit.

audits.t: TPTh 9.03 Improving Early Management of Acute Pancreatitis: A Six-Month Audit at Royal Surrey County Hospital
audits.st: National guidance and WATERFALL trial moderate fluid resuscitation (10ml/kg bolus then 1.5ml/kg/hr), two regular and one PRN analgesic, imaging sequence and Glasgow-Imrie scoring
audits.f: 33% received recommended minimum fluids in 24 hours; 37% had one or no regular analgesic; urine output monitored in 25%; ultrasound first in 25% (CT in 87%); Glasgow-Imrie documented in 12%.

audits.t: TPTh 9.10 Imaging and Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Compliance
audits.st: RCR and UK national guidelines for acute pancreatitis (CT timing, ultrasound within 24 hours, antibiotics)
audits.f: CT on admission in 43 and within 3 days in 13 more, all with diagnostic amylase, contrary to guidance; ultrasound in 62 at mean 1.9 days (target 24 hours); MRCP in 49 at mean 2.3 days; 22 of 56 given antibiotics without evidence of infection or necrosis.
audits.c: Local recommendations implemented and junior teaching started; 2nd cycle planned.

audits.t: TPTh 9.11 Acute Pancreatitis in Surgical Admissions: A Closed- Loop Audit of Compliance Against the British Society of Gastroenterology Guidelines
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for diagnosis, aetiology assessment and risk stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.f: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 97%; risk stratification within 48 hours 38%; aetiology assessment 62%.
audits.c: Results presented at audit meeting, MDT posters and teaching sessions.

audits.t: EP 018 Closed Loop Audit: Assessing the Children’s Appendicitis Score
audits.st: Regional Children's Appendicitis Score (CAS) pathway
audits.f: Documented CAS 9% (1/11); surgical referral 100% (11/11); theatre 55% (6/11).
audits.c: Educational sessions to promote the use of CAS.

audits.t: EP 179 Closed Loop Audit of Prophylactic Antibiotic Practices in Ventral Hernia Repair According to the Local Hospital Guidelines
audits.st: Local guideline (in line with European and British Hernia Societies): prophylaxis only for high-risk mesh repair using the standard regimen
audits.f: Overall compliance 27.1%; unnecessary antibiotics in 35.6%; only 1 of 23 high-risk mesh patients received recommended prophylaxis.
audits.c: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters.
audits.r2: Overall adherence 80%; 90.9% compliance among high-risk mesh patients; 2 of 4 low-risk patients received unnecessary prophylaxis.

audits.t: EP 183 Quality Improvement in Surgical Discharge Summaries: An Audit of the Performance of a London Tertiary Colorectal Surgery Department
audits.st: Professional Records Standards Body and Royal College of Physicians national discharge summary guidelines (7-point score)
audits.f: Median and modal score 5.00/7.00, mean 4.15/7.00; safety netting advice lowest (14%); events/procedures highest (89%); 4 had no discharge summary.
audits.c: Results presented locally and a discharge summary proforma based on national standards disseminated.
audits.r2: Median and modal score 6.00/7.00, mean 6.06/7.00; safety netting lowest (32%); reason for admission, events/procedures and post-op plan 100%.

audits.t: EP 184 Prophylactic Antibiotics in Groin Hernia Repair: Are We Compliant with Current Guidelines? Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: HerniaSurge, European and British Hernia Society and trust guidelines: no routine prophylaxis for low-risk elective open mesh or laparoscopic repair
audits.f: 6 of 22 high-risk patients received compliant prophylaxis; antibiotics unnecessary in 32.5%; overall compliance 27.1%.
audits.c: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters
audits.r2: 90.9% of 11 high-risk patients compliant; 1 of 2 low-risk patients given unnecessary antibiotics; overall adherence 84.6%.

audits.t: EP 292 Improving Adherence to Pre-Operative Assessment Investigation Guidelines for Elective Breast Surgery: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE NG45 pre-operative tests; trust guidance POA at least two weeks before surgery
audits.c: Planned: MDT discussion, EPR virtual checklist and staff education (not yet implemented).

audits.t: EP 312 A Closed-Loop Audit of Surgical Antibiotic Prophylaxis: Enhancing Perioperative Safety through Multi-Disciplinary Process Integration
audits.st: Local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guideline: correct antibiotic choice, dose and timing (≤30 minutes pre-incision)
audits.f: Correct antibiotic choice 50.4%, correct dose 44.1%, correct timing 58.5%.
audits.c: Targeted teaching, QR-enabled guideline posters at point of care, and 'antibiotic dose and timing confirmed?' added to the WHO time-out checklist.
audits.r2: Improvements in antibiotic selection, weight-based gentamicin dosing and timing (figures not stated).

audits.t: EP 349 Audit of Updated ERAS Guidelines Followed in Elective Colorectal Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
audits.st: ERAS 2025 guidelines (10 of 23 recommendations with high-grade evidence)
audits.f: More than 90% compliance in PONV prophylaxis, NG tube removal, multimodal analgesia, post-op enteral nutrition, IV antibiotics and VTE prophylaxis; mechanical bowel prep routinely prescribed in more than 85% of resections (not recommended); more than 78% minimally invasive; 73% no drain.

audits.t: EP 368 Evaluating Missed Opportunities for Emergency Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Retrospective Single-Centre Audit
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: Priority (P-status) timeframes for surgery
audits.f: Only 3 patients had surgery within P2 targets; 79 (41%) had multiple booking requests; 52 (27%) potentially suitable for earlier emergency cholecystectomy, with deferral reasons documented for 8.

audits.t: EP 519 ECG Analysis and Documentation in Surgery at UHNM, an Audit of Practice
audits.st: ECGs should show documented clinician analysis and actions where required
audits.f: 33% of ECGs adequately scrutinised and documented; 52% had documented actions.
audits.c: Staff education programme and a proforma stamp applied to each trace before presentation to a clinician.
audits.r2: Final (third) cycle: 51% documented and 43% had actions taken.

audits.t: EP 678 A Retrospective Audit of Surveillance Practices of Screen-Detected B3 Lesions in a Tertiary Breast Unit
audits.st: NHSBSP guidance: previously five-year annual mammography for B3 lesions with atypia after excision; new guidance returns to routine screening
audits.f: 64% (36/56) referred for five-year annual mammograms; concordance with previous guidance 86% (48/56); 57% (32/56) would not need surveillance under new guidance.

audits.t: EP 687 Are we Overscoping?: An Audit of Colonoscopic Follow-up in Acute Diverticulitis Management
audits.st: ASGBI and ACPGBI: endoscopic evaluation at 6-8 weeks only for complicated diverticulitis (Hinchey 2 and above)
audits.f: Hinchey score recorded in 8.7% (10/115); 27 uncomplicated cases had unnecessary follow-up colonoscopy.

audits.t: EP 697 Audit Report: Diagnosis-to-Operation Timing in Emergency Appendicectomy
audits.st: WSES: emergency appendicectomy within 24 hours of diagnosis
audits.f: 49.1% operated within 24 hours; 50.9% exceeded 24 hours.

audits.t: A single-centre audit of early warning scores and medical emergency team activation in medical and surgical admissions at Wellington Regional Hospital
audits.tp: Early warning score response and escalation
audits.st: New Zealand early warning score (NZEWS) calculation and MET callout criteria
audits.f: NZEWS correctly calculated and documented in 75.8%; 46.8% of 47 NZEWS instances mandating MET activation led to a callout; 20 of 23 patients meeting MET criteria had a callout.

audits.t: EP01 Audit of the monitoring and documentation of DAS28 score in patients prescribed high cost DMARDs for rheumatoid arthritis every 6 months according to British Society for Rheumatology guidelines
audits.st: NICE and BSR: DAS28 recorded at least every 6 months for patients with RA on high-cost DMARDs
audits.f: 166 (80%) had a documented DAS28; 14 (7%) had DAS28 at least 6-monthly; 152 (73%) did not meet the standard

audits.t: P05 Involving patients in the discussion about results from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Patient involvement in national early inflammatory arthritis audit results
audits.st: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA) seven quality standards
audits.f: Significant room for improvement across all seven quality standards (figures not given).
audits.c: Results shared with MDT and an NRAS patient support group (45 patients and carers), driver diagrams developed and a patient waiting-area poster produced.

audits.t: P06 Driving up quality: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE QS33: QS2 seen in rheumatology within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 newly diagnosed RA offered short-term glucocorticoids and combination DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: 22 patients (8.9%) seen within 3 weeks of referral; 5 (7%) started DMARD within 6 weeks; mean wait 66 days (range 5-138) to be seen and diagnosed; 65 (90%) given bridging steroids; 65 (92%) started DMARDs.
audits.c: Process mapping and driver diagrams identified changes: primary care referral guidelines, more triage and new appointment capacity, simpler booking, text reminders, one-stop clinic with ultrasound, more drug education clinic capacity.

audits.t: P07 Improving patient care in psoriatic arthritis through quality improvement and audit against the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence NG65 guidelines
audits.st: NICE NG65 spondyloarthritis guideline (NICE baseline assessment tool)
audits.f: CASPAR or peripheral ASAS criteria documented 78%; X-rays of symptomatic hands/feet 83%; information on PsA 58%; csDMARD monotherapy escalated 83%; flare advice access 100%; CV and skin cancer risk discussion on anti-TNF 30%.

audits.t: P08 The impact of patient’s compliance and delivery delays: a cost-saving audit on biologics
audits.tp: Biologic home delivery stock checks and cost saving
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 133/168 patients answered; home stock 0 to 12 weeks; repeat prescriptions delayed in 62 patients by 1 to 8 weeks, a theoretical saving of £13,546.585 (6.5% of the monthly anti-TNF cost of £208,099.94).
audits.c: Biologic patient education programme launched and patients encouraged to contact the biologic coordinator if non-compliant.

audits.t: P09 Audit of anti-nuclear antibody testing in East Kent and the British Society for Rheumatology Choosing Wisely recommendations
audits.st: BSR Choosing Wisely recommendations on ANA testing
audits.f: Only 17% of requests met the standards; 41% inappropriate; 42% had insufficient details.
audits.c: Local ANA testing guidelines devised from Choosing Wisely standards.

audits.t: P15 An audit of the management of Behçet's disease in a tertiary referral centre against guidelines from EULAR and the National Centres of Excellence
audits.st: EULAR guidelines and National Centres of Excellence guidelines for Behçet's disease (escalation and de-escalation of treatment)
audits.f: 26/50 had used anti-TNFalpha therapy and 9/50 IV cyclophosphamide; EULAR guideline followed least well by rheumatology; low adherence to the national guideline due to methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine use in less severe disease and failure to switch from IV to subcutaneous anti-TNFalpha (adherence figures given in a table only).

audits.t: P167 Pulmonary hypertension in patients with systemic sclerosis: an audit of screening practices, incidence and cost over 10 years
audits.tp: Pulmonary hypertension screening in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: Every SSc patient screened annually with echocardiography or NT pro-BNP (European Society of Cardiology)
audits.f: 65% screened, all by echocardiography.
audits.c: NT pro-BNP introduced as an adjunct to echocardiography in 2014.
audits.r2: 88% screened; 25% had echocardiogram and 83% NT pro-BNP; 63% screened by NT pro-BNP only.

audits.t: BSR guideline on the management of adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 2018: baseline multi-centre audit in the UK
audits.st: BSR 2018 guideline for management of adults with SLE, NICE technology appraisal for belimumab and NHS England commissioning policy for rituximab
audits.f: 1021 episodes of care audited; low documented compliance (<60% of visits) for formal disease-activity assessment, reduction of drug toxicity and protection against comorbidities; prednisolone recorded in 497 (49%) visits, including 28.5% of visits with inactive disease.

audits.t: P003 An audit of the uptake of vaccinations against influenza, pneumonia and varicella zoster among rheumatology outpatients
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: Public Health England, BSR and EULAR vaccination guidance; target 90% uptake; departmental vaccination advice in standard letter template
audits.f: Influenza 63/87 (72%); pneumococcus 61/87 (70%); zoster 7/12 (64%); vaccination advice in 24/126 (19%) clinic letters.

audits.t: P007 Service evaluation of the nurse-led telephone advice line in the wake of COVID-19: a report of audit and staff satisfaction
audits.tp: Rheumatology nurse advice line response times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Multiple attempts needed to return the call in 19/97 (19.6%), of which 13/19 (68.4%) needed ≥2 nurses; first return attempt average 7.6 hours (range 0.1–27.7); time to conclude call average 12.7 hours (range 0.1–142.6); doctor advice needed in 18/97 (18.5%).

audits.t: P010 Management of fibromyalgia patients in secondary care: a retrospective audit
audits.st: 2017 EULAR recommendations for the management of fibromyalgia
audits.f: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 34/50 (68%), physiotherapy 5/50 (10%), psychological input 3/50 (6%); referred to multidisciplinary pain management programme 4/50 (8%).
audits.r2: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 71/82 (87%, p=0.008), physiotherapy 28/82 (34%, p=0.002), psychological input 16/82 (20%, p=0.03); referred to pain management programme 64/82 (78%, p<0.0001); all had pain and function assessed; psychosocial context assessed in 64/82 (78%); information given to 53 (65%).

audits.t: P013 Driving improvement through audit: impact of 2017 regional audit and survey upon giant cell arteritis services in 2020
audits.st: BSR guidance on giant cell arteritis (revised)
audits.f: 14/16 sites responded; 2 sites had a GCA pathway; routine steroid leaflets 6/14 (43%); 1 site had a GCA database; 8 had a steroid taper protocol.
audits.c: 2017 audit and survey results fed back to sites and regionally; sites introduced GCA pathways, temporal artery ultrasound, steroid leaflets and local QI.
audits.r2: 15/16 sites responded; 6 sites had a GCA pathway; temporal artery ultrasound 6/15 (40%); routine steroid leaflets 12/15 (80%); GCA database 4 (27%); steroid taper protocol 7.

audits.t: P016 When and how to deliver advice about self-management: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Self-management advice in early inflammatory arthritis
audits.st: NICE QS33 QS4: RA patients offered educational and self-management activities within 1 month of diagnosis
audits.f: All RA patients received written information at baseline; only 39 (71%) documented as given self-management advice at 3-month follow-up; 41 (56%) started DMARD within 6 weeks of referral.
audits.c: Driver diagrams with patient group input identified changes: agreed definition of self-management, patient activation measure, different delivery formats and expert patients.

audits.t: P017 Out of outlier status: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE QS33: QS2 seen within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 RA started on DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: 10% of all patients seen within 3 weeks; 7% of RA cohort (n=77) started DMARD within 6 weeks.
audits.c: Primary care referral guidelines, prompts for RF/CCP requests and changed antibody report wording, more triage and new appointment capacity (extra consultant, upskilled ESP), simpler booking, more drug education and monitoring clinic capacity, signposting to NRAS.
audits.r2: 54% seen within 3 weeks; 56% of RA cohort (n=73) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.t: P019 Audit of prostanoid use in severe Raynaud’s and adherence to treatment of digital ulcers in patients with SSc NHSE pathway: commissioning policy cost analysis and alternative therapeutic pathway proposed
audits.tp: Digital ulcer treatment in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: NHS England 2015 commissioning policy pathway for digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis
audits.f: Prior trials: CCB 77.4%, ACEi/ARB 41.1%, fluoxetine 9.59%, sildenafil 87.1%, tadalafil 25.8%; 22.6% of SSc patients had tried bosentan; only 2 SSc patients (6.45%) had trialled all pathway drugs before prostanoid.

audits.t: P177 Management of patients with axSpA: an audit against the NICE diagnosis and management of adults with spondyloarthritis quality standard, QS170, and clinical practice guidelines
audits.st: NICE QS170 (MRI if no radiographic evidence, structured exercise programme, patient information) and clinical practice guidelines
audits.f: MRI in 18/19 (94.7%) with X-rays showing no sacroiliitis; education in 228/267 (85.4%); referral to structured exercise 217/259 (83.8%); first-line NSAIDs 246/248 (99.2%); 6-monthly renal monitoring on NSAIDs 80.3%; 12-week bDMARD response assessment 198/233 (85.0%).

audits.t: OA41 Audit of the rheumatology PIFU pathway at the UHMB Trust
audits.st: BSR draft guidance on patient-initiated follow-up
audits.f: 9/100 triggered a review; 8 received a nurse call-back within 48 hours; 1 needed urgent consultant review and was seen within 7 days; all 9 reverted to regular follow-up.

audits.t: P001 Audit on giant cell arteritis fast track clinic in Tayside
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) GCA standards
audits.f: 70.8% seen by rheumatology within 24 hours; 50% with visual symptoms seen by ophthalmology within 24 hours; 89% given steroids within 24 hours; 80.8% had ultrasound or biopsy; written information, recurrence advice, CRP and bone protection documentation 100%.

audits.t: P011 Audit and Outcomes of Hydroxychloroquine Screening for Retinopathy in a Cohort of Patients with Rheumatological Conditions
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists 2018 guidelines on hydroxychloroquine dosing and retinopathy screening
audits.f: Of 86 eligible patients, 23% were prescribed a dose of >5mg/kg/day; 10% had eGFR <60; none on tamoxifen. 29 patients attended screening and none had HCQ retinopathy.

audits.t: P012 Cross-specialty audit of Infliximab prescribing at the Great North Children’s Hospital (GNCH)
audits.st: Local trust guidelines based on BSPAR guidance (rheumatology) and ESPGHAN guidelines (gastroenterology)
audits.f: 17 rheumatology and 17 age-matched Crohn's gastroenterology patients audited; specialties were not following all guidelines perfectly, particularly pre-treatment viral screening (detailed results in a table not supplied).
audits.c: Recommended development of cross-specialty infliximab guidance.

audits.t: P016 Steroid prescribing and risk of adrenal insufficiency: an audit of giant cell arteritis cases
audits.tp: Steroid emergency card and adrenal insufficiency advice
audits.st: National Patient Safety Alert (August 2020) on steroid emergency cards and adrenal insufficiency risk
audits.f: No patients given steroid emergency cards at first visit (4 during follow-up); 5/90 given written information on adrenal insufficiency risk at first visit; 1/90 given information on symptoms; none given sick day rules at first visit (9 during follow-up).
audits.c: Dedicated GCA clinics and improved follow-up, standardised written steroid information and personalised reduction plans, education sessions for medical and nursing teams, and electronic prescribing of emergency cards (being incorporated).

audits.t: P020 The impact of COVID-19: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE quality standard QS33 (QS2 and QS3), measured as being seen within 3 weeks of referral and starting DMARD within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: 41% of all patients seen within 3 weeks of referral and 58% of RA patients started DMARD within 6 weeks, compared with 54% and 56% in year 2 (268 patients).

audits.t: P022 Audit of vitamin D and calcium level monitoring in sarcoidosis patients taking calcium and/or vitamin D supplements
audits.tp: Calcium and vitamin D monitoring in sarcoidosis
audits.st: Monitoring of serum calcium and vitamin D in sarcoidosis patients on calcium and/or vitamin D supplementation
audits.f: 46/102 (45%) had serum calcium and vitamin D measured in the community in the last 12 months.

audits.t: P026 Sugar rush: single-centre audit of screening and counselling for steroid-induced hyperglycaemia, based on the British Society for Rheumatology giant cell arteritis guideline
audits.tp: Glycaemic monitoring on glucocorticoids in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology GCA guideline: HbA1c monitoring and documented counselling on steroid-induced hyperglycaemia
audits.f: Baseline HbA1c checked in 32/60 (53%); counselling documented 7/60 (12%); hyperglycaemia detected 8/60 (13%).
audits.c: Results presented at a regional meeting to raise awareness and a GCA clinic was set up.
audits.r2: Baseline HbA1c checked in 28/30 (93%); counselling documented 9/30 (30%); hyperglycaemia detected 11/30 (36%).

audits.t: P138 Real-world incidence and management of hypocalcaemia after denosumab administration in patients with chronic kidney disease: a UK secondary-care based audit
audits.tp: Calcium monitoring after denosumab in renal impairment
audits.st: Local protocol: weekly calcium and renal function for 4 weeks after each denosumab injection if CrCl <35 ml/min
audits.f: 29/52 (56%) missed one or more post-injection blood tests, most often the 1st and 4th weekly checks. 18/54 (33%) developed hypocalcaemia; only 3 had adjusted calcium <2.0 mmol/l.

audits.t: P293 Tocilizumab for refractory or relapsing giant cell arteritis: audit data from the Bristol and Bath regional multidisciplinary meetings 2018-2021
audits.tp: Tocilizumab approval criteria in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: NHS England criteria (Blueteq) for tocilizumab in refractory or relapsing GCA; MDT discussion required before starting
audits.f: 38 cases discussed, 31 approved for tocilizumab; 100% of approved cases met criteria for refractory (n = 11) or relapsing (n = 20) disease.

audits.t: P009 Navigating giant cell arteritis (GCA) service during and post COVID-19 pandemic: an audit of GCA care at North Bristol NHS Trust against the BSR quality standards
audits.st: BSR quality standards for GCA
audits.f: Mean referral to specialist review 2.7 days; temporal artery biopsy 41%.
audits.c: Twice-weekly registrar-led hot clinics, ad hoc slots in on-call consultant clinics for GCA referrals, and increased vascular ultrasound capacity during the pandemic.
audits.r2: Mean referral to specialist review 1.6 days; all had vascular ultrasound; temporal artery biopsy 7.5%. 33% diagnosed and treated as GCA.

audits.t: P012 Using the BSR Lupus audit as a springboard to improve management of SLE in the outpatient clinic
audits.st: BSR national Lupus audit standards (11 standards) based on BSR Lupus guidelines
audits.f: 5/11 audit standards met.
audits.c: Nurse education and urine testing added to the clinic observation form; electronic SLE review form and electronic SLEDAI score introduced.
audits.r2: 4/11 standards met across all clinics; 9/11 in the specialist clinic. Urine testing rose from 22% (2020) to 90%. When the SLE review form was used, all standards were met apart from lipid testing and pregnancy discussion (79% vs standard 80%).

audits.t: P013 A three-year audit of dose tapering biologic medications in a rheumatology service
audits.st: ACR and EULAR guidance supporting biologic tapering; locally agreed eligibility criteria
audits.f: Patients tapered increased from 24 in 2019 to 51 in 2021; tapering failed in 7/116 (6%); estimated saving up to £170,000 per annum
audits.c: EHR records flagged to prompt shared decision-making discussion at routine appointments

audits.t: P020 Audit of bosentan use in Rapid Access to Digital Ulcer Clinic (RADUC) in systemic sclerosis: a single-centre experience
audits.tp: Digital ulcer treatment in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: NHS England clinical commissioning policy for sildenafil and bosentan in SSc digital ulceration (bosentan for severe vasculopathy or ≥3 digital ulcers; oral agents before IV prostanoids)
audits.f: All 21 had severe/≥3 digital ulcers; 20/21 started bosentan after inadequate response or intolerance to both sildenafil and iloprost. At 6 months (11/21), total ulcers fell from 5±2.2 to 2.7±2.2 (p < 0.05); 8/11 (72.7%) had fewer ulcers.

audits.t: P023 National care of patients with Polymyalgia Rheumatica: Audit of steroid usage from UK GP data - a cause for concern?
audits.st: BSR PMR guidelines: glucocorticoids for one to two years with taper; cumulative thresholds 0-6 months >2100mg, 7-12 months >1400mg, 13-18 and 19-24 months >910mg
audits.f: A considerable number of patients were prescribed glucocorticoids above recommended levels (figures given in a table not supplied).

audits.t: P110 Challenges of meeting NICE guidance for rheumatoid arthritis in the modern era: a service audit
audits.st: NICE NG100 rheumatoid arthritis annual review standards
audits.f: DAS28 documented 74.4% (253/340); erosions 42% (144/340); blood pressure 33% (113/340); mental health screen 7.9% (27/340); neck pain 14%; respiratory 21%; eye 21%; bone health 27.9% (95/340); AHP referral considered 38%; HAQ 22%.
audits.c: Planned digital RA annual review tool incorporating PROMs.

audits.t: P154 Real-world audit of patients with idiopathic inflammatory myositis-related interstitial lung disease in a European population
audits.tp: Interstitial lung disease screening in myositis
