audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines for managing idiopathic inflammatory myositis (no target stated)
audits.f: 65% (46/70) of adult IIM patients screened for pulmonary involvement. 31% (22/70) had IIM-ILD; 21/22 had PFTs; 76.2% (16/22) had ILD changes on imaging.

audits.t: E002 Management of adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in 2021: a multi-centre audit within Wales as part of an ongoing quality improvement exercise
audits.st: 2018 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for the management of adults with SLE
audits.f: No widespread significant changes in care compared with 2019; blood pressure and urinalysis not consistently measured; 48% of consultations were virtual.

audits.t: E005 An audit of demographics, symptoms & investigations: Part of the survey of GCA in the SEHSCT during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All had ESR and CRP; ANCA in 43 (3 positive); CT brain in 40; TA ultrasound once; CT-PET in 6; 70 TAB with 12 positive and 4 suggestive.
audits.c: Rapid access GCA pathway being designed

audits.t: E006 An audit showing the successful operation of a nurse-led gout clinic during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: Clinic protocol based on BSR guidance; serum urate <360 µmol/L (<300 µmol/L with erosions or tophi)
audits.f: Mean serum urate 509 µmol/L at referral and 322 µmol/L at discharge; all offered and took prophylaxis (85.8% for 3–6 months); 95% had ≤2 flares; no ED attendances for gout.

audits.t: P004 Empowering the reproductive choices of patients with rheumatic disease: using the BSR 2022 pregnancy guidelines audit tool to evaluate pre-conception medication advice
audits.st: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (linked BSR audit tool)
audits.f: Antibody screening 70%; asked about wish to conceive 26%; contraception asked in 21% of those not wishing to conceive; referred to obstetric-rheumatology clinic 17%; appropriate pre-pregnancy drug counselling 22.8% of 35 on medication; none signposted to further information.

audits.t: P008 High response rate to Janus Kinase inhibitors after multiple biologic drug failures, across disease indications, in a District General Hospital: results from an audit of the prescribing, safety and efficacy of Janus Kinase inhibitor
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Side-effect discussion documented at baseline in <10%; 2% MACE and 3% herpes zoster; 36% discontinued; remission or significant reduction in disease activity in 64%.
audits.c: Recommended better patient education before starting treatment.

audits.t: P010 To establish compliance with British Society for paediatric and adolescent rheumatology (BSPAR) and the Royal College of Ophthalmology (RCOphth) guidelines for screening for uveitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) at a District General Hospital: a retrospective audit
audits.tp: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.st: BSPAR/RCOphth 2006 uveitis screening guidelines
audits.f: Initial screen within 6 weeks 40/42 (95%); symptomatic seen within 1 week 4/13 (30%); screening after stopping DMARDs 9/13 (70%); ongoing screening 15/20 (75%).

audits.t: P081 Out-patient management of gout in secondary care: Results from the North West regional audit
audits.st: NICE, EULAR, BSR and MHRA gout guidelines
audits.f: Treat-to-target levels agreed in 49 (57%); cardiovascular risk tool used in 3 (3%); no patient with major cardiovascular disease on febuxostat; 16 (17%) no planned follow-up; 18 (78%) new patients appropriately referred; 15 (75%) started on first-line ULT; 11 (79%) allopurinol started at low dose; 10 (67%) given colchicine prophylaxis.

audits.t: E009 An audit looking into bisphosphonate co-prescription and compliance in patients with giant cell arteritis
audits.st: BSR giant cell arteritis guideline: consider pharmacological bone protection at presentation
audits.f: Bisphosphonate consideration documented at diagnosis in 96% overall (TOC 94%, MTX 91%, MONO 100%); compliance for recommended duration 88% overall

audits.t: E016 An audit on patient initiated follow up in rheumatology in Manchester Royal Infirmary
audits.st: NHS England PIFU guidance: stable inflammatory arthritis, face-to-face review within 2–4 weeks of contact, around 5% of patients on PIFU
audits.f: Only 22 (17%) met NHS England criteria; 0% seen within the recommended time after contact; 1.5% of department patients on PIFU (target 5%).

audits.t: E019 Management of idiopathic inflammatory myositis - a Northamptonshire audit of British Society for Rheumatology guidelines
audits.st: BSR guideline on idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (March 2022), 26 recommendations
audits.f: Steroids tapered 100%; DMARDs for muscle inflammation 91%; treatment for active skin disease 100%; ILD screening 100%; therapist-led exercise for active muscle disease 56%; psychological well-being formally considered 45%.

audits.t: E021 Patient initiated follow-up long term condition pathway audit
audits.st: Departmental PIFU-LTC standard operating procedure based on GIRFT guidance (entry and exclusion criteria, documentation standards, response to contacts)
audits.f: 81% (n = 42) met diagnostic entry criteria; 92% joined ≥12 months after diagnosis; 40% (n = 21) had no record of an information leaflet; 33% (n = 17) had no documented flare plan; contact to telephone review 1-3 days.

audits.t: E022 Audit on the baricitinib dose in elderly and patients with chronic kidney disease among a cohort of rheumatoid arthritis patients
audits.st: NICE guidance (2 mg daily if 75 years or older) and BNF (avoid if creatinine clearance <30 ml/min; reduce dose if 30–60 ml/min)
audits.f: Of 13 aged 75+ still on baricitinib, 10 on 2 mg and 3 on 4 mg; 4 of 7 started after 75 began on 4 mg; 14 of 16 with creatinine clearance 30–60 ml/min were at some point on 4 mg, 6 still on 4 mg

audits.t: OA13 Preliminary results from the National Axial Spondyloarthritis Society time to diagnosis audit: two years on
audits.tp: Time to diagnosis in axial spondyloarthritis
audits.st: NASS 'Act on Axial SpA' campaign target to reduce time to diagnosis to 12 months
audits.f: Mean total time to diagnosis 8 years (SD 8.91); median 4.7 years (IQR 9.25).

audits.t: P016 Audit on the use of avacopan in ANCA-associated vasculitis at a tertiary rheumatology centre
audits.tp: Glucocorticoid tapering with avacopan in ANCA vasculitis
audits.st: PEXIVAS glucocorticoid tapering protocol and local guideline (twice the PEXIVAS tapering rate)
audits.f: 50% tapered glucocorticoids in line with PEXIVAS; none followed the accelerated local guideline rate.

audits.t: P026 Enhancing care for giant cell arteritis: a closed-loop audit on adherence to Chelsea and Westminster Trust pathway guidelines
audits.st: Ambulatory Care Giant Cell Arteritis Fast Track Pathway Guidelines (Chelsea and Westminster Trust)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff education on the GCA pathway, results presented at trust ambulatory emergency care governance meeting, and streamlined documentation
audits.r2: GCA probability score calculated in 69% (21% improvement); TAUS within 72 h 85% (9% improvement); appropriate steroid dose 100% (29% improvement); appropriate bone protection 46% (41% increase).

audits.t: P128 Implications of newly established malignancy screening guidelines for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: a multi-centre, international evaluation of clinical and economic impact by the Myositis Audit and Research Collaborative group
audits.st: IMACS guidelines for malignancy screening in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
audits.f: Full IMACS screening panel received by 7.5% of high-risk, 6.6% of intermediate-risk and 27.5% of standard-risk patients; 9.1% of high-risk patients had annual screening for 3 years as recommended.
audits.co: Multinational (Australia, Brazil, Hong Kong and others)

audits.t: E012 Giant cell arteritis: single-centre, four-year audit of baseline and follow up glycaemic assessment in patients on corticosteroid treatment
audits.tp: Glycaemic monitoring on glucocorticoids in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: BSR GCA guideline: baseline HbA1c within two weeks of steroid start; wean steroids within 18 months
audits.f: Baseline HbA1c 32 (69.57%); HbA1c at least 3 months after starting steroids 36 (78.26%); both baseline and follow-up by rheumatology 17/46 (36.96%); steroids weaned within 18 months 31 (67.39%).

audits.t: E014 Audit on outpatient referrals done by primary care providers to the Rheumatology assessment at Airedale Hospital NHS Trust: are the new clinical prioritisation criteria required?
audits.st: GIRFT (Getting It Right First Time) guidance on rheumatology referrals
audits.f: 134 of 674 referrals rejected; 101/134 (75.3%) rejected as more appropriate for MSK/pain services or atypical for RMD; 52/134 (37.9%) advised further assessment or investigations in primary care.

audits.t: Current UK practice in pulmonary screening in paediatric connective tissue disease: UK multi-centre audit and proposed standards
audits.tp: Pulmonary screening in paediatric connective tissue disease
audits.st: Audit standards derived from national and international guidelines on pulmonary screening in juvenile CTD (proposed standards)
audits.f: Pulmonary involvement identified in 27/68 (39.7%) jSLE, 5/41 (12.2%) jDM, 4/7 (57.1%) jSSc and 3/12 (25.0%) jMCTD; 50% or fewer had regular assessment of pulmonary symptoms and signs during follow-up.

audits.t: OA24 Annual prescribing of biologic agents: a six-month audit of implementation and safety at Guy’s and St Thomas’ Rheumatology
audits.st: BSR guidance (at least 6-monthly review) and a local guideline for annual bDMARD prescribing
audits.f: 233/644 (36.2%) eligible patients switched to annual prescribing; 6/233 (2.6%) flared and 1/233 (0.43%) had a significant blood abnormality; 177 (43.1%) met criteria but were not switched.
audits.c: Local guideline moving suitable patients from 6-monthly to annual bDMARD prescriptions.

audits.t: P001 An audit on the management of Familial Mediterranean Fever in Malta
audits.st: EULAR 2016 recommendations for FMF management
audits.f: Initial follow-up within 6 months 54.1% (33); 3-monthly SAA/CRP with dose escalation 8.3% (2/24); 6-monthly monitoring 31.2% (19); SAA and CK on yearly bloods 20.9% and 12.5%; no 3-monthly SAA/CRP during dose reduction.

audits.t: P039 Audit into multi-disciplinary team care of haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
audits.st: GIRFT guidance on broad MDT input (rheumatology, haematology, infectious diseases, critical care) and local HLH guidelines
audits.f: MDT discussion in 26/34; 1/26 (4%) met guideline standards; 13/26 (50%) single-specialty discussions; median 10 days admission to MDT, 19/26 (73%) within 14 days.

audits.t: P040 An Audit of Menopause Assessment and Hormone Replacement Therapy Use in Rheumatology Patients
audits.tp: Menopause and HRT documentation in rheumatology
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Menopause status documented in 10/90 (11.1%) clinic letters; menopause discussed in 4/16 (25%) new patient appointments; HRT documentation accurate and concordant in 83/90 (92.2%); rheumatological diagnosis accurately coded in primary care record in 68/90 (75.6%).

audits.t: P078 Tertiary care centre audit of measles, mumps, rubella and varicella vaccination in children on immunomodulating therapy
audits.tp: Live vaccination in children on immunosuppression
audits.st: 2017 Public Health England / Green Book guidance supporting MMR and varicella vaccination on methotrexate and case-by-case after MDT assessment
audits.f: 81 vaccinations (38 VZV, 43 MMR) recommended by the vaccine MDT; 34/81 (42%) administered (20/38 VZV and 14/43 MMR).
audits.c: Recommended strengthening follow-up pathways, standardising communication and reinforcing primary care engagement.

audits.t: P099 National audit of England shows suboptimal compliance with ophthalmology recommendations for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy screening
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists guideline: annual retinopathy screening after 5 years of HCQ, or after 1 year if tamoxifen, eGFR <60 or dose >5 mg/kg/day
audits.f: Of 13,298 meeting screening criteria, 2,808 (21.1%) seen in ophthalmology in the previous 365 days; range 0% to 45.9% by ICB.

audits.t: P100 Ethnic disparities in NICE rheumatoid arthritis quality standard 33 attainment: data from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE RA quality standard 33: QS1 referral within 3 working days of primary care presentation; QS2 conventional DMARD within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: QEHB QS1: 79% (115/146) White vs 21% (31/146) BAME referred within 3 days; QS2: 26.5% (27/102) BAME vs 73.5% (75/102) White. Nationally QS1 43% (12,561/29,417) White vs 47% (2,333/4,964) BAME; QS2 60% (723/1,204) BAME vs 57% (4,919/8,695) White.

audits.t: P101 Sustaining rehabilitation gains in rheumatoid arthritis: a six-month functional status audit guided by EULAR treat-to-target standards
audits.tp: Functional status follow-up after rheumatoid arthritis rehabilitation
audits.st: EULAR treat-to-target: disease activity and functional status monitored every six months
audits.f: 33/36 (92%) completed six-month functional follow-up; median EQ-5D 46 at admission, 65 at discharge, 62.5 at six months; median self-efficacy 3.4, 7.0 and 5.5.

audits.t: P141 Assessing the appropriateness and outcomes of antinuclear antibody testing requests in primary care: a retrospective audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 605 (19.67%) positive; 190 (31.57%) of positives referred; new CTD diagnosed in 38 patients; 314 (51.9%) of positives were 1/80 homogeneous.
audits.c: Recommended clearer testing guidelines and targeted education for primary care clinicians.

audits.t: P189 Giant cell arteritis: audit of a fast-track assessment pathway including the use of positron emission tomography-computed tomography as an early diagnostic tool
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology audit tool standards for suspected GCA
audits.f: All reviewed within 3 days (95% by next day); all started on corticosteroids with FBC and ESR; all with visual symptoms given high-dose steroids and ophthalmology review (60% same day); 95% had baseline glucose, 75% vitamin D checked, 70% DEXA; of confirmed GCA, 54% had documented written information and 77% safety-netting advice.

audits.t: E019 Rheum for Improvement: an audit of the electronic referral system and referral quality of the rheumatology department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde from 7th August 2024-31st October 2024
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30.89% lacked examination findings; 69.10% no further investigations documented beyond haematological/radiological; 53.65% had no differential diagnosis documented.

audits.t: E056 Treat-to-target gout management: a full cycle audit of allopurinol therapy in primary care
audits.st: NICE gout guideline: titrate allopurinol to serum urate below 360 µmol/L with annual monitoring
audits.f: 68/141 had a urate level in the past 12 months; of these 40 (58.8%) had urate below 360 µmol/L or allopurinol increased. 6 had never had a urate level on EMIS.
audits.c: Clinician education on NICE treat-to-target guidance
audits.r2: 65/142 had a yearly urate; 57 (87.7%) managed in line with NICE. Six-fold decrease in patients with no urate ever recorded.

audits.t: E136 MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis: an audit against the ASAS guidance
audits.tp: MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis
audits.st: ASAS guidance on requesting and reporting MRI in suspected axial spondyloarthritis
audits.f: Requests: age in 11 (11.4%), sex in 6 (3.8%), HLA-B27 in 35 (22.2%), back pain duration in 30 (18.9%), suspected diagnosis in 149 (94.3%). Reports: bone marrow oedema mentioned in 128 (81.0%), fat metaplasia in 10 (6.3%), statement on whether 'in keeping with axSpA' in 98 (62.0%).

audits.t: E137 Obesity, comorbidity burden and weight management discussions in psoriatic arthritis patients referred for occupational therapy: a service audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean BMI 33.5 kg/m²; 38% BMI >35; only around half of letters for BMI >30 recorded weight, and none discussed weight management plans or referrals.
audits.c: Recommended training for rheumatology staff on raising weight and better BMI recording.

audits.t: E158 A closed cycle audit of assessment of suspected giant cell arteritis at North Middlesex University Hospital
audits.st: BSR and GIRFT guidelines for GCA assessment and management
audits.f: Steroids 34%; rheumatology referral 55%; temporal artery ultrasound 15%; CRP 92%; median time to eye clinic 2 days.
audits.c: Trust SDEC GCA pathway guideline, streamlined temporal artery ultrasound order on IT system, local teaching, pathway poster in clinic rooms and Southend GCA probability score.
audits.r2: Steroids 54%; rheumatology referral 77%; temporal artery ultrasound 77% (p < 0.001); CRP 100%; median time to eye clinic 1 day.

audits.t: P18 Audit on pre-methotrexate screening in a paediatric rheumatology centre
audits.st: BSPAR consensus guidance: check varicella immunity before methotrexate and immunise if non-immune; consider measles status and TB testing in high-risk patients
audits.f: Varicella status checked before methotrexate in 91 (89%), after starting in 7 and not checked in 4; 20 non-immune, of whom 16 were vaccinated; measles serology checked in 57 (31 before methotrexate); TB Quantiferon checked in 35 before and 39 after starting.

audits.t: P32 Kawasaki disease: learning points from 6 years of audit data from a large university teaching hospital
audits.st: RCPCH guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: P57 Ensuring safe and efficient prescribing: an audit of external prescription requests from the National Centre of Paediatric Rheumatology, Ireland
audits.tp: External prescription requests between clinic visits
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Parents gave a dose in 10/36 requests; charts available for 27; 21 had blood tests on hospital database in the last 3 months; 27 had clinic appointments in the preceding 6 months.
audits.c: Planned: prescription request form for parents detailing dose, route and latest blood results

audits.t: P58 A re-audit on the adherence to blood monitoring guidelines in paediatric rheumatology patients on methotrexate, etanercept and adalimumab after the introduction of a blood clerk in the team
audits.st: Blood monitoring guidelines for methotrexate, etanercept and adalimumab: starters must meet 6 criteria (frequency, FBC, LFTs, renal function, varicella and measles immunity); maintenance patients 4 criteria
audits.f: Over 60% of patients on methotrexate not monitored according to guidelines.
audits.c: A blood clerk was introduced to the team to chase patients for blood results.
audits.r2: 76/216 (35%) appropriately monitored, similar to the previous audit. Main failure was delayed blood timing (50% methotrexate, 65% maintenance biologics); missing varicella/measles immunity documentation in 42% of biologic starters.

audits.t:
Transfusion in critical care – a
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    regional audit of current practice
audits.st: UK best practice: restrictive transfusion threshold of haemoglobin below 70 g/l in stable non-bleeding patients
audits.f: Median pre-transfusion Hb 73 (68-77 [53-106]) g/l; only 34% of episodes used a threshold below 70 g/l.

audits.t: Five‐year audit of adherence to an anaesthesia pre‐induction checklist
audits.st: Institutional airway (anaesthesia pre-induction) checklist; primary outcome proportion of wholly performed checklists
audits.f: Checklist completed in 57.3% overall; adherence improved from 48.3% in the first year to 66.7% by the fifth year (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Peri‐operative decisions about cardiopulmonary resuscitation among adults as reported to the 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists
audits.st: Current guidance: CPR should usually be attempted for cardiac arrest during anaesthesia and pre-existing DNACPR recommendations should be suspended
audits.f: 595 (3%) of 20,717 adults had a pre-operative DNACPR recommendation, of which 175 (29%) were suspended. Of 881 peri-operative cardiac arrests, 54 (6%) had a pre-operative DNACPR; 25 (46%) of these were formally suspended.

audits.st: Association of Anaesthetists' 2020 consensus guideline on peri-operative glucocorticoid management
audits.f: Of 219 on ≥5 mg prednisolone equivalents, 67 (31%) pre-operatively and 43 (20%) postoperatively supplemented according to guideline; overall compliance 19/219 (9%); 30/219 (14%) no supplementation; 28/58 (48%) on <5 mg received inappropriate supplementation.

audits.t:
Time critical diagnoses and transfers of patients with acute type A aortic dissection in the
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    : national audit of current practice*
audits.tp: Type A aortic dissection diagnosis and transfer times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median symptom onset to ED arrival 2.3 h (IQR 1.4–4.7); median ED arrival to start of surgery 9.5 h (IQR 6.1–18.2); delays in diagnosis and transfer in 158 (47.3%); initial misdiagnosis in 52 (15.6%).

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING
audits.st: Local paediatric vancomycin guideline: 100% correct starting dose, 90% levels at correct time, 80% third-dose troughs in range (10–15 mg/L), 90% appropriate action for out-of-range levels
audits.f: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at the correct time; 33% of initial levels in range (a further 31% after dose change); 93% appropriate actions; three of six standards met.
audits.c: Suggested changing dosing frequency to four times a day or continuous infusion.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE PAIN IN CHILDREN
audits.st: Locally developed MDT standards: 80% of severe pain scores to get analgesia within 20 minutes and mild/moderate within 30 minutes with timely reassessment; 80% on regular analgesia to have pain scored at least 4-hourly; 90% on strong opioids co-prescribed naloxone
audits.f: Analgesia given in the same hour for 58% (34/59) severe and 30% (28/92) mild/moderate pain scores; pain reassessed within 60 minutes after 52% (37/71) and 34% (31/92) of administrations; 15/18 (83%) on regular analgesia assessed at least 4-hourly; of 11 on strong opioids 45% had no naloxone, 27% fully prescribed and 27% for respiratory depression only.
audits.c: Planned: specific timing guidance added to the revised guideline, with medical and nursing training sessions.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE PAEDIATRIC EMPIRIC ANTI-INFECTIVE GUIDELINES AND ANTI-INFECTIVE DRUG DOSE TABLE FOR CHILDREN
audits.st: 90% adherence to empirical anti-infective guidelines; 90% indication recorded; 90% duration or review date recorded; 95% initial doses per children's dose table
audits.f: Guideline adherence 40/41 (98%); indication recorded 40/42 (95%); duration or review date recorded 26/42 (62%); initial doses per dose table 67/69 (97%).

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF WHETHER PRESCRIBED DOSES ARE MEASURABLE ON THE GRADUATIONS OF ONE ORAL SYRINGE
audits.tp: Measurable oral liquid doses in children
audits.st: Local dispensing standard: prescribed volumes measurable on the printed graduations of one oral syringe
audits.f: Electronic prescriptions: 61/257 (24%) not measurable; paper charts: 57/303 (19%) not measurable (p=0.19). 77 of 457 liquid doses needed up to 4% adjustment and 10 up to 9%; 19/560 (3.4%) needed measuring to two decimal places.
audits.c: Recommended dose rounding at prescribing and adding liquid strength information to local guidelines.

audits.t: AUDIT OF OXYGEN PRESCRIBING IN A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL.
audits.st: Local guidelines: all patients receiving oxygen have a prescription with target saturations, device and nurse signature within 12 hrs; target 100%
audits.f: 0/14 had an oxygen prescription.
audits.c: New paediatric medication chart with oxygen section and training package.
audits.r2: 4/18 (22%) had a prescription, all medical patients; target saturation 100%, device 25%, nurse signature 100%.

audits.t: AUDIT OF PARACETAMOL PRESCRIPTIONS IN PAEDIATRIC SURGICAL PATIENTS
audits.st: Local 2012 perioperative pain guideline (dosing by ideal body weight) and BNFC; 100% compliance with weight and height documentation, ideal-weight dosing, separate IV prescribing and 48-hour IV-to-oral review
audits.f: Weight recorded on 84% of inpatient and 94% of discharge prescriptions; height never documented; IV/PO prescribed together in 32 inpatients; 20 of 52 on IV paracetamol not reviewed at 48 hours (only 3 appropriate).
audits.c: Feedback led to amended local guidelines in 2015 (dosing by lean body mass and ideal weight; maximum 75 mg/kg/day).

audits.t: THE DEVELOPMENT OF A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT SYSTEM TO MONITOR, ASSESS AND FEEDBACK PRESCRIBING ERRORS IN PAEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE.
audits.st: Local Zero Tolerance prescribing standards
audits.f: Unit mean error rate 12.5%.
audits.c: Automated individual feedback forms for prescribers, posters and discussion at clinical governance meetings.

audits.t: CHILDREN'S WARFARIN CLINIC-AN AUDIT OF THE NEW PHARMACIST-LED TELEPHONE SERVICE BASED ON A UNIQUE COMPUTERISED SYSTEM COMPARED TO THE WARD BASED PAPER SYSTEM
audits.st: NPSA safety standards for warfarin dosing
audits.f: Original ward-based paper system: 44 patients, 1289 INRs; 11 patients (25%) lost to follow-up.
audits.c: Pharmacist-led telephone warfarin service using a computerised documentation system.
audits.r2: Pharmacist-led service: 73 patients, 1547 INRs; fully compliant with NPSA standards; none lost to follow-up; safety indicators not significantly different.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES.
audits.st: Desired therapeutic vancomycin plasma concentration 15-25 mg/L
audits.f: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.
audits.c: Switch to continuous intravenous infusion regimen (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and CGA).
audits.r2: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (first 60.8%, second 60%, subsequent 65.6%); 71.3% allowing 10% variability.

audits.t: AN AUDIT TO ASSESS THE TIMINGS OF TTAS AND INPATIENT ORDERS IN PAEDIATRICS; FROM WRITING, TO SCREENING, TO DISPENSING, AND TO LEAVING DISPENSARY.
audits.st: Trust KPI: 85% of urgent items (TTAs) dispensed within 1 hour; 85% of non-urgent items within 3 hrs
audits.f: TTAs averaged 2 hrs from logging in to checking (n=12, standard 1 hour); inpatient orders averaged 5 hrs 51 minutes to leave dispensary (n=22, standard 3 hrs).

audits.t: P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units
audits.st: Local neonatal vancomycin guideline; 100% adherence
audits.f: Correct initial dose 28/28 (100%); level taken at correct time 13/15 (87%); 19/31 levels (62%) within 10–20 mg/L; all 6 levels >20 mg/L had next dose held, but follow-up adjustment often suboptimal; 3 of 4 low levels not acted on.
audits.c: Guideline amended (single safe range 10–20 mg/L, doses adjusted on levels not age) and teaching sessions with worked examples planned for prescribers and nurses.

audits.t: P26 An audit of the use of amikacin for early onset sepsis in premature neonates in an inpatient neonatal unit
audits.st: Trust Neonatal Infection Guideline: 100% adherence to criteria, amikacin 15 mg/kg, level at 24 hours before second dose, further doses only if level <5 mg/L or on pharmacist advice
audits.f: 100% adhered to guideline criteria and 100% prescribed 15 mg/kg; 12 (24%) had no level at 24 hours; of 38 with 24-hour levels only 6 (16%) were <5 mg/L; 17/23 (74%) in range at 36 hours; 2 patients received doses despite levels >5 mg/L.
audits.c: Recommended change from 24-hourly to 36-hourly dosing; re-audit planned in one year.

audits.t: P34 Quality improvement project aimed at reducing gentamicin errors in neonates
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency (NPSA) recommendations on gentamicin
audits.f: 18 gentamicin errors reported; 84% at prescribing and 16% at administration; 67% due to complexity of calculating a 36-hourly dosing interval.
audits.c: PDSA cycles from July 2017: simplified standardised dosing interval, updated local monograph with example prescription, posters in prescribing areas, MDT feedback session, guideline promotion and error monitoring, lower-risk alternative antibiotic in low-risk babies, and gentamicin prescribing exercise at new doctor induction.

audits.t: P37 Audit on the quality of documentation of paediatric prescriptions using electronic prescription charts
audits.st: Legal prescribing requirements (Medicines Act 1968), trust Medicines Management Policy; ten standards based on RCP Generic Medical Record Keeping Standards 2017
audits.f: 100% compliance for most demographics and prescription items and all fluid standards; allergy status 95% (severity 93%); weight 73%; antimicrobial indication 81% and duration 46%.
audits.c: Results presented locally and emailed to staff; recommended e-prescribing training and compulsory weight and allergy entry.

audits.t: P38 An audit to assess influenza vaccination uptake amongst asthmatic children in a city in the northwest of england
audits.tp: Influenza vaccination and asthma prescribing in children
audits.st: BTS/SIGN British guideline on the management of asthma 2016 for prescribing; influenza vaccine uptake
audits.f: 148 (31.2%) had flu vaccination; 194/297 (65.3%) prescriptions followed BTS guidelines.

audits.t: P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation
audits.st: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance
audits.f: Loading, initial continuous dosing and TDM generally in line with local guidelines; 9% of first levels subtherapeutic; of 298 levels 56% therapeutic, 19% supratherapeutic, 25% subtherapeutic

audits.t: P41 An audit of the screening and treatment of uveitis in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (jia) at a paediatric tertiary centre
audits.tp: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.st: BSPAR/RCO uveitis screening guidelines (screen within 6 weeks of referral); NHS England JIA treatment recommendations
audits.f: Referred for screening 50/54 (92.6%); screened 45/50 (90%); screened within 6 weeks of referral 8/45 (17.8%); JIA treatment in line with NHS England 100% of 41 documented.

audits.t: P7 An audit of the management of resuscitation drugs and trolley contents
audits.st: Resuscitation Council (UK) acute care equipment and drug lists (2013) and local Trust trolley content list; daily trolley checks
audits.f: Drug content compliance 50%; oxygen cylinders on trolley 5/29; daily trolley checks 29/32; guidelines present on 31/32 trolleys but needed revision.
audits.c: Trolley content list changed from 250 mL to 500 mL sodium chloride 0.9% bags kept as routine stock, and resuscitation guidelines revised for clearer paediatric dosing.

audits.t: P12 An audit on the use and monitoring of azathioprine (aza) in a paediatric gastroenterology centre. could nhs england via specialist commissioning rules (nhs-e-spr) be affecting quality of care?
audits.st: BSPGHAN guidelines: eleven azathioprine monitoring points (clinic attendance, height, weight, baseline VZV status, TPMT, and FBC, U&Es, amylase, CRP and LFT monitoring)
audits.f: Only 16 patients (19%) met all eleven points; 27 (24.5%) fully compliant with blood monitoring frequency; TPMT measured in 104 (97%) but late in 48 (46%); weight and height not documented in 31 (28%) and 47 (43%); baseline VZV not checked in 23 (21%).
audits.c: Suggested shared-care guidelines, order sets with all parameters at diagnosis and a tick-box monitoring proforma for clinic.

audits.t: P15 Melatonin prescribing audit
audits.st: Regular clinic review of melatonin treatment (efficacy, dose, duration)
audits.f: 238 (59%) had melatonin reviewed at follow-up; 81 (20%) attended clinic without documented review; 42 (10%) on long-term melatonin not seen for over a year; 39 (10%) newly started not followed up.

audits.t: P16 An audit of domperidone prescribing in children
audits.st: MHRA May 2014 drug safety update and NPPG May 2015 statement on domperidone (dose, duration, indication, ECG monitoring in high risk, non-pharmacological trial in GORD)
audits.f: Dose 43/50 (86%); duration 6/50 (12%); indication 9/50 (18%); ECG monitoring in high risk 12/33 (36%); non-pharmacological trial in GORD 11/17 (64%).
audits.c: National MHRA and NPPG alerts on domperidone.
audits.r2: Dose 10/10 (100%); duration 1/10 (10%); indication 1/10 (10%); ECG monitoring 0/4 (0%); non-pharmacological trial 2/3 (66%).

audits.t: P17 An audit of enoxaparin prescribing and monitoring in child health
audits.tp: Enoxaparin prescribing and anti-Xa monitoring in children
audits.st: BNFc dosing and anti-Xa monitoring
audits.f: 71% (n=17) of therapeutic prescriptions dosed per BNFc; 35% had anti-Xa within 36 hours; 71% of levels taken 4–6 hours post dose; 82% (n=11) out-of-range levels led to dose change, 56% (n=9) rechecked within 24 hours; 76% (n=25) prophylactic prescriptions per BNFc.

audits.t: P39 Start smart: improving the quality of empiric antimicrobial prescribing at a tertiary paediatric hospital
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines: ≥90% of children admitted via ED and started on antibiotics have a documented indication and guideline-compliant choice
audits.f: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance median 30%.
audits.c: Weekly audit feedback with run charts, antibiotic discussion at Monday handover, prescriber spot quiz, updated guidelines and prescribing app, ID badge guideline cards, and reminders at point of prescribing in ED.
audits.r2: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance 100% consistently.

audits.t: Home use of breast milk fortifier to promote postdischarge growth and breast feeding in preterm infants: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Home breast milk fortifier after preterm discharge
audits.st: Use of breast milk fortifier after discharge until 48 weeks' gestational age
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Electronic patient information sheet promoting home breast milk fortifier, developed over four PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Improved growth at discharge (cSDS weight -0.7, head circumference 0.4, length -0.8) and at 1 year (weight 0.9, length 0.8) compared with baseline.

audits.t: P003 Intermittent vancomycin in paediatrics: implementation and audit of a new guideline
audits.st: Trust intermittent IV vancomycin guideline (2016) with loading dose and increased dose and frequency versus BNFC
audits.f: Pre-implementation audit: 7% of levels in therapeutic range at 48 hours; lack of support for appropriate dosing and monitoring.
audits.c: New trust guideline for intermittent IV vancomycin (loading dose, higher dose and frequency) with pharmacist intervention.
audits.r2: Loading dose used appropriately in 83%; levels at correct times in 90%; 40% in range at 48 hours; 100% reviewed at 48 hours; out-of-range levels reviewed per guideline in 40%, rising to 80% with pharmacist intervention.

audits.t: P014 An audit assessing the prescribing of naloxone in paediatric patients
audits.st: Local Multidisciplinary Guidelines for Acute Pain Management in Children and Young People: all patients on opioids have PRN naloxone with correct directions
audits.f: Naloxone prescribed in 17% (7/41); on PRN section 100% (7/7); correct directions 86% (6/7).
audits.c: Planned: presentation at paediatric and surgical paediatric audit meetings to educate prescribers.

audits.t: P020 Vitamin supplementation survey: an audit of the usage of vitamin D supplementation in paediatric patients, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers
audits.tp: Vitamin D supplementation in children and pregnancy
audits.st: SACN (2016) vitamin D recommendations and local guidelines
audits.f: Under 30% of parents (16/54) received advice on childhood vitamin supplementation; 24.5% of children (25/102) received supplementation. 77% (30/39) of pregnant/breastfeeding mothers received advice but only 54% (21) took supplements.

audits.t: P029 Audit of aciclovir prescribing to assess whether changing the order of drop down box options in an electronic prescribing system can reduce prescribing errors
audits.st: Aciclovir dosing per BNF for Children and trust empirical antibiotic guidelines
audits.f: 26% (9/35) of aciclovir doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option chosen in 78% (7/9) of incorrect prescriptions.
audits.c: Aciclovir drop-down options in the electronic prescribing system reordered so the most frequently used option appeared first (from 01/02/17).
audits.r2: 17% (5/30) of doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option in 0% (0/5) of incorrect prescriptions.

audits.t: Prediagnosis pathway benchmarking audit in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy
audits.st: Benchmark criteria from a prior single-centre UK audit of 20 patients with no DMD family history
audits.f: Mean age at definitive diagnosis 53.9±29.7 months, at first HCP engagement 49.9±28.9 months, at first symptoms 36.4±26.8 months; presentational delay 21.1 (±21.1) months; time to diagnosis 4.6 (±7.9) months; symptoms to diagnosis 24.2±20.9 months.

audits.t: P05 An audit of proton pump inhibitor prescribing, in adherence with the trust’s guidance, in gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
audits.tp: Proton pump inhibitor prescribing in children
audits.st: Trust guidance: lansoprazole capsules/orodispersible tablets first line; three standards (appropriate PPI, documented indication, appropriate dose)
audits.f: Appropriate PPI 76%; documented indication 88%; appropriate dose 100%. Infants and toddlers had the lowest appropriate PPI choice (63%).
audits.c: Recommended clinicians monitor prescribing and switch omeprazole suspension to lansoprazole where appropriate.

audits.t: P10 An audit to assess the prescribing of analgesia in children who present with pain crisis due to Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)
audits.tp: Analgesia in sickle cell pain crisis
audits.st: 100% prescribed regular paracetamol and NSAIDs unless contraindicated (NICE CG143, BCSH); 100% prescribed appropriate doses by weight and age per local policy
audits.f: 45% (95% CI 31.9%–58.1%) prescribed regular analgesia; 78% (95% CI 67.9%–88.9%) prescribed appropriate doses. Neither standard met.
audits.c: Recommended education and training, an integrated care pathway booklet and a compulsory weight field on electronic prescribing.

audits.t: P32 An audit to assess the suitability of patients at a tertiary/quaternary paediatric hospital to switch from intravenous (IV) to oral (PO) antimicrobial therapy
audits.st: PHE Start Smart then Focus: blood culture before therapy, senior antimicrobial review at 48–72 hours, and IV to oral switch when set clinical criteria are met
audits.f: 100% had blood cultures within 72 hours of starting therapy; 82% had senior review at 48–72 hours; 46% eligible to switch to oral at 72 hours, of whom 33% were switched.
audits.c: Recommended an IV to oral switch guideline, education of pharmacists and nurses, and exploring hard stops on IV antimicrobials in the electronic system.

audits.t: P34 An audit of the testing and documentation of genetic mutation m1555a>g and aminoglycoside prescribing
audits.st: 100% of positive m.1555A>G results recorded on prescribing record; 100% tested before aminoglycoside; 100% of positives not given an aminoglycoside
audits.f: 12 (0.31%) tested positive; 100% had the result recorded as an aminoglycoside allergy on JAC; 5/12 (42%) positives had received aminoglycosides, 1 before testing.

audits.t: P38 An audit of antibiotic use in the treatment of neonatal necrotising enterocolitis (NEC): what do we use and how long for?
audits.st: Local NEC guideline: first-line amoxicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole for up to 10 days
audits.f: Guideline regimen (amoxicillin, gentamicin, metronidazole) used in 1/7; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 4; meropenem and vancomycin in 2. Median course 10 days (range 2 to 16).
audits.c: Results presented to a neonatal surgery quality improvement meeting in January 2019 to highlight the issue to surgical and neonatal teams.
audits.r2: Guideline regimen used in 4/5; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 1. Median course 11 days (range 5 to 12).

audits.t: P48 An audit of compliance of age and critical drug related monitoring criteria/requirements for patients receiving carboplatin doses with therapeutic pharmacokinetic drug monitoring
audits.tp: Carboplatin therapeutic drug monitoring in children
audits.st: Local carboplatin protocol requirements for age criteria, baseline audiology, creatinine clearance and pharmacokinetic monitoring before administration
audits.f: Audiology done in 85.7% (n=6) but at baseline pre-treatment in only 28.6% (n=2); creatinine checked before first course in 71.4%; 20/26 courses (76.9%) had PK monitoring with dose modification as per protocol; 2 (29%) patients did not meet the age criteria for PK monitoring.
audits.c: Recommended information for all practitioners on monitoring requirements and production of an SOP.

audits.t: P49 An audit of baseline vitamin D level tests for newly diagnosed paediatric haematology/oncology patients against trust guidelines
audits.st: Trust guideline for vitamin D deficiency: 100% tested at diagnosis; 100% of results acted on; 100% given appropriate dose
audits.f: 56% tested for vitamin D during admission; 35% of oncology and 83% of haematology patients tested. 6% of haematology and 5% of oncology patients with sufficient levels received treatment not indicated; the 5% of oncology patients with insufficient levels were not treated. Standards not met.

audits.t: P14 Identification of prescribing errors in a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU): an audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 36 pharmacist interventions: 92% per patient and 2.3% per prescription reviewed; 77.5% (n=31) related to intravenous medicines and 52.5% (n=21) to intravenous antibiotics.

audits.t: P38 An audit of excipients of one manufacturer’s unlicensed liquid preparations in a tertiary paediatric hospital
audits.tp: Excipients in unlicensed paediatric liquid medicines
audits.st: European Medicines Agency guidelines on excipients; acceptable daily intake (ADI) of each excipient, assessed with the local New Products Assessment Form
audits.f: 14 unlicensed liquid preparations from one manufacturer reviewed: 4/14 (29%) suitable for all age groups; 4/14 (29%) exceeded the ADI for an excipient in neonates (suitable for all other ages); 5/14 (36%) changed to a more appropriate alternative.

audits.t: P01 Audit of labinic probiotics on the neonatal unit
audits.st: Trust guideline: Labinic probiotic for babies <32 weeks and/or <1.5 kg at birth, at correct dose, given with first feed or within 12 hours of birth
audits.f: 76/76 (100%) eligible babies prescribed and given Labinic; 76/76 (100%) correct dose; only 17/76 (22%) received it within the first 12 hours.

audits.t: P12 An audit of the use of dexmedetomidine for sedation in a tertiary PICU
audits.st: Local PICU analgesia and sedation guideline (2020): approved indication; dose not above 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; duration not above 72 hours
audits.f: 32/33 (97%) prescribed for approved indications; no patient exceeded 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; infusion exceeded 72 hours in 3 (9%).

audits.t: P15 Two-cycle audit on paediatric vancomycin prescribing and monitoring: tertiary centre experience
audits.st: Local trust guideline (2018) for intravenous vancomycin in children
audits.f: Correct frequency 75.9%; correct first dose 58.6%; concentrations taken at correct time 89.7%; therapeutic first concentration 24.1% (70.4% under range); second concentration in range 61.9%.
audits.c: Significant changes to electronic prescription and concentration report templates; guideline recirculated to all paediatric prescribers.
audits.r2: Correct frequency 92.6%; correct first dose 71.4%; concentrations taken at correct time 96.2%; therapeutic first concentration 19.2% (65.4% under range); second concentration in range 57.9%.

audits.t: P16 Audit on outsourcing investigational medicinal product (IMP) production
audits.st: IMP arrival at the clinical trials unit by 1300h (later arrival defined as delayed treatment)
audits.f: Manufacturing unit 1: 33 items, 71.86% late. Manufacturing unit 2: 23 items, 30% late (mostly due to late prescribing at site).
audits.c: Recommended agreed KPIs with third-party suppliers, scoping local aseptic manufacture, and timely prescribing.

audits.t: P24 Compliance audit of ethanol linelocks for prophylaxis and treatment of central line infections
audits.tp: Ethanol line lock prescribing and documentation
audits.st: Trust paediatric ethanol line lock guideline (volume, concentration, indication, review, duration and consent documentation)
audits.f: 98% prescribed accurately per guideline; only 28% had documented indication, review and duration; 0 had consent documented.
audits.c: Change to the electronic prescribing order suggested to aid documentation.

audits.t: P28 An audit of liver function testing in paediatric patients newly started on Kaftrio®
audits.tp: Liver function monitoring on CFTR modulators
audits.st: Local trust guideline, SmPC and MHRA Drug Safety Update: baseline LFTs, then every 3 months in the first year; defined actions for raised ALT/AST
audits.f: Baseline LFTs 30/31 (97%); LFTs at 3 months 10/31 (32%) (15 too early, 6 late); 0 patients had four sets at correct 3-monthly intervals; 4 (13%) had abnormal LFTs, 50% of which were acted on per guidelines.

audits.t: P36 An audit of standardised (NEON) PN use in a tertiary NICU
audits.st: NICE NG154 and local guidelines on indications and timing of standardised (NEON) PN (within 6 hours of life if <31+0 weeks) and on electrolyte and glucose corrections
audits.f: 11/11 correct indication; PN on time in 2/5 babies <31+0 weeks and 11/11 for other indications; electrolyte or glucose corrections per guideline 1/3; reasons for switching or stopping documented 11/11.

audits.t: P42 An audit to assess prescribing of paediatric CD TTOs
audits.st: Legally and clinically correct CD TTO prescriptions on the CD TTO template
audits.f: 67% of prescribers failed the CD TTO test question, mostly dose and frequency errors; 50% of live CD TTOs (two audited) not on the template; average 40 minutes to triage one CD TTO.
audits.c: Recommended awareness of template location, teaching sessions, adding template to the back of the Child Health chart, and a pocket guide.

audits.t: Use of audit, feedback and education increased guideline implementation in a multidisciplinary stroke unit
audits.st: Australian guideline recommendations for stroke rehabilitation; minimum target of 10% change per practice area
audits.f: Baseline compliance across 27 targeted practice areas (figures not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Four cycles of audit feedback plus education and training for staff.
audits.r2: 20 of 27 targeted areas (74%) met or exceeded the 10% change target; sensation screening +75%, rehabilitation +100%, neglect screening +92%, assessment 100%.

audits.t: Improving adherence to lung cancer guidelines: a quality improvement project that uses chart review, audit and feedback approach
audits.st: Lung cancer guidelines: pathological diagnosis, staging before treatment, tumour board within 30 days, EGFR testing, end-of-life care
audits.f: Histological subtype identified in 94%; tumour board presentation 35%; EGFR testing for non-squamous 77%.
audits.c: Education and discussion with team members about deviations, with annual audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Histological subtype 100%; tumour board presentation 82%; EGFR testing 100%; staging documented in 100%.

audits.t: ENT Quality Improvement Program as a tool to improve the collection of morbidity and mortality data: a multisite audit carried out over 6 months.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 180 case discussions (170 morbidities, 10 mortalities); 133 postoperative complications, post-tonsillectomy 62/133 (47%) and post-thyroid 19/133 (14%); 66% low grade
audits.c: Standardised ENT Quality Improvement Program data collection tool

audits.t: Introduction of an electronic patient record (EPR) improves operation note documentation: the results of a closed loop audit and proposal of a team-based approach to documentation.
audits.st: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014: 19 operation note items
audits.f: 0 of 19 items had 100% compliance before EPR
audits.c: Introduction of an electronic patient record; results presented at local governance meeting
audits.r2: Compliance improved by almost 19% (p=0.0003) between periods 1 and 5; 11 of 19 items (57.9%) reached 100% compliance post-EPR

audits.t: Wessex Acute Frailty Audit: applying quality improvement methodology to design and implement a regional frailty audit using a collaborative, multiprofessional approach
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Three themes: lack of frailty awareness and training outside older people's medicine, and significant variability in frailty identification and comprehensive geriatric assessment (no figures given).

audits.t: Improving intravenous-to-oral antibiotic switch in children: a team-based audit and implementation approach.
audits.st: Evidence-based guideline eligibility criteria for switch within 24 hours
audits.f: 32/50 (64%) switched within 24 hours of eligibility; median time to switch 15 hours 42 min.
audits.c: Guideline launch with team-based education, audit and feedback.
audits.r2: 203/249 (82%) switched within 24 hours (p=0.006); median time to switch 4 hours 20 min (p=0.0006).

audits.t: Using a comprehensive audit to identify local context prior to care bundle design and implementation for inadvertent perioperative hypothermia in colorectal surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Observations of four patient journeys, interviews with 21 staff and clinical data identified specific local warming practices to address in a care bundle.

audits.t: Doing today’s work today: real-time data recording and rolling audit in an IVF clinic
audits.st: Local project targets for total cycle time and data administration time
audits.f: Average total cycle time for administrative steps around 17 days; data administration time around 30 min per patient.
audits.c: Real-time data entry into a single data system (IDEAS) as part of clinical jobs, over five PDSA cycles plus two sustainability cycles
audits.r2: Total cycle time cut to 0 or 1 days and data administration time to around 18 min; all metrics reliably within targets.

audits.t: Improving surgical wound classification accuracy through education and audit processes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Education and awareness bundle on wound classification plus a formal wound class audit process.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in wound class accuracy and provider compliance reported; no figures given.

audits.t: Improving inpatient hyperglycaemia in non-critically ill adults in resident wards through audit and feedback
audits.st: Inpatient hyperglycaemia guidelines; aim to reduce glucose values above 180 mg/dL by 30%
audits.f: 25.1% of glucose values were above 180 mg/dL.
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles of resident education plus a pharmacy and resident audit and feedback process.
audits.r2: 23.0% of glucose values above 180 mg/dL (p<0.05); 1045 audits of 16 095 accu-checks, mostly compliant with guidelines.

audits.t: Improving appropriate use of intravenous albumin: results of a single-centre audit and multifaceted intervention
audits.st: Evidence-based recommendations for albumin indications
audits.f: Appropriate albumin use by indication 30%; about 800 vials per month.
audits.c: Dissemination of evidence-based recommendations, new electronic order set, education, prescriber interviews and a return policy change to reduce wastage.
audits.r2: Appropriate use 50% (p<0.0001); usage fell to 450 vials per month, mainly less 5% albumin (p<0.0001); less wastage (p=0.017).

audits.t: Patient safety in actioning and communicating blood test results in primary care: a UK wide audit using the Primary care Academic CollaboraTive (PACT).
audits.tp: Blood test result actioning and communication
audits.st: Blood test results filed, actioned and communicated safely
audits.f: Auditors agreed with initial actioning in 89.9% (n=2311); specified actions carried out in 89.7% (1015/1132); no evidence of communication in 47% (n=1210) overall and 30.6% (360/1176) with abnormal results.

audits.t: Exploring the role of audit and feedback cycle in primary healthcare quality improvement
audits.st: Clinical protocols for consultation and management (not specified)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Structured feedback sessions to physicians after on-site and EMR audits.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in consultation skills, history taking, provisional diagnosis and protocol adherence (figures not stated).

audits.t: AUDIT STANDARDS IN PAEDIATRIC SEVERE SEPSIS
audits.tp: Paediatric sepsis management in the emergency department
audits.st: RCEM adult severe sepsis audit standards applied to children (e.g. vital signs within 15 mins 100%, fluid bolus within 1 hour 75%, antibiotics within 1 hour 50%)
audits.f: Vital signs within 15 mins 47%; capillary glucose 84%; IV fluid bolus within 1 hour 42%; lactate 89%; antibiotics within 1 hour 42%; blood cultures before antibiotics 37%. No RCEM standard was met.

audits.t: Impact of a targeted bundle of audit with tailored education and an intubation checklist to improve airway management in the emergency department: an integrated time series analysis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: First-attempt success rate 88.5%; hypoxia 8.3%; hypotension 8.3%; any complication 27.4%.
audits.c: Bundle of monthly audit, monthly airway management education and an airway management checklist.
audits.r2: First-attempt success rate 94.6% (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.14, p=0.014); hypoxia 8.9%; hypotension 7.0%; any complication 23.6%.

audits.t: 042 Scottish code red audit report 2015–2017
audits.tp: Major haemorrhage (Code Red) transfusion in trauma
audits.st: Recommendations of the Scottish Transfusion and Laboratory Support in Trauma (TLST) group from the previous Code Red audit
audits.f: Previous audit: median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 70 minutes; 70% received pre-hospital TXA; survival to discharge 63%.
audits.c: Recommendations from the previous audit adopted to optimise transfusion support in major trauma
audits.r2: 66 activations; 93% received blood components; pre-hospital transfusion in 48 patients (73%), a 300% increase; median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 37 minutes; 78% received pre-hospital TXA; CRC:FFP ratios improved; survival to discharge 66%.

audits.t: 1421 The Scottish Code Red Audit report for the period 1st January 2018 to 31st December 2019 with comparison to previous audit findings of Scottish Code Red practice since 1 June 2013
audits.tp: Major haemorrhage (Code Red) transfusion in trauma
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 56 activations; pre-hospital TXA 70%; ED arrival to CRC transfusion 9 mins; ED arrival to FFP 50 mins; clotting screen order to result 119 mins; survival to discharge 63%.
audits.r2: 96 activations; 77 (93%, n=93) received pre-hospital TXA; median ED arrival to CRC transfusion 4 minutes (IQR 0–17) and to FFP 16 minutes (IQR 5–28); median ED arrival to FBC result 70 mins and clotting 74 mins; 65 (68%) survived to discharge.

audits.t: 170 A closed loop audit on oxygen prescription in the emergency department in Ipswich Hospital
audits.st: BTS guidelines on emergency oxygen (2017): oxygen prescribed with target saturations
audits.f: 14% of patients had target oxygen saturations prescribed.
audits.c: Results and BTS recommendations presented in departmental teaching sessions.
audits.r2: 20% had target oxygen saturations prescribed (p=0.595, not significant).

audits.t: PTU-113 A Regional Audit Of The Management Of Patients With Decompensated Liver Disease
audits.st: NCEPOD 'Measuring the Units' report recommendations on early management of decompensated liver disease in the first 24 h
audits.f: Of 82 with ascites, 62% had a diagnostic tap within 24 h, 21% after 24 h, 17% not at all. Previous alcohol history documented in 43%, current consumption 81%. Of variceal bleeds, 19% did not receive terlipressin and 30% no vitamin K; endoscopy within 12 h 67%, within 24 h 78%. 17% not seen by a consultant within 12 h.
audits.c: Planned: regional 'care bundle' for decompensated liver disease

audits.t: PWE-012 Audit Of Nhs Tayside Colonoscopy Surveillance Programme
audits.st: BSG guidelines for colorectal cancer screening and surveillance
audits.f: 319 requests adhered to guidelines (73.5%); 328 (75.6%) scoped; 44 colonoscopies fell outside guidelines, 38 of them brought back too early or late.

audits.t: PWE-064 Management Of Large Colonic Polyps In The Severn Deanery Hospitals: An Audit Of Current Practice
audits.st: Draft BCSP guidelines for management of large (>2 cm) colonic polyps, 9 auditable outcomes
audits.f: All 6 malignant polyps tattooed; mean time to definitive resection 34 (BCSP) and 30 (symptomatic) days; adenoma recurrence at 12 months 0/22 and 2/37; 17 benign polyps referred for surgery, none discussed with local EMR experts; 1 haemorrhage, 0 perforations.
audits.c: Large polyp referral pathway established at two centres in the region.

audits.t: PWE-162 An Audit Of Testing For Coeliac Disease In Patients Diagnosed With The Irritable Bowel Syndrome At A Large Primary Care Centre
audits.tp: Coeliac testing in irritable bowel syndrome
audits.st: NICE guidance: test for coeliac disease in patients with IBS symptoms
audits.f: 65/250 tested for coeliac disease; 185 not tested.

audits.t: OC-053 Results Of The Uk Multi-regional Audit Of Blood Component Use In Cirrhosis
audits.st: Guidelines on use of red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate
audits.f: 391/1313 (30%) transfused; Hb >8 g/dL before RBC transfusion for bleeding in 69/220 (31%); prophylactic transfusion without a planned procedure in 94/153 (61%); FFP at INR ≤1.5 for high-risk procedures 3/16 (19%) and INR ≤2 for low-risk 6/18 (33%); platelets at count >50 before a procedure 9/25 (36%).

audits.t: PTH-129 A Retrospective Audit Of Peg Indications And Complications At A District General Hospital Following The Introduction Of A Multi-disciplinary Nutrition Team
audits.st: National confidential enquiry into PEG outcomes (patient selection); PEG indication, antibiotic prophylaxis documentation and MDT review
audits.f: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 80%; 7 patients had no MDT discussion; 3 deaths within 30 days.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary nutrition team approach and PEG referral proforma.
audits.r2: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 83%; all patients had MDT discussion; 2 immediate complications; no deaths at 30 days.

audits.t: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the UK: 2022 audit update
audits.st: Guideline adherence in AUGIB, notably pre-endoscopic risk stratification and restrictive transfusion thresholds
audits.f: Pre-endoscopic risk stratification not performed in 42%. Of early transfusions (38%), 43% given at Hb >70 g/L and 24% inappropriate due to haemodynamic stability. Inpatient endoscopy 83%; endotherapy 27%; rebleeding 9.7%; in-hospital mortality 8.8%; median stay 5 days.

audits.t: Prescription of secondary prevention medications, lifestyle advice, and referral to rehabilitation among acute coronary syndrome inpatients: results from a large prospective audit in Australia and New Zealand.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Optimal in-hospital preventive care: lifestyle advice, rehabilitation referral and secondary prevention medicines
audits.f: 46% referred to rehabilitation, 65% discharged on sufficient preventive medicines, 27% received optimal preventive care.

audits.t: Variation in hospital performance for heart failure management in the National Heart Failure Audit for England and Wales
audits.st: Three key performance measures: ACE-I/ARB on discharge, beta-blocker on discharge, referral to specialist follow-up
audits.f: Composite KPM adherence by hospital ranged 50% to 97% (median 79%); referral to specialist follow-up median 81% (range 20% to 100%).

audits.t: 3 A retrospective audit of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (mra) and device therapy following myocardial infarction (mi) complicated by left ventricular (lv) systolic dysfunction
audits.tp: MRA and ICD therapy after myocardial infarction with LV dysfunction
audits.st: MRA for eligible patients with post-MI LVEF ≤40% and heart failure or diabetes (EPHESUS); repeat LV imaging at 6-12 weeks and device therapy if LVEF ≤35% persists
audits.f: 47 (14%) eligible for MRA, 22 (47%) prescribed. 27 eligible for device consideration; 23 (85%) had repeat LV assessment (mean 107 days); 4 had ongoing severe LVSD, of whom 1 (25%) had an ICD.

audits.t: 46 Audit of new oral anticoagulant monitoring in primary care; are patients being prescribed the correct dose?
audits.tp: DOAC renal function monitoring and dosing
audits.st: NICE: regular renal function testing for patients on NOACs with dose adjustment by creatinine clearance; target 100% monitored at correct frequency
audits.f: Renal function tested in last 12 months in 84.5%; weight checked in last 12 months in 49%; accurate CrCl calculable in 46% (81/176); all apixaban and dabigatran doses correct but only 81% (59/73) of rivaroxaban doses correct.

audits.t: Coronary sinus reducer implantation for refractory angina: a national audit of UK practice
audits.st: Current guideline recommendations for CSR in refractory angina (appropriate patient selection)
audits.f: 84% had CCS class ≥3 angina despite ≥2 antianginals in 94%; baseline ischaemia testing 79%; procedural success 95%; periprocedural adverse events 9.2% (46 in 41 patients); 98% stayed ≤1 night.

audits.t: Audit of compliance with WHO surgical safety checklist and building a shared mental model in the operating theatre
audits.st: WHO surgical safety checklist (mandated for all NHS surgery) and 5 qualitative criteria
audits.f: Brief 7/8, Sign In 32/34, Time Out 30/34, Sign Out 18/34, Debrief 2/8; 3/34 operations achieved grade 3.

audits.t: An audit of the effect of oxygen prescription charts on clinical practice
audits.st: Adequate oxygen prescription (device, flow rate or inspired oxygen concentration, and target saturation), administration and monitoring
audits.f: Oxygen prescribed in 15/85 (17.6%); adequate prescription 5/85 (5.9%).
audits.c: New drug chart with a specific oxygen prescription section and targeted educational lectures mainly to medical staff.
audits.r2: Oxygen prescribed in 39/98 (39.8%), RR 2.3 (95% CI 1.3 to 3.9); adequate prescription 36/98 (36.7%), RR 6.2 (95% CI 2.5 to 15.0).

audits.t: Republished: unlocking the potential: longitudinal audit finds multifaceted education for general practice increases HIV testing and diagnosis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Trained practices: 2.29 HIV tests/1000 registered patients/year (526 tests p.a.); untrained 1.54.
audits.c: Sexual Health in Practice (SHIP) training in sexual health skills for GPs and practice nurses, with communication tools and resources.
audits.r2: Trained practices: 6.66 tests/1000/year (projected 1556 p.a., p=0.0016); untrained 1.90 (p=0.5195).

audits.t: National multicentre audit of pregnancy status in general surgery admissions in Scotland
audits.st: Documentation of pregnancy status in women of reproductive age
audits.f: Pregnancy status documented in 274 (51.7%): elective 52 (30.8%), emergency 222 (61.5%); possibility of pregnancy established in 237 (44.7%).

audits.t: Audit of the prevalence and investigation of iron deficiency anaemia in patients with heart failure in hospital practice
audits.tp: Iron deficiency investigation in heart failure
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 138 (63.3%) anaemic; only 40 of 138 (29%) had a full haematinic screen; 49 (56.3%) of those with iron studies were iron deficient, of whom only 12 (24.5%) were prescribed oral iron.

audits.t: Audit of oxygen administration to achieve a target oxygen saturation range in acutely unwell medical patients
audits.st: Documented target SpO2 range and SpO2 kept within it
audits.f: Target SpO2 range documented in 62 of 100; mean (SD) proportion of SpO2 measurements within range 56.2 (30.6)%.

audits.t: Improving metronidazole prescription practices in surgical patients: a full cycle audit.
audits.st: Proportion prescribed intravenous metronidazole when the oral route was available
audits.f: Oral 11 (20.4%), IV 43 (79.6%); IV prescribed without clear contraindication to oral in 35/43 (81.4%)
audits.c: Education of prescribers about similar pharmacokinetics of oral and IV metronidazole
audits.r2: Oral 23 (37.7%), IV 38 (62.3%); IV despite oral suitability 13/38 (34.2%) (risk ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.26 to 0.67)

audits.t: Audit of PSA requesting practices in primary care compared to guidelines established by the Prostate Cancer Risk Management programme in the Avon region of the South West of England
audits.st: Prostate Cancer Risk Management programme guidelines; NICE guidelines
audits.f: Overall good practice with room for improvement in advice on limitations of prostate biopsy and relevance of testing in the elderly; nearly half of abnormal primary-care PSA tests were repeated.

audits.t: The History and clinical examination for self-reported erectile dysfunction: are we following European guidelines? The results of the North West of England Regional Audit
audits.st: EAU Guidelines on Male Sexual Dysfunction 2012: detailed medical history and clinical examination in all patients
audits.f: Diabetes 99.6%, hypertension 41.8%, cardiovascular disease 22.2%, hyperlipidaemia 28.5%, smoking 89.1%, alcohol 83.3%. IIEF 32%, orgasm 39.3%, ejaculation 53.1%. Examination: genitalia 85.4%, blood pressure 74.9%, secondary sexual characteristics 41%, BMI 77.4%, peripheral pulses 56.5%.
audits.c: None reported; recommended a specific pro forma and dedicated andrology clinics.

audits.t: A culture of open reporting results in improved quality of bladder tumour resections: a closed loop audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.r2: Significant improvement in quality of T1 and Ta resections (p=0.04; p=0.02); percentage of inadequate resections significantly decreased (p=0.02).

audits.t: Does regional audit improve practice in the management of urological cancers?
audits.st: 42 agreed regional guidelines for prostate, testis, bladder and kidney cancer care
audits.f: Overall adherence to guidelines 63.4% in the original audits.
audits.c: Regional audit process with annual repeat audits.
audits.r2: Overall adherence 73.4% (p < 0.05); preoperative investigation +13% and planning, counselling, follow-up and documentation +12% (p < 0.05).

audits.t: An audit of urological MDT decision making in the South West of England
audits.st: NICE Improving Outcomes in Urological Cancer (2002) and NICE guidelines in force at the time
audits.f: MDTs were not consistent in decision making, and some decisions contradicted NICE guidelines.

audits.t: Rationalising bone scan usage in prostate cancer staging – A UK nationwide audit of the BAUS Radical Prostatectomy (RP) database
audits.st: Guidelines to avoid staging bone scans in low-risk prostate cancer
audits.f: Proportion of low-risk patients having bone scan fell to less than 1% in 2016; intermediate-risk proportion remained stable; no staging scan before RP 3.66% in 2016.

audits.t: Closed-loop audit of muscle sampling in Trans-Urethral Resection of Bladder Tumour
audits.st: European Association of Urology guidelines (detrusor muscle in TURBT specimens)
audits.f: Detrusor muscle present (quality resection) in 39%.
audits.c: Awareness of current practice; EAU guidance with separate tumour-base specimen pot; dedicated bladder cancer urologists using en-bloc resection where appropriate.
audits.r2: Quality of resections improved to 66% (50–84% for intermediate and high grade).

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis following transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP): An audit of practice in Scotland
audits.st: European Association of Urology guidelines (recommend against pharmacological prophylaxis after TURP)
audits.f: 71.4% of responding urologists prescribed pharmacological VTE prophylaxis after TURP; 94.6% used TED stockings; none routinely prescribed prophylaxis on discharge.

audits.t: Evaluating the management pathway for suspected testicular cancer: Results from the BAUS EMPAST national audit
audits.tp: Suspected testicular cancer referral pathway timeliness
audits.st: NHS Faster Diagnosis Standard (28-day proxy) and 14-day consultation standard
audits.f: Median referral-to-consultation 7.5 days (IQR 5–14), 79% seen within 14 days; median referral-to-outcome communication 14 days (IQR 8–25), 81% achieved FDS proxy; median referral-to-orchidectomy 23 days (IQR 15–35).

audits.t: Completed audit of the use of seclusion in the Approved Centre in Tallaght University Hospital following the introduction of an Integrated Care Pathway
audits.st: Mental Health Commission rules governing the use of seclusion (13 rules)

audits.t: Assessing the compliance of accurately documenting medication history in CAMHS – completion of the audit cycle
audits.st: Locally agreed protocol: medication history recorded in specified section of PARIS database

audits.r2: 58/78 (74%) recorded in correct section; of those, 86% drug names correct, 79% correct dose, 71% correct frequency, 81% regular/PRN recorded

audits.t: A closed audit reviewing the electrocardiograms of patients presenting to the memory assessment team

audits.t: An audit to look at the prescribing of psychotropic medication in the general adult inpatient setting in patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder
audits.st: Mersey Care EUPD prescribing guidelines
audits.f: With comorbidities (n=25): 80% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication, 4 of 7 new prescriptions followed guidelines. Without comorbidities (n=25): 96% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication, 5 of 8 followed guidelines. 78% of 50 prescribed PRN psychotropics; 21 had PRN for over one week

audits.t: A quality improvement project focused on improving the completion of ‘notification of diagnosis’ forms for the dementia register, in an outpatient setting

audits.f: 12/40 (30%) diagnosed patients were on the dementia register.

audits.r2: Form completion 75% in November, 66.7% in December and 50% in January 2021.

audits.t: Pregnancy audit in the PATH (Psychosis Prevention, Assessment and Treatment in Hertfordshire) early intervention in psychosis service
audits.tp: Preconception and contraception advice on psychotropics

audits.f: Asked about pregnancy plans 34/177 (19%); contraception advice 28/177 (16%); of 27 planning pregnancy, 15 offered perinatal referral (56%) and 12 received advice on antipsychotic risks in pregnancy (44%)

audits.t: Audit on resuscitation equipment in Carseview Centre (NHS Tayside)

audits.f: Resuscitation trolleys often lacked ligature packs; masks generally not by oxygen cylinders; hypoglycaemia dextro-tablets not readily available; learning disability unit had no emergency resuscitation trolley
audits.c: Feedback to wards, multidisciplinary meetings, amendment of the local protocol (not reviewed since 2012) finalised November 2020, and a list of recommendations
audits.r2: All first-cycle recommendations implemented; some equipment still incomplete or missing on individual wards but none consistently missing across the site

audits.t: An audit assessing the monitoring of SSRIS after initiation in children and adolescents
audits.tp: Antidepressant prescribing and monitoring in children and young people
audits.st: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: follow-up one week after starting SSRI and review every 4–6 weeks
audits.f: 17/18 followed up; median follow-up 42 days; none within a week. Improvement monitored in 88%, adverse effects in 36%; 53% had no documented adverse-effect monitoring.

audits.t: Clinical audit of prescribing for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and young people services (CYPS)
audits.st: TEWV ADHD prescribing guidelines and NICE NG87 (2018)
audits.f: Verbal information 92% and written 58%; pre-treatment assessment in all but 3 cases; methylphenidate not first line in 4 cases (3 atomoxetine by parental choice, 1 contraindication); lisdexamfetamine used second line in 75%

audits.t: Effects of tailored quality improvement programme for effective medication management in high dependency in-patient psychiatry rehabilitation unit
audits.st: Safe prescription and administration of psychotropic medication; Mental Health Act 1983 treatment certificate compliance
audits.f: Phase I: prescription errors 19%; administration errors 34%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 77%; patient knowledge of medication 15%.

audits.r2: Phase II: prescription errors 3%; administration errors 11%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 98%; patient knowledge 32%.

audits.t: Audit on the monitoring of metabolic side effects of antipsychotics in acute inpatient psychiatric units at Fieldhead Hospital
audits.st: POMH-UK guidance: BMI, blood pressure, blood glucose and lipids checked at least once a year for patients on continuing antipsychotics
audits.f: Lipids screened in 68%, BMI 71%, blood glucose 74%, blood pressure 87%.

audits.t: Audit to assess discussion of sexual dysfunction for new patients entering a community mental health recovery service
audits.st: NICE guidelines: assessment of biological symptoms and discussion of treatment side effects at initiation and follow-up
audits.f: No record of sexual dysfunction as present or absent at initial assessment or follow-up (0/71)

audits.t: Psychiatric staff training in managing medical emergencies: re-audit
audits.st: NICE CG25 (2005) and NPSA Rapid Response Report 2008/RRR010 on medical emergency training
audits.f: Nursing staff training met standards except new staff or staff returning from prolonged leave; gaps in other staff and in the remaining standards.

audits.t: Audit of compliance with WHO surgical safety checklist (modified for electroconvulsive therapy including NPSA advice)
audits.st: WHO surgical safety checklist modified for ECT including NPSA advice, per ECT accreditation service standards (target 100% completion)
audits.f: 19/20 (95%) completed; 5/20 (25%) not signed; 75% complete and valid; checklists present in all case notes

audits.t: An audit addressing the quality of prescribing sodium valproate in early intervention service
audits.st: POMH-UK (Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health) valproate QIP standards
audits.f: All 31 had target symptoms documented; 94% started valproate as inpatients (physical health checks unclear); 55% on off-licence preparation, of whom 93% had no documented rationale and 93% no evidence of discussion with patient; 74% had adequate community monitoring

audits.t: Audit on Prolactin Monitoring for Patients on Oral/Intramuscular Risperidone and Intramuscular Paliperidone
audits.st: BNF: prolactin at baseline, 6 months and then annually; all patients on risperidone or paliperidone should have prolactin checked at least once a year
audits.f: 8 of 27 (29.6%) had no prolactin check within the last year; 8 of 19 (42.4%) checked had not been checked annually previously; approximately 60% not receiving regular monitoring.
audits.c: Proposed: recommendation in clinic letters to GPs to include prolactin in annual health check bloods, symptom monitoring in clinic and caregiver education.

audits.t: The hidden cost of not having a dual diagnosis team (an audit looking at inpatient admissions for Redbridge Community Recovery Team West)

audits.t: Audit of ADHD medication prescription and monitoring in intellectual disability services, Greater Glasgow & Clyde
audits.st: NICE/RCPsych ADHD medication prescription guidance: 100% of patients with all audit tool components documented
audits.f: Previous cycle results not reported.
audits.r2: Blood pressure/pulse recorded in 84%; height/weight/BMI 81%; symptom severity, dose, side effects, need for treatment and review frequency 97%.

audits.t: Clozapine & constipation: an audit of bowel habit monitoring and laxative prescribing in inpatients on clozapine
audits.st: Local trust guidance: bowel habits monitored at least with every FBC
audits.f: 54.8% (17) had bowel habits monitored at least with every FBC (range 0% to 100% between wards); 87.1% (27) had a laxative prescribed.

audits.t: Oppurtunistic completion of the 9 diabetic care processes during inpatient admission to a mental health hospital: an audit of local practice

audits.t: An audit into the use of psychotropic medications in patients with autism spectrum disorder in a high security psychiatric hospital
audits.tp: Psychotropic prescribing in autism and neurodevelopmental disorders
audits.st: NICE CG142: Autism spectrum disorder in adults
audits.f: 13 (76.5%) with confirmed ASD prescribed antipsychotics; none prescribed for core ASD symptoms; off-licence use not documented in any relevant patient in the preceding 12 months.

audits.t: An audit into the management of diabetes mellitus at Broadmoor Hospital
audits.tp: Diabetes care in severe mental illness
audits.st: NICE NG28 Type 2 diabetes in adults: management
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Recruitment of a dietician to the hospital.
audits.r2: Improved adherence to six-monthly HbA1c monitoring, but less than 50% had HbA1c at or below target; 23 patients offered dietician referral.

audits.t: An audit into the management of COVID-19 in a high security psychiatric hospital
audits.st: Public Health England national guidance on investigation and management of suspected and confirmed COVID-19
audits.f: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 1 patient; practice consistent with national guidance.

audits.t: Audit examining memantine initiation in dementia patients in an older adult service in the north west

audits.t: Hyponatraemia monitoring in those prescribed antidepressants - an audit from an inpatient older adult ward
audits.st: Trust guidance: 3-monthly sodium levels for patients on antidepressants with hyponatraemia risk factors
audits.f: 11/13 eligible patients (85%) had 3-monthly sodium levels; only 2 (15%) had a plan for GP sodium monitoring in the discharge summary.

audits.t: Audit on antipsychotic prescribing in children and young people with a learning disability under the care of mental health services in Surrey
audits.st: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing in learning disability
audits.f: Reasons for starting documented for all 5 on antipsychotics; for 4 started over 12 months ago, no documentation of side effect, EPSE, weight, blood pressure, glycaemic or lipid monitoring; 1 lacked a 6-monthly review.

audits.t: “Are they medically fit?” - clinical audit on the physical assessment of mental health patients in A&E
audits.tp: Physical assessment of mental health patients in the emergency department
audits.st: Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidelines on physical assessment before mental health referral
