audits.f: Median first follow-up 3 weeks for 18–25 year olds (8% compliance) and 4 weeks for over 25s (19% compliance)

audits.t: Audit of Prescribing Practices & Medication Monitoring on Learning Disability Female Low Secure Unit
audits.st: Trust and national guidelines on psychotropic prescribing and monitoring (indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment and capacity forms, annual health check, blood monitoring, annual valproate risk acknowledgement form).
audits.f: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment form 71%; annual valproate risk acknowledgement form in women of childbearing age 0%.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit on Adult ADHD From Community Mental Health Teams: Experience From the East of North Wales
audits.st: RCPsych 'ADHD in Adults: Good Practice Guidelines'
audits.f: Referrals documented ASRS in 34%, AQ-10 in 18%, W-FIRS in 0%; 46% diagnosed with a standardised instrument over more than one session; baseline BP 58%, pulse 70%, weight 50%, height 44%.

audits.t: Physical Health Assessment and Monitoring for Adults Receiving Pharmacological Treatment for ADHD in an Adult CMHT:Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE: baseline height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and cardiovascular assessment before stimulant treatment, then 6-monthly weight, blood pressure and pulse
audits.f: Baseline blood pressure 57% (19); pulse 39% (13); weight 51% (17); cardiovascular assessment 6% (2). At 6-month follow-up (10 patients), 0% had blood pressure, pulse or weight documented.
audits.c: New proforma for baseline and 6-monthly physical health monitoring to be placed in case notes; results presented at CMHT meeting.

audits.t: Clinical Re-Audit of the Interface Between Community and Inpatient Management of Service Users
audits.st: Trust Admission, Transfer and Discharge policy (community team involvement, care plan copy offered, GP informed within 24 hours of admission)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Ward invited community team to meetings in 96%; contact between community team and patient in 100%; GP informed in 20% (increased but still red); written care plan copy offered increased compared with original audit

audits.t: An Audit of Planned Follow-Up Following Discharge From Four Black Country CRHT's
audits.st: All patients discharged from CRHT should receive planned follow-up within 3 months of discharge
audits.f: Wolverhampton: all had 72-hour follow-up but 12% lost to long-term follow-up or in crisis first; Dudley 51% and Sandwell 47% followed up within 3 months; Walsall followed up all unless discharged to GP.

audits.t: A Re-Audit of the Assessment and Management of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorders Following Admission to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Alcohol history documented 45%; weekly quantity 22%; CIWA-R on admission 0.7%; referral to community alcohol services 3%
audits.c: Recommendations implemented after the original audit (not detailed)
audits.r2: Alcohol history documented 81%; weekly quantity 8%; CIWA-R on admission 4.0%; referral to community alcohol services 7%

audits.t: Audit on Baseline Physical and Metabolic Investigations Before Prescribing Antipsychotics in Children and Adolescent With Psychosis and Schizophrenia
audits.tp: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children and young people
audits.st: NICE guidelines on baseline physical and metabolic investigations before prescribing antipsychotics in children and young people
audits.f: Indications, record keeping and nutrition/activity assessment 100%; pulse and BP 88.9%; growth chart 77.8%; movement disorders always 44.4%; lipids always 44.4%; fasting glucose and HbA1c 33.3%

audits.t: Audit of On-Call Assessments (Acute and Urgent Care)
audits.st: Local algorithm/Trust protocol for doctors (allocated team or on-call) participating in Mental Health Act assessments.
audits.f: At least one trust doctor involved in 91% of assessments (92% in Section 136 suite; 89% out of hours).

audits.t: Retrospective Analysis of a Single Centre Experience of the Pharmacological Management of Patients With Intellectual Disability & Challenging Behaviour Across Three Audit Cycles
audits.tp: Behaviour that challenges in learning disability
audits.st: NICE and STOMP guidelines for pharmacological management of challenging behaviour in intellectual disability.
audits.f: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviours 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%; physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%.
audits.r2: Risk assessment 100%; target behaviours 100%; metabolic monitoring 95%; interventions documented 86%; mental health evaluation 60%; physical health 60%; consent 46%; side-effect discussion 50%; 6-week review 50%; positive behaviour support plan 75%.

audits.t: Pathways to Care at Early Intervention in Psychosis Liverpool: A Cross-Sectional Retrospective Audit Cycle
audits.tp: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
audits.st: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral
audits.f: Average referral pathway time 9.8 days
audits.c: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (details not reported)
audits.r2: Average pathway time 22.5 days, exceeding the NICE standard

audits.t: An Audit on Glycosylated Haemoglobin & Fasting Plasma Glucose Blood Tests Done on Admission to an Older People's Inpatient Ward
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Trust protocol for admission blood tests including fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c
audits.f: 23 (57.5%) had HbA1c or plasma glucose on admission; only 6 (15%) had plasma glucose, not specified as fasted; 17 (42.5%) had neither.

audits.t: Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: standardised admission blood tests within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: 30% had bloods within 24 hours; 40% declined or unsafe; 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant bloods
audits.c: Standardised PICU guideline with a pre-filled blood test request form
audits.r2: Only 6% not done within timeframe; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised bloods; bloods within 24 hours increased from 80% to 94%; direct admissions with all bloods 77% to 100%

audits.t: The Management of Short-Term Insomnia for Inpatients in an Adult Acute Admissions Ward: Audit of Compliance With Local and National Guidelines
audits.st: Local and national guidance: sleep hygiene advice before drugs; non-benzodiazepine hypnotic prescribed; one-off trial dose before regular prescription; target 100%
audits.f: Of 8 reviewed for insomnia: 12.5% (n=1) offered sleep hygiene advice; 25% (n=2) trial dose of non-benzodiazepine hypnotic; 25% (n=3) regular hypnotic with no trial dose; 50% (n=4) alternative sedative.
audits.c: Planned: sleep hygiene leaflet, presentation of data to medical and nursing staff, guidelines made available on the ward; re-audit in six months.

audits.t: Seclusion Reviews: Audit of Medical Documentation in a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice: medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly until first MDT review, twice daily thereafter with at least one by the Responsible Clinician, with specified documentation content
audits.f: 20% seen within 1 hour; 75% seen 4-hourly until MDT review; mental health documented 97%, physical health 61%, medication 69%, rationale for continuing 72%, adverse medication effects and observation level 2%, risk to self 7%

audits.t: Secondary Service Communications to GPs-a Regional Audit
audits.st: RCPsych and PRSB recommendations for letters to GPs
audits.f: Missing care coordinator details 91.7%, medical comorbidities 61.22%, non-psychiatric diagnosis 79.59%, actions for GP 71.43%; psychiatric diagnosis 83.47%; psychiatric medication and follow-up plan 80.17%
audits.c: Local guidelines and letter template with recommended headings, and formal teaching for junior doctors
audits.r2: Psychiatric diagnosis 97.1% (previous 83.5%); psychiatric medication 91.4% (previous 80.17%); follow-up plan 98.6% (previous 80.2%); medical comorbidity 28.6% vs 31.4%; non-psychiatric medication 65.7% vs 34.7%; care coordinator 54.3% vs 8.3%; action for GP 27.1% vs 44.6%

audits.t: Management of medically assisted withdrawal from alcohol in acute adult mental health and specialist addictions in-patient services: UK clinical audit findings.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 908 patients on acute adult wards/PICU and 347 on specialist addictions units; addiction specialist oversight in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients

audits.t: An Audit Exploring Ethnic Inequalities in Accessing Perinatal Mental Health Services in Southwark
audits.tp: Ethnic equity in mental health service access
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists gold standards for equitable access to perinatal mental health care.
audits.f: Ethnicity not documented in 6.6% of referrals; no clear inequity at referral, but 3 of 4 admissions (75%) were Black women and all detained; only 2/35 Asian and Mixed ethnicity women referred for psychology; 83% (5/6) of antipsychotics prescribed to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women.

audits.t: Inpatient Ward Review Documentation Audit
audits.st: 80% completion of ward review documentation questions considered satisfactory
audits.f: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.
audits.c: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.
audits.r2: 9 questions satisfactory (at least 80%); 7 above 45%; 17 low; 'Responsible clinician' 99.5% after automation.

audits.t: Physical Health Monitoring in Patients on Antipsychotics: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE yearly physical health monitoring (BMI, BP, ECG, bloods, alcohol and smoking status); audit standard 100%
audits.f: BMI recorded 91.67% (n=33); BP 86.11% (n=31); alcohol, smoking and drug use 97.22% (n=35); ECG not recorded in 72.22% (n=26); up-to-date bloods 75% (n=27); QRISK not collected in 22.73% (5/22)

audits.t: Clinical Audit of the Quality of Care Delivered by Community Mental Health Services for Older People to People Living With Dementia and Their Carers
audits.tp: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
audits.st: NICE 2018 dementia guideline and TEWV 2019 person-centred dementia care pathway
audits.f: Consent recorded 80%; prognosis information 47%; dementia and driving 26%; accessible information leaflets 16%; carer's assessment offered 26%
audits.c: Action plans on areas needing improvement (not detailed)
audits.r2: Consent recorded 65%; prognosis information 80%; dementia and driving 53%; accessible leaflets 50%; carer's assessment offered 18%

audits.t: Intensive Home Treatment Team (IHTT) Antipsychotic Initiation Baseline Physical Health Investigations Audit
audits.st: Trust Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines.
audits.f: 32% had a full physical health check before antipsychotic initiation, 56% incomplete; no individual investigation fully compliant; BMI/weight least completed, HbA1c least completed blood test; 40% had results reviewed by a relevant professional.

audits.t: Audit: Medical Seclusion Reviews at Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Trust seclusion policy in line with Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015: 1-hour and 4-hourly medical reviews, MDT within 12 hours, documented review content
audits.f: Reviewed within 1 hour 34%; 4-hourly 41%; internal MDT 47%; review documented 57%; ongoing concerns 50%; MSE 47%; physical health 42%; medication 44%; risk 44%; need for seclusion 58%; intervention 52%.

audits.t: An Audit Looking at the Monitoring for Long-Term Antipsychotic Use on an Adult Inpatient Psychiatry Ward
audits.st: NICE guidance on monitoring patients on long-term antipsychotics (14 standards: BMI, ECG, blood pressure, lipids, prolactin, urea and electrolytes at baseline, set time points and dose changes).
audits.f: 5 of 14 standards attained, 7 not attained, 1 partially analysed and 1 (12-month monitoring) not analysable.

audits.t: Audit of Antimanic Agents Monitoring in a High Secure Hospital
audits.st: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) pre-initiation and ongoing monitoring for lithium, valproate and carbamazepine (16 standards)
audits.f: Valproate FBC monitoring within 6 months 92% (other 2018 figures not reported)
audits.r2: Valproate pre-initiation LFT 35.8%, FBC 41.5%, 6-month monitoring 85.7% and 87.5%; lithium pre-initiation ECG 73.1%, TFT 88.5%, U&E 96.2%, monitoring 100%; carbamazepine pre-initiation 50%, monitoring 100%; all standards improved except valproate FBC monitoring

audits.t: An Audit on the Prescribing of Antipsychotics Among People With Recorded Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD) Within a Community Mental Health Service in Stroud, Gloucestershire
audits.st: NICE guidance: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with aim of reducing and stopping.
audits.f: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication; mean duration 36.79 months; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic; only 10 (42%) had prescriptions reviewed to stop or reduce; none offered routine physical review.

audits.t: Mental Health Triage Form Use in Emergency Department Clerking – Audit at Royal Cornwall Hospital
audits.tp: Mental health triage form use in the emergency department
audits.st: RCEM recommendation (in line with NCEPOD 'Treat as One') to use a mental health proforma; local Mental Health Triage Form.
audits.f: Mental Health Triage Form used in 44/125 (35%); 15 (12%) had missing ED documentation; 25% average increase in information recorded when the form was used.

audits.t: Audit on the Adherence to Guidelines for the Management of Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome in a General Hospital
audits.st: Health board policy NU16 for alcohol withdrawal syndrome management, based on NICE guidelines
audits.f: Complete drinking history 4%; physical examination 84%; Wernicke's signs documented 20%; CIWA-Ar applied 44%, correctly scored 24%; benzodiazepines prescribed 38%; oral thiamine 58%; alcohol liaison opinion 16%.
audits.c: Training programmes on alcohol withdrawal management by the alcohol liaison team for all clinical staff.

audits.t: Audit of DNA & Disengagement of Patients in West Essex Community MH Teams
audits.st: Trust policy on non-attendance (DNA) and disengagement
audits.f: 98.1% notified adequately with letters to patient and GP; risk assessment completed in 50.9%; risk assessment updated in 25%; contingency plan reviewed for 26 patients; family contacted for 3.

audits.t: A Trust Wide Audit Evaluating Prescribing Practices in Clients With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD)
audits.st: NICE EUPD guidance: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD; time-limited crisis prescribing only; written information and regular reviews if prescribing.
audits.f: 71/87 (81.6%) prescribed medication; of these 39.4% (n=28) consistent with time-limited prescribing, 57.7% (n=41) had timely reviews, 4.2% (n=3) had written information recorded.

audits.t: Clinical Audit Reviewing Compliance With Respective Trust-Based Physical Health Monitoring Guidelines, Amongst Inpatients Prescribed Anti-Psychotic Medication in Two Distinct Secure Care Facilities: A Low Secure Unit and a Prison Personality Disorder Unit
audits.st: Respective trust (CPFT and NHFT) physical health monitoring guidelines for patients on antipsychotics.
audits.f: Laboratory markers monitored in 88–100% at both sites; waist circumference omitted in 100% at both sites; ECG omitted in 60% (prison) and 14% (low secure unit).

audits.t: A Re-Audit of Teesside On-Call Email System
audits.st: Local trust criteria for on-call email requests (complete request form, adequate clinical information, patient identification and location, doctor response within 45 minutes); expected standard 100%
audits.f: Three of four standards above 70% compliance
audits.r2: Compliance below 70% across all four standards, a notable decrease from previous results

audits.t: Clinical Audit on the Measurement of Antipsychotic Side Effects Using Rating Scales (GASS, LUNSERS, and SESCAM) in Community Settings
audits.st: NICE guidelines and Trust policy on monitoring of psychotropic medications: side effects assessed with a recommended rating scale (GASS, LUNSERS or SESCAM) at three months and one year after starting antipsychotics
audits.f: No rating scales used (0%) at three months or one year; side effects documented informally in case notes in 96%
audits.r2: Use of an objective rating scale improved to 24%

audits.t: Collateral History-Taking on Acute General Adult and Older Person Inpatient Wards: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Collateral history taken within the first 14 days of admission
audits.f: 33% had a collateral history within 14 days; where omitted, 10% attempted and 46% planned
audits.c: Questionnaire and two junior doctor focus groups to explore barriers; visiting restrictions lifted
audits.r2: 38% had a collateral history within 14 days; where omitted, 13% attempted and 27% planned

audits.t: Audit of the Metabolic Side-Effects on Autistic Inpatients on a Rehabilitation Ward
audits.st: NICE guideline recommendations on monitoring metabolic side effects of antipsychotics
audits.f: Blood pressure, BMI and HbA1c recorded in 100%; lipid profile 86.6%; waist circumference 60%.

audits.t: Naloxone Audit
audits.st: Local guidelines and UK guidelines on clinical management of drug misuse and dependence (2017)
audits.f: Naloxone provision recorded under two unclear headings (episode and event); 367 patients who had never injected heroin were given naloxone; documentation of training was sparse.

audits.t: An Audit Reviewing the Completion and Quality of the Admission, Then Six Monthly ALL-Physical Health Assessments (A Six Monthly Health Check) on a Low Secure, Inpatient Forensic Psychiatric Ward in Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Physical health monitoring of psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: Trust guidance: mandatory ALL-Physical Health Assessment on admission and six-monthly (14 categories).
audits.f: 76.4% of patients had ALL done; 67.2% of completions green, 15.5% amber, 17.2% red; QRISK 70%, alcohol 58%, diet 82%, exercise 70%, diabetes 58%, smoking 76%.
audits.r2: 15/17 (88%) had ALL in last 6 months; 89.9% of completions green, 4.6% amber, 5.5% red; QRISK, alcohol, diet and exercise 100%; diabetes 82%, smoking 88%.

audits.t: Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: An Audit of Prescribing Practices in the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults
audits.st: NICE NG97 (June 2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring.
audits.f: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% risk discussion documented; 63% baseline bloods; 54% baseline ECG; 33% of those treated over 12 weeks had discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

audits.t: An Audit on the Uptake of Psychosocial Interventions in a Nationally Accredited Memory Service
audits.st: NICE NG97 and Memory Services National Accreditation Programme standards
audits.f: 23/140 (16.4%) referred to the Involvement, Recovery and Wellness Centre, 12 booked onto workshops; 16 (11.4%) clinic letters documented referral, none gave a rationale; 100% compliance for trained staff and carer support standards; 99.3% offered pharmacological intervention.

audits.t: Re-Audit of Prescribing Responsibility for Antipsychotic Depots for Shared Care Patients(PRAD-SCP)
audits.st: Greater Manchester Medicines Management Group shared care protocol: prescribing transferred to GP for stable patients; target 100%
audits.f: Overall compliance 83%
audits.r2: Overall compliance 96%; first generation antipsychotics 98%; paliperidone and risperidone 94%; aripiprazole 91%

audits.t: Improving Acute Treatment of Alcohol Withdrawal at an Inpatient De-addiction Ward (‘Vimukthi’) at Kerala State, India: Full Cycle of a Clinical Audit
audits.st: ASAM, NICE and Government of India guidelines: long-acting benzodiazepines with fixed-dose, symptom-triggered or front-loading regimens according to setting and risk
audits.f: Fixed-dose regimen of short-acting lorazepam used for all patients; no documentation of risk profiling.
audits.c: Standard operating procedure with risk profiling, symptom-triggered regimen using nurse-administered CIWA-Ar and front-loading for high risk, introduced after team discussion and training in October 2023.
audits.r2: Risk stratification documented (34% low, 52% intermediate, 14% high risk); symptom-triggered regimen given to all patients with front-loading for all high-risk patients; oral lorazepam fell from 3324 mg for 63 patients (Oct–Dec 2022) to 10 mg for 39 patients.

audits.t: Audit of Patients Prescribed Psychotropic Medication in the Community Learning Disabilities Psychiatry Services of the Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: NHS England STOMP (Stopping Overmedication of People with a Learning Disability, Autism or Both) recommendations
audits.f: Good evidence of capacity, consent, best interests, MDT input and regular review of medication, side effects and response (no figures given); rationale for off-label use could be recorded more clearly.

audits.t: Weight Management Quality Improvement Project in Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service
audits.tp: Weight and BMI monitoring in learning disability
audits.st: Project target: up-to-date BMI for 70% or more of service users by September 2024
audits.f: 26.7% of 71 service users had an updated weight and BMI
audits.c: Planned PDSA cycles; weekly MDT meetings with service users; waiting-room machine for weight, height and blood pressure; staff education

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Junior Doctor Handover in Tyrone and Fermanagh Hospital, Northern Ireland
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Password protection used in 69%; other baseline figures not reported.
audits.c: New handover template with prompts for staff, date and key patient information, emailed to doctors on the rota and highlighted at changeover.
audits.r2: Staff identification 98% and shift date 99%; password use 91%. Improvements in patient initials (29.4%), health and care number (9.2%), MHO status (15.46%), patient summary (19.76%), working diagnosis (34.91%) and an 88.74% increase in identifying who follows up outstanding tasks.

audits.t: Assessing Clinical Coding Compliance in a Mental Health Inpatient Unit: An Audit and Intervention Study
audits.st: Local and national clinical coding guidelines
audits.f: 5 (25%) had coding completed during admission; 1 of 4 (25%) updated after diagnosis change; 3 of 9 (33%) physical health diagnoses coded; 16 (89%) coded on last discharge.
audits.c: Doctors informed about clinical coding, how to access the form and its importance through teaching sessions and doctor communication groups.
audits.r2: 10 (50%) had coding completed during admission; 3 of 4 (75%) updated after diagnosis change; 2 of 7 (29%) physical health conditions coded; 12 (75%) coded on last discharge.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project: Lithium Monitoring in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team
audits.st: Nine standards from NICE and Trust guidelines (e.g. lithium level 3-monthly, kidney function 3–6-monthly, calcium 6-monthly); target 100%
audits.f: Average compliance 57%; six of eight standards below 60%, including lithium levels, kidney function and calcium.
audits.c: Physical health nursing team took over investigations from primary care using a bespoke database, plus a staff education session (PDSA).
audits.r2: Average compliance 94%; lithium level, kidney function and calcium monitoring 100%.

audits.t: An Audit of the First Stage of Service Development Initiatives Undertaken as Part of a Quality Improvement Process to Improve the Screening and Management of Older Adults Presenting With Delirium in Queen's Hospital (NELFT)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 47% of older adult referrals to PLS had delirium; 87% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention after initial assessment; 31 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team.
audits.c: Simplified PLS referral form with a mandatory 4AT delirium score and mandatory referral to the Dementia and Delirium Team for positive screens (November 2023).
audits.r2: 35% of referrals had delirium; 58% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention; prior screening and referral to Dementia and Delirium Team rose by 4%; 85 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team (174% increase).

audits.t: Assessment and Management of Eating Disorders at Community CAMHS in South Lanarkshire: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: MEED and SIGN 164
audits.f: Recording: weight change 40%, hydration 40%, temperature 5%, over-exercising 85%, purging 75%, self-harm 85%, BP/HR 80%, ECG 75%, engagement 75%.
audits.r2: Weight change 80%, hydration 70%, temperature 30%, over-exercising 90%, purging 85%, self-harm 90%, BP/HR 50%, ECG 40%, engagement 60%.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of the Assessment and Management for Those Diagnosed With Young Onset Dementia Within the Shepway CMHSOP
audits.tp: Young onset dementia assessment and support
audits.st: NICE dementia guidelines and Royal College of Psychiatrists recommendations for young onset dementia service provision
audits.f: Mood considered in all; young onset bloods when indicated 89%; physical examination 43%; all had imaging; named practitioner in half; cognitive stimulation therapy and post-diagnostic support offered to 79%.

audits.t: Assessing Adherence: Audit of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale Completion for Patients on Antipsychotic Depot Injections at Guildford CMHRS SABP
audits.st: Trust guideline: GASS completed at 12 weeks and 6 months after initiation, annually thereafter and at each dose titration
audits.f: GASS conducted in 8 cases (26.6%); 7 (23.3%) within the last year.
audits.c: Findings shared at the service with a recommendation for staff to use GASS at outpatient appointments and document scores on depot charts and SystmOne.
audits.r2: GASS completed in 16 cases (55.17%), all within the last year.

audits.t: Substance Misuse History Documentation at Admission to Secure Rehabilitation Ward Audit
audits.tp: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
audits.st: Electronic admission documentation of substance use history
audits.f: 7/12 patients asked about substance misuse at admission review; 5 not asked.

audits.t: Improving Women's Sexual and Reproductive Health in Acute Inpatient Psychiatric Services – A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Sexual health screening in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: Current national guidance on sexual and reproductive health (not named)
audits.f: 12.5% of inpatients offered at least one of contraceptive counselling, cervical and breast screening or STI screening.
audits.c: Women's health assessments with provision of emergency contraception and STI swabs, sexual health clinic referral protocol, dedicated clinic time, poster and leaflet, and an outcome proforma, over six PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: 87.7% offered a leaflet and 63.1% offered counselling; 48.8% of these accepted at least one intervention.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Investigate How Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) Training Improves the Accuracy of ACE-III Scoring in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team
audits.st: ACE-III Administration and Scoring Guide (2012)
audits.f: Inaccuracies and inconsistencies in ACE-III scoring identified (figures not reported).
audits.c: ACE-III training delivered by a neuropsychologist to the multidisciplinary team.
audits.r2: ACE-III scores more accurate (figures not reported).

audits.t: Revisiting Dental Care and Mental Health: A Quality Improvement Project of Dental Care for Patients With Severe Mental Illness Living in a Community Rehabilitation Centre
audits.st: NICE oral health quality standards: mouth care needs assessed on admission, recorded in care plan, and support for twice-daily tooth cleaning and denture care
audits.f: More than 90% of patients had unmet oral health needs.

audits.t: Audit Review of GP Referrals to Perinatal Mental Health Team – Emphasis on Medication
audits.tp: GP referrals to perinatal mental health
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66% used the referral proforma and 20% a letter; 25% did not state antenatal or postnatal status; medication stopped in 10%, and 64% of those proformas were incomplete.

audits.t: Naltrexone Treatment for Methamphetamine Dependence – Service Evaluation Audit
audits.st: Best practice recommendations for initiation and monitoring of naltrexone
audits.f: All patients had keyworker involvement and physical health checks; 18 of 28 took naltrexone over one week; 16 reported reduced cravings; 6 abstinent and 10 partial response; 9 of 18 had side effects.

audits.t: Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
audits.st: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting
audits.f: About 24% started on medication without trial of non-pharmacological methods; those started on medication were properly followed up; overall adherence around 75%.

audits.t: Audit on PRN Prescriptions in Adult Inpatient Female Ward
audits.st: NICE guidance on PRN prescribing and local Trust policy
audits.f: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 25%; oral and IM grouped 7.2%; minimum dose documented 10.7%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 100%.
audits.c: Guidelines added to junior doctor induction, weekly discussion with team pharmacist, prompts on the medication chart and weekly PRN review in ward MDT.
audits.r2: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 56%; oral and IM grouped 28%; minimum dose 24%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 96%.

audits.t: Audit for Patients Who Are Discharged on Community Treatment order (CTO) in North East Part of Essex: Exploring the Section Paperwork and the Readmissions in 2 Year Period
audits.st: Mental Health Act guidance on CTO paperwork completion and renewal hearings
audits.f: CTO3 paperwork missing in 2 cases; one tribunal hearing missed; one CTO lapsed; remaining patients had regular timely hearings.

audits.t: Audit of Psychotropic Polypharmacy Amongst Inpatients in East Suffolk
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Polypharmacy in 52% of inpatient episodes; 74% combination and 26% augmentation therapy

audits.t: Audit of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) Prescribing Among Inpatients in East Suffolk
audits.st: BNF and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines antipsychotic dosage; HDAT monitoring form for each patient on HDAT
audits.f: 166 (64.6%) on antipsychotics; 2 (1.2%) discharged on HDAT, of whom one did not have the monitoring form completed.

audits.t: Audit of Annual Blood Tests for Patients on Antipsychotic Medications in the Recovery Team

audits.t: Monitoring of Patients Who Presented With First Episode Psychosis, Under the Early Intervention Team, Against NICE Guidance for Psychosis and Schizophrenia

audits.f: Overall compliance 51%; weight/BMI and waist circumference 0%; pulse and BP 43% (90% by 1 year); lipids 48% (86% within a year); prolactin 52%; FBC 86%, U&E 86%, LFT 90%; glucose/HbA1c 48%; ECG at 1 year 67%
audits.c: Recommended: disseminate results through the team, add waist circumference to the physical health assessment form and create blood sample sets

audits.t: Prescribing and Monitoring of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) in the Acute Inpatient Setting
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists HDAT guidance: documented rationale, risk-benefit discussion or capacity/legal process, and ECG, BMI and blood monitoring
audits.f: 3/49 (6%) on HDAT, with no documented rationale and variable physical health monitoring
audits.c: Education sessions for rotational junior doctors in the six months after the initial audit
audits.r2: 11/47 (23%) on HDAT; only 2 of 7 MDT/consultant-initiated cases noted HDAT initiation; 8 had ECG within a month before HDAT; only 3 had repeat ECG within 7 days

audits.t: A Gap in Psychiatry On-Call Training: Post-Ligature Assessment
audits.st: Post-ligature assessment including ABCDE documentation, NEWS monitoring and follow-up plan
audits.f: Medic informed in 4; 0 ABCDE documentation; 0 NEWS monitoring; 3 follow-up plans.
audits.c: Locality teaching on audit findings, post-ligature assessment tool, and trial in simulation induction for new trainees.
audits.r2: Medic informed in 4; 0 ABCDE documentation; NEWS monitored in 6; 4 follow-up plans.

audits.t: Buckinghamshire Early Intervention Service’ (BEIS) Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Antipsychotic Monitoring Guidelines: Practical Challenges, Including Those Posed by the Pandemic, in an Outpatient Setting
audits.st: NICE antipsychotic monitoring guidelines (updated September 2021); 80% compliance target per National Clinical Audit of Psychosis
audits.f: First three months after initiation: 6/9 parameters met standard (range 2% to 100%), failing weekly BMI, pulse, BP and one-month HbA1c; only 2 parameters met for outpatient initiations; after three months only 3/9 met (lipids, HbA1c, side effects)
audits.c: Planned: checklist for medical and nursing staff and home monitoring of blood pressure and weight by patients

audits.t: High Risk Care Plans in Liaison Psychiatry
audits.tp: Crisis safety plans for high intensity users
audits.st: Local guidance: 100% completion of appropriate high risk care plans with all mandatory fields (no national guideline)
audits.f: 11 plans completed with 2 more required but missing; non-pharmacological de-escalation 2/11; regular medication 5/11; rapid tranquillisation advice 8/11; absconsion risk 8/11; observation level 10/11

audits.t: N20 Safety of extended blood monitoring for adult Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) patients on oral azathioprine during the COVID-19 pandemic: a single-centre audit
audits.st: Locally agreed standards for extended 6-monthly blood monitoring during COVID-19 (ECCO advises 3-monthly)
audits.f: 54% (n = 50) had extended blood monitoring, of whom 43 (86%) were eligible; one had raised ALT that improved after a treatment break; one advice-line call for side effects; no admissions due to deranged bloods or adverse effects

audits.t: 48 Consenting Surgical Patients for the Risk Associated with Contracting COVID-19 During Their Stay at the Hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidance on consent during COVID-19, Section 3A (discuss risk of contracting COVID-19 in hospital)
audits.f: 37% consented for risk of contracting COVID-19
audits.c: Teaching sessions, regular emails to the general surgical department and posters in common areas, repeated each cycle
audits.r2: 85% consented for COVID-19 risk (fourth cycle); significant increase from first cycle

audits.t: An audit of acute respiratory antibiotic prescribing in COPD patients during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: NICE NG114, NG168 and local formulary: 100% no prophylactic antibiotics for COVID-19; 100% no antibiotics for COVID-19 symptoms; 90% of regimens adherent to guidelines
audits.f: Standard 1 100% adherence; standard 2 99.4% (2 patients given antibiotics for suspected COVID-19); standard 3 only 28.7% adherent, mainly due to 7-day rather than 5-day courses.

audits.t: TH2.8 Continuing fast-track (Expedited) pancreaticoduodenectomy service during the Covid-19 pandemic: Experience from an established pancreatic surgical centre
audits.st: NICE NG85: avoid preoperative biliary drainage to allow early curative surgery
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Additional theatre sessions obtained and a fast-track referral pathway established after the prior audit.
audits.r2: 42/71 received preoperative biliary drainage; 29 did not. Median imaging to surgery 21 days (3–42) without drainage vs 62 days (22–305) with drainage (p=0.00028).

audits.t: TU3.4 A relook into the effects of Covid-19 on emergency theatre utilisation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline sending, anaesthetic, operating and recovery times (values not reported).
audits.c: Established COVID-19 testing protocols and recommendations from first audit, including a second emergency theatre.
audits.r2: Sending time decreased by 27% (p=1.25*10–7); anaesthetic time decreased by 31% (p=0.0001); recovery time in theatre decreased by 26% (p = 0.06); total recovery time increased by 19% (p=0.097).

audits.t: 541 Pre-Operative Assessment of Patients Undergoing Elective TURBT or Rigid Cystoscopy + Bladder Biopsy: Is a Group & Save Clinically Required?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 32.8% (21/64) had a preoperative group and save; 98.4% (63/64) had Hb measured; no transfusions required.
audits.c: Telephone pre-operative assessment during COVID-19 where group and save was deemed unnecessary.
audits.r2: 6.25% (3/48) had a group and save; 70.8% (34/48) had Hb measured; no transfusions required.

audits.t: Lithium monitoring in clinical practice
audits.st: NICE guidelines (2014): lithium levels every 3 months for patients at increased risk of toxicity; target level 0.4–0.8 mmol/L
audits.f: Only 1 of 28 high-risk patients had 3-monthly lithium levels; 35.7% of last levels within 0.4–0.8 mmol/L.
audits.c: Lithium monitoring sheet created in line with NICE guidance.
audits.r2: 12 patients (42%) met 3-monthly testing; 50% of last levels within 0.4–0.8 mmol/L.

audits.t: P69 COVID vaccine uptake in young persons on immunosuppression under the care of tertiary paediatric rheumatology service
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: National guidance: immunocompromised 12–18-year-olds offered three primary Pfizer BioNTech doses 8 weeks apart plus a booster within 3 months
audits.f: 6/31 (19%) knew the correct regime (3 + 1); 18/31 (58%) had received the vaccine.

audits.t: 12 VACCINATION UP-TAKE IN DERMATOLOGY PATIENTS OVER THE AGE OF 65 YEARS ON BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT
audits.tp: Vaccination in patients on biologic therapy
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines (August 2021): COVID-19, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination for patients on biologics
audits.f: 100% (n=18) had three COVID-19 vaccines; 94% (n=17) influenza vaccine; 66% (n=12) pneumococcal vaccine.

audits.t: O01 Auditing the duration of antibiotic therapy for children treated as inpatients for community acquired pneumonia
audits.st: Trust guidelines: 5–7 days of amoxicillin for simple community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: Median antibiotic duration 7 days (range 1–9); 7 children (23.3%) received more than 7 days. 40% amoxicillin only, 26.7% co-amoxiclav only, 33.3% combinations.
audits.c: Trust guideline changed via Paediatric Microguide to allow a 3-day amoxicillin course.

audits.t: Audit Report of Central Venous Catheter Insertion Practices in a Teaching Hospital of Rawalpindi
audits.st: Structured checklist based on Johns Hopkins Medicine and American Society of Anesthesiologists CVC insertion guidelines; satisfactory threshold 80%
audits.f: Compliance with key practices below the 80% threshold; full barrier precautions 47.1%; sterile draping 58.8%.
audits.c: Targeted intervention including educational materials and checklist-based guidance.

audits.t: Enhancing Compliance with Central Venous Catheterization Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Audit in a Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Structured checklist based on Johns Hopkins Medicine and American Society of Anesthesiologists CVC insertion guidelines; satisfactory threshold 80%
audits.f: Compliance with key practices below the 80% threshold; full barrier precautions 47.1%; sterile draping 58.8%.
audits.c: Targeted intervention including educational materials and checklist-based guidance.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic prescribing practices for pediatric pneumonia in the outpatient department: focus on amoxicillin and azithromycin.
audits.st: WHO AWaRe and IMNCI guidance on antibiotic choice, dose and duration
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed 116/132 (87.9%); amoxicillin 26/132 (19.7%), appropriate 1/26 (3.8%); azithromycin 66/132 (50.0%), appropriate 20/66 (30.3%).

audits.t: Improving meropenem prescribing through antimicrobial stewardship interventions: a prospective clinical audit in a UK district general hospital
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines; documentation of indication, duration and penicillin allergy status
audits.f: Guideline compliance 50% (50/100); indication documented 86% (86/100); duration 94% (94/100); penicillin-allergy label 69% (69/100).
audits.c: Daily multidisciplinary antimicrobial stewardship ward rounds, prospective audit with real-time feedback and focused prescriber education.
audits.r2: Guideline compliance 74% (74/100); indication and duration documented 100% (100/100); penicillin-allergy label 53% (53/100).

audits.t: Interrupting source-dependent verification cascades after a near-miss wrong-side surgery event: a pre-post quality-improvement study of closed-loop imaging-based laterality verification
audits.tp: Surgical site marking and laterality verification
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist process compliance
audits.f: Checklist process compliance 85.0%; checklist quality pass rate 40.0%; item completion 91.9%; site marking accuracy 73.1%; preparation-area verification 89.6%; theatre entry verification 91.2%.
audits.c: Standardised site marking with mandatory original-imaging review, revised challenge-response laterality checklist items, three-stage closed-loop digital verification workflow and HIS/EMR/PACS integration with forced constraints.
audits.r2: Checklist process compliance 100.0%; quality pass rate 90.0%; item completion 99.0%; site marking accuracy 97.7%; preparation-area verification 95.0%; theatre entry verification 98.0%.

audits.t: The Infection Prevention and Biosafety Assessment Initiative: Impact of a Structured Multimodal Training Intervention on Infection Prevention and Biosafety Compliance in a Resource-Limited Setting
audits.st: IPBAI tool of ten domains aligned with WHO IPC core components
audits.f: General indicator score 72.5%; standard and transmission-based precautions 20%; environmental cleaning 0%; spill response 20%; antimicrobial stewardship 20%.
audits.c: Structured multimodal IPC training module delivered in two cycles to 607 healthcare workers.
audits.r2: General indicator score 94%; all ten domains 100%.

audits.t: Clinical audit in the Pediatric primary care office and overweight prevention in toddlers.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overweight/obesity 26.3%.
audits.c: Revised weaning and feeding protocol up to 36 months, mainly reducing excess protein and sugar.

audits.t: Evaluating documentation of social history in paediatric medical notes at a regional paediatric centre - a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Full compliance with comprehensive biopsychosocial history documentation for all medical admissions
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Teaching interventions, educational sessions and a survey of NCHDs

audits.t: Improving the quality of nursing documentation at a residential care home: a clinical audit.
audits.st: N-Catch II audit instrument: complete documentation (score 3) for admission assessment, nursing diagnoses, aims, interventions and evaluation
audits.f: No records met standards; mean scores from 0.4 (aims for nursing care) to 1.1 (nursing diagnoses).
audits.c: Tailored multifaceted implementation strategy addressing local barriers.
audits.r2: Improvement reported but standards not yet met (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Assessment of Malnutrition in Emergency Laparotomy Patients. A QIP Highlights Simple Measures To Improve Early Recognition and Optimisation of High-Risk Patients.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on nutritional assessment; accurate MUST scoring
audits.f: MUST accurate in 27 (54%); 23 (46%) inaccurate.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary approach and a standard online MUST calculator.

audits.t: Online prescribing for sexually transmitted infections – what’s on offer? An evaluation of internet pharmacies based in the United Kingdom
audits.st: British Association of Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines
audits.f: Gonorrhoea: 3 of 5 (60%) sold BASHH-approved antibiotics; chlamydia first-line options 22 of 25 (88%); herpes simplex 13 of 22 (59%); trichomonas 4 in line with BASHH.
audits.c: Results fed back to each provider.
audits.r2: Improvement in standards (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: The Role of Assistant Psychologists within Inpatient Units: A Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Assistant psychologist role in inpatient units
audits.st: Current guidelines for employment of assistant psychologists
audits.f: All standards unmet.

audits.t: Developing and Implementing a Quality Assurance Strategy for Electroconvulsive Therapy
audits.st: Electroconvulsive Therapy Accreditation Service (ECTAS) standards
audits.f: ECT prescription completed by consultant in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 40%.
audits.r2: ECT prescription completed in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 21%.

audits.t: An Assessment of the Management of Dizzy Patients in a Specialist Multi-Disciplinary Clinic; The Impact of Effective Telephone Triage
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 40% of patients referred with dizziness did not require a face-to-face appointment.
audits.c: Telephone triage to a rapid access BPPV clinic or a multidisciplinary complex balance clinic with audiologists, physiotherapists and ENT surgeons.
audits.r2: Only 35.8% streamed to face-to-face appointment; 90% of face-to-face appointments by non-ENT surgeons; 60% discharged after first assessment (61% previously).

audits.t: A national audit of pancreatic enzyme prescribing in pancreatic cancer from 2015 to 2023 in England using OpenSAFELY-TPP.
audits.tp: Pancreatic enzyme replacement in pancreatic cancer
audits.st: UK guidelines: PERT for all people with unresectable pancreatic cancer (100% standard)
audits.f: National PERT prescribing rates rose from 41% in 2015 to 48% in early 2023, still below the 100% standard.

audits.t: An Audit of Referrals to the Minor Operating Theater of the Patient Presenting in Otolaryngology OPD with Ear Discharge
audits.st: Hospital OPD guidelines enacted by the Pakistan Otolaryngology Association
audits.f: 52.5% of patients with ear discharge required referral to ENT theatre/emergency for suctioning.
audits.c: Changes in practice and simple protocols to allow ear suction in the outpatient clinic.
audits.r2: Referrals to ENT theatre fell to 9.5%.

audits.t: Pre-biologic screening and biologic monitoring in a tertiary dermatology department in Ireland
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for biologic therapy
audits.f: Baseline disease severity scores documented in 68%; full viral screen 87%; vaccination status 80%.
audits.c: Screening and monitoring checklists created and being implemented.

audits.t: Outcomes of newly referred patients with suspected angle closure: do we need to redefine the clinical pathways?
audits.st: Gonioscopy as reference standard for occludable angle
audits.f: 431/1754 (24.6%) were PACS referrals; only 42/393 (10.7%) had an occludable angle on gonioscopy
audits.c: Virtual clinic triaging criterion changed using AS-OCT

audits.t: An audit to assess and improve the quality of referrals received by Community Dental Services from General Dental Practitioners for the one-off treatments of patients under 18 years, with inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia, in Salford
audits.st: Referral quality/acceptance for inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia; no numeric target stated
audits.f: 48% acceptance rate; most referrals had 2 errors; almost 2 in 5 inhalation sedation referrals not justified appropriately or lacked a diagnosis.
audits.c: Contacted the triaging hub and local GDPs and created local triaging guidance.

audits.t: WHO Surgical Checklist in Transplant Surgery: Still another tick box exercise? Results from a Closed Loop Audit at a Medium-Sized Transplant Centre
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (Sign in, Time out, Sign out)
audits.f: Adherence to the WHO Surgical Checklist was less than optimal (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Recommendations from the 2014 audit (details not reported).
audits.r2: Checklist adhered to in 100% of operations (N=54) across all phases; statistically significant improvement in recall of patient ID and primary surgeon's name.

audits.t: Adequate Completion of Radiology Request Forms: A clinical Audit at Managil Teaching Hospital, Sudan
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists standard structured request form
audits.f: Many request forms incomplete; patient's age written in 13% of forms.
audits.c: A ready (pre-designed) request form was introduced.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in most areas; patient's age written in 92% of forms.

audits.t: Discharge summaries: One size does not fit all
audits.st: Essential discharge summary elements agreed with departmental clinicians
audits.f: Poor documentation, especially of medical issues during admission, clinical condition on discharge and safety-netting.
audits.c: Visual aid of key components placed above computer stations in junior doctors' offices and formal departmental teaching sessions.
audits.r2: Documentation in all key components improved dramatically (figures not given).

audits.t: Improving delirium assessments in acute senior health: A quality improvement project for care of the older person.
audits.st: NICE delirium guidelines
audits.f: Full delirium assessment 1.9%; formal diagnosis 5.8%.
audits.c: Posters and education-based multidisciplinary team interventions developed after literature analysis and ward discussion.

audits.t: Emergency paediatric bronchoscopy: A freely available, durable, effective training resource.
audits.st: Naming, function and assembly tasks for the paediatric bronchoscope; no external standard stated
audits.f: Baseline naming, function and assembly time scores recorded (figures not given).
audits.r2: Average improvements of 29% in naming and 15% in function scores; assembly time improved by an average of 49 seconds.

audits.t: Evaluation of criterion-based audit in improving quality of neonatal birth asphyxia care at Balaka district hospital in Malawi.
audits.st: Locally established criteria based on Malawi guidelines on care of the infant and newborn and WHO documents
audits.f: Vital signs checked 80%; laboratory investigations 0.9%; thermal support 82.7%; correct diagnosis 60%; correct treatment 18.7%; correct feeding 12.7%; clinical officer ward rounds 0%; daily weight check 49.1%.
audits.c: Gaps discussed by a multidisciplinary team and recommendations implemented (details not reported in abstract).
audits.r2: Vital signs 98.2% (p = 0.000); laboratory investigations 74%; thermal support 91.8% (p = 0.041); correct diagnosis 81% (p = 0.001); correct treatment 81%; correct feeding 56.4%; clinical officer ward rounds 72%; daily weight check 93%.

audits.t: Retrospective study on pain management pathway for patients with suspected renal/ ureteric colic in a U.K. accidents and emergency department: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: NICE guideline for pain management in suspected renal/ureteric colic: NSAIDs first line, IV paracetamol second, opioids third, no antispasmodics
audits.f: Full compliance with NICE pain management guidance in 23%; unsatisfactory in 78%.

audits.t: Clinical audit of the process of referral to genitourinary medicine of patients found to be chlamydia positive in a family planning service.
audits.st: All women having termination of pregnancy or IUD fitting offered chlamydia screening, informed of positive results and referred to GUM
audits.f: 999 offered a test and 988 tested; 38 positive (3.8%); result documented as given in 27/38 (74%); 24 (63%) seen in GUM.

audits.t: Children presenting with convulsions (including status epilepticus) to a paediatric accident and emergency department: an audit of a treatment protocol.
audits.tp: Acute convulsion and status epilepticus management
audits.st: Local convulsion protocol: diazepam 0.4 mg/kg up to two doses, then phenytoin 18 mg/kg with rectal paraldehyde 0.4 mL/kg
audits.f: Convulsion terminated in ED in 76 (94%); 69 (85%) after a single diazepam dose; 5/10 (50%) stopped with phenytoin plus paraldehyde; 9 (11%) needed ICU.

audits.t: Quality assurance of data collection in an aminoglycoside dosing service.
audits.st: Complete documentation of data needed to interpret serum aminoglycoside levels
audits.f: Complete documentation in 75% of pre-dose and 63% of post-dose levels.
audits.c: Education via Pharmacy Bulletin, revision of Laboratory and IV Medication Manuals, communication with head nurses and active pharmacist follow-up of missing information.
audits.r2: Complete documentation 93% for pre-dose and 84% for post-dose levels (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Do we measure up? The development of a multidisciplinary quality assurance and audit system in a psychiatric rehabilitation setting.
audits.st: Criteria for assessing performance in a long-term and rehabilitation setting (developed by the team)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of thrombolysis initiated in an accident and emergency department.
audits.st: Early thrombolysis after acute myocardial infarction; door to needle and pain to needle times
audits.f: Group 1 (thrombolysis in CCU): geometric mean door to needle 128 min, pain to needle 242 min.
audits.c: Selected patients given thrombolysis in the A and E department before transfer, after oral confirmation of myocardial infarction by the CCU admitting officer on receipt of a faxed ECG.
audits.r2: Group 2b (thrombolysis in A and E): geometric mean door to needle 38 min and pain to needle 141 min, v 121 min and 237 min in ineligible patients treated in CCU (group 2a, n=30); both p < 0.0001.

audits.t: Improving information given to patients before endoscopy: a regional audit.
audits.st: Regionally agreed 12-item standard for endoscopy information leaflets
audits.f: Leaflets included 35% (range 8-67%) of standard items.
audits.c: Each unit given a comparison of its leaflet with the standard.
audits.r2: All 11 units with new leaflets had made changes; 80% of items included overall.

audits.t: Improving management of asthma: closing the loop or progressing along the audit spiral?
audits.st: Checklist of important aspects of acute asthma management
audits.f: Oral corticosteroids 69 (68%); oxygen 62 (61%).

audits.t: Audit of bronchial artery embolisation in a specialist respiratory centre.
audits.st: Appropriateness of bronchial arteriography and embolisation for haemoptysis (retrospective assessment)
audits.f: 58 procedures in 35 patients; embolisation technically successful in 33/40 procedures for major haemoptysis, but haemoptysis recurred within 10 days in 17; overall success rate 40% (16/40).

audits.t: Audit of the use of doctors' holding power under Section 5(2) of the Mental Health Act 1983.
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 Section 5(2)
audits.f: 80 of 146 Section 5(2) orders converted to Section 2 or 3; Section 5(2) may have been used inappropriately in up to 45% of cases.

audits.t: Completing the clinical audit cycle: discharge medication.
audits.st: Three indicators: personal visits to pharmacy by ward staff and patients; nurse telephone calls chasing prescriptions; written patient complaints
audits.f: All three measures increased substantially compared with the previous four-month period.
audits.c: Action plan to change behaviour of consultants, junior doctors, ward and nursing staff, patients and pharmacy staff by raising awareness of the consequences of their actions.
audits.r2: Substantial reductions in all three measures.

audits.t: National audit of acute severe asthma in adults admitted to hospital. Standards of Care Committee, British Thoracic Society.
audits.tp: Acute severe asthma management in adults
audits.st: British Thoracic Society national guidelines for hospital management of acute severe asthma
audits.f: Peak flow measured initially in 661/766 (86%); arterial blood gases ever assessed in 534 (70%); 65 (8%) had no steroid in first 24 hours; peak flow variability measured before discharge in 597/759 (78%), of whom 334 (56%) had good control. Only 237 (31%) prescribed oral steroids before admission despite 429 (56%) having treatment increased.

audits.t: Education and audit can improve the identification of excessive drinkers among medical inpatients.
audits.st: Recording of quantitative alcohol history, CAGE questionnaire use and alcohol notification in discharge summaries
audits.f: Quantitative alcohol history in medical notes 175/792 (22%) and nursing notes 31/792 (4%); excessive drinkers identified 40/792 (5.1%).
audits.c: Training of junior medical and nursing staff, then feedback of results at a clinical audit meeting.
audits.r2: After audit feedback: quantitative history in medical notes 241/497 (48%) and nursing notes 237/497 (48%); excessive drinkers identified 45/497 (9.1%); chi 2 for trend p < 0.0001 for notes.

audits.t: Managing meningitis in children: audit of notifications, rifampicin chemoprophylaxis, and audiological referrals.
audits.st: Statutory notification, nationally agreed chemoprophylaxis and hearing assessment for all survivors
audits.f: Notified 20/36 (56%); chemoprophylaxis to 5/23 (22%) index cases; audiology arranged for 19/32 (59%) survivors.
audits.c: Written information for all doctors including each junior intake, and guidelines displayed on wards.

audits.t: Continuity of care on admission to hospital: an audit of Airedale NHS Trust's transfer policy.
audits.tp: Care transfer communication on hospital admission
audits.st: Airedale NHS Trust transfer policy
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Recommendations: pre-admission checklist, changes to nursing documentation, faster information transfer and clearer responsibility for contact across the hospital-community interface.

audits.t: Does medical audit lead to explicit standards? Experience with thrombolysis in four UK hospitals.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Locally set explicit standards for proportion of patients with definite and probable AMI given intravenous thrombolysis (technical standards in two hospitals, population standards in two)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Peer review meetings of baseline results, with standard setting requested by letter and telephone.
audits.r2: Six of the eight standards set were achieved in at least one of four audits in each hospital.

audits.t: Why is evaluation of the cost effectiveness of audit so difficult? The example of thrombolysis for suspected acute myocardial infarction.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Proportion of patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction given thrombolysis
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Repeated audits with a series of four audit meetings and subsequent actions.
audits.r2: Thrombolysis rose by 20% to 37% in three auditing hospitals and fell by 6% in the fourth (baseline over 90%); control rose 15%. Only one hospital differed significantly from control (51 extra treatments per year, 95% CI 0.5 to 61).

audits.t: An audit of the quality of operation notes in an otolaryngology unit.
audits.st: Operation notes should record accurate data, ward, department and name of surgeon, and avoid unacceptable abbreviations
audits.f: Clear identification of operating surgeon 74%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 53%.
audits.c: Aide-memoire attached to the front of the operation sheet.
audits.r2: Clear identification of operating surgeon 93%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 84%; all criteria improved.

audits.t: Quality of care of patients with diabetes: collation of data from multi-practice audits of diabetes in primary care.
audits.st: Annual key process measures for diabetes care
audits.f: Annual mean compliance: HbA1c or fructosamine 72.5%, fundi 67.5%, urine 65.8%, blood pressure 87.6%, smoking 71.4%, feet 67.7%, BMI 52.5%, with wide ranges between groups.

audits.t: Implementing evidence based medicine in general practice: audit and qualitative study of antithrombotic treatment for atrial fibrillation.
audits.st: Evidence-based antithrombotic (warfarin) treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation at risk of thromboembolism
audits.f: 132 of 13 239 patients had a history of atrial fibrillation, 100 of them at risk of thromboembolism.
audits.c: Assessment and educational interview with eligible patients about antithrombotic treatment.
audits.r2: After the study 52 patients were taking warfarin; of the other 48 (41 on aspirin), eight too ill, 16 unable to consent, four refused interview and 20 declined warfarin.

audits.t: Can audit improve antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice?
audits.st: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines issued as part of the audit
audits.f: 2316 antibiotic prescriptions issued; 81% for therapeutic reasons; amoxycillin most commonly prescribed (57.6% overall).
audits.c: Audit with an educational component and issuing of guidelines.
audits.r2: Prescriptions reduced by 42.5% to 1330; antibiotic regimens significantly changed.

audits.t: Cooperation between general practitioners and diabetologists and clinical audit improve the management of type 2 diabetic patients.
audits.st: Consensus guidelines based on French St Vincent recommendations
audits.f: Standards not met for several criteria; lack of HbA1c standardisation and delayed intervention for inadequate glucose control.
audits.c: Cooperative protocols for foot care, nephropathy and retinopathy prevention, HbA1c standardisation and a primary care educational programme.
audits.r2: Improvement in foot care (+33.6%), quality (+39.9%), HbA1c prescription (+11.9%), blood pressure control (+11.9%), lipids (+12.8%); early interventions for poor glucose control +10.5%.

audits.t: An audit of the investigation and treatment of localised prostatic cancer in the south west region.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean referral to clinic interval 67 days (54 days if GP PSA > 10 ng/ml, 104 days if < 10 ng/ml); 34% had radical treatment (10% prostatectomy, 24% radiotherapy); 27% hormone treatment; all had histological diagnosis and 84% were staged before treatment.

audits.t: Better by half: hypertension in the elderly and the 'rule of halves': a primary care audit of the clinical computer record as a springboard to improving care.
audits.st: 'Rule of halves' for hypertension; locally agreed guidelines and targets
audits.f: Using strict definitions the rule of halves still applied; using looser definitions three-quarters of hypertensives known, two-thirds treated and just under two-thirds controlled.
audits.c: Feedback of results to practices, agreed management guidelines, standardised computer recording, targets and review dates.

audits.t: An audit of primary surgical treatment for women with ovarian cancer referred to a cancer centre.
audits.st: National and international guidelines for initial surgery and staging of ovarian cancer
audits.f: 92% presented via outpatient clinic (elective surgery); up to seven consultants per hospital operated; less than half underwent the recommended surgical procedure

audits.t: An audit of waiting times in a haematology clinic before and after the introduction of point-of-care testing.
audits.st: Patient-set maximum clinic waiting time of 30 min (longer-term target 20 min)
audits.f: Patient survey of 50 consecutive patients set the standard; air-tube sample transport with electronic results did not achieve it despite repeated audits.
audits.c: Point-of-care testing in the clinic, with the backup analyser moved weekly and tests done by trained nurse specialists.
audits.r2: Clinic waiting times consistently achieved the standard.

audits.t: Introducing and auditing a nurse-led leg ulcer service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a nurse-led leg ulcer clinic.

audits.t: An audit of error rates in a UK district hospital transfusion laboratory.
audits.st: Error rates reported in the transfusion literature
audits.f: Most errors were preanalytical (incomplete sample or request form data) and corrected before action; main analytical errors were transcription of patient identification and incorrect blood group testing; main postanalytical error was nurses not following blood component collection procedures.

audits.t: Improving the repeat prescribing process in a busy general practice. A study using continuous quality improvement methodology.
audits.st: 48 hour target for processing repeat prescription requests
audits.f: Turnaround within 48 hours 95%; prescriptions needing records checked 18%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: synchronising repeat medications and recording drugs prescribed on visits, prioritising prescription signing at an agreed time, and moving prescription printing to reception.
audits.r2: Turnaround within 48 hours 99%; prescriptions needing records checked 8.6%.

audits.t: Oesophageal and gastric cancer pathology reporting: a regional audit.
audits.st: Minimum dataset (tumour type, depth of invasion, lymph node involvement, completeness of excision) and best practice reporting
audits.f: Minimum standards met in 77% of gastric (156/203) and 53% of oesophageal (42/79) resection reports; best practice in 20% of gastric and 18% of oesophageal reports.

audits.t: The investigation of iron deficiency anemia--a hospital based audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 94% had upper GI endoscopy (yield 54%, including 4 malignancies); 84% had lower GI investigation by colonoscopy or barium enema (yield 37%). Combined endoscopic and barium examinations gave a diagnosis in 69%; overall an underlying diagnosis was made in 92%.

audits.t: Quality assurance in myocardial perfusion tomography: a collaborative BNCS/BNMS audit programme. British Nuclear Cardiology Society/British nuclear Medicine Society.
audits.st: Expert panel scoring of six parameters (stress technique, radiopharmaceutical usage, image acquisition, processing, report images, report text) as good (2), adequate (1) or poor (0)
audits.f: Stress technique inadequate in 10 (11%) studies; radiopharmaceutical usage and acquisition inadequate in 5 (6%); processing inadequate in 8 (10%); report images inadequate in 2 (3%); report text inadequate in 21 of 66 (32%). Mean quality score 1.3 (range 0.5-2.0); 17 of 88 (19%) scored below 1.0.

audits.t: The British Association of Dermatologists audit of atopic eczema management in secondary care. Phase 3: audit of service outcome.
audits.st: Eight working standards for service outcome (e.g. 60% relative DLQI improvement, 70% improvement in sleep loss, 80% improvement in worst aspect, 80% return to work or school)
audits.f: Mean DLQI 12.5 falling to 9.7 at 6 weeks (P = 0.001); mean CDLQI 10.5 falling to 8.7. Sleep loss improved in 44% of adults and 47% of children (standard 70%); worst aspect improved in 61% of adults and 59% of children (standard 80%). Return to work/school 70% of adults and 87.5% of children (standard 80%). Only one of eight standards met nationally.

audits.t: A completed audit to reduce hospital outpatients non-attendance rates.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-attendance 34% (32.5% Europeans, 50% Asian patients).

audits.t: Informed choice in genetic screening for thalassaemia during pregnancy: audit from a national confidential inquiry.
audits.tp: Antenatal thalassaemia screening and informed choice
audits.st: Antenatal screening and counselling for haemoglobin disorders as standard UK practice; offer of prenatal diagnosis
audits.f: Risk detected by screening before or during first pregnancy in 49% (68/138) of couples. Prenatal diagnosis offered in 69% (274/400) of pregnancies; uptake 80% (216/274). Demonstrable service failure in 28% (110/400) of pregnancies.

audits.t: An audit of long-stay patients in an inner city palliative care centre.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A prospective audit of hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
audits.st: THRIFT risk assessment criteria
audits.f: Overall rate of clinically apparent hospital-acquired thromboembolic complications 0.4% (n = 35); 2.1% (n = 17) in the high-risk group. Prophylaxis did not appear to reduce incidence, even when stratified by risk.

audits.t: Prospective 5-year audit for day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Day-case rate 16%; successful day-case allocation 56%.
audits.c: 23-hour stay ward established, adding a third option.

audits.t: Management of acute pancreatitis: a comparative audit of clinical practice against the recommendations of the british society of gastroenterology
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology 1998 acute pancreatitis guidelines (e.g. mortality <10%, <30% in severe AP)
audits.f: Mortality 17% (standard <10%), 56% in severe AP (<30%); diagnosis within 48 h 100%; severity stratification about 80%; CRP measured in 51%; aetiology found in 77% (75-80%).
audits.c: None yet; prospective re-audit of 1999 admissions planned.

audits.t: An audit of antiretroviral medication offered to patients with HIV attending a district general hospital for outpatient care.
audits.st: British HIV Association (BHIVA) antiretroviral guidelines
audits.f: All patients eligible under BHIVA guidelines were being offered triple therapy. Viral load undetectable in 75% of 20 patients on their first established regimen and 36% of 14 patients who had failed at least one drug.

audits.t: The surgical management of cervical carcinoma within the South West of England: progress through an audit loop. Gynaecology Tumour Panel.
audits.st: Minimum clinical dataset; proposed targets 100% FIGO staging and 95% appropriate radical surgery
audits.f: Retrospective audit; results not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Prospective collection of a defined minimum dataset on paper forms.
audits.r2: FIGO staging 92% (98% for cases above Stage Ia); tumour diameter not measured in 20% and thickness in 28%.

audits.t: Methodological issues in the use of guidelines and audit to improve clinical effectiveness in breast cancer in one United Kingdom health region.
audits.st: Regional evidence-based breast cancer clinical guidelines and guideline targets
audits.f: Chemotherapy use 17% and axillary surgery 46% (previous studies in this population).
audits.c: Regional guidelines, senior clinicians as local leads, audit of quality, clinician ownership of data, confidential feedback to participants and education.
audits.r2: Chemotherapy use rose to 23% and axillary surgery to 76%.

audits.t: The role of staging CT scans in the treatment of prostate cancer: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All 97 had a planning CT; 85 also had a diagnostic staging CT, 51 (60%) with pelvic and abdominal imaging. 20 abnormalities were found in 19 patients; 13 were considered metastatic but only 4 altered treatment intent. Overall 4% were denied radical treatment on CT findings.

audits.t: Can district-wide audits improve primary care epilepsy management? An audit of seizure frequency recording.
audits.st: Recording of seizure frequency
audits.f: Seizure frequency recorded in 54.7%.
audits.r2: Seizure frequency recorded in 68% (improvement 13.2%, CI 8.9 to 17.6).

audits.t: An audit of the management of uterine malignancy within the West Midlands. West Midlands Gynaecological Oncology Group.
audits.st: 15 regional standards for uterine malignancy management
audits.f: Of 15 standards, 11 were met by at least one hospital; no hospital met all standards. Standards on initial referral and diagnostic intervals were universally failed. Outpatient diagnosis in only 30%. Surgery was usually within six weeks of diagnosis.

audits.t: Audit of time to emergency trauma laparotomy.
audits.tp: Major trauma time to CT and theatre
audits.st: Audit filter set at the upper quartile of emergency call to operating room time; comparison with national trauma database
audits.f: Median emergency call to operation 127 min (140 blunt, 86 penetrating); emergency department arrival to theatre 54 min. Audit filter selected 21 patients, with five correctable delays identified.

audits.t: The rate of breast-conserving surgery in early breast cancer: an audit of surgical practice at St Vincent's campus, NSW in 1990 and 1994.
audits.tp: Breast-conserving surgery rate in early breast cancer
audits.st: Comparison with published Australian breast-conserving surgery rates
audits.f: Breast-conserving surgery rate 33% in 1990 and 36% in 1994, lower than expected.

audits.t: A quality assurance audit: phase III trial of maximal androgen deprivation in prostate cancer (TROG 96.01).
audits.st: Technical adherence to the trial protocol
audits.f: Unacceptable protocol violation rate 10%.
audits.c: Improved audit design, staff education and increased data management resources.
audits.r2: Unacceptable protocol violation rate fell to 4%, with improved data quality and quantity.

audits.t: Comparative audit of tonsillectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Two-thirds had tonsillectomy for recurrent acute tonsillitis; 3% were day cases. Return to theatre for haemorrhage 0.75%; readmission almost 7%. 92% felt their throat was better and 88% were pleased they had the operation.

audits.t: Use of a computerised maternity information system to improve clinical effectiveness: thromboprophylaxis at caesarean section.
audits.st: Local thromboprophylaxis protocol for caesarean section
audits.f: Overtreatment of low-risk and undertreatment of high-risk women.
audits.c: Routine computer-generated risk assessment profile added to the maternity information system.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in protocol adherence in all risk groups.

audits.t: Monitoring quality of audit in obstetrics and gynaecology.
audits.st: Seven RCOG Clinical Audit Unit quality criteria for audit
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Significant improvement in audit quality over time.

audits.t: Integrated care pathways: an audit tool in paediatric oncology.
audits.st: Local standards set from neutropenia guidelines
audits.f: Retrospective notes review of care before the pathway; results not given in the abstract.
audits.c: Integrated care pathway for fever and neutropenia introduced to all members of the oncology unit.

audits.t: Audit of rheumatology services for adolescents and young adults in the UK. British Paediatric Rheumatology Group.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18% of units (n = 9) had a dedicated adolescent clinic. Seven clinics had a standardised transfer process, first discussed at a median age of 13 years, but none provided literature or pre-visits. Generic health issues were addressed by only two clinics.

audits.t: Quality assurance audit in an Australasian phase III trial of accelerated radiotherapy for head and neck cancer (TROG 91.01). Trans-Tasman Radiation Oncology Group.
audits.st: Technical adherence to the trial protocol
audits.f: Unacceptable protocol violation rate 10%.

audits.t: An audit of MRI for bone and soft-tissue tumours performed at referral centres.
audits.tp: MRI staging of bone and soft-tissue tumours
audits.st: MR imaging and reporting requirements for staging musculoskeletal tumours (e.g. whole-bone imaging for skip metastases)
audits.f: Mean 4 sequences (range 2-8); enhancement used in 19. Whole bone not imaged for skip metastases in 50% of appropriate cases. Reports (available in 40) commonly omitted intraosseous and extraosseous extent and relation to the neurovascular bundle and joint.

audits.t: An audit of indications and techniques for supraclavicular fossa irradiation in early breast cancer in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Supraclavicular fossa irradiation in early breast cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Significant variation in indications for supraclavicular fossa irradiation and in target volume definition; broad agreement on technique, including matching tangential and SCF fields.

audits.t: Performance and standards for the process of head and neck cancer care: South and West audit of head and neck cancer 1996-1997 (SWAHN I). South and West Regional Cancer Organisation Tumour Panel for Head and Neck Cancer.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer care standards
audits.st: Established standards for head and neck cancer care, e.g. pretreatment chest X-ray 95%, multidisciplinary clinic pretreatment 95%
audits.f: 59% had pretreatment chest X-ray (standard 95%); 45% seen in multidisciplinary clinic pretreatment (standard 95%); median cases per surgeon 4 (1-26), per radiotherapist 10 (1-51)

audits.t: Cost-effective prescribing of proton pump inhibitor therapy: an audit in general practice.
audits.st: Practice policy to step PPI therapy down to low-dose cost-effective therapy, or to antacids, H2 receptor antagonists or no treatment where PPI not needed
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Patients on PPI were identified and switched to low-dose therapy or alternatives where PPI was not required.

audits.t: Rationalised prescribing for community acquired pneumonia: a closed loop audit.
audits.st: Local management protocol for community acquired pneumonia
audits.f: 26% received intravenous penicillin or erythromycin.

audits.t: Incidence of incomplete excision in surgically treated basal cell carcinoma: a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.tp: Basal cell carcinoma management and histology reporting
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 41 of 879 lesions (4.7%) were incompletely excised in 754 patients; 16 were re-excised and the rest followed up.

audits.t: Reducing red blood cell transfusion in elective surgical patients: the role of audit and practice guidelines.
audits.st: Transfusion guidelines requiring haemoglobin measurement immediately before transfusion
audits.f: Two-unit transfusions were 60% of all transfusions; haemoglobin was rarely measured before transfusion and the main trigger was estimated blood loss over 500 ml. Mean blood loss with a 2-unit transfusion 608 (373) ml; post-transfusion haemoglobin 12.4 (1.8) g/dl.
audits.c: Transfusion guidelines introduced requiring haemoglobin measurement immediately before transfusion.
audits.r2: Total transfusions fell by 43%. Mean blood loss with a 2-unit transfusion rose to 1320 (644) ml (p < 0.01) and post-transfusion haemoglobin fell to 9.9 (2.4) g/dl (p < 0.01).

audits.t: Has the breast cancer 'two week wait' guarantee for assessment made any difference?
audits.st: Two-week wait guarantee for suspected breast cancer
audits.f: Cancer detection 22%; all cancers seen within 1 week; GP referral accuracy 42%; routine wait 4 weeks.
