audits.r2: Cancer detection 19%; 85% seen within 2 weeks; GP accuracy 49%; routine wait at least 8 weeks.

audits.t: Who should manage primary retinal detachments?
audits.st: not reported (authors suggest 85-90% single-procedure reattachment)
audits.f: Single-procedure reattachment 76.1%.
audits.c: Primary retinal reattachment surgery centralised in the specialist vitreoretinal unit.

audits.t: Audit of small-incision cataract surgery using an anterior chamber maintainer.
audits.st: Comparison with the National Cataract Surgery Survey (RCO 1993)
audits.f: 90% gained visual acuity at 3 months. Posterior capsule opacification 13%, comparable to the national survey; corneal endothelial decompensation and endophthalmitis marginally higher.

audits.t: Radiological review of accident and emergency radiographs: a 1-year audit.
audits.tp: Radiology reporting of emergency department radiographs
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 684 actual or suspected A&E interpretation errors flagged; 351 missed or strongly suspected fractures (mainly ankle, finger and elbow), 11 missed chest abnormalities and 24 A&E false positives. Further A&E action was taken in 286 (42.6%).

audits.t: Surgical management of intractable epistaxis: audit of results.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 8 patients had surgery (septoplasty, nasal packing, external carotid ligation); mean post-operative stay 3.9 days (range 3-6).
audits.c: Endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy, with or without anterior ethmoid artery diathermy, offered instead of conventional surgery.
audits.r2: 10 patients (7%) needed surgery, all endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy; mean post-operative stay 2.1 days (range 1-3); one recurrence managed conservatively and no surgical complications.

audits.t: Dementia care mapping: an approach to quality audit of services for people with dementia in two health districts.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline mapping highlighted limited staff-client interaction and a need for a wider range of activities to promote person-centred care.

audits.t: Audit of thromboprophylaxis following caesarean section.
audits.st: RCOG 1995 guidelines for thromboprophylaxis following caesarean section
audits.f: 62.9% were moderate and 20.4% high risk. Overall 34 (17%) of 200 eligible women received thromboprophylaxis.

audits.t: How are abnormal results for liver function tests dealt with in primary care? Audit of yield and impact.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Follow-up data in 873 (94%); 531 already under hospital review. Of 157 suitable for investigation, no further tests were requested in 91 (58%); in seven, results suggesting treatable chronic liver disease had not been followed up. On investigation 97 (62%) had a diagnosis needing hospital intervention or follow-up.

audits.t: Effect of audit on door-to-inflation times in primary angioplasty/stenting for acute myocardial infarction.
audits.st: Door-to-inflation time; no target stated
audits.f: Pre-audit mean door-to-inflation time similar to the national average (figure not given).
audits.r2: Door-to-inflation times markedly reduced (figures not given).

audits.t: Culturally sensitive mental health services through quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clinical file audits showed non-English-speaking patients received more pharmacological treatment and less cognitive behavioural therapy than English-speaking patients.
audits.c: Planned cross-cultural training, revised policies and procedures, and revised roles for bilingual counsellors as cultural consultants.

audits.t: A national audit to monitor and promote the uptake of clinical guidelines on the management of diabetes in pregnancy.
audits.st: National clinical guideline on management of diabetes in pregnancy (criterion-based audit)
audits.f: Antenatal care was organised in line with guideline recommendations, but formal prepregnancy care provision was lower and pregnancy planning and periconceptual care fell short of recommendations; care during pregnancy was meticulous.

audits.t: An audit of psychiatric case notes in relation to antipsychotic medication and information giving.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Case notes were examined for the type, nature and frequency of information given to patients on depot neuroleptics; results not given in the abstract.

audits.t: Drugs for dementia: the first year. An audit of prescribing practice.
audits.tp: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
audits.st: Department of Health and Social Services (March 1998) prescribing guidelines for drugs for dementia
audits.f: Guidelines generally followed; 3 patients prescribed drugs outside the guidelines; most failures (10) were due to poor recording of data in the clinical record.
audits.c: Changes made to documentation of patient assessments; suggestions made to review CREST guidelines.

audits.t: Neonatal cranial ultrasound interpretation: a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 42 of 59 questionnaires returned (71%); mean accurate identification of cerebral abnormalities 59% (range 45-71%); only 44% of neonatal registrars had formal training in cranial ultrasonography.

audits.t: An audit of general dental practitioners' referral practice following the distribution of third molar guidelines.
audits.st: Local guidelines for management of impacted third molars issued to general dental practitioners (April 1998)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Distribution of third molar referral guidelines to local general dental practitioners in April 1998.

audits.t: Audit of pain management at home following tonsillectomy in children.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 36 responders; 50% consulted their GP for pain; many had moderately severe to severe pain.
audits.c: Five days of discharge analgesia and improved written discharge advice.
audits.r2: 56 responders; GP consultation 27%; moderately severe to severe pain not reduced.

audits.t: Patterns of referral, management and survival of patients diagnosed with prostate cancer in Scotland during 1988 and 1993: results of a national, retrospective population-based audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 8% managed by both a urologist and a clinical oncologist within a year of diagnosis; 14% managed by clinical oncologists in first year; documentation of staging information was poor.
audits.r2: 13% managed by both a urologist and a clinical oncologist; 20% managed by clinical oncologists in first year.

audits.t: Audit of bloodborne virus infections in injecting drug users in general practice.
audits.tp: Bloodborne virus testing and hepatitis B immunisation in injecting drug users
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 115 studied: 71 tested for HBV (44% previous infection), 75 tested for hepatitis C antibodies (72% positive), 80 tested for HIV (33% positive).
audits.c: Attempts to improve testing and HBV immunisation; an abbreviated immunisation protocol was devised including post-vaccination checks and boosting; hepatitis C testing offered after counselling.
audits.r2: 99 tested for HBV (40% previous infection), 108 tested for hepatitis C antibodies (68% positive), 105 tested for HIV (25% positive).

audits.t: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation and contrast media reactions in a radiology department.
audits.tp: Contrast media reaction prevention and management
audits.st: National standards; knowledge score target 70%
audits.f: Resuscitation knowledge below 70% in all staff groups; radiologists' mean 50%.
audits.c: Retraining, guidelines and handouts, then wallcharts, lectures and regular feedback.
audits.r2: All staff groups surpassed the required standard.

audits.t: Community dental officers' use and knowledge of restorative techniques for primary molars: an audit of two Trusts in Wales.
audits.st: Research evidence on best practice in restorative techniques (stainless steel crowns)
audits.f: No dental officers were using stainless steel crowns routinely for restoring primary molars; all 18 used glass ionomer cement and amalgam; 6 used GIC exclusively; 11 used stainless steel crowns only with pulpotomy.

audits.t: Improving standards in the treatment of acute otitis externa by the use of a treatment protocol and open access to aural toilet.
audits.tp: Otitis externa management in emergency clinic
audits.st: Treatment protocol for acute otitis externa
audits.f: Heterogeneous approach and clinical isolation of junior staff.
audits.c: Treatment protocol, GP liaison and education, and open access aural toilet.
audits.r2: Treatment protocols effective and adhered to by junior staff.

audits.t: An audit of the management of the acute scrotum in children with Henoch-Schonlein Purpura.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 22 of 93 boys with HSP (24%) had scrotal involvement; 3/22 (14%) investigated radiologically; 8/22 (36%) had surgical exploration; none had testicular torsion.

audits.t: Burns and scalds in pre-school children attending accident and emergency: accident or abuse?
audits.st: Nine predetermined documentation standards for NAI in pre-school burns and scalds
audits.f: Documentation of NAI was poor; referral for further opinion 0%.
audits.c: NAI education programme and a reminder checklist in A&E notes.
audits.r2: Significant increases in several documentation items; checklist included in 60% of notes and completed in 97% of those; referral 3%.

audits.t: Re-audit of antiretroviral prescribing in HIV patients.
audits.st: British HIV Association guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Overall improvement in ART prescribing; one clinic still had many patients on suboptimal treatment.

audits.t: An audit of clinic consultation times in a cancer centre: implications for national manpower planning.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists calculation of 10 minutes per follow-up consultation
audits.f: 848 consultations in 81 clinics; of 67 clinics with finish time recorded, 19 (28%) finished on time and 48 (72%) were late by a mean of 49 minutes; follow-up consultations averaged 21 minutes.

audits.t: Emergency drug availability for the cardiac arrest team: a national audit.
audits.st: Resuscitation Council (UK) recommendations and international resuscitation guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: The reduction of broken appointments in general dental practice: an audit and intervention approach.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Majority of patients failing to attend were unemployed.
audits.c: Changes to recall letters and appointment cards (new methods of patient information) in two target groups.
audits.r2: Statistically significant reduction in failed appointments.

audits.t: Audit of acute admissions of COPD: standards of care and management in the hospital setting.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society COPD guidelines
audits.f: FEV1 recorded in 53%; arterial blood gases in 79% (range 40-100%); oxygen formally prescribed in 64% (range 9-94%); 35% of acidotic hypercapnic cases had no repeat blood gas and 13% received ventilatory support; smoking cessation advice documented in 30% of current smokers.

audits.t: An audit of management of differentiated thyroid cancer in specialist and non-specialist clinic settings.
audits.st: Points of good practice from published guidelines and reviews (adequacy of surgery, T4/TSH suppression, thyroglobulin monitoring, radioiodine ablation)
audits.f: Inadequate surgery and inadequate TSH suppression in approximately one-fifth of cases; ablative radioiodine not given despite being indicated in 11.7%; thyroglobulin monitoring and action inadequate in some cases.

audits.t: Regionalisation of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) screening improves compliance with guidelines: an audit of ROP screening in the Northern Region of England.
audits.st: National ROP screening guidelines; standard 100% compliance
audits.f: Compliance 47% (262/558).

audits.t: Public health physicians' knowledge of core skills and current policy: clinical audit by questionnaire.
audits.st: Model answers agreed by experts (no pass mark)
audits.f: Median uncorrected score 44 out of 80; no negative scores; highest scores on communicable disease and critical appraisal, lowest on Primary Care Trusts.

audits.t: Holding up a mirror: changing obstetric practice through criterion-based clinical audit in developing countries.
audits.st: 31 criterion-based audit criteria for good quality care of haemorrhage, eclampsia, genital tract infection, obstructed labour and uterine rupture
audits.f: Many common areas for improvement identified across the four hospitals.
audits.c: Feedback of findings and target setting; clinical protocols, reviews of staffing and training workshops.
audits.r2: Some aspects of clinical monitoring, drug use and record keeping improved significantly.

audits.t: Paediatric pelvic imaging: improvement in gonad shield placement by multidisciplinary audit.
audits.st: Gonad shield present, appropriate and correctly positioned where one should have been
audits.f: Gonad shield present in 77.9% of boys' films and 76% of girls' films where one should have been.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team formed; radiographer training and introduction of digital fluoroscopy for follow-up patients.
audits.r2: Gonad shield present in 85.2% of boys' films and 85.4% of girls' films.

audits.t: Failure to thrive in babies with cleft lip and palate.
audits.tp: Feeding and growth in cleft lip and palate
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Failure to thrive: unilateral cleft lip and palate 32%, bilateral 38%, cleft palate 49%, Pierre Robin sequence 100%.
audits.c: Feeding-support nurse appointed and supervised airway management for Pierre Robin sequence.
audits.r2: Failure to thrive: unilateral 9%, bilateral 20%, cleft palate 26%, Pierre Robin sequence 40%.

audits.t: Reducing waiting times for sleep apnoea hypopnoea syndrome and snoring using a questionnaire and home oximetry: results of a second audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Long waiting times, mainly from unnecessary interspecialty referrals.
audits.c: Questionnaire triage (symptoms, Epworth score, BMI) with home or video oximetry for higher-risk patients.
audits.r2: Wait to sleep study cut by about 90 days and to nCPAP trial by 32 days; ENT clinic visits reduced by over 50%.

audits.t: Effects of mental health training and clinical audit on general practitioners' management of common mental disorders.
audits.tp: GP management of common mental disorders
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: First audit of 33,235 patients; results not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Four-seminar training programme and practice audit with feedback.
audits.r2: Re-audit of 13,280 patients; audit alone did not improve mental health practice.

audits.t: Vestibular schwannoma screening: closing the audit loop.
audits.st: Local vestibular schwannoma screening guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Good agreement with guidelines and fewer inappropriate scan requests.

audits.t: A paediatric otolaryngology pre-admission assessment clinic audited.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clinic attendance 97%; 90% of attenders had their operation as planned; complications 2.9%; operation delayed in 20 patients, with no cause documented in 11.
audits.c: Senior House Officer now sees the patient on the day of admission rather than in the nurse-staffed pre-admission clinic.

audits.t: Sedation and analgesia for transvaginal oocyte retrieval: an audit resulting in a change of clinical practice.
audits.tp: Sedation and analgesia for oocyte retrieval
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Many women found single-dose intramuscular pethidine and prochlorperazine unsatisfactory and requested general anaesthesia for subsequent retrievals.
audits.c: Intravenous sedation and analgesia with midazolam and fentanyl introduced from June 1999.

audits.t: Closing the loop: the role of audit in reducing groin complications associated with coronary angiography.
audits.tp: Access site complications after coronary angiography
audits.st: Acceptable false aneurysm incidence 0.06-0.7%; US-directed compression success 50-93%
audits.f: False aneurysm incidence 1.5% vs 0.5% in historical controls.
audits.c: Fluoroscopy to identify the femoral head, strict adherence to sheath removal protocol and adequate analgesia and sedation before US compression.
audits.r2: False aneurysm incidence fell to the standard; US-directed compression successful in 100%.

audits.t: National audit of the blood transfusion process in the UK.
audits.st: Standard procedures for administration of blood and national transfusion guidelines
audits.f: Over 20% of hospitals had no Hospital Transfusion Committee; only one-third trained doctors in blood sampling; considerable variation in performance of standard procedures for administration of blood.
audits.r2: Little change in practice between the two audits.

audits.t: The impact of a 10-year audit cycle on blood usage in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Cross-match to transfusion ratio < 1.5
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Maximum blood order schedule implemented and continuously revised; review by hospital transfusion committee; usage reported by site, procedure and individual consultant.

audits.t: The psychosocial assessment of deliberate self harm: using clinical audit to improve the quality of the service.
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists' standards for general hospital management of adult deliberate self harm
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Simple service developments, including encouraging staff to use a comprehensive checklist.
audits.r2: Recording of information in case notes significantly improved in all areas of the psychosocial assessment.

audits.t: Achieving sustainable quality in maternity services - using audit of incontinence and dyspareunia to identify shortfalls in meeting standards.
audits.st: Established standards for childbirth complications (not specified)
audits.f: Questionnaire response 48% (470/970). At 9-14 months: dyspareunia 29% (102/347), urinary incontinence 35% (133/382), faecal incontinence 4% (17 women)

audits.t: Opportunity for audit: establishing and monitoring the use of protocols for nurse-led treatments of minor injuries.
audits.st: Assessment and treatment protocols for nurse-led minor injury treatment
audits.f: Baseline results reported but not given in the abstract.

audits.t: Local anaesthesia for vitreoretinal surgery: an audit of patient and surgical experience.
audits.st: Surgical standards and patient acceptability not compromised (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: 135 (76%) had local anaesthesia alone, 13 (7%) local with sedation, 29 (16%) general anaesthesia; 96.4% of patients compliant; 98.8% of operating conditions good or excellent; mean perioperative pain score 0.1 (range 0-1); 97% would choose local anaesthesia again.

audits.t: An audit of problems associated with urinary catheter withdrawal.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All-silicone catheters appeared to have a higher incidence of reported removal problems.

audits.t: Quality counts: auditing day-surgery services.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Pulse oximetry: an audit of nursing and medical staff understanding.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall deficit in knowledge of pulse oximetry; medical staff showed no greater knowledge than many trained nurses.

audits.t: The use of special observations: an audit within a psychiatric unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Person-centred care for people with dementia: a quality audit approach.
audits.st: Dementia care mapping (well-being values and Dementia Care Index)
audits.f: Results gave some idea of quality of care and identified where improvement and staff development were needed; no figures in the abstract.

audits.t: The introduction of a paediatric anaesthesia information leaflet: an audit of its impact on parental anxiety and satisfaction.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a paediatric anaesthesia information leaflet.
audits.r2: Parents who received the leaflet reported greater satisfaction with information provision than a control group; many perceived lower preoperative anxiety.

audits.t: Audit of a nurse endoscopist based one stop dyspepsia clinic.
audits.st: UK Health Department two week cancer wait initiative
audits.f: 84 gastroscoped the same day and 11 had an ultrasound scan; inappropriate tests avoided in 16%; 70% dealt with at a single attendance; waiting time rose progressively over the first six months.
audits.c: Introduction of a one-stop dyspepsia clinic with a nurse endoscopist and a purpose-designed referral form.

audits.t: A general practice pilot audit study to assess advice and treatment offered to women following hysterectomy.
audits.st: Offer of appropriate information on fracture prevention (advice and HRT) to hysterectomised women aged 25-64 years
audits.f: 2888 (50%) ever-users of HRT; 2083 (36%) current users (both ovaries removed 53%, one ovary removed 40%, both conserved 30%); 80% of those given HRT reported some advice, 77% of those not given HRT had received no advice.
audits.c: Women with no evidence of fracture prevention advice and not taking HRT were recalled for counselling.
audits.r2: By the end of the audit 424 had commenced HRT (20% increase); current use rose to 44% (both ovaries removed 59%, one ovary conserved 46%, both conserved 39%).

audits.t: An audit of oral care practice and staff knowledge in hospital palliative care.
audits.st: Oral care practice (assessment, implementation, prescribing, evaluation) and staff knowledge
audits.f: Baseline audit of oral care practice and nursing knowledge; numbers not reported.
audits.c: Oral care guidelines and a programme of ward-based teaching were introduced.
audits.r2: Improvement in all aspects of oral care and staff knowledge (numbers not reported).

audits.t: Detection of colorectal carcinoma on double contrast barium enema when double reporting is routinely performed: an audit of current practice.
audits.st: Miss rate compared with previous studies (15-24%) where double reporting was not used
audits.f: Of 70 patients with colorectal cancer who had a DCBE within 5 years, cancer was not diagnosed on DCBE in 5 (7%); 64 diagnosed on DCBE and 1 as a sessile polyp.

audits.t: An audit of referrals of children with autistic spectrum disorder to the dietetic service.
audits.tp: Dietetic referrals for autistic spectrum disorder
audits.st: Draft protocol agreed within the dietetic profession
audits.f: Requests for gluten-free and casein-free dietary advice and/or management of food selectivity and dysfunctional feeding behaviour made up the majority of referrals.

audits.t: An audit of oxygen prescribing in acute general medical wards.
audits.st: Oxygen should be prescribed
audits.f: Less than a fifth of patients receiving oxygen had a prescription written in their medical notes.

audits.t: The West Midlands "Severe Hypertensive Illness in Pregnancy" (SHIP) audit.
audits.tp: Management of severe hypertension in pregnancy
audits.st: Standard of care for acute-onset hypertension in pregnancy (not specified)
audits.f: 81% severe pre-eclampsia, 14% HELLP syndrome, 5% eclampsia; 7% admitted to intensive therapy unit; 70% of births preterm and 62% low birth weight.

audits.t: Keep taking the tablets? Evidence-based approaches to AD(H)D. Part 2: Audit and changing practice.
audits.st: New local standards set from the literature evidence
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Practice refined and new ways of assessment implemented.

audits.t: An audit of pressure ulcer incidence in a palliative care setting.
audits.st: Pressure ulcer incidence; Waterlow risk assessment
audits.f: 26.1% admitted with pressure ulcers and 12.0% developed pressure damage during stay; 95.3% accurately assessed at high or very high risk on Waterlow; 89.2% of ulcers Grade 1 or 2.

audits.t: The decision-to-delivery interval for emergency caesarean section: is 30 minutes a realistic target?
audits.st: Decision-to-delivery interval within 30 minutes
audits.f: Interval exceeded 30 minutes in 47 women (64%).
audits.r2: Target met in 71% of caesarean sections.

audits.t: Increased post-tonsillectomy secondary haemorrhage with disposable instruments: an audit cycle.
audits.st: Incidence of secondary haemorrhage after tonsillectomy
audits.f: 9.5% re-admitted with secondary haemorrhage and 4% required emergency surgery; with single-use bipolar forceps (57%), 16.8% re-admitted and 7% needed surgery; none of the 43% with ties re-admitted.
audits.c: Single-use bipolar diathermy forceps replaced by a new design.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in postoperative morbidity (numbers not reported).

audits.t: An audit of post-operative analgesia in children following tonsillectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Moderately severe to severe pain on return to ward 70%, as maximum score 85%, at discharge 6%.
audits.c: Pre-operative paracetamol and diclofenac, uniform printed post-operative prescription, uniform nursing policy and regular pain recording.
audits.r2: Moderately severe to severe pain on return to ward 48%, maximum score 56%, at discharge 2%.

audits.t: Retrospective audit of different antenatal screening policies for Down's syndrome in eight district general hospitals in one health region.
audits.st: Antenatal detection of Down's syndrome before 24 weeks' gestation
audits.f: 335 cases identified, 171 detected antenatally; detection 57% with serum screening, 52% with maternal age plus serum or nuchal translucency, 54% with maternal age 35+ and anomaly scans; least successful district 31%.

audits.t: The Leeds University Maternity Audit Project.
audits.st: Evidence-based recommendations: steroids in preterm delivery, antibiotics at Caesarean section, ventouse as first-choice instrument, PGA sutures for perineal repair
audits.f: Median unit rates: ventouse first choice 8%, PGA sutures 0%, steroids in preterm delivery 0%, antibiotics at Caesarean section 7%.
audits.c: No specific intervention; change over time assessed.
audits.r2: Ventouse 64% (range 0-98%), PGA sutures 72% (0-100%), steroids 82% (63-95%), antibiotics at Caesarean section 84% (10-100%).

audits.t: Factors influencing the use of thoracic radiotherapy in lung cancer--an analysis of the 1995 Scottish lung cancer audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1118 (30.8%) of 3855 patients received thoracic radiotherapy.

audits.t: Audit of primary care angina management in Sandwell, England.
audits.st: Sandwell's published angina audit criteria and local clinical guidelines
audits.f: Aspirin 66.5%, short-acting nitrates 62.1%, beta-blockers 58.4%; smoking advice 83.5%, weight 75.1%, alcohol 75.1%, exercise 64.5%; BP check 77.4%, cholesterol 40.5%, glucose 33.5%; none of the standards met.

audits.t: Preventing falls in older people: charting practice change by audit.
audits.tp: Falls risk screening and multifactorial assessment
audits.st: Formal falls risk assessment for older patients
audits.f: There was no formal means of assessing falls risk before the audit.
audits.c: Staff awareness raised and a specific falls-risk assessment developed.
audits.r2: Follow-up audits showed a change in practice, with the assessment widely used (numbers not reported).

audits.t: The safety and efficacy of peripheral intravenous catheters in ill neonates.
audits.st: Practice standards for peripheral intravenous catheters
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of turnaround times for processing Mycobacterium tuberculosis specimens in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Acceptable turnaround times for mycobacterial processing
audits.f: Median time to identification 21.5 days and to antibiotic susceptibility results 35 days.

audits.t: National sentinel clinical audit of evidence-based prescribing for older people: methodology and development.
audits.st: Evidence-based prescribing criteria for specific conditions in patients over 65, assessed by computerised algorithms
audits.f: Methodology paper; baseline results not given in the abstract.
audits.c: Feedback to participants plus nationally guided and locally driven intervention
audits.r2: Re-audit described as showing encouraging results; no figures given in the abstract.

audits.t: Patient recall of medication details in the outpatient clinic. Audit and assessment of the value of printed instructions requesting patients to bring medications to clinic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 774 patients on treatment, 15% attended with their tablets, 28% with a note, 40% empty handed but confident and 17% empty handed and unsure.
audits.c: Appointment cards stamped with the request to bring medications to the cardiology clinic.

audits.t: Triple cycle audit of primary retinal detachment surgery.
audits.st: Goal of 100% retinal reattachment
audits.f: Primary reattachment 67%, final success 84%; vitrectomies 1.5%, open conventional procedures 78%; visual acuity 6/12 or better 55%.
audits.c: Increasing subspecialisation and organisational changes; shift in operative technique.
audits.r2: Primary reattachment 87% (P = 0.0004), final success 97% (P = 0.0003); vitrectomies 48%; visual acuity 6/12 or better 49% (P = 0.34).

audits.t: A completed audit cycle and integrated care pathway for the management of depression following brain injury in a rehabilitation setting.
audits.st: Locally set standards for documentation, assessment, management and review of depression
audits.f: Baseline mood and start of medication documented in 54-61%; review 29%; subsequent treatment 27%.
audits.c: Evidence-based multidisciplinary integrated care pathway (ICP) for depression
audits.r2: All documentation standards improved to 94-100%, except assessment with a validated measure (84%) and follow-up assessment (76%).

audits.t: An audit of outpatient management of pelvic inflammatory disease.
audits.tp: Outpatient management of pelvic inflammatory disease
audits.st: Current standard of care for PID
audits.f: Chlamydia 30%, gonorrhoea 4%; with oral doxycycline and metronidazole, symptoms resolved in 57%, 18% persistent, 25% did not attend follow-up; partner notification discussed in 87%.
audits.c: Antibiotic regimen for PID changed in the department.

audits.t: A pragmatic approach to dosimetric audit in radiotherapy.
audits.st: Detection of dosimetric errors greater than 5%
audits.f: No dose discrepancies greater than 5% detected.

audits.t: Lingual nerve injury subsequent to wisdom teeth removal--a 5-year retrospective audit from a high street dental practice.
audits.tp: Lingual nerve injury after wisdom tooth removal
audits.st: Established lingual nerve injury rates reported elsewhere
audits.f: Low incidence of lingual nerve trauma, comparable with that reported elsewhere (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: A criterion audit of women's awareness of blood transfusion in pregnancy.
audits.st: Set audit standard on women's awareness of blood transfusion in pregnancy (CEMD report); target not stated
audits.f: Response rate 100%; 43% aware of possible need for transfusion in pregnancy; 92% would accept transfusion; 4% would refuse for religious reasons or infection risk; 4% gave no reason

audits.t: A critical audit of the surgical management of intractable epistaxis using sphenopalatine artery ligation/diathermy.
audits.st: Success rates from the literature
audits.f: Recurrent bleed rate 33% after SPA ligation/diathermy, higher than published results; mean stay 3.3 days.

audits.t: Mouth care in cancer nursing: using an audit to change practice.
audits.st: Mouth care practice and staff knowledge
audits.f: Oral problems common but under-reported, underdiagnosed, inadequately treated and inadequately documented; nursing knowledge deficits.
audits.c: Oral care guidelines, patient information leaflets, posters and staff education programme.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in diagnosis and treatment of oral problems and increased patient reporting (numbers not reported).

audits.t: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) guidelines on tonsillectomy: a three cycle audit of clinical record keeping and adherence to national guidelines.
audits.st: SIGN guidelines (January 1999) on indications for tonsillectomy
audits.f: Documentation of number of tonsillitis attacks 30%; adherence to SIGN in documented cases 75%.
audits.c: Publication of SIGN guidelines, then presentation of the results of cohorts 1 and 2.

audits.t: Audit of cancer pain management in a cancer centre.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 186 patients, 52 had cancer pain and 47 assessed; more than half had unrelieved pain that was severe at worst.

audits.t: Audit in practice: the referral of dying patients to palliative care.
audits.st: Referral of dying inpatients to the palliative care service
audits.f: Relatively few dying patients were referred to the palliative care team.
audits.c: Audit data presented on several occasions to nursing and medical staff.

audits.t: An audit of subcutaneous syringe drivers in a non-specialist hospital.
audits.tp: Syringe driver use in palliative care
audits.st: Standard of current practice in syringe driver use (MDA 1998 concerns)
audits.f: Many areas of unregulated practice in setting up, monitoring and maintaining syringe drivers; drug choice, doses, evaluation and review of treatment were also of concern.

audits.t: The use of oxygen in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a prospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management.
audits.st: National COPD guidelines: initial FiO2 no more than 0.28
audits.f: Oxygen with FiO2 above 0.28 was common and predominantly initiated in the ambulance (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Blood pressure measurement--does anyone do it right?: An assessment of the reliability of equipment in use and the measurement techniques of clinicians.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 82% response on equipment showed it in relatively good condition but with maintenance and health and safety problems; 67% response on technique showed considerable variation in measurement technique.
audits.c: All mercury devices replaced with aneroid devices; staff guidelines and updating on measurement technique

audits.t: Evaluating and developing contraceptive services: the results of an audit of the North Lambeth Primary Care Commissioning Group.
audits.tp: Contraceptive service provision in general practice
audits.st: Literature-derived factors for effective, acceptable, accessible and equitable contraceptive services
audits.f: Scope for development in all key areas; practice leaflet and waiting area information on contraceptive services generally limited.

audits.t: Audit of acute myocardial infarctions at Saint James's Hospital, Dublin, from 1996 to 1999.
audits.st: Comparison with trial evidence and 1992 figures
audits.f: Revascularisation 72% (thrombolysis 67%, primary angioplasty 5%) vs 35% in 1992; aspirin or warfarin 99%, beta-blockers 67%, ACE inhibitors 34%, statins 28%; case fatality 16%.

audits.t: Secondary prevention following myocardial infarction: evidence from an audit in South Wales that the National Service Framework for coronary heart disease does not address all the issues.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: National Service Framework for coronary heart disease: 80-90% prescribed appropriate secondary prevention by April 2002
audits.f: At discharge, unless contraindicated: aspirin 100%, beta-blockers 84%, statin and/or dietetic advice 66%, ACE inhibitors in heart failure 97%.

audits.t: Guidelines, compliance, and effectiveness: a 12 months' audit in an acute district general healthcare trust on the two week rule for suspected colorectal cancer.
audits.st: Department of Health two week rule: suspected colorectal cancer seen within two weeks of GP referral; referral guideline criteria
audits.f: 96.2% given appointments within two weeks; 97.4% of referrals incomplete and 37.6% did not comply with the guidelines.

audits.t: Open-access endoscopy: are age-based guidelines justified? An audit of experience of 1000 open-access endoscopies at a district general hospital.
audits.st: Accepted guidelines for open-access endoscopy
audits.f: 301 (30.1%) did not meet accepted guidelines; no malignancy would have been missed if guidelines applied; malignancy in 17 patients, all died.

audits.t: A national pilot to implement pressure ulcer guidelines: results of the baseline audit.
audits.tp: Pressure ulcer risk assessment and prevention
audits.st: RCN clinical guideline on pressure ulcer risk assessment and prevention
audits.f: Baseline audit provisional results reported; no figures given in abstract.
audits.c: Tailored, evidence-based dissemination and implementation strategy with implementation resources and local initiatives.

audits.t: The National Health Service Breast Screening Programme and British Association of Surgical Oncology audit of quality assurance in breast screening 1996-2001.
audits.st: NHSBSP clinical outcome measures defined by surgeons, radiologists and pathologists; preoperative diagnosis rate minimum standard 70 per cent or more
audits.f: Preoperative diagnosis rate 63 per cent; lymph node status recorded in 81 per cent.
audits.c: Feedback of results and dissemination of good practice at local and national level.
audits.r2: Preoperative diagnosis rate 87 per cent; lymph node status recorded in 93 per cent.

audits.t: The 'Severe Hypertensive Illness in Pregnancy' (SHIP) audit: promoting quality care using a high risk monitoring chart and eclampsia treatment pack.
audits.st: Audit standards for care of severe hypertensive illness in pregnancy (not detailed in abstract)
audits.f: Baseline compliance with audit standards measured; figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: Feedback of baseline results to each hospital, a high risk monitoring chart and an eclampsia treatment pack.
audits.r2: Compliance increased in all but one standard; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Evaluation of emergency caesarean sections--completion of the audit cycle in a Central London teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Total CS rate 20.9%; emergency CS 14.8%; failure to progress delivered within 1 hour 76%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 60%; ranitidine prescribed 53%; heparin 88%.
audits.r2: Total CS rate 19.2%; emergency CS 13.6%; failure to progress within 1 hour 64%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 96%; ranitidine 81%; heparin 87%.

audits.t: A prospective audit of external cephalic version at term: are ultrasound parameters predictive of outcome?
audits.tp: External cephalic version for breech presentation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 102 breech presentations at term; 47 women had ECV with 55% success and no adverse outcomes; only 49% of women with uncomplicated breech agreed to ECV.

audits.t: A prospective regional audit of surgical management of endometrial cancer in the South and West of England.
audits.st: Basic staging procedures for endometrial cancer (minimum data set defined)
audits.f: Only one-third of patients had basic staging procedures performed fully.

audits.t: Audit on the use of thromboprophylaxis during caesarean section.
audits.st: RCOG 1995 working party: risk assessment for all caesarean sections and heparin prophylaxis if high risk
audits.f: Heparin given to 0% of high-risk emergency and 25% of high-risk elective caesarean sections.
audits.c: Structured thromboembolism risk assessment form for every caesarean section
audits.r2: Adequate heparin prophylaxis in 72.7% of high-risk emergency and 85.7% of high-risk elective caesarean sections.

audits.t: Development of a treatment outcome standard as a result of a clinical audit of the outcome of fixed appliance therapy undertaken by hospital-based consultant orthodontists in the UK.
audits.st: Audit used to establish a benchmark outcome standard for consultant fixed appliance treatment
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Third regional audit of antiretroviral prescribing in HIV patients.
audits.st: BHIVA guidelines
audits.f: Not reported in detail.
audits.r2: Improvement with more patients on three or more drugs; 53% of patients on ART had viral load <50 copies/mL; 42% of ART-naive starters suppressed at 24 weeks.

audits.t: An audit of the hepatitis B vaccination status of staff in general dental practices in Lancashire.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination status of healthcare staff
audits.st: British Dental Association recommendations on vaccination against hepatitis B
audits.f: Vaccinated: 98.9% of dentists, 96.7% of nurses, 72.7% of non-clinical staff. Written evidence of immune status: 46.5% of dentists, 51.0% of nurses, 62.5% of non-clinical staff.

audits.t: Audit of a policy of magnetic resonance imaging with diffusion-weighted imaging as first-line neuroimaging for in-patients with clinically suspected acute stroke.
audits.tp: First-line neuroimaging in suspected acute stroke
audits.st: Local policy of diffusion-weighted MRI as first-line neuroimaging for suspected acute stroke
audits.f: Audit standard achieved in 88 (73.9%) of 119 MRI-safe patients; 31 had CT first because of lack of MRI capacity.

audits.t: Open access echocardiography: a prospective audit of referral patterns from primary care.
audits.st: Recently published recommendations and guidelines for open access echocardiography (not specified)
audits.f: Waiting time for open access echo shorter than for outpatient clinic; numeric compliance not reported in abstract.

audits.t: A complete audit cycle of intrapartum group B streptococcus prophylaxis.
audits.st: Local intrapartum prophylaxis protocol: adequate if antibiotics given more than 4 hours before delivery in women with risk factors
audits.f: Of 359 deliveries, 37 (10.3%) had risk factors; adequate prophylaxis in 32%.
audits.c: Changes to the indications for prophylaxis in the protocol and circulation of results to medical and midwifery staff
audits.r2: Of 378 deliveries, 49 (13%) had risk factors; adequate prophylaxis in 42%.

audits.t: A national audit of radiotherapy in head and neck cancer.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy treatment interruptions and waiting times
audits.st: Published guidelines on compensation for treatment gaps and national waiting time targets
audits.f: 55 of 56 centres returned data. 1467 (55%) had one or more interruptions; of these 56% still completed on time but 32% had no attempted compensation. Seven centres had no interruption policy. Mean time from first clinic visit to radiotherapy 40 days; six centres averaged under 28 days.

audits.t: An audit of delays before and during radical radiotherapy for cervical cancer--effect on tumour cure probability.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy treatment interruptions and waiting times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 22% completed EBRT without interruption; median overall treatment time 49 days; median wait to start radiotherapy 14 days.
audits.r2: 94% completed EBRT without interruption (P = 0.0009); median overall treatment time 39 days (P = 0.001); median wait increased to 35 days (P = 0.007).

audits.t: Management of colorectal cancer: variations in practice in one hospital.
audits.st: RCS England and ACPGBI 1996 guidelines for colorectal cancer management
audits.f: Marked variation; colorectal specialists more likely to meet guidelines, performed fewer APRs and more extensive lymphadenectomy.
audits.r2: Compliance with guidelines markedly improved and fewer rectal procedures done by non-colorectal surgeons.

audits.t: Reducing antibiotic use on the neonatal unit by improving communication of blood culture results: a completed audit cycle.
audits.tp: Antibiotic use for suspected early onset neonatal infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Improved communication of blood culture results.

audits.t: Patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction to a district general hospital: baseline results and effect of audit.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis call to needle time in myocardial infarction
audits.st: Cardiovascular Health Strategy: thrombolysis within ninety minutes of alerting medical or ambulance services
audits.f: Thrombolysis given in 31%; median call to needle time 200 minutes (rural median 227.5 minutes, n = 64; urban median 175 minutes, n = 37). Median arrival to CCU 90 minutes.

audits.t: National audit of emergency department child protection procedures.
audits.tp: Child protection procedures in the emergency department
audits.st: Two official 1999 documents on child protection procedures and staffing in emergency departments
audits.f: Many standards met; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Clinical outcome monitoring program (COMP): a new application for use in orthodontic audits and research.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average PAR improvement 77.5% for the unit; clinician A marginally better than clinician B.

audits.t: An audit of out of hours interventional vascular radiology.
audits.tp: Out of hours interventional radiology workload
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists 1996 guidelines that units should regularly assess their out of hours workload
audits.f: 1093 (57%) under vascular surgeons; only 17 (1.6%) of these investigated out of hours; 13/17 (76%) had intervention within 24 h.

audits.t: An audit of the laboratory interpretation of growth hormone response to insulin-induced hypoglycaemia in the assessment of short stature in children.
audits.tp: Laboratory interpretation of growth hormone stimulation tests
audits.st: Consensus cut-off concentrations for GH response in insulin stress test
audits.f: A number of laboratories used out-of-consensus cut-offs; five laboratories (9.6%) reported equivocal results for specimens not indicative of GH deficiency.

audits.t: National guidance on gynaecological cancer management: an audit of gynaecological cancer services and management in the South East of England.
audits.st: National guidance on gynaecological cancer management (centre/unit requirements, FIGO stage-based management)
audits.f: Ovarian cancer: stage recorded in 53% (262/492); 81% (169/209) managed per guidelines. Cervical cancer: stage recorded in 60% (188/315); 76% (142/188) managed per guidelines; 40% (127/315) not assessable.

audits.t: Using audit to monitor and improve the quality of anaesthesia for caesarean section.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: General anaesthesia in 58.0% of emergency and 45.5% of elective sections (53.0% overall); 25.3% had anaesthetic complications or side-effects; 90.3% satisfied.
audits.c: Findings presented to the multidisciplinary team and changes to anaesthetic practice introduced
audits.r2: General anaesthesia fell to 23.8% (P < 0.05); complications or side-effects 17.2%; satisfaction maintained.

audits.t: Audit of chest X-rays in general practice--a case for local guidelines?
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists referral guidelines, including six weeks' delay after onset of chest wall pain
audits.f: 569 CXRs in 482 patients; 30% assessed as not indicated.

audits.t: Breast cancer audit: adapting national audit frameworks for local review of clinical practice.
audits.st: Scottish Cancer Therapy Network (SCTN) minimum data set for breast cancer
audits.f: Minimum data set identified outliers from the normal range of process indicators; no figures given in abstract.

audits.t: An audit of the vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis practices amongst patients splenectomised in Lothian.
audits.st: Department of Health guidelines on post-splenectomy vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis
audits.f: Vaccinated against S. pneumoniae 80.6%, H. influenzae 65.9%, N. meningitidis 48.2%; 74.8% on long-term prophylaxis; only 37.4% both vaccinated and on prophylaxis as recommended.

audits.t: Audit can ensure the safe and effective introduction of seizure prophylaxis with magnesium sulphate in obstetric practice.
audits.st: Local magnesium sulphate protocol compliance and achievement of therapeutic magnesium levels
audits.f: Protocol violations caused delayed therapeutic levels or high magnesium concentrations in 5 of 8 cases.
audits.c: Circulation of results and staff education
audits.r2: Near complete protocol compliance and more consistent time to therapeutic magnesium concentration.

audits.t: An audit of the implementation of guidelines to reduce wound infection following caesarean section.
audits.st: National guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis at caesarean section; wound infection rate <5%
audits.f: Wound infection rate 10%; failure to give antibiotics, especially at elective caesarean section.
audits.c: Local protocol for antibiotics at all caesarean sections introduced.

audits.t: Significant improvement in quality of caesarean section documentation with dedicated operative proforma--completion of the audit cycle.
audits.st: CNST documentation guidelines
audits.f: Under 80% documented several key items; only 41% had complete signature with printed name and 35% correct time and date.
audits.c: Dedicated caesarean 'operative delivery note' proforma designed to CNST guidelines
audits.r2: Significant improvement in almost all items assessed.

audits.t: Audit of primary care and initial secondary care investigations set against RCOG guidelines as standard in cases of subfertility.
audits.st: RCOG evidence-based guidelines on initial investigation of the infertile couple
audits.f: Mid-luteal progesterone and semen analysis performed correctly with results available in only 33% and 2% of occasions; many patients lacked clearly documented advice.

audits.t: An audit of interventions for dual diagnosis in a psychiatric unit.
audits.tp: Dual diagnosis interventions in mental health
audits.st: Key standards for dual diagnosis care based on national and local recommendations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Training programme on dual diagnosis for mental health nurses.
audits.r2: Improvement observed in standards of care; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Monitoring blood transfusion in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting: an audit methodology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 47.4% of patients received red blood cell transfusion.
audits.c: Transfusion database built from patient administration system and blood transfusion service data allowing continuous audit.
