audits.t: Completed audit cycle to explore the use of the STOPP/START toolkit to optimise medication in psychiatric in-patients with dementia.
audits.st: STOPP/START criteria
audits.f: Benzodiazepines, antipsychotics and opiates most commonly prescribed inappropriately; statins, calcium and vitamin D most commonly unprescribed
audits.r2: Overall 7% reduction in comorbidities and 8% reduction in prescriptions (average prescriptions per patient P = 0.022)

audits.t: POST-OP: A Strategy to Improve Clinical Documentation in the Early Postoperative Period.
audits.st: RCS Good Surgical Practice documentation standards
audits.f: Patient identification 17.8%; thromboprophylaxis 7.1%.
audits.c: POST-OP mnemonic educational tool (physiotherapy, operative diagnosis, sepsis, thromboprophylaxis, oral intake/fluid balance, pain).
audits.r2: Patient identification 78.1% (p 0.001); thromboprophylaxis 75.8%; all standards improved.

audits.t: Evaluation of a newly introduced tonsillectomy operation record for the analysis of regional post-tonsillectomy bleed data: a quality improvement project at the London North West Healthcare NHS Trust.
audits.st: National recommendations for post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage audit
audits.f: 62 of 642 (9.7%) had post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage and 19 (2.9%) returned to theatre; free-text operative data were variable and did not allow factor analysis.
audits.c: Standardised paper tonsillectomy operation proforma, then an electronic version.
audits.r2: Completeness and quality of data significantly improved after the paper proforma and further after the electronic proforma.

audits.t: Optimisation of intravenous fluid prescribing: framework for changing practice through education and audits.
audits.st: 2013 NICE intravenous fluid guidelines (target 100% adherence)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Intravenous fluid team with educative, managerial, administrative and technological measures from 2015.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in appropriateness of maintenance and replacement fluids since March 2016; 29-fold increase in use of 4% dextrose/0.18% sodium chloride as maintenance fluid since 2015.

audits.t: Obstetric competence and compliance with surgical hand antisepsis prior to elective and emergency surgical procedures: a closed-loop audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.c: Pathway mapping for specific anatomical areas to standardise delegated treatments, competence and training needs analysis, and training of physiotherapy assistants before pathway implementation.
audits.r2: Time spent treating patients rose to 16%; job satisfaction 100%.

audits.t: Audit of physical health monitoring in children and adolescents receiving antipsychotics in neurodevelopmental clinics in Northumberland.

audits.t: Improvement to visualization of nodes in breast cancer patients following audit: are we seeing the problem?
audits.tp: Sentinel node visualisation in breast lymphoscintigraphy
audits.st: Guidelines: nodes visualised in more than 95% of patients
audits.f: Nodes visualised in 81% of patients.
audits.c: Changes to the injection and imaging technique after a period of investigation and review.
audits.r2: Node visualisation rate 97%, meeting the standard.

audits.t: Electrocardiographic Monitoring of Psychiatric In-patients Taking Antipsychotic Medications.

audits.c: Quality improvement interventions delivered after baseline audit (not detailed in abstract).

audits.t: Can patient safety be improved by reducing the volume of "inappropriate prescribing tasks" handed over to out-of-hours junior doctors?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Inappropriate prescribing tasks (mainly oral anticoagulation and drug chart rewrites) quantified from the computerised task system.
audits.c: Friday morning checklist for ward teams to check drug charts would not need oral anticoagulation or rewriting over the weekend.
audits.r2: Overall 46% reduction in inappropriate prescribing tasks; 65% reduction in inappropriate oral anticoagulation prescribing and 30% in drug chart rewrites; mean reduction 6.94% of prescribing tasks (95% CI -0.54 to 14.42, p=0.062).

audits.t: A re-audit of cervical screening uptake in a dermatology cohort on immunosuppressive medications.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Antimicrobial stewardship in the neonatal unit reduces antibiotic exposure.
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines
audits.f: 572 days of therapy (DOT) per 1000 patient days; courses >36 hours in negative sepsis evaluations 82 DOT; courses >5 days for culture-negative sepsis 46.5 DOT.
audits.c: Educational interventions and introduction of electronic prescribing in the neonatal unit.
audits.r2: 417 DOT per 1000 patient days (27% reduction); courses >36 hours in negative sepsis evaluations 7.5 DOT; courses >5 days for culture-negative sepsis 7 DOT.

audits.t: Audit of child maltreatment medical assessments in a culturally diverse, metropolitan setting.
audits.st: Established minimum standards for clinical assessment of child maltreatment
audits.f: Most assessments were multidisciplinary and used protocols; half were not followed up; a third were after-hours and a third had no carer present.

audits.t: A UK clinical audit addressing the quality of prescribing of sodium valproate for bipolar disorder in women of childbearing age.
audits.st: National treatment guidelines and safety alerts on valproate in women of childbearing age
audits.f: Valproate prescribed for 24% of women and 43% of men aged 50 or under; documented information on risks to the unborn child and contraception for only half of such women.

audits.t: Managing antibiotics wisely: a quality improvement programme in a tertiary neonatal unit in the UK.
audits.st: Reduce antibiotic usage rate by 20% of baseline by 31 December 2016
audits.f: Baseline median antibiotic usage rate 347 per 1000 patient-days; antibiotics stopped within 36-48 hours in 32.5% of culture-negative sepsis screens.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary quality improvement programme with Vermont Oxford Network, shared strategies and PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Antibiotic usage rate reduced to 198 per 1000 patient-days (43% reduction); stopping within 36-48 hours rose to 91%; antibiotic days per patient fell from median 3 to 2.

audits.t: Caesarean section audit to improve quality of care in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania.
audits.st: Appropriateness of Caesarean section indications judged by local audit panel and external auditor
audits.f: Unjustified Caesarean sections 34% (local panel) and 75% (external auditor).
audits.c: Introduction of a focused Caesarean section audit system with local panel and external auditor review.
audits.r2: Unjustified Caesarean sections fell to 23% (p = 0.29) and 52% (p = 0.01) by local panel and external auditor respectively.

audits.t: Management of children and young people (CYP) with asthma: a clinical audit report.
audits.st: National Review of Asthma Deaths (NRAD) recommendations
audits.f: Risks for future attacks not recognised, few assessed objectively during attacks and only 10% of attacks followed up within 2 days.

audits.t: Barriers to improving tracheostomy care in low- and middle-income countries: Our experience of a 23 patient closed loop audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Orbital infections: a complete cycle 7-year audit and a management guideline.
audits.st: not reported (new local multidisciplinary guideline developed)
audits.f: not reported

audits.r2: Standardising management proved achievable through the guideline (no figures given).

audits.t: Bedside paediatric HIV testing in Malawi: Impact on testing rates.

audits.t: Piloting online self-audit of methadone treatment in Irish general practice: results, reflections and educational outcomes.
audits.st: 25 essential national criteria for methadone maintenance treatment provision
audits.f: The majority of GPs scored 80% or over on the 25 essential criteria.

audits.t: Implementing a standardised discharge analgesia guideline to reduce paediatric post tonsillectomy pain.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25 (16.6%) readmitted; 13 (8.6%) readmitted for pain control; 12 (7.9%) postoperative haemorrhage; discharge analgesia varied widely.

audits.r2: 17 (14.4%) readmitted; 0 readmitted for pain control (reduction from 7.3% to 0%, p = 0.0027); 12 (10.2%) postoperative haemorrhage.

audits.t: Otitis Externa in Secondary Care: A Change in Our Practice Following a Full Cycle Audit.
audits.tp: Otitis externa management in emergency clinic
audits.st: NICE guideline for otitis externa
audits.f: Ear swabs sent in 14 of 19 cases; Sofradex most popular empirical eardrop
audits.c: Recommendation of Betnesol-N and swabs only for refractory cases, disseminated by posters and email reminders
audits.r2: Ear swabs sent in 3 of 25 cases; Betnesol-N used in 24 of 25 cases

audits.t: Use of a safe procedure checklist in the cardiac catheterisation laboratory.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Reported complication rate 2.0% (95% CI 1.6% to 2.4%).
audits.c: WHO-derived safe procedure checklist refined by weekly PDSA cycles, with team briefing before each procedure list.
audits.r2: Complication rate fell to 0.8% (95% CI 0.6% to 1.1%, p≤0.001); average turnaround time reduced by 3 min (p=0.027); dose area product reduced by 641.5 cGy/cm2 (p=0.002).

audits.t: Making surgical wards safer for patients with diabetes: reducing hypoglycaemia and insulin errors.
audits.st: National perioperative diabetes guidelines; aim to reduce hypoglycaemia, insulin errors and harm events by 50%
audits.f: Poor glycaemic control in 90% of amputation patients; hypoglycaemia and insulin management errors in 75%; less than 15% had specialist diabetes input; 20% needed third-party help for hypoglycaemia.
audits.c: Education and guidelines (2015), diabetes in-reach service (2016) and whiteboard sugar cube alert system for poor glycaemic control (2017) over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Hypoglycaemia reduced by more than 50%, insulin management errors by 70% and patient harm events by 75%.

audits.t: Do ward round stickers improve surgical ward round? A quality improvement project in a high-volume general surgery department.

audits.f: Checking of drug chart, IV fluid chart, analgesia, antiemetic, enoxaparin and TEDs ranged from 0% to 6%
audits.c: Ward round sticker introduced, then redesigned after questionnaire feedback
audits.r2: Noticeable improvement from baseline in all items when stickers used; entries without stickers similar to baseline

audits.t: Quality Improvement Bedside Rounding Audits Enhance Protein Provision for Pediatric Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy.
audits.tp: Nutrition delivery in paediatric intensive care

audits.t: The prescription of lidocaine patches in osteoarthritis-a complete audit cycle.

audits.t: A repeat audit of primary care management of group A streptococcal pharyngitis in Northland, New Zealand 2016.
audits.st: National guidelines for management of GAS pharyngitis
audits.f: Audit suggested adherence to national guidelines needed improvement.

audits.t: Nursing and medical contribution to Defence Healthcare Engagement: initial experiences of the UK Defence Medical Services.

audits.t: Monitoring of extrapyramidal side effects in patients on antipsychotic treatment: a completed audit cycle.

audits.t: 'CPR for Feet' care bundle to improve foot assessment in inpatient diabetes.

audits.t: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis on Discharge Following Major Cancer Surgery in the Abdomen: Improving Compliance With National Guidelines.

audits.r2: 81.25% completed prescribed course; 14.8% inpatient-only prophylaxis; 3.7% exceeded 28 days; overall non-compliance fell from 50.9% to 18.5%.

audits.t: Improving capacity and flow in a children and young people's Community Eating Disorder Service (CEDS): how a quality improvement initiative led to a reduction in waiting times in the service.
audits.st: Commissioned target of routine assessment within 2 weeks (urgent within 5 days); national standards 1 week urgent and 4 weeks routine. Aim: reduce routine referral wait from 17 weeks to 2 weeks in 12 months.
audits.f: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.
audits.c: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.
audits.r2: Average routine wait fell to 2 weeks (88% reduction), sustained; psychiatry wait list 73 to 0 by December 2022; therapy wait list 50 to 0 by April 2023; inactive cases 65 to 0.

audits.t: Standardizing Best Practices: An Initiative Utilizing Surgical Ward Round Checklists to Enhance Patient Safety and Documentation in Our Trust.

audits.t: Developing an online educational platform to expedite ADHD medication initiation in child and adolescent mental health services: a quality improvement project.

audits.t: Impact of Multi-Disciplinary Team in Implementing Clinical Audit Recommendations to Improve Health Educators' Practice at Primary Care in Qatar.

audits.st: GIRFT national 30-day readmission benchmarks: 6.1% for elective colonic resections and 8.8% for elective rectal cancer resections.
audits.f: 30-day readmission rate 14.2% (4/28), above GIRFT benchmarks; median length of stay 6 days. Causes: blocked catheter/urinary retention, port-site hernia, collection near anastomosis, gastrointestinal symptoms.
audits.c: Proposed/initiated: ERAS refresher training with quarterly compliance audits, pilot prehabilitation pathway for high-risk patients, virtual telephone follow-up within 7 days of discharge, revised discharge checklists and updated patient leaflets.

audits.t: Restoring the core acute medical unit (AMU) function - a quality improvement initiative from a district general hospital.
audits.tp: Acute medical unit function and flow
audits.st: National guidance and GIRFT principles for acute medical units
audits.f: National benchmarking and local audit showed core acute medicine processes had drifted from standards (no figures given).
audits.c: Real-time oversight, standardised multidisciplinary board rounds and rota alignment to peak demand.
audits.r2: AMU length of stay halved, daily discharges doubled and ED-to-AMU transfers increased.

audits.t: Diagnostic Yield of Upper-Tract Imaging in Visible Haematuria: A Single-Centre Retrospective Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Upper tract imaging in visible haematuria
audits.st: GIRFT Greener Pathway guidance (ultrasound first line, CT urogram for high risk)
audits.f: All 100 had upper tract imaging (CT urogram for all); potentially malignant findings in 18% (n=18); bladder cancer in 4/91 (4.3%) cystoscopies.

audits.t: Strengthening Patient Safety in Respiratory Wards by Developing a Weekend Continuity Checklist.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incomplete blood test handovers 20% (9/44); missed antibiotic coverage 11% (4/38); incomplete discharge summaries 55% (6/11).
audits.c: Structured weekend continuity checklist completed by weekday teams.
audits.r2: Missed blood test handovers 2% (1/50, p = 0.024); antibiotic lapses 4% (2/48, p = 0.469); discharge summaries 100% complete (p = 0.038).

audits.t: Audit of a Streamlined Multidisciplinary Team Meeting (MDT) to Results Clinic Pathway in Urology: Evaluating the Impact of a Nurse-Led Intervention on Consultant Clinic Waiting Times.
audits.tp: Cancer MDT to results clinic waiting time
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean wait from MDT to consultant results clinic 34.1 days (SD 7.89).
audits.c: Weekly eight-slot nurse-led results clinic opened in October 2024, with select patients booked directly from MDT.
audits.r2: Mean wait 16.0 days (SD 3.16), a 53.1% reduction (Welch's t-test p = 0.00003; paired t-test by month p = 0.0016).

audits.t: Pause the Draws: A Quality Improvement Project to Minimize Unnecessary Liver Function Tests in a Small District General Hospital.
audits.tp: Blood test requesting in acute admissions
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists guidance: LFT repeated within 72 hours inappropriate unless excluded; aim to halve inappropriate tests
audits.f: Inappropriate LFTs 72/257 (28.0%); weekly carbon footprint 263.34 kgCO2e; weekly cost £140.79.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles of simple interventions, with physician education described as central.
audits.r2: Inappropriate LFTs 18/98 (18.4%); weekly carbon footprint 83.2 kgCO2e; weekly cost £44.46.

audits.t: Impact of Electronic Prescribing on Parkinson's Disease Medication Management: A Retrospective Before-and-After Audit at a UK Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: NICE QS164, NG71 and QS120: 100% accurate prescribing and administration within 30 minutes
audits.f: Correct dose 48/50 (96%); correct formulation 48/50 (96%); correct administration times 39/50 (78%); first dose on time 36/50 (72%); all doses given 28/50 (56%).
audits.r2: Correct dose 45/50 (90%); correct formulation 44/50 (88%); correct administration times 33/50 (66%); first dose on time 36/50 (72%); all doses given 24/50 (48%).

audits.t: Using Criteria-Based Audit to Improve the Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage in a University Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia: A Before and After Study.
audits.st: Eight co-created criteria-based audit criteria for postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.f: Only 6.7% (3/45) women met all audit criteria.
audits.r2: 22% (12/55) met all criteria (p = 0.03); criteria met ranged from 24% (13/55) for fluid monitoring to 100% (55/55) for admission history and haemoglobin measurement.

audits.t: Acute Pancreatitis Management and Scoring in the Department of General Surgery, Northwick Park Hospital, 2022-2024.
audits.st: NICE NG104; modified Atlanta, Modified Marshall and Glasgow-Imrie scoring on admission and at 48 hours
audits.f: 30% had documented scoring on admission; none had repeat scoring at 48 hours; Atlanta scoring on admission and at 48 hours 0%.
audits.c: Departmental teaching, posters, and email and messaging reminders.
audits.r2: Admission scoring 40%; Atlanta scoring on admission and at 48 hours 7.5%.

audits.t: Beyond the Scalpel: Improving Operative Note Quality in Gabeet Specialized Hospital, Sudan.
audits.st: RCS Good Surgical Practice (2025) operative note standards
audits.f: Mean compliance 41.3%; date, time and type 60.8%; diagnosis and findings 55%; prophylaxis 39.2%; complications 29.4%; postoperative instructions 20%; surgeon signature 35%.
audits.c: Staff education, standardised proformas, visual reminders and increased supervision.
audits.r2: Mean compliance 71.6%; date, time and type 98% (p < 0.001); diagnosis and findings 84.3%; prophylaxis 90%; complications 65% (p = 0.02); postoperative instructions 29.4% (p = 0.08); surgeon signature 51% (p = 0.04).

audits.t: Improving Delirium Screening and Management in a Hospice Inpatient Unit: Audit and Quality Improvement Cycles Using the 4AT (Alertness, Abbreviated Mental Test-4 (AMT4), Attention, Acute Change) Tool.
audits.st: 4AT delirium screening on admission
audits.f: 4AT completed in 88%; 36% scored 4 or more; no explicit causes or structured action plans recorded.
audits.c: Modified electronic record template, embedded delirium clinical guide and clinician education over two PDSA cycles.

audits.t: From Audit to Action: Assessing and Implementing Improvements in the Operative Note Documentation for Day-Case Surgeries.
audits.st: RCS Good Surgical Practice operative note standards
audits.f: Overall 30.3%; estimated blood loss 0%; incision description 0%; DVT prophylaxis 2%; surgeon signature 8%.
audits.c: Staff education, standardised templates and supervision.
audits.r2: Overall 71.6%; operative findings, complications, closure, DVT prophylaxis and surgeon signature 100% (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Enhancing Timing and Referral Pathways for Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Two-Cycle Audit.
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: Local guidance and national guidelines: cholecystectomy within two to six weeks of presentation
audits.f: Only 3% had pre-assessment clinic arranged; readmission rate 36%.
audits.c: Structured cholecystectomy pathway, teaching sessions and a standardised booking email.
audits.r2: Pre-assessment clinic 16%; follow-up avoided in 30%; readmissions 22%.

audits.t: Sustained Improvement in Paediatric ENT Emergency Referral Accuracy Through a Multimodal Educational Strategy: A Longitudinal Study.
audits.st: Local Trust paediatric ENT emergency clinic referral guidelines (100% adherence)
audits.f: Baseline adherence 38.5%.
audits.c: Targeted junior doctor teaching, dissemination of referral criteria via online platforms and a poster campaign.
audits.r2: Guideline-compliant referrals increased to 74.0%, sustained across subsequent cycles.

audits.t: Enhancing Clinical Practice in Adult Airway Suctioning: A Two-Cycle Audit at Aswan University Hospital.
audits.st: Adult airway (endotracheal) suctioning guidelines
audits.f: Recognition of suctioning indications 24 (23%); post-suctioning procedures performed 21 (20%); awareness of special considerations 26 (25%).
audits.c: Educational intervention with didactic sessions, hands-on training and protocol reinforcement after root cause analysis.
audits.r2: Recognition of suctioning indications 91 (72.8%); post-suctioning procedures 100 (80%); awareness of special considerations 94 (75%).

audits.t: A Two-Cycle Audit of Oxygen Prescription in Hospitalised Patients Receiving Supplemental Oxygen: A Retrospective Study.
audits.st: National guidelines and local policy requiring a documented oxygen prescription with target saturation range (British Thoracic Society)
audits.f: 19% had an appropriate oxygen prescription documented on the medication chart.
audits.c: Poster campaign on oxygen prescription requirements and a mass email reminder to resident doctors.

audits.t: Translating Guidelines into Practice: A Multicentre Audit of the Implementation of ERC Survivorship and Follow-Up Recommendations After Cardiac Arrest.
audits.st: European Resuscitation Council guidelines: functional assessment before discharge and systematic review within three months covering cognition, mood, fatigue and family support (five operational criteria)
audits.f: Pre-discharge assessment offered to 116/143 (81%), completed in 81 (57%). Of 132 eligible for follow-up, 108 (82%) contacted and 87 (66%) attended; only 25% seen within 3 months (median 185 days, IQR 81-225). Cognition assessed in 44%, mood 52%, fatigue 51%; family attended in 45%.

audits.t: Antibiotic Prescribing in Patients Presenting with COVID-19: A Closed-Loop Audit with a Targeted Educational Intervention in a South Australian Hospital.
audits.st: Local consensus recommendation for antibiotics in suspected community-acquired bacterial coinfection (criteria on leukocyte count, neutrophilia and radiological findings)
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed in 26% of admissions; 16% of patients not meeting criteria received antibiotics; 62% of prescriptions met consensus criteria. (126 episodes across both periods.)
audits.c: Targeted education: guideline-focused presentations at unit meetings, emails and posters in clinical areas, and brief electronic reminder messages.
audits.r2: Antibiotic prescribing 22% of admissions (p = 0.57); prescribing in patients not meeting criteria 6% (p = 0.30); prescriptions meeting criteria 80% (p = 0.43).

audits.t: Prescription Audit as a Quality Improvement Tool: Impact of Repeated Interventions in Paediatric Outpatient Department (OPD) and Inpatient Department (IPD) Settings.
audits.st: Prescription completeness and rational drug use indicators (OPD number, legibility, generic prescribing, drugs per prescription, antibiotic use, allergy documentation)
audits.f: OPD number documented 50%; legibility 30%; generic prescribing 60%; mean 4.4 drugs per prescription; antibiotic use 80%; allergy documentation 0%.
audits.c: Repeated audit-feedback cycles with structured feedback and brief prescriber education (PDSA, 10 cycles).
audits.r2: OPD number 99%; legibility 90%; generic prescribing 92%; mean 1.5 drugs per prescription (p<0.01); antibiotic use 20% (p<0.01); allergy documentation 32%.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project for the Management of per Vaginal (PV) Bleeding in Early Pregnancy: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Patient Information Leaflets.
audits.tp: Early pregnancy bleeding management in the emergency department
audits.st: National and local standards for communication and information provision: patient information leaflet, verbal explanation and confirmation of understanding
audits.f: Leaflet provision 19%; verbal explanation 25%; confirmation of understanding 25%.
audits.c: Staff education, improved leaflet accessibility and visual reminders.
audits.r2: Leaflet provision 81%; verbal explanation 75%; confirmation of understanding 80% (all p < 0.001).

audits.t: Optimizing Ergonomic Practices in Radiology: A Closed-Loop Audit of Workstation Standards and Staff Wellbeing.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists ergonomic guidance 'Correct Use of Reporting Workstation'
audits.f: Voice recognition access 25/25 (100%); variable lighting 9/25 (36%); regular breaks 9/25 (36%).
audits.r2: Voice recognition 21/21 (100%); variable lighting 14/21 (67%); regular breaks 10/21 (48%); eye test compliance declined.

audits.t: Enhancing Adherence to Chronic Heart Failure Monitoring: A Student-Led Quality Improvement Project During Clinical Placement.
audits.st: NICE chronic heart failure monitoring standards plus local daily 12-lead ECG, six parameters within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Baseline median adherence 50.9%; fluid status and nutritional status monitoring particularly poor.
audits.c: Simplified CHF care bundle flowchart distributed to AMU staff with orientation (two PDSA cycles, student-led).
audits.r2: Median adherence 86.8% after the second PDSA cycle; nutritional status +52.6%, daily ECG +63.2%, fluid status +52.6%.

audits.t: Compliance With the British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) Standards on Ureteric Stent Documentation: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
audits.st: BAUS standards on ureteric stent documentation; target 100%
audits.f: Logbook completeness 98.2% (54/55).
audits.c: New electronic stent-tracking database introduced alongside the handwritten logbook.
audits.r2: Completeness 97.1% in both the electronic database (66/68) and the logbook (66/68).

audits.t: Appropriateness of CT Pulmonary Angiography Requests at Croydon University Hospital: An Audit.
audits.st: NICE NG158 (two-level Wells score and D-dimer before CTPA); RCR expected CTPA diagnostic yield 15-35%
audits.f: Wells score documented in 4 (6.9%); D-dimer recorded in 45 (77%); diagnostic yield 19% (11 positive).
audits.c: Mandatory Wells score and D-dimer fields added to the Cerner CTPA request form, plus educational messaging.
audits.r2: Wells score recorded in 84 (87.5%); D-dimer in 86 (89.6%); diagnostic yield 16.7% (16 positive).

audits.t: Enhancing Radiology Request Form Completeness With a Standardized Tool and Targeted Education: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists request form standards
audits.f: Patient address 0 (0.0%), urgency 0 (0.0%), clinical background 8 (16.0%), clinical question 3 (6.0%).
audits.c: Structured RCR-compliant request form and clinician educational sessions over one month.
audits.r2: Address documentation 47 (94.0%); other statistically significant improvements reported (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Understanding barriers to receiving psychological intervention for older persons who experience hallucinations.
audits.tp: Psychological therapy referral for hallucinations in older people
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 6% of older persons with hallucinations were referred to psychological services, and 1.3% received psychological interventions.
audits.c: Staff survey followed by a Plan-Do-Study-Act improvement phase (details not reported)

audits.t: Enhancing IV Cannulation Documentation in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Quality Improvement Project From Dongola Specialized Hospital.
audits.st: International standards for IV cannulation documentation (patient identifiers, insertion details, aseptic technique, site monitoring, removal data)
audits.f: Most parameters documented in 2% or fewer records (e.g. cannula gauge 2%, indication 2%, aseptic technique 2%, inserter's name 2%).
audits.c: Structured IV cannula documentation sticker and brief educational sessions.
audits.r2: Cannula gauge 100%; indication 96%; aseptic technique 86%; inserter's name 92%.

audits.t: Reducing the environmental impact of nitrous oxide in dentistry: a national quality improvement project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average carbon footprint 28.62 kg CO2e per sedation appointment (range 10.74-40.67). Estimated wastage averaged 30% with central piped supply and 4% with individual cylinders.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Follow-Up Documentation Using a Structured Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan (SOAP)-Based Template: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit at Hasahesa Teaching Hospital, Sudan.
audits.st: SOAP (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) documentation structure
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standardised SOAP documentation template, staff education sessions and routine reinforcement.
audits.r2: Marked improvement across all SOAP domains; overall adherence to SOAP structure rose considerably (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Regional Audit and Feedback Intervention to Improve Quality of Care in Ovarian Cancer Treatment: The Easy-Net Experience.
audits.st: Key recommendations and indicators from international guidelines (global adherence)
audits.f: Global adherence to guidelines 51.3%.
audits.c: Audit and feedback with quarterly feedback meetings.
audits.r2: Global adherence rose to 70.4% (2.1% increase every 6 months, 95% CI 1.6 to 2.6).

audits.t: Improving Braden Scale Risk Assessment Documentation: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit at Al-Managil Teaching Hospital, Sudan.
audits.st: Complete Braden Scale documentation (subscales, total score, risk level)
audits.f: 0% recording of all Braden subscales, total score and risk level.
audits.c: Two-month intervention: staff education and a standardised Braden documentation form.
audits.r2: 100% completion across all Braden components; significant improvements in patient identifiers and administrative fields.

audits.t: Systematic Quality Improvement in Dobutamine Stress Echocardiography: A Two-Cycle Audit Demonstrating Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy.
audits.st: Diagnostic accuracy of DSE against coronary angiography as reference standard
audits.f: Overall accuracy 82.7% (62/75); false positives 4.0%; false negatives 13.3%. (160 DSE procedures, 75 with angiography.)
audits.c: Quality interventions after analysis of cycle 1 (details not stated in abstract); a three-tier medication verification checklist was introduced after cycle 2.
audits.r2: Overall accuracy 88.9% (16/18); false positives 0%; false negatives 11.1%. (27 DSE procedures, 18 with angiography.)

audits.t: A Regional Audit on Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis Compliance and Cultural Considerations in Prescribing Porcine-Derived Low-Molecular-Weight Heparins.
audits.st: NICE NG89 VTE risk assessment and timely prophylaxis, with culturally sensitive prescribing
audits.f: JCUH had 100% VTE risk assessment compliance; other cycle 1 figures not reported.
audits.c: Staff education, posters, prescribing alerts and community outreach.
audits.r2: Risk assessment improved by 14% at UHNT; JCUH maintained 100%. Timely prophylaxis fell at UHNT, with 80% receiving it late. Leaflet distribution rose by 10% at JCUH but was absent at UHNT.

audits.t: An audit of endodontic diagnostic documentation compliance among undergraduate dental students in a UK primary care-based dental school.
audits.st: British Endodontic Society Guide to Good Endodontic Practice (2022) and UK record-keeping guidance
audits.f: Core record keeping compliance high. Provisional diagnosis recorded in 12.37% and definitive diagnosis in 66.31%; signs and symptoms documented in 65.83% (2022-2023) and 67.76% (2023-2024).

audits.t: Management and co-morbidities in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder diagnosis: A clinical audit in the Eastern Cape province, South Africa.
audits.st: NICE ADHD guideline (16-point audit tool)
audits.f: 8 of 16 standards over 80% compliance, 2 fair (50-79%), 6 poor.

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Bowel Movements Using the Bristol Stool Chart: A Quality Improvement Project in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: Nursing documentation standards for daily bowel movement recording using the Bristol Stool Chart (frequency, consistency, correct chart format, escalation/clinical action).
audits.f: Daily bowel documentation 8/30 (27%); Bristol Stool Chart used 17 (57%); stool frequency 9 (30%); correct chart format 14 (47%); consistency 15 (50%); clinical action taken 15 (50%).
audits.c: 'Bowel Matters' reminder posters at workstations, ward areas and toilets; summary to ward manager to cascade; staff advised to add bowel documentation to shift handover checklist and daily nursing care bundles.
audits.r2: Daily documentation 18 (73%) (χ2 p=0.0092); Bristol Stool Chart 27 (87%) (p=0.0035); frequency 16 (60%); correct chart format 21 (70%, reported elsewhere as 87%); consistency 23 (87%) (p=0.0321); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

audits.t: Compliance and Quality of Endoscopic Tattooing in Colorectal Cancer: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.st: Local trust endoscopic tattooing guidelines
audits.f: Of 142 lesions where tattooing was mandatory, 102 (72%) were tattooed at index colonoscopy; adequate tattooing details documented in 41.4%.
audits.c: None yet; education, standardised proformas and system changes recommended, with repeat audit.

audits.t: Improving Constipation in Critical Care Patients: A Single-Centre Prospective Cohort Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Local ICU bowel protocol
audits.f: Senna and docusate prescribed on admission in 50% of medical and 25% of surgical patients; bowels opened within 48 hours in 64.3% of medical and 36.1% of surgical patients.
audits.r2: Senna and docusate prescribed in 90% of medical and 13.2% of surgical patients; bowels opened within 48 hours in 90% of medical and 21.1% of surgical patients.

audits.t: Economic and environmental impact of reducing unnecessary coagulation screen testing on an acute medical unit: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Blood test requesting in acute admissions
audits.st: Clear clinical indication for coagulation screen requests; aim to reduce unnecessary coagulation screens by 90% within 12 months
audits.f: 34%-39% of coagulation screens were inappropriate across AMU areas; one-third of requests lacked a clear clinical indication
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: revised triage order sets, condition-specific electronic order sets, and a digital decision prompt requiring clinicians to confirm test indication
audits.r2: Inappropriate testing reduced to 20% in mSDEC, 10% in AMU 1B and 15% in AMU 1C

audits.t: Adapting the modified WHO safety checklist for non-operating room anesthesia: A Quality improvement project.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standards for sedation, including safety checklist use
audits.f: Compliant with all RCR standards except safety checklist use, which was absent in all 30 cases.
audits.c: Modified WHO safety checklist for radiology introduced, including high-risk patient identification and independent double-checking of medications.
audits.r2: 100% compliance across all RCR indicators including checklist use.

audits.t: An Audit of the Use of Total Parenteral Nutrition: Are We Using It Correctly?
audits.st: NICE (2017) and NCEPOD (2010) standards for parenteral nutrition, plus local guidelines
audits.f: Three previous audit cycles (results not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Indication documented 100%; other feeding routes excluded 13 (81.25%); MUST used 100%; 15 (93.75%) no weight/BMI documented at end of TPN; 5 (31.25%) emergency TPN started out of hours; all prescribed adequately.

audits.t: Improving Braden Scale Documentation for Pressure-Injury Risk Assessment: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit at Dongola Specialized Hospital.
audits.st: Predefined standards from international pressure-injury prevention guidelines
audits.f: None of the Braden subscales, total scores, risk levels or preventive actions were documented (0%).
audits.c: Two-month intervention: staff education, reinforcement of documentation expectations and a standardised Braden documentation form.
audits.r2: All six subscales 96.4-100%; total score 89.1%, risk level 83.6% and preventive actions 89.1%.

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Follow-Up Time of Patients Admitted With Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
audits.st: Outpatient follow-up within 14 days of discharge after acute decompensated heart failure (international guidelines)
audits.f: 14-day follow-up compliance 32 (53.33%); follow-up documented at discharge in 45 (75%); mean interval 12.43 ± 5.12 days.
audits.c: Intervention phase June to July 2025 (content not described).

audits.t: Improving ECG Interpretation Skills Among Healthcare Providers at Aswan University Hospitals: A Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Six-stage approach to ECG interpretation (local standards)
audits.f: Identified electrical activity 67 (65.7%); calculated heart rate 47 (46.1%); recognised regular rate 66 (64.7%); QRS width changes 33 (32.4%); atrial activity 68 (66.7%); atrial-ventricular relationship 49 (48.0%).
audits.c: Training and educational materials based on the new local standards.
audits.r2: Electrical activity 118 (95.2%); heart rate 103 (83.1%); regular rate 100 (80.6%); QRS width 90 (72.6%); atrial activity 91 (73.4%); atrial-ventricular relationship 94 (75.8%).

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Transfusion Safety and Monitoring at Al-Kareemat Specialized Complex, Sudan: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: WHO-aligned bedside transfusion safety, monitoring and haemovigilance criteria (eight criteria)
audits.f: Patient identification 96.8% (213/220); 15-minute observation 69.5% (153/220); end-of-transfusion vital signs 80.9% (178/220); haemovigilance reporting of suspected reactions 33.3% (2/6).
audits.c: Targeted quality improvement package of staff reinforcement and standardised monitoring and reporting documentation.
audits.r2: 15-minute observation 90.0% (108/120); end-of-transfusion vital signs 91.7% (110/120); haemovigilance reporting 100.0% (3/3).

audits.t: Transforming surgical outcomes in conflict zones: A closed-loop audit of ERAS protocols for emergency laparotomy.
audits.st: ERAS protocols for emergency laparotomy
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A Prospective Clinical Audit to Improve Compliance With Perioperative Atrial Fibrillation Prevention Protocols in Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
audits.tp: Atrial fibrillation prophylaxis after cardiac surgery
audits.st: Perioperative AF prevention: beta-blocker continued on morning of surgery, serum potassium 4.5-5.0 mmol/L, beta-blocker restarted within 12 hours postoperatively
audits.f: Preoperative beta-blocker continuation 66.3%; potassium within target 42.1%; reinstitution 96.8%.
audits.c: Permanent ICU/theatre posters, checklist attached to patient records, weekly team meetings and four-times-daily ward rounds.
audits.r2: Beta-blocker continuation 94.1% (p<0.001); potassium within target 81.2% (p<0.001); reinstitution 95.0% (p=0.72).

audits.t: Improving the Completeness of Surgical Consent Documentation Through a Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Audit at a Secondary Care Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: Predefined surgical consent documentation standards
audits.f: Hospital/file number 1.8%; surgical indication 5.4%; explanation of procedure 16.1%; anaesthetic and surgical risk explanation 1.8% each.
audits.c: Staff education, feedback and introduction of a revised consent form over two months.
audits.r2: Documentation of consent, anaesthesia type, physician and witness details and patient satisfaction confirmation 100%; anaesthetic risk explanation 97.7%; surgical risk explanation 93.2%.

audits.t: Standardizing Antimicrobial Use in a Resource-Limited Pediatric Surgical Unit in Botswana.
audits.st: WHO AWaRe guideline-based clinical pathways for appropriate antimicrobial use
audits.f: Appropriate use: paediatric surgery 33 (50.8%), orthopaedics 3 (10.3%), neurosurgery 5 (27.8%), ENT 4 (33.3%).
audits.c: Clinical pathway booklet for common surgical diagnoses, informed by WHO AWaRe, distributed to prescribers
audits.r2: Appropriate use: paediatric surgery 99 (93.4%), orthopaedics 26 (89.7%), neurosurgery 13 (72.2%), ENT 19 (95.0%).

audits.t: Diabetes in Pregnancy: A Review of Service Provision and Practice at a Maternity Center.
audits.st: National Guideline for Diabetes in Pregnancy in Qatar
audits.f: Diabetes complicated 36.1% of births (GDM 34.6%). Pre-pregnancy weight documented in 140 (52.7%) women with diabetes; 52.9% of GDM referred to dietician; early OGTT in 9/164 (5%) with BMI >30; postpartum OGTT ordered for 33.7% of GDM.

audits.t: Airway management complications: an audit from a large tertiary hospital: A single-centre study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 63 airway complications in 48 patients, overall incidence 3.4%; emergency vs elective 5.4% vs 2.2% (P = 0.002); outside theatre (ED, ICU, wards) 16.2% vs 2.5% in theatre and remote sites.

audits.t: Impact of audit and feedback on transurethral resection of bladder tumour quality: a monocentric post-completion evaluation of the RESECT trial.
audits.st: Four RESECT surgical quality indicators: detrusor muscle sampling, completeness of resection, accuracy of operative documentation, and single immediate intravesical chemotherapy
audits.f: Detrusor muscle presence 61.9% in the pre-audit phase; 70.7% during the prospective audit phase (128 patients across all phases, March 2023 to June 2025)
audits.c: Participation in the RESECT audit and feedback programme
audits.r2: Detrusor muscle presence 85.9% in the post-audit phase

audits.t: Improving Adequacy of Fine-Needle Aspiration Cytology in Non-Thyroid Head and Neck Patients Using Concurrent Liquid Cytology Sample Preparation: A Prospective Study.
audits.tp: Fine-needle aspiration cytology adequacy in head and neck
audits.st: Sample adequacy of fine-needle aspiration cytology in non-thyroid head and neck masses
audits.f: 134 of 207 (64.7%) samples adequate (dry slides only)
audits.c: From 2017, samples prepared as both dry slides and liquid cytology

audits.t: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit on Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines (NG232) for CT Cervical Spine Imaging in Adult Head Injury Patients.
audits.tp: CT cervical spine with CT head in head injury
audits.st: NICE NG232 criteria for CT cervical spine imaging in adult head injury
audits.f: 34 of 37 patients met criteria; 10 (29.4%) of these underwent CT cervical spine.
audits.c: Staff education, guideline posters and reinforcement of documentation practices.
audits.r2: 30 of 33 met criteria; 25 (83.3%) received appropriate imaging.

audits.t: Enhancing lymph node harvest in hemicolectomies: A before-and-after study of surgical preceptorship and audit feedback.
audits.tp: Lymph node yield in colorectal cancer resection
audits.st: ≥12 lymph nodes retrieved (high-yield lymphadenectomy)
audits.f: Mean LN yield 15.4 ± 7.8; high-yield cases 69%.
audits.c: Structured surgical preceptorship programme: didactic sessions, hands-on training and standard operating protocols.

audits.t: Improving Compliance With the World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist Through a Clinical Audit at Prince Osman Digna Hospital, Sudan.

audits.r2: Mechanism of injury 100%; past medical history 18% (p = 0.329); preceding investigations 4% (p = 1.000); requests meeting RCR WBCT criteria 96%

audits.t: Improving the Quality and Completeness of Cesarean Section Operative Note Documentation Through a Structured Proforma: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.st: RCOG operative documentation standards
audits.f: Suboptimal compliance across mandatory documentation, clinical operative details and postoperative management domains (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Structured operative note proforma, educational sessions, departmental feedback meetings and visual reminder posters.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in all parameters, most indicators at complete or near-complete compliance (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Effectiveness of a Structured Educational Intervention on Healthcare Providers' Knowledge of Paediatric Dehydration Management: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit at Almanagil Teaching Hospital, Sudan.
audits.st: WHO IMCI guidelines for dehydration classification and Plans A, B and C
audits.f: Correct identification of severe dehydration 23 (46.0%).
audits.c: Two-week educational programme based on WHO IMCI guidelines.

audits.t: Reporting of colorectal anastomotic leakage: Worldwide audit of national databases.
audits.tp: Anastomotic leak reporting in national registries
audits.st: 79 CoReAL (Consensus for Reporting of colorectal Anastomotic Leaks) variables
audits.f: 7 countries (18.4%) had national registries capturing post-operative outcomes; median 28 variables registered (range 18-37); median 11/25 preoperative, 6/16 intraoperative, 8/16 early post-operative and 2/22 long-term elements.

audits.t: Secondary prevention lipid management after ACS at a DGH: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Guideline-based post-ACS lipid management: inpatient lipid profile, inpatient lipid-lowering therapy management and outpatient repeat lipid profile
audits.f: Baseline full lipid profile testing 10%; appropriate LLT management 65%; post-discharge repeat testing 37%
audits.c: Structured intervention including updated blood testing panels, education and reference resources
audits.r2: Full lipid profile testing 75%; appropriate LLT management 78%; post-discharge repeat testing 63%

audits.t: An Audit of Adherence to the Agitation and Arousal Chart on an Inpatient Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Ward.
audits.st: 100% adherence to the agitation and arousal chart
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff education; results presented in multiple formats.
audits.r2: Overall improvement across all chart areas; 100% standard met only for medication choice and dose as per guideline.

audits.t: Driving Improvement in Prostate Cancer Radiotherapy Outcomes through a National Quality Assurance Program: Results from a Large UK Academic Center.
audits.st: National Prostate Cancer Audit severe late GI toxicity rate after EBRT; national average 10%
audits.f: Severe late GI toxicity confirmed in 16% (follow-up available for 281/290, 96.8%)
audits.c: Protocol changes in 2020-2021: tighter rectal dose constraints, enema use, updated verification pathway and reduced CTV-PTV margins
audits.r2: NPCA reported severe late GI toxicity reduced to 7.5%

audits.t: Improving Surgical Triage Documentation Through Implementation of a Care of the Critically Ill Surgical Patient (CCrISP)-Based Proforma: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: RCS England CCrISP framework: five criteria (A-E assessment, sepsis assessment, stability, blood gas or lactate, management plan)
audits.f: A-E assessment 0%; sepsis assessment 0%; patient stability 26.7%; management plan 60%; blood gas or lactate 73.3%.
audits.c: CCrISP-based Surgical Take Proforma with staff education via Teams and face-to-face.
audits.r2: A-E assessment 80%; sepsis assessment 46.7%; stability 93.3%; management plan 100%; blood gas or lactate 86.7% (p=0.333).

audits.t: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit of Preoperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis Adherence for Surgical Procedures at Care Medical Hospital-Alrawabi in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: International prophylaxis guidelines: correct antibiotic, weight-based dose, and administration within 60 minutes before incision
audits.f: Correct dose 21 (56.75%); timing within 60 minutes 25 (67.56%); prophylaxis correctly administered 15 (40.54%); overall adherence 15 (23.07%).
audits.c: Staff education, reinforcement of guideline-based prescribing and improved coordination between surgical and nursing teams.
audits.r2: Correct dose 55 (96.49%) (p < 0.001); timely administration 54 (94.73%) (p = 0.001); correctly administered 54 (94.73%); overall adherence 54 (83.07%) (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Improving Compliance With the Sepsis Six Care Bundle in the Surgical Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Sepsis Six bundle delivered within one hour of recognition
audits.f: Bundle within one hour 15/60 (25.0%); median time to first antibiotic 95 minutes; sepsis documented 18/60 (30.0%).
audits.c: Educational sessions for medical and nursing staff, sepsis-awareness teaching and a standard sepsis proforma.
audits.r2: Bundle within one hour 42/60 (70.0%); median time to antibiotic 50 minutes (p < 0.001); sepsis documented 51/60 (85.0%) (p < 0.0001).

audits.t: Assessment of Knowledge and Practice Gaps in the Prevention of Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury Among Doctors of Multiple Specialties in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Clinical Audit.
audits.st: KDIGO and European Society of Urogenital Radiology recommendations on risk assessment, hydration, medication review and counselling
audits.f: Mean knowledge score 3.61/4; KDIGO definition 89.2%; diagnostic timeframe 90.2%; IV hydration 91.2%; ACE inhibitor withholding 50.0%; heart failure hydration 44.1%; routine counselling 61.8%.

audits.t: Effect of pharmacist intervention on the use of serum drug assays.
audits.st: Criteria for appropriate use of serum drug assays (digoxin, theophylline, gentamicin, phenytoin) defined by the audit committee and a clinical pharmacist
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Two housestaff conferences, educational materials, an SDA report form for each order and pharmacist discussion with prescribers.
audits.r2: Appropriate overall use increased significantly (p<0.05), with significant improvement for each criterion.

audits.t: An audit of morphine prescribing in a specialist cancer hospital.
audits.st: Palliative care unit recommendations for morphine prescribing
audits.f: Weaknesses included lack of breakthrough doses, prn oral morphine without regular oral morphine, and no guideline reference to co-prescription of aperients, antiemetics and night sedation
audits.c: Education programme targeting the identified deficiencies
audits.r2: Some improvement in prescribing practice (no figures reported)

audits.t: Wessex regional radiology audit: barium enema in colo-rectal carcinoma.
audits.tp: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
audits.st: 100% demonstration and 100% diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma on barium enema performed in the 12 months before histological diagnosis
audits.f: Carcinoma demonstration rate 97%; reporting rate 85% (471 of 557 enema reports)

audits.t: Use of vitamin B-12 in Leicestershire practices: a single topic audit led by a medical audit advisory group.
audits.tp: Folate and vitamin B12 testing and treatment
audits.st: Agreed criteria for appropriate use of vitamin B12 injections
audits.f: Appropriate use 62%; 521 patients inappropriately receiving B12; correct frequency 58%; full pernicious anaemia diagnostic criteria established in 27%
audits.c: Central analysis and feedback of anonymous aggregated data by the medical audit advisory group
audits.r2: Appropriate use 72%; 352 inappropriately receiving B12 (32% reduction); correct frequency 72%; diagnostic criteria established in 28%

audits.t: Laboratory turnround time: closing the loop.
audits.st: Recommendations from an earlier laboratory turnaround time study
audits.f: GP reports reaching destination within one and two days: 13% and 68%; satellite hospital 25% and 60%; median total turnaround 50 hours (GP) and 69 hours (satellite)
audits.c: Posting results directly from the laboratory, then a twice-daily courier service
audits.r2: Within one and two days: GP 29% and 82%, satellite 78% and 82%; courier cut median turnaround to nine hours (GP) and 18 hours (satellite)

audits.t: Auditing the quality of care in emergency departments.
audits.st: Physician panel criteria for management of six chief complaints (provisional standards)
audits.f: Cases not meeting standards: chest pain 51% (36), abdominal pain 35% (35), wounds 51% (51), sore throat 43% (22).
audits.r2: Being tabulated; preliminary findings indicate an improvement in cases meeting criteria.

audits.t: Changing physicians' behavior using combined strategies and an evidence-based protocol.
audits.st: Evidence-based hospital protocol to discontinue superficial cultures in neonatal infection assessment
audits.f: Superficial cultures performed in 50.5%.
audits.c: Evidence-based protocol, opinion leader, CME rounds, immediate feedback to physicians and barriers to accessing microbiological tests.

audits.t: A clinical audit of cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
audits.st: Published survival data used as a benchmark
audits.f: Immediate survival 43% of cardiorespiratory arrests; 70% of immediate survivors alive at 24 h and 69% at six weeks or beyond; survival 71% from VF, 20% asystole, 9% EMD.

audits.t: Thrombolysis in acute myocardial infarction: an audit of practice.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Local thrombolysis guidelines (appropriate use)
audits.f: 212/335 (63%) received thrombolysis; withheld inappropriately in 8 cases and given inappropriately in 2; inpatient mortality 12% with vs 26% without thrombolysis (p < 0.005).

audits.t: Audit of start of anticoagulation treatment in inpatients.
audits.st: Local guidelines in accordance with British Society for Haematology recommendations
audits.f: Confirmatory investigations in 93% (DVT) and 79% (PE); baseline coagulation screen 52%, platelets 95%, LFT 70%, renal 87%; 33% of APTT and 58% of INR subtherapeutic; 72% of 62 discharged with therapeutic INR; 74% had anticoagulant clinic appointments

audits.t: Medical audit--need for a positive commitment.
audits.st: Criteria set of 18 questions devised by 66 dermatologists
audits.f: Centre B 60% satisfactory completion of the criteria set
audits.c: Policy decisions and protocols established at centre B only; no changes at centre A
audits.r2: Centre B 74% satisfactory completion (P < 0.0001); no improvement at centre A

audits.t: Minimum standards for the management of cleft lip and palate: efforts to close the audit loop. Royal College of Surgeons of England.
audits.tp: Cleft lip and palate care standards
audits.st: Recommended minimum standards of care for cleft lip and palate produced by a multidisciplinary steering group
audits.f: Widespread involvement of low-volume operators, incomplete networks of associated professionals and non-standardised record keeping

audits.t: Audit of the investigation and outcome of iron-deficiency anaemia in one health district.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 109 incident cases without non-GI cause, 19% had upper and lower GI investigation, 21% upper only, 7% lower only; 55 had no investigation or only faecal occult blood tests.

audits.t: Audit of medical students' experiences of paediatric teaching: a tool to monitor and improve clinical teaching.
audits.st: Departmental aims and objectives for the child health attachment
audits.f: 45.4% of students completed the questionnaire; 32% received less than 1 hour per week of protected teaching; 54% did not visit casualty.

audits.t: The use of continuous quality improvement methods to implement practice guidelines in asthma.
audits.st: National asthma management guidelines
audits.f: Satisfactory emergency assessment and treatment but poor compliance with patient education aspects of the asthma management plan
audits.c: Asthma education and management service developed
audits.r2: Improvements in asthma control and management skills for attenders and reduced re-admission rates for referred patients (no figures reported)

audits.t: Acute medical admissions: results of a national audit.
audits.st: Guidelines and standards suggested by a multidisciplinary working group on communication, referral appropriateness, finding beds, waiting and organisation of clinical care
audits.f: Main problems: suboptimal consultant involvement in acute care, frequent mismatch of admitting specialty to condition, and confusion about admission policies for elderly patients.

audits.t: Laparoscopic sterilisation: opinion and practice among gynaecologists in Scotland.
audits.st: 15 evidence-based criteria for good quality care in female laparoscopic sterilisation
audits.f: 6% of women under 25; over 85% documented counselling on failure and permanency; 88% by consultant or senior registrar; only 22% mentioned vasectomy discussion; 30% of gynaecologists provided local leaflets; day-case use 19% to 99%

audits.t: Audit on the use of prophylactic parenteral antimicrobial agents and the use of co-amoxiclav and metronidazole.
audits.st: Agreed written protocols for prophylactic antimicrobials and parenteral co-amoxiclav and metronidazole
audits.f: 65% of courses appropriate; 16% of courses too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 30%
audits.c: Agreed protocols distributed and explained to each resident; automatic stopping system
audits.r2: 72% of 226 courses appropriate; 9% too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 68% and use 33% lower

audits.t: Clinical audit and standard setting for symptomatic breast imaging in South Thames region.
audits.st: Standards set by the Regional Radiology Audit Committee at the end of the first cycle
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standards set after the first cycle
audits.r2: No significant difference in accuracy or false negative and false positive rates between screening and non-screening units; non-screening units more likely to issue equivocal reports (P = 0.000001)

audits.t: A repeat audit of hospital discharge letters in patients admitted with acute asthma.
audits.st: Recommendations from a previous audit of acute asthma discharge letters
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of recommendations from the previous audit.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation of precipitating factors (p<0.001), previous admissions (p<0.01), admission ABG (p<0.001), admission peak flow (p<0.05), discharge peak flow (p<0.001), corticosteroid and beta-2 agonist prescription (p<0.01) and inhaler device (p<0.001).

audits.t: Patient dose reduction by audit of grid usage in barium enemas.
audits.st: Removal of antiscatter grid during filling phase of barium enemas
audits.f: Grid removed in 6 of 100 examinations
audits.c: Data presented at local audit meeting; departmental policy changed to recommend routine grid removal
audits.r2: Grid removed in 96 of 100 enemas; 46.5% dose reduction for filling phase (95% CI 38-61%)

audits.t: Factors influencing blood loss in transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP): auditing TURP.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Blood loss equivalent to Hb fall of 10-15 g/L (8-11%); overall transfusion rate 10.8%
audits.r2: Overall transfusion rate 8.2%; 4.4% to 1% in smaller resections

audits.t: Length of postoperative hospital stay after transurethral resection of the prostate.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean length of stay 6.4 nights, median 5 nights.
audits.c: Increased regional anaesthesia, earlier catheter removal and pre-planned discharge.

audits.t: The development of regional nuclear medicine audit in south Thames.
audits.st: Guidelines set for ventilation-perfusion, bone, liver, thyroid and renal DMSA imaging
audits.f: Organisational audits in 10 departments found lack of facilities and space; high patient satisfaction in nine departments

audits.t: Audit of care of newly diagnosed children with diabetes mellitus in East Anglia.
audits.tp: Care of newly diagnosed childhood diabetes
audits.st: Agreed indicators of good practice
audits.f: Good education on injection, blood testing and diet; variable home visits; poor school contact and support group introduction; only three units had adolescent joint clinics; 75% questionnaire return
audits.c: Peer review and implementation of an action plan
audits.r2: Modest improvements in problem areas (no figures reported)

audits.t: COVERS for anaesthetic machines: an audit and standard.
audits.st: Extended checklist based on Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland checklist
audits.f: 236 faults found by 24 tests (range 1.1-64%); 65 (27.5%) day to day, 171 (72.5%) non-recurring
audits.r2: Faults on 59 occasions by 20 tests (range 1.0-11.6%); 16 (27%) day to day, 43 (73%) non-recurring

audits.t: Audit of practice in platelet refractoriness.
audits.st: Guidelines on management of platelet refractoriness produced by a working group
audits.f: Clinicians differed on the definition of platelet refractoriness; non-immune causes considered less important
audits.c: Guidelines on recommended practice produced and implemented
audits.r2: More patients receiving HLA-compatible platelets tested for HLA antibodies; mean 50.9% reduction in HLA-compatible platelet use

audits.t: Audit of neonatal intensive care transport--closing the loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Three serious deteriorations in transit
audits.c: Nine-person nursing transport team formed, improved training and upgraded monitoring
audits.r2: Improved temperature and pH transport scores on completion; no serious deteriorations in transit

audits.t: Audit of neonatal screening programme for phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism.
audits.st: Locally agreed clinical standards, including treatment of congenital hypothyroidism or phenylketonuria by 28 days
audits.f: All eligible babies offered screening; affected babies treated by the 28-day standard.
audits.c: Annual reports with recommendations communicated to service representatives.

audits.t: Reaudit of acute asthma admissions using a severity marker stamp and determinants of an outcome measure.
audits.st: Documentation of acute asthma severity markers
audits.f: PEFR 52%, respiratory rate 44%, ABG 72%, air entry 58%, speech 27%, exhaustion 4%; no patient received FiO2 >0.35.
audits.c: Severity marker stamp in case notes.
audits.r2: PEFR 83%, respiratory rate 81%, ABG 80%, air entry 86%, speech 86%, exhaustion 86% (p = 0.001 to 0.04); 66% received FiO2 0.60.

audits.t: Getting a validated guideline into local practice: implementation and audit of the SIGN guideline on the prevention of deep vein thrombosis in a district general hospital.
audits.st: SIGN guideline on prevention of deep vein thrombosis; target 90% of at-risk patients prescribed prophylaxis
audits.f: 72.8% (n = 163) prescribed prophylaxis; 54% (n = 122) prescribed correct prophylaxis
audits.c: Local prevention protocols developed or upgraded in line with SIGN guideline; seconded clinician coordinated implementation

audits.t: The use of audit to improve clinical effectiveness in an infrequent obstetric therapy: magnesium sulphate in severe pre-eclampsia.
audits.st: Local protocol for magnesium sulphate in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia
audits.f: Problems with time to therapeutic levels and clinical monitoring of magnesium levels
audits.c: Protocol changes and introduction of an administration and monitoring chart
audits.r2: Significant improvement in monitoring and adequacy of prophylaxis (no figures reported)

audits.t: Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit.
audits.tp: Geriatric long-term and day hospital care standards
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians CARE scheme (long-term care) and RCP geriatric day hospital audit scheme
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Improvement outweighed deterioration in all domains of geriatric care.

audits.t: A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Significant inter-laboratory variability.
audits.c: Recommendations to improve consistency and national and regional training workshops for laboratory staff.
audits.r2: Most variables had a coefficient of variation under 5%; improvements for predicted FEV1, TLC, TLCO, FVC, FRC and RV and measured FEV1 and FVC.
